text:
PIEDMONT BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
482 Fairgrove Avenue, Hickory, NC 28601
Phone: (828) 555-0148 | Fax: 828-555-0199
Email: jalvarez@piedmontbilingualslp.com

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Hernández Rodríguez
Date of Birth: March 3, 2022
Chronological Age: 4;6
Medicaid ID: NC4487219B
Case Number: CVHS-20264471
Home Address: 119 Willow Bend Court, Conover, NC 28613
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Rodríguez Pérez (mother), Carlos Hernández Gómez (father)
Home Language(s): Spanish (primary), English
Referral Source: Dr. Angela Weiss, Catawba Valley Pediatrics – Northwest Campus
Evaluation Dates: September 15, 2026 and September 22, 2026
Report Date: September 29, 2026
Evaluator: Jennifer Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Interpreter: Maria Santos, bilingual medical interpreter

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by his pediatrician, Dr. Angela Weiss, due to ongoing concerns about limited intelligibility and delayed expressive language in both Spanish and English. Mateo's mother, Lucía Rodríguez Pérez, reports that unfamiliar listeners frequently cannot understand Mateo's speech and that he often becomes frustrated when he is not understood at Little Explorers Bilingual Daycare. Mateo's teacher, Ms. Patel, raised similar concerns at Mateo's most recent parent conference.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestational age at Catawba Valley Health System – Hickory Campus on March 3, 2022, weighing 4 lbs 6 oz at birth, with Apgar scores of 6 and 8 at one and five minutes. He spent 19 days in the Newborn Intensive Care Unit at Catawba Valley Health System – Hickory Campus for respiratory distress and feeding difficulties. His mother reports no seizures, no prolonged NICU ventilation beyond the first week, and steady weight gain after discharge.

Mateo has a history of recurrent ear infections. He was followed by Dr. Thomas Brooks at Foothills Ear, Nose and Throat and Audiology – Morganton Office, part of the Catawba Valley Health System, and received bilateral pressure-equalization tubes at age 18 months. A follow-up audiological evaluation by Dr. Hannah Kim, also at Foothills Ear, Nose and Throat and Audiology – Morganton Office, on January 14, 2025, documented hearing within normal limits bilaterally with normal tympanometry. No further ENT follow-up is currently scheduled. Vision was screened as normal by the pediatric clinic at Catawba Valley Pediatrics – Northwest Campus.

Mateo's developmental motor milestones were mildly delayed: he walked independently at 17 months. He received physical therapy through early intervention from June 2023 through December 2023 and was discharged after meeting gross motor goals.

Family and Language History

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Pérez; his father, Carlos Hernández Gómez; his older brother, Diego Hernández Rodríguez, age 8; and his younger sister, Camila Hernández Rodríguez, age 2. The family's primary home language is Spanish. Lucía Rodríguez Pérez reports that she speaks Spanish almost exclusively with Mateo, while Carlos Hernández Gómez speaks a mix of Spanish and English. Diego Hernández Rodríguez primarily speaks English with Mateo at home, since he is more comfortable in English after starting school. Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Gómez, lives with the family three days a week and speaks only Spanish with the children. A neighbor, Sra. Martínez, provides occasional evening babysitting for all three children.

Carlos Hernández Gómez works full-time at Foothills Poultry Processing Plant, where he has been employed for six years; the family also refers to his workplace in Spanish as the Planta Procesadora de Pollo Foothills. Lucía Rodríguez Pérez works part-time at Bright Homes Cleaning Service, called in Spanish the Servicio de Limpieza Bright Homes, cleaning offices in the evenings after Carlos Hernández Gómez returns home from his shift. Rosa Gómez previously worked at La Cosecha Restaurant, referred to by the family as Restaurante La Cosecha, and an uncle, Pedro Gómez, currently works seasonally at Deer Creek Farm, or Finca Deer Creek as the family calls it, about forty minutes from the family's home.

Mateo has attended Little Explorers Bilingual Daycare since age two. His current teacher is Ms. Patel, and the assistant teacher in his classroom is Mr. Diaz. Mateo's mother reports that he has a close friend in his classroom, Ethan, and that he sometimes plays with another classmate whose family asked that she be referred to only by her initials, M.R.. The family dog, Luna, is reportedly Mateo's favorite playmate at home; his mother recounted that he recently told the dog "quédate aquí, Luna" during a home visit.

Previous Services

Mateo was enrolled in early intervention through the Western Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency beginning June 10, 2024, following his first Individualized Family Service Plan meeting. His service coordinator, J. Ortiz, can be reached at 1-800-555-0123 for records requests. Mateo received monthly speech-language consultation from Rebecca Chen, an early intervention SLP, from June 2024 through March 2025, focused primarily on expanding his expressive vocabulary. The family also receives nutrition support through the Catawba County WIC Program and has participated in parent workshops through Catawba County Smart Start. Mateo was discharged from early intervention at age three and transitioned to preschool special education services, though his mother reports he has not received direct speech-language therapy since early intervention ended.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted across two sessions at 482 Fairgrove Avenue, Hickory, in Catawba County. The first session, on September 15, 2026, began at 9:00 a.m. and consisted of parent interview, oral-motor examination, and administration of English-language measures. The second session, on September 22, 2026, began at 10:30 a.m. and consisted of Spanish-language measures, administered with the support of interpreter Maria Santos, along with informal conversational sampling and play-based observation. A brief phone consultation with Mateo's pediatrician's office occurred at 1:15 p.m. on September 22, 2026 to confirm current hearing status, reached at 919.555.0162.

The following standardized measures were administered in English:
- Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication subtests
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5)

Spanish-language and bilingual measures and procedures included:
- A Spanish adaptation of the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale protocol for selected informal probes
- Spanish conversational language sample, transcribed and analyzed for mean length of utterance and intelligibility
- Parent-report checklist of Spanish vocabulary and grammatical forms
- Oral-motor structural-functional examination
- Review of prior assessment history, including a Bayley-4 cognitive and motor assessment administered during early intervention in July 2023, which yielded cognitive scores within the average range

TEST RESULTS

Standardized Test Scores (English)

Test/Subtest — Standard Score — Percentile Rank — 95% Confidence Interval — Age Equivalent
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension — 73 — 4th — 68–78 — 2;9–3;0
PLS-5 Expressive Communication — 70 — 2nd — 65–75 — 2;6–2;9
PLS-5 Total Language Score — 70 — 2nd — 65–75 — 2;6–2;9
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words — 65 — 1st — 60–70 — 2;3–2;6
PPVT-5 — 78 — 7th — 73–83 — 3;0–3;3

Informal Spanish Measures

Using the Spanish conversational sample, Mateo's mean length of utterance was 3.1 morphemes, below expectations for his chronological age of 4;6. Intelligibility in connected Spanish speech to an unfamiliar listener was judged at 40%, and intelligibility to a familiar listener (his mother) was judged at 65%. In structured single-word naming tasks in Spanish, Mateo correctly named 11 of 20 common objects.

Articulation and Phonology

Mateo demonstrated a restricted phonetic inventory in both languages. In English, he produced final consonant deletion in approximately 60% of opportunities and stopping of fricatives, substituting /t/ for /s/ and /d/ for /z/. He produced the target word "sun" as "tun" and "zoo" as "du." In Spanish, he exhibited difficulty with the trilled /r/ and the tap /ɾ/, frequently substituting [w] or omitting the sound, producing "perro" as "peo" and "para" as "paa." Both error patterns were consistent with developmental phonological processes but were judged more frequent and more persistent than typical for his age in both languages.

Oral-Motor and Voice/Fluency

Oral-motor structural-functional examination revealed adequate strength, range of motion, and symmetry of the lips, tongue, and jaw for speech purposes. No structural abnormalities were observed. Voice quality was within normal limits. No dysfluencies were noted during either session.

Receptive and Expressive Language

In English, Mateo followed 2-step directions with mod cues and understood basic spatial and quantity concepts with 70% accuracy. Expressively, his utterances in English were primarily 2-3 word combinations, with limited use of grammatical morphemes such as plural -s and past tense -ed. In Spanish, receptive vocabulary and comprehension of simple commands appeared stronger than expressive output; Mateo could point to 9 of 10 requested familiar objects but used primarily single-word or two-word Spanish utterances expressively. Code-switching between English and Spanish occurred frequently, consistent with typical bilingual development, but overall language functioning was reduced relative to age expectations in both languages.

Social Communication and Behavioral Observations

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with play materials. He demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking in play-based interaction with the examiner and interpreter. He showed mild frustration, including brief vocal protest and gesture use, when he was not understood during conversational attempts, consistent with his mother's report. No concerns regarding social reciprocity, restricted interests, or repetitive behaviors were observed or reported.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, informal measures, parent report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a bilingual language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, along with a moderate speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility in both languages. His receptive and expressive language scores fall in the moderately to severely delayed range in English, and his informal Spanish measures similarly indicate delay relative to same-age bilingual peers. His difficulties are not attributable to hearing loss, given normal audiological findings, nor solely to typical bilingual language-learning patterns, given that his delays are present and comparable in magnitude across both of his languages.

Mateo's phonological error patterns, including final consonant deletion, stopping, and difficulty with Spanish rhotics, are contributing significantly to reduced intelligibility, particularly for unfamiliar listeners. These patterns, combined with reduced mean length of utterance and limited grammatical morpheme use, are consistent with a diagnosis of:
- Developmental Language Disorder, expressive-receptive, affecting both languages (ICD-10 F80.2)
- Phonological Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0)

CPT codes for this evaluation include 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) and 92521 (evaluation of speech fluency), modifier -GN.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo is recommended for individual speech-language therapy two times weekly, 30 minutes per session, with goals addressed bilingually whenever possible, coordinated with his preschool special education team at Little Explorers Bilingual Daycare.

2. Therapy should target:
   a. Increasing phonological inventory and accuracy of final consonants, fricatives, and Spanish rhotics using a Cycles phonological approach, targeting one to two patterns per cycle.
   b. Expanding mean length of utterance and grammatical morpheme use in both English and Spanish, with home carryover activities for Lucía Rodríguez Pérez and Carlos Hernández Gómez using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies.
   c. Supporting functional communication and reducing frustration using visual supports and modeling, with consideration of PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing as needed for motor speech placement.

3. IFSP/IEP outcome goals, if applicable, should include:
   a. Outcome 1: Mateo will produce final consonants in at least 80% of opportunities across both languages during structured and conversational speech.
   b. Outcome 2: Mateo will combine 3-4 words into grammatically appropriate utterances in both English and Spanish with min cues.

4. A re-evaluation is recommended in approximately six months, or sooner if progress is slower than expected, to reassess intelligibility and language growth in both languages.

5. Continued coordination with Dr. Angela Weiss at Catawba Valley Pediatrics – Northwest Campus and with audiology at Foothills Ear, Nose and Throat and Audiology – Morganton Office is recommended to monitor for any recurrence of middle ear effusion, which could affect progress.

6. The family may benefit from continued connection with Western Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency service coordination, through J. Ortiz, to support transition planning and access to community resources, including continued participation in Catawba County Smart Start parent programming.

7. The clinician recommends that all providers working with Mateo communicate with the family bilingually when possible, given that Rosa Gómez and other caregivers are primarily Spanish-speaking. For urgent communication when the family is traveling to visit relatives, Lucía Rodríguez Pérez provided an alternate contact number for her mother's household in Mexico, +52 81 5555 0147, where Mateo and his siblings sometimes stay during school breaks.

This report and its recommendations were discussed with Lucía Rodríguez Pérez and Carlos Hernández Gómez on September 29, 2026, with interpretation support provided by Maria Santos. Questions regarding this report may be directed to the undersigned at (828) 555-0148 or jalvarez@piedmontbilingualslp.com.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Licensed Speech-Language Pathologist
Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

Client: Mateo Alejandro Cruz (DOB 04/12/2022; age 4;6)

Provider: Diana Flores, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish), Carolina Pediatric Speech Partners
Service coordinator: Ms. Renata Soto, Piedmont CDSA
Interpreter: not needed; mother is bilingual.

2. BACKGROUND / SUBJETIVO

Su mamá, Marisol Cruz, reports Mateo had a good week. "Está hablando más en casa," she said, aunque "a veces se frustra cuando no le entendemos." The family continues to attend the Saturday playgroup at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida and the bilingual story hour at the East Branch Library. Marisol noted that WIC recertification is due next month and that Ms. Soto is helping schedule the IFSP review. Mateo also attends two mornings at Little Sprouts Early Head Start, where la maestra Carmen has been working on turn-taking during circle time.

3. SESSION OBJECTIVE

Per IFSP outcome #2: increase intelligibility of final consonants and expand use of two-word combinations in spontaneous speech, targeting /k/, /t/, and /s/ in final position.

4. PROCEDURES / ACTIVITIES

Session used structured play with Mateo's toy animals and a picture book about pets, incorporating Hanen strategies and PROMPT tactile cueing. Mateo's dog, Rocky, was present and served as a natural motivator; Mateo pointed and said "Rocky go out," targeting final /t/. He also spontaneously named his sister, saying "Ximena sock off," approximating final /k/ with mod cues. Clinician modeled target words and provided min to mod cues throughout.

5. DATA / RESULTS

Final consonant production: /k/ 6/10 trials correct with mod cues; /t/ 7/10 with min cues; /s/ 3/10, emerging. Two-word combinations occurred spontaneously in 8 of 12 opportunities (67%). Intelligibility estimated at 60% in context for unfamiliar listeners, up from 45% at last formal assessment. No formal standardized testing administered this session; most recent PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension standard score was 76 (5th percentile), age equivalent 2;6–3;0.

6. ASSESSMENT

Mateo continues to demonstrate steady progress toward final consonant accuracy and expressive syntax goals. Code-switching observed is developmentally appropriate given the home bilingual environment; no disfluency or oral-motor concerns noted today.

7. PLAN

Continue weekly 45-minute sessions in-home. Will coordinate with Little Sprouts Early Head Start staff, including la maestra Carmen, regarding carryover of final-consonant targets. CPT 92507, ICD-10 F80.1. Next IFSP review scheduled November 18, 2026 with Ms. Soto and possible input from DSS regarding transportation support.

8. COORDINATION OF CARE

Spoke briefly with doña Lupe, the children's babysitter, who confirmed availability for the next two sessions. Will follow up with Smart Start of Orange County regarding a possible referral for a sibling screening for Ximena. Family can be reached at (919) 555-0148 or marisolcruz26@example.com.

Signed: Diana Flores, M.S., CCC-SLP
Carolina Pediatric Speech Partners

Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC
1275 Fairview Park Drive, Suite 220
Greensboro, 27410
Main line: (336) 555-0184 | Fax: 336-555-0185
"Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy" (CBSLT)

October 2, 2026

Re: Mateo Alejandro Flores Ramírez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: November 14, 2022
Medicaid ID: 784512093K
Record ID: CBSLT-22104

Dear Lucía Ramírez Torres and Francisco Flores Delgado,

Thank you for trusting our team with Teo's speech-language evaluation. I know it can feel like a lot to sit through an appointment like this, so I want to walk you through everything we found in plain language, and then talk about what we recommend next. My name is Daniela Marín, MS, CCC-SLP, and I am a bilingual (English/Spanish) speech-language pathologist with Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC. I met with your family on September 24, 2026 at 9:30 a.m. here at our Greensboro office, and the session lasted about two hours. Mr. Rafael Ortiz, our Spanish-language interpreter, was present for the parts of the interview where you felt more comfortable speaking Spanish, and I want to thank him for his help making sure nothing got lost between languages.

**Reason for Referral**

Teo was referred to us by his pediatrician, Dr. Angela Byrne, after his 3-year well-child visit, because you both shared concerns that he was not yet combining words the way his older sister Guadalupe ("Lupita") did at the same age, and that unfamiliar adults often cannot understand him. His teacher at The Blue Acorn Treehouse Preschool, Ms. Hannah Whitfield, also mentioned to you that Teo tends to point and gesture more than he talks during circle time, and that she has to guess at what he wants during snack and playground time. Mr. Carlos Núñez, the assistant teacher in his room, told you something similar during afternoon pickup a few weeks ago.

**Background Information**

Mateo is a 3;10-year-old boy who lives at home with both of his parents, his older sister Lupita (age 6), and his younger brother Jesús, whom the family calls "Chuy" (age 1). You told me that Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Torres Mendoza, lives in Mexico City and speaks with the family almost every evening by phone at +52 55 4821 3367; she is a big part of Teo's life even from a distance, and he often says "abuela" when he hears her voice on speaker. You also mentioned that Mateo's cousin José Torres Ramírez, whom everyone calls "Pepe," stays with your family most weekends while his own parents work, and that Teo follows him around the house constantly. At daycare, his best friend is a boy named Juan Pérez, known to his classmates as "Juanito," and the two of them are nearly inseparable during outdoor play.

The family's home address is 4482 Willow Creek Lane, Lexington, Davidson County, 27292. Lucía works at Henderson Poultry Processing on the second shift, and Francisco works for Carolina Tile & Stone doing installation work, which sometimes means he travels out of town for a few days at a time. You can be reached at 336-555-0198 (mother's cell), (336) 555-0162 (father's cell), or 336.555.0147 (home line).

**Birth and Medical History**

You shared that Teo's pregnancy and delivery were largely uncomplicated. He was born at 38 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 6 lbs 11 oz and Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. He stayed in the hospital for the standard two days and went home with no NICU stay. His early motor milestones (sitting, crawling, walking) were all within typical ranges, with walking starting around 13 months.

Medically, Teo has had frequent ear infections since he was about 18 months old, and he saw an ENT who placed bilateral ear tubes in March 2024. Since the tubes were placed, the frequency of infections has gone down a lot, which is good news. An audiologist, Dr. Priya Shah, completed a hearing screening on August 12, 2026 and found hearing within normal limits bilaterally, which tells us that hearing loss is not contributing to his speech and language difficulties right now. He has no history of seizures, no significant head injuries, and is not currently taking any daily medications. His vision screening at his last pediatric visit was also normal.

**Family and Language History**

Your family speaks primarily Spanish at home, with English used more and more as Lupita brings home vocabulary from kindergarten and shares it with her brothers. You estimated that Teo hears roughly 70 percent Spanish and 30 percent English in a typical week, mostly because The Blue Acorn Treehouse Preschool operates in English during the day. You noted that Teo's first words came later than his sister's, closer to 18-20 months rather than the 12-14 month range you remember for Lupita. You also shared that there is a family history of late talking on Francisco's side; he mentioned that he himself did not combine words until he was almost 4, and that his younger brother had a similar pattern.

You described Teo's current communication as mostly single words in both languages, with a handful of two-word combinations like "más agua" and "no quiero," but very few true sentences. He understands much more than he says, following simple directions in both English and Spanish, like bringing you his shoes or putting his cup in the sink. He does use gestures frequently, pointing, pulling your hand, and shaking his head, to get his needs met, and this has actually reduced some frustration at home, though it does not help much at daycare where teachers are not always sure what he wants.

**Assessment Procedures**

During our session, I administered a combination of standardized and informal measures in both English and Spanish, with support from interpretation services where needed, and I also gathered information from you both through structured interview. The following tools were used:

- Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool, Third Edition (CELF Preschool-3), screening items only
- Language sample analysis using SALT coding, including codes such as [EW] for word-level errors
- Parent/caregiver interview and observation of play-based interaction

Mateo was cooperative throughout testing, though he needed frequent breaks and benefited from being allowed to hold a small toy car during tabletop tasks. He separated from you easily and engaged well with both me and Mr. Ortiz.

**Test Results**

Below is a summary of Teo's scores. I want to walk through what these numbers mean rather than just leaving you with a table, because standard scores and percentiles can look scarier than they actually are.

| Measure | Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 (English) | Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12th | 76-88 |
| PLS-5 (English) | Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd | 62-74 |
| PLS-5 (Spanish) | Auditory Comprehension | 85 | 16th | 79-91 |
| PLS-5 (Spanish) | Expressive Communication | 71 | 3rd | 65-77 |
| GFTA-3 | Sounds-in-Words | 73 | 4th | 65-81 |
| CELF Preschool-3 | Screening Total | Below cutoff | — | — |

On the PLS-5, Teo's understanding of language (Auditory Comprehension) was mildly below average in both English and Spanish, landing in the low-average to below-average range. His Expressive Communication scores, however, were significantly below average in both languages, which matches what you have told me about his limited word combinations. Because his scores were low in both English and Spanish rather than just one, this points toward a true language disorder rather than something related only to learning two languages, which is an important distinction. Bilingualism itself does not cause language delays, and I want to be very clear about that.

On the GFTA-3, Teo scored in the below-average range for speech sound production. He substitutes /t/ for /k/ in word-initial position (so "cat" becomes "tat"), and he simplifies consonant clusters, saying "poon" for "spoon" and "téfono" for "teléfono." During the session, he attempted the word "camión" and produced "tamión," showing that same /k/-to-/t/ pattern in Spanish as well, which tells us this is a consistent articulation pattern across both languages rather than two separate problems.

In our language sample, Teo used mostly single-word utterances, with occasional two-word combinations. Out of 20 opportunities to combine words during structured play, he produced two-word phrases on 6 of 20 (30%) attempts, well below what we would expect for his age. He used almost no grammatical markers, such as plurals or past tense, in either language.

**Clinical Impressions**

Based on today's results, parent report, and classroom observations, Teo presents with a Mixed Expressive-Receptive Language Disorder, more pronounced in expressive language, along with a Speech Sound Disorder affecting intelligibility. His difficulties are present across both English and Spanish, which rules out typical second-language acquisition as the explanation and instead points to a true underlying language and speech disorder. This pattern is consistent with ICD-10 codes F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (speech sound disorder), billed today under CPT codes 92523 and 92522.

It is encouraging that Teo's comprehension, while mildly delayed, is a relative strength, and that he is already using gestures and some words purposefully to communicate. These are good building blocks for therapy. Given the family history you shared about Francisco and his brother, there may also be a genetic component to consider, though this does not change our recommendations.

**Recommendations**

1. I recommend that Teo begin individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, with sessions delivered in both English and Spanish, through Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC or a comparable bilingual provider in your area.
2. Therapy should target expressive vocabulary growth, two- and three-word combinations, and early grammatical markers, alongside articulation work on cluster reduction and the /k/ versus /t/ substitution pattern, using a structured approach such as Cycles for the phonological component.
3. I recommend a referral to Piedmont CDSA (Children's Developmental Services Agency) to explore eligibility for additional early intervention supports, given Teo's age. Ms. Denise Caldwell, the service coordinator who has worked with families in your area, can be reached at 336-555-0210 to begin that process.
4. At The Blue Acorn Treehouse Preschool, I would encourage Ms. Whitfield and Mr. Núñez to model short phrases ("I want ball," rather than just "ball") and to pause expectantly after asking Teo questions, giving him extra time to respond before jumping in.
5. At home, continue speaking Spanish naturally; there is no need to reduce Spanish exposure to "help" his English. Narrate daily routines in whichever language feels most natural to you in the moment, and expand on what Teo says rather than correcting him directly. For example, if he says "agua," you might respond, "Sí, quieres más agua."
6. Please schedule a follow-up hearing check with Dr. Shah's office in six months given his history of ear infections, even though today's screening was normal.
7. I will plan to reassess Teo's progress in approximately six months, or sooner if your family or his teachers have new concerns.

**Next Steps**

Our front desk will reach out within the next week to schedule Teo's first therapy sessions. If you have any questions in the meantime, please do not hesitate to call me directly at 336-555-0184, extension 214, or reach our main scheduling line at 336-555-0190. If it is easier to text, our Spanish-language care coordinator, Mr. Ortiz, can be reached at (336) 555-0233.

Thank you again for the time you spent with us, and for being so open about Teo's history during our visit. It is clear that he is surrounded by people who love him, from Lupita and Chuy at home, to his cousin Pepe on weekends, to his friend Juanito at school, and even his grandmother Rosa checking in every evening from Mexico. That kind of support will make a real difference as Teo works on his communication skills, and we are glad to be part of that team.

Warm regards,

Daniela Marín, MS, CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC (CBSLT)
Direct: 336-555-0184 ext. 214
Email: d.marin@carolinabilingualslt.com

Piedmont CDSA, attn. Ms. Denise Caldwell

La madre, Ana María de la Cruz, dijo en la reunión: "Nos preocupa que Teo todavía no dice frases completas. Él solo dice una palabra a la vez, como 'agua' o 'más', y a veces se frustra porque no lo entendemos."

La abuela, Rosa Gómez Herrera, comentó a través de la intérprete Patricia Soto: "Cuando lo cuido yo, él me señala las cosas, pero no intenta decir las palabras. Me preocupa que dependa demasiado de señalar."

Historial de nacimiento relevante para el expediente: Mateo nació con 34 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 2.1 kg y puntuación de Apgar de 8/9.

**V. EVALUACIÓN ACTUAL DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE**

Se administró el PLS-5 en español el 20 de febrero de 2026. Resultados:
- Subprueba de Comunicación Auditiva: puntuación estándar de 73, percentil 4, equivalente de edad de 1;8.
- Subprueba de Comunicación Expresiva: puntuación estándar de 68, percentil 2.
- Intervalo de confianza del 95%: 65-75.

Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, Mateo produjo la palabra meta "pelota" como [peo], omitiendo la consonante final. En 3 de 10 intentos produjo el sonido /s/ correctamente en posición inicial, equivalente al 30% de precisión. Con claves moderadas, logró combinar dos palabras en 25% de las oportunidades durante la sesión.

Se recomienda continuar monitoreando el progreso usando el CELF Preschool-2 en la próxima evaluación formal, prevista cuando el niño alcance la edad de 2;6.

**Resultado 3:** Mateo iniciará interacciones de juego con pares, incluyendo su compañera Valentina Ríos, usando al menos una palabra o gesto comunicativo.

NOTA DE SESIÓN DIARIA DE TERAPIA DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

1. INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Cliente: Mateo Fernández
Fecha de nacimiento: 04/12/2021
Edad cronológica: 4;6
Número de caso: WCD-88213-F
Número de Medicaid: 998712345A
Fecha de la sesión: October 9, 2026
Hora de la sesión: 2:15 p.m.
Clínica: María Elena Vásquez, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC

2. ANTECEDENTES

Mateo recibe servicios de terapia del habla a través del Agencia Comunitaria para el Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios Familiares (ACDISF), coordinados por su coordinadora de servicios, Yolanda Reyes. Es estudiante de prekínder en la Escuela Primaria Forest Pines, dentro del Sistema de Escuelas Públicas del Condado de Wake, en el salón de la maestra Patricia Hidalgo. Vive con su madre, Lucía Rodríguez, su padre, Carlos Fernández, y su hermana mayor, Camila Fernández, en 412 Hollow Creek Lane, Raleigh, Carolina del Norte. Su niñera, Rosa Martínez, lo recoge de la escuela tres días por semana. La familia tiene un perro llamado Rocky, al que Mateo menciona con frecuencia durante las sesiones.

3. ASISTENCIA Y PARTICIPACIÓN

La sesión se realizó en el hogar con la presencia de la madre y, por teléfono, el intérprete Esteban Núñez. Mateo estuvo alegre y cooperador durante los 30 minutos de intervención directa.

4. OBSERVACIÓN CONDUCTUAL

Mateo jugó con figuras de animales y relató que fue al parque con sus primos Diego y Valentina el fin de semana. También describió un juego con su compañero de clase Ethan y su amiga Sofía durante el recreo.

5. OBJETIVOS TRABAJADOS Y RESULTADOS

Se trabajó el objetivo 2 del IFSP: producción del fonema /r/ en posición inicial de palabra. Mateo produjo la palabra objetivo correctamente en 8/10 ensayos con mod cues, mejorando desde 5/10 en la sesión previa. Durante el juego con el perro de juguete, dijo "Rocky corre", aproximando el sonido meta. Se usó el enfoque PROMPT junto con estrategias de Hanen para modelar el lenguaje en el contexto del juego. Se registró el código [EW] en la transcripción SALT para marcar un intento fallido de palabra.

6. EVALUACIÓN Y PROGRESO

En la evaluación administrada el mes pasado, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 82 en el PLS-5, subprueba de Comprensión Auditiva, correspondiente al percentil 12. En el CELF-5 obtuvo un intervalo de confianza de 73-83. Su edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo fue 2;6–3;0. El pediatra, Dr. Juan Pablo Ortiz, documentó el código F80.1 en el expediente médico, facturado bajo el código 92507.

7. COMENTARIOS DE LA FAMILIA Y DEL ENTORNO ESCOLAR

La madre, Lucía Rodríguez, reportó que Mateo practica en casa con su hermana Camila Fernández y que la niñera Rosa Martínez refuerza las palabras meta durante las tardes. La maestra Patricia Hidalgo indicó que Mateo participa más en círculo con sus compañeros desde que inició las sesiones.

8. PLAN

Se continuará con sesiones semanales de 30 minutos. Próxima cita: October 16, 2026 a las 2:00 p.m.. Contactar a la familia al (919) 555-0148 o por correo a lucia.rodriguez88@example.com para reprogramar si fuera necesario.

Firmado,
María Elena Vásquez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC

PLAN DE SERVICIOS FAMILIARES INDIVIDUALIZADO (IFSP) – REVISIÓN
Programa de Infantes y Niños Pequeños de Carolina del Norte

Oficina del CDSA: Centro de Desarrollo y Servicios para Niños del Área de Piedmont Central (CDSA Piedmont Central)
Dirección de la oficina: 215 Avenida Worth, Asheboro, NC 27203
Teléfono de la oficina: (336) 555-0148

Fecha de la revisión del IFSP: 14 de agosto de 2026
Fecha del IFSP anterior: 10 de febrero de 2026
Próxima revisión programada: 12 de febrero de 2027

Niña: María José Hernández Paz (conocida como "Majo")
Fecha de nacimiento: 3 de junio de 2023 (edad cronológica: 3;2)
Número de expediente del CDSA: 048372-RC
Número de Medicaid: 900412785B
Diagnóstico/elegibilidad: retraso en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y receptivo (ICD-10 F80.2), elegible bajo la categoría de retraso establecido.

Historia de nacimiento: Majo nació a las 35 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 2,268 gramos y un puntaje de Apgar de 8 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. Permaneció 6 días en la unidad de cuidados especiales para recién nacidos antes de ir a casa.

INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR

Madre: Lucía Fernanda Paz Rivera
Padre: Ernesto Hernández Soto
Domicilio familiar: 742 Calle Mill, Liberty, NC 27298, Condado de Randolph
Teléfono de la madre: (336) 555-7762
Teléfono del padre: (336) 555-3391
Correo electrónico de la familia: lupaz1990@mailweb.com

Hermanos en el hogar:
- Sol Hernández Paz, 6 años, de primer grado.
- Mateo Hernández Paz, 9 años, de cuarto grado.

Otra persona que ayuda con el cuidado: la abuela materna, Rosa Rivera Campos, quien cuida a Majo tres tardes por semana mientras su mamá trabaja.

Mascota de la familia: una perrita llamada Luna, muy querida por los niños.

Coordinadora de servicios: Carla Jiménez Ortiz, de la Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Familiares de Randolph (ACSF Randolph), bajo contrato con CDSA Piedmont Central.
Teléfono: (336) 555-9013
Correo: cjimenez@acsfrandolph.org

Tabla de contactos del equipo:

Nombre	Rol	Agencia	Teléfono
Carla Jiménez Ortiz	Coordinadora de servicios	ACSF Randolph	(336) 555-9013
Patricia Gómez Lara	Patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe	Terapias Integrales de Carolina del Norte, PLLC	(336) 555-4420
Andrés Villalobos	Pediatra	Clínica Pediátrica de Asheboro	(336) 555-6002
Karen Suárez	Audióloga	Hospital Regional de Randolph	(336) 555-7788

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA

La familia comparte, en sus propias palabras: "Queremos que Majo pueda decirnos lo que necesita sin frustrarse tanto. A veces grita o nos jala de la ropa porque no le entendemos", dice la señora Paz Rivera. El padre añade: "Yo trabajo turnos largos en Muebles Castle Hill y no siempre puedo venir a las citas, pero quiero aprender qué hacer en casa con ella."

La familia también menciona su preocupación de que Majo confunde ciertas palabras. Por ejemplo, informan que Majo confunde la palabra "sol" (el astro) con el nombre de su hermana Sol, y durante los ejercicios de los sonidos /s/ y /l/ a veces le dice "Sol" a su hermana cuando en realidad quiere producir la palabra objetivo "sol". La madre comenta: "Es gracioso, pero a veces no sabemos si está llamando a su hermana o intentando decir la palabra del sol."

Prioridades de la familia:
1. Que Majo use palabras para pedir lo que quiere en vez de llorar o gritar.
2. Que Majo siga instrucciones sencillas en español e inglés en la guardería.
3. Que la familia reciba materiales bilingües para practicar en casa.
4. Prepararse para la transición a servicios de preescolar antes de que Majo cumpla 3 años.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Majo se despierta a las 6:30 a.m. y desayuna con su familia. Su mamá la lleva al Centro Early Head Start de Liberty a las 7:45 a.m., donde está en el salón de la maestra Brenda Whitfield junto con otros siete niños de edades similares. Durante el día, Majo participa en tiempo de círculo, juego libre y una siesta a las 12:30 p.m.. Su papá la recoge a las 5:15 p.m. los días que no trabaja hasta tarde; los otros días la recoge su abuela, Rosa Rivera Campos.

En las noches, la familia cena junta alrededor de las 6:45 p.m. y después los niños juegan con Luna en el patio. Majo se baña a las 7:30 p.m. y se acuesta a las 8:00 p.m. después de que su hermana Sol le lee un cuento corto. Los fines de semana, la familia suele visitar a la abuela Rosa Rivera Campos o asistir a actividades en la biblioteca local.

OTRAS AGENCIAS QUE APOYAN A LA FAMILIA

- Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Randolph (DSS de Randolph): la familia recibe asistencia alimentaria; la trabajadora de caso es Yesenia Morales.
- Programa WIC del Condado de Randolph: provee fórmula y asesoría nutricional; la familia asiste a citas mensuales.
- Asociación Smart Start del Condado de Randolph (Smart Start de Randolph): ayudó a la familia a conseguir una beca de guardería para Majo.
- Early Head Start de Randolph: programa bajo el cual Majo asiste al Centro Early Head Start de Liberty; su trabajadora de enlace familiar es Diana Osorio.

La familia también planea la transición futura con el Sistema de Escuelas Públicas del Condado de Randolph (Escuelas de Randolph); se anticipa que Majo asistirá al programa de preescolar de la Escuela Primaria Liberty cuando cumpla tres años, si continúa calificando para servicios.

RESULTADOS DE LA EVALUACIÓN

Evaluación realizada el 28 de julio de 2026 por Patricia Gómez Lara, CCC-SLP, con instrucciones traducidas e interpretación cultural para la familia hispanohablante.

Prueba	Subprueba	Puntaje estándar	Percentil	Edad equivalente
Preschool Language Scales, Quinta Edición (PLS-5)	Comprensión auditiva	78	7	20-22 meses
Preschool Language Scales, Quinta Edición (PLS-5)	Comunicación expresiva	72	3	18-20 meses
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Tercera Edición (GFTA-3)	Sonidos en palabras	81	10	—

Los puntajes compuestos de lenguaje se ubican dentro de un intervalo de confianza de 68-84 (95%). En producción espontánea, Majo combina dos palabras en aproximadamente 3 de 10 enunciados y usa un vocabulario expresivo estimado de 45 palabras, según el informe de los padres y la observación clínica.

En cuanto a los sonidos del habla, Majo omite consonantes finales y simplifica grupos consonánticos. Produce los sonidos /m/, /p/, /n/ y /t/ de forma consistente, pero sustituye /s/ por [t] en posición inicial (por ejemplo, dice "tol" por "sol") y omite /l/ en grupos como "azul", que produce como "azú". Con apoyo moderado (mod cues), logra aproximar /s/ en sílabas aisladas el 60% de las veces.

RESULTADOS DEL IFSP Y ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado IFSP n.º 1: Majo usará palabras y frases cortas en español e inglés para pedir objetos y acciones deseadas, en casa y en el Centro Early Head Start de Liberty.
Estrategias:
- Terapia de lenguaje individual usando el enfoque Hanen para fomentar el lenguaje dentro de las rutinas diarias.
- Modelado de lenguaje durante las comidas y el juego, con énfasis en combinaciones de dos palabras.
- La familia practicará el uso de tableros de comunicación sencillos en casa durante las comidas.
Criterio de logro: Majo combinará dos palabras de forma espontánea en al menos 8 de 10 oportunidades observadas durante dos sesiones consecutivas.

Resultado IFSP n.º 2: Majo producirá los sonidos /s/ y /l/ en palabras objetivo con min cues, en al menos el 75% de los ensayos.
Estrategias:
- Práctica de palabras objetivo con pares mínimos, incluyendo la palabra objetivo "sol", "silla" y "luna".
- Uso del enfoque Cycles para la reestructuración fonológica en ciclos de seis semanas.
- La familia recibirá una lista de palabras objetivo bilingües para practicar durante el baño y el juego con Luna.
Nota clínica: dado que la palabra objetivo "sol" coincide con el nombre de la hermana de la niña, Sol, la terapeuta usará también la palabra "gol" como alternativa para evitar confusión durante las sesiones de práctica en casa.

Resultado IFSP n.º 3: Majo seguirá instrucciones de un paso en el salón del Centro Early Head Start de Liberty el 80% de las veces observadas por la maestra Brenda Whitfield.
Estrategias:
- Consulta mensual entre Patricia Gómez Lara y la maestra Brenda Whitfield para alinear estrategias de aula y terapia.
- Uso de apoyos visuales y gestos junto con instrucciones verbales breves.
Criterio de logro: documentado en las notas semanales del salón y revisado por la coordinadora de servicios, Carla Jiménez Ortiz.

Resultado IFSP n.º 4 (prioridad familiar): la familia recibirá materiales de práctica bilingües y participará en al menos una sesión de capacitación para padres antes de la próxima revisión, programada para el 12 de febrero de 2027.

CALENDARIO DE SERVICIOS

Servicio	Proveedor	Frecuencia	Duración	Lugar	Fecha de inicio
Terapia del habla y lenguaje	Patricia Gómez Lara, Terapias Integrales de Carolina del Norte, PLLC	2 veces por semana	30 minutos	Centro Early Head Start de Liberty	18 de agosto de 2026
Coordinación de servicios	Carla Jiménez Ortiz, ACSF Randolph	1 vez al mes	45 minutos	Domicilio familiar	18 de agosto de 2026
Consulta de audiología	Karen Suárez	Según necesidad	60 minutos	Hospital Regional de Randolph	2 de septiembre de 2026

Facturación: código CPT 92507 para terapia individual de lenguaje, modificador GN; código CPT 92523 para la evaluación inicial de habla y lenguaje.

CONSENTIMIENTO Y FIRMAS

La familia participó en la elaboración de este plan y da su consentimiento para los servicios descritos arriba. Este IFSP fue revisado y aprobado en una reunión celebrada el 14 de agosto de 2026 en las oficinas de CDSA Piedmont Central, con interpretación simultánea provista por Marisol Delgado, intérprete certificada.

PROGRAMA INFANTIL Y PARA NIÑOS PEQUEÑOS DE CAROLINA DEL NORTE
REVISIÓN DEL PLAN INDIVIDUALIZADO DE SERVICIOS PARA LA FAMILIA (IFSP)

Fecha de la revisión: 10 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del IFSP inicial: 12 de abril de 2026
Fecha de la evaluación inicial: 2 de abril de 2026

INFORMACIÓN DEL NIÑO Y DE LA FAMILIA

Niño: Mateo Hernández Rodríguez (conocido en casa como "Teo"), fecha de nacimiento 3 de enero de 2024, número de expediente NC-ITP-240317-M, número de Medicaid 8827341905K.

Madre: Lucía Rodríguez Paz, teléfono (919) 555-0148, correo electrónico lucia.rodriguezpaz@gmail.com.
Padre: Carlos Hernández Vega, teléfono (919) 555-0162.
Hermana mayor: Camila Hernández Rodríguez, de 6 años, quien asiste a kínder.
Abuela materna y cuidadora principal durante el día: Rosa Paz, quien vive con la familia en 214 Calle Mimosa, Durham, Carolina del Norte, 27703, Condado de Durham.
Perro de la familia: Rocky, muy querido por Teo, quien lo señala cada vez que lo ve en el patio.

Coordinadora de servicios: Marisol Jiménez, de la Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios para la Primera Infancia del Condado de Durham (en adelante "ACSPI Durham"), teléfono (919) 555-0177, correo marisol.jimenez@acspidurham.org.

Oficina del CDSA: Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios para Niños del Triángulo (en adelante "CDSA del Triángulo"), ubicada en 4420 Avenida Roxboro, Durham, Carolina del Norte, 27704.

Patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe que redacta este informe: Ana Beltrán, contratada por Terapias Pediátricas Bilingües del Triángulo.
Terapeuta ocupacional: Jennifer Smith.
Fisioterapeuta: David Chen.
Pediatra de cabecera: Dr. Raúl Fernández, de la Clínica Pediátrica Valle Verde.

HISTORIA MÉDICA Y DE DESARROLLO

Teo nació a las 34 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 2,100 gramos y un Apgar de 7 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. El tamizaje auditivo neonatal fue normal, y una evaluación audiológica de seguimiento el 15 de mayo de 2025 confirmó audición dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos. El Dr. Fernández refirió a la familia al programa de intervención temprana tras notar un retraso significativo en el lenguaje durante la revisión de los 18 meses.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (en las palabras de la familia)

La madre, Lucía, expresó: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no nos dice lo que quiere. Él señala y hace sonidos, pero no usa palabras como su hermana Camila las usaba a esta edad." Agregó: "Yo trabajo de noche en el Centro de Distribución Horizonte Logística, de 11:00 p.m. a 7:00 a.m., y mi mamá Rosa se queda con él. Me gustaría que él pudiera decirle a mi mamá cuando tiene hambre o cuando le duele algo, porque ella solo habla español y a veces la guardería no entiende lo que él necesita."

El padre, Carlos, dijo: "Para mí es importante que pueda jugar con otros niños en la guardería. A veces se frustra y llora porque no lo entienden, y eso me rompe el corazón." Carlos trabaja en construcción con Construcciones Vega Hermanos y llega a casa después de las 6:00 p.m.

La familia priorizó, en orden: (1) que Teo use palabras o señas para pedir comida y atención; (2) que juegue junto a otros niños sin frustrarse; (3) que la familia, incluyendo a la abuela Rosa, aprenda estrategias para usar en casa en español.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Teo se despierta alrededor de las 7:30 a.m. y desayuna con su abuela Rosa. Tres días a la semana asiste a Little Learners Daycare, en el salón de la Maestra Teresa López, de 9:00 a.m. a 1:00 p.m.. Los otros dos días se queda en casa con Rosa y su hermana Camila, quien asiste a Escuela Primaria Hope Valley. Por la tarde, Teo toma una siesta de aproximadamente una hora y luego juega en el patio con Diego, el niño vecino de la misma edad, y con Rocky. La hora del baño es a las 7:00 p.m., seguida de un cuento antes de dormir. La cena es en familia cuando el padre llega del trabajo; la madre, Lucía, duerme durante la tarde antes de salir a su turno nocturno.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

La familia recibe apoyo nutricional de WIC y participa en actividades de alfabetización temprana con Smart Start del Condado de Durham. El Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Durham ("DSS de Durham") ayudó a la familia a solicitar la subvención de cuidado infantil que cubre parte de la mensualidad de Little Learners Daycare. La familia también fue referida al Little Learners Program, un programa comunitario de terapia de grupo para el desarrollo del lenguaje, sitio web www.littlelearnersprogram.org, que no está afiliado a la guardería a pesar del nombre similar.

RESUMEN DEL PROGRESO DESDE LA EVALUACIÓN INICIAL

En la evaluación inicial, a la edad de 2;3, Teo obtuvo en el PLS-5, subprueba de Comprensión Auditiva, una puntuación estándar de 73 (percentil 4), con un intervalo de confianza de 68-78; en Comunicación Expresiva, una puntuación estándar de 71 (percentil 3), equivalente a una edad de desarrollo de 14-16 meses.

En la sesión de hoy, Teo, ahora de 2;9, produjo de forma espontánea las palabras "mamá", "más" y "agua" (esta última como "awa", omitiendo el fonema /g/). También imitó la palabra meta "pan" sustituyendo /p/ por [b] con claves mínimas. Produjo "tete" por "leche" con claves moderadas. En el área motora gruesa, Teo caminó de forma independiente en la evaluación de hoy y subió escalones alternando los pies con claves moderadas, según observó David Chen.

El equipo usó estrategias del enfoque Hanen y técnicas de PROMPT para apoyar la producción de consonantes iniciales, con buena respuesta de Teo a las claves táctiles. Las sesiones de habla ocurrieron los martes a las 10:00 a.m. en el hogar, con interpretación no necesaria dado que la terapeuta, Ana Beltrán, es bilingüe. La familia reportó que las estrategias en español han sido más fáciles de aplicar que el material en inglés recibido anteriormente.

TABLA DE RESULTADOS DEL IFSP

Resultado	Estrategias	Progreso	Fecha
Resultado 1: Teo usará al menos 10 palabras o aproximaciones para pedir comida, juguetes o atención durante las rutinas diarias.	Modelado de palabras durante las comidas; uso de PROMPT para claves táctiles en consonantes iniciales; la abuela Rosa practica el modelado en español durante el desayuno y la merienda.	Logro parcial: Teo usa ahora 6 de 10 palabras meta de forma espontánea, un aumento desde 2 de 10 en la revisión anterior.	10 de octubre de 2026
Resultado 2: Teo jugará junto a otro niño durante al menos 5 minutos sin llorar ni alejarse, con apoyo mínimo del adulto.	Juego estructurado en parejas en Little Learners Daycare con Diego; la Maestra Teresa López facilita los turnos con apoyo visual; práctica adicional una vez por semana en el Little Learners Program.	Logrado de forma consistente: juega 8-10 minutos con claves mínimas, observado por Jennifer Smith y la Maestra Teresa López.	10 de octubre de 2026
Resultado 3: Teo caminará de forma independiente en superficies irregulares del patio de recreo.	Práctica de equilibrio en el patio de Little Learners Daycare; ejercicios de fuerza en el tronco guiados por David Chen durante visitas quincenales en el hogar.	Logrado: camina de forma independiente en césped y superficies desiguales con supervisión distante únicamente.	10 de octubre de 2026
Resultado 4: La familia, incluyendo a la abuela Rosa, usará dos estrategias de comunicación aumentada (señas simples y un tablero de imágenes) en casa.	Entrenamiento familiar en español sobre señas básicas ("más", "ayuda", "terminado"); tablero de imágenes bilingüe enviado a casa; seguimiento telefónico con Lucía y Rosa cada dos semanas.	En progreso: la familia usa las señas de forma consistente; el tablero de imágenes se usa 3 de 5 días según reporte de Lucía.	10 de octubre de 2026

FECHAS DE SERVICIOS Y PRÓXIMOS PASOS

El equipo acordó continuar la terapia de habla y lenguaje una vez por semana, terapia ocupacional cada dos semanas y fisioterapia cada dos semanas, con la próxima revisión del IFSP programada para el 8 de abril de 2027. La coordinadora de servicios, Marisol Jiménez, enviará la documentación actualizada a la CDSA del Triángulo antes del 24 de octubre de 2026. Se recomienda una nueva evaluación con el PLS-5 en la próxima revisión anual para documentar el progreso continuo en comprensión auditiva y comunicación expresiva.

La familia puede comunicarse con cualquier pregunta a través del correo de la ACSPI Durham, marisol.jimenez@acspidurham.org, o visitando el sitio web del CDSA del Triángulo en www.cdsatriangulo.org para más información sobre los servicios disponibles en el Condado de Durham. La familia firmó su consentimiento para continuar los servicios según lo descrito en este plan revisado.

+ CA: 4;2
+ Context: Nota diaria de terapia del habla y lenguaje, sesión individual en el domicilio familiar bajo el Centro de Intervención Temprana y Apoyo Familiar del Condado de Johnston (CIATFCJ), 14 de octubre de 2025, 3:30 p.m. a 4:15 p.m.. ID de Medicaid: HM7294831B. Caso: JC-00482.

Resumen:

Hoy visité a Teo en su casa en 214 Maple Grove Lane, Clayton, condado de Johnston, 27520. Me recibió su mamá, Lucía Rodríguez, quien trabaja en la tienda Fresh Mart. Su papá, Jorge Hernández, trabaja en la planta Carolina Poultry Processing y llegó tarde del segundo turno. También estaba la abuela materna, doña Lupe, quien cuida a Teo por las tardes y trabaja los fines de semana en el servicio de limpieza Clean Shine. El padrastro, Mike Sánchez, trabaja en la compañía de construcción Hernández y Asociados, y el tío, Beto, trabaja en Sunny Acres Farm. El vecino, Mr. Tom, pasó a saludar y comentó que su sobrina trabaja en el restaurante El Rodeo.

Teo llegó jugando con su hermana mayor, Camila, y con el perro de la familia, Rocky. Estaba de buen humor y participó bien en las actividades planeadas. Trabajamos en el objetivo IFSP #2: aumentar la inteligibilidad del habla en oraciones de tres a cuatro palabras. Usando láminas y el enfoque Cycles, Teo practicó palabras con el sonido /k/. Produjo "casa" correctamente 8/10 veces con mod cues, una mejora respecto a la sesión anterior. También imitó la frase "el Rocky corre" sin omitir la sílaba final, algo que no lograba hace un mes.

En el área de lenguaje receptivo administramos el subtest de Comprensión Auditiva del PLS-5 en español. Obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 85 (percentil 16, IC 79-91), dentro del rango bajo-promedio, con una edad equivalente de 3;6.

Teo asiste a Little Sprouts Daycare tres días por semana. Su maestra, la maestra Carmen, reporta que juega bien con su compañero Juanito, pero aún muestra episodios de [EW] durante las transiciones de actividad. Hablé con ella brevemente al recoger a Teo y coordinamos estrategias compartidas de apoyo visual.

La coordinadora de servicios de la CIATFCJ, Jennifer Walsh, llamó durante la sesión para confirmar la próxima revisión del IFSP, programada para el 10 de enero de 2026. La intérprete, Miss Ana, tradujo la llamada para Lucía, quien tenía preguntas sobre el transporte al centro.

Yo, Sarah Thompson, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services, PLLC, recomiendo continuar las sesiones semanales en el hogar y reforzar en casa las palabras meta con el sonido /k/ usando el modelo recomendado por Hanen. La familia se mostró receptiva y comprometida con las tareas enviadas.

Plan: próxima sesión el 21 de octubre de 2025 a las 3:30 p.m.. Contacto para reprogramar: (919) 555-0148 o sthompson@carolinapedstherapy.com.

Children's Developmental Services Agency of the Piedmont Foothills
Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil de las Estribaciones del Piedmont
("CDSA Piedmont Foothills" / "CDSA de las Estribaciones")
North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program — Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) Six-Month Review

Child ID: IT-204871
Medicaid ID: 803452219K
Review Date: September 22, 2026
Original IFSP Date: March 10, 2026
Date of Report: September 25, 2026

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Child's Name: Jesús Alejandro Ramírez Castillo, conocido por su familia como "Chuy."
Date of Birth: November 4, 2023. Current age: 2;10.
Primary Language(s) in the Home: Spanish and English.
Address: 142 Willow Bend Lane, Mill Creek, NC 28601, Pinebrook County.
Mother: Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez. Phone: (828) 555-0147. Email: rosaisela.castillo27@mailhaven.net.
Father: Francisco Ramírez Domínguez, llamado "Pancho" por la familia. Phone: (828) 555-0198.
Sibling: Esmeralda Ramírez Castillo, a quien le dicen "Mely," edad 6 años.
Caregiver (grandmother / abuela materna): Dolores Castillo Vega, conocida como "Lola," who provides childcare three days a week while Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez works.

Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez reports: "Mom works nights at Ridgeline Poultry Processing, so Lola gets Chuy up and gives him breakfast most mornings." Francisco Ramírez Domínguez works days at Mill Creek Auto Body as a mechanic.

Pediatrician: Dr. Ahmed Qureshi, Foothills Pediatric Associates.

2. SERVICE COORDINATION / COORDINACIÓN DE SERVICIOS

Service Coordinator: Erica Hollis, CDSA Piedmont Foothills (Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil de las Estribaciones del Piedmont). Phone: (828) 555-0210.

Erica Hollis coordinated this review meeting and confirmed continued eligibility under diagnosed condition F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) per the evaluation completed February 18, 2026. The family requested that today's meeting be conducted bilingually; Marisol Peña, M.S., CCC-SLP, of Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC, served as the primary interpreter for sections not conducted directly in Spanish by Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez and Erica Hollis.

3. FAMILY INFORMATION, RUTINAS DIARIAS, AND PRIORITIES

Rutina diaria / Daily Routine: Chuy wakes around 6:30 a.m. and has breakfast with Dolores Castillo Vega. He attends Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez reports that evenings at home include dinner together, bath time, and a bedtime story, often read half in English and half in Spanish. Francisco Ramírez Domínguez takes Chuy and Esmeralda Ramírez Castillo to the park on Saturdays.

Preocupaciones y Prioridades de la Familia (Family Concerns and Priorities, in the family's own words):

Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez shared: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Chuy no habla como los otros niños de su edad. En la casa le entendemos casi todo, pero cuando llega gente que no es familia, él se frustra porque nadie le entiende."

She added, in English: "At daycare, Miss Keisha Lopez says he gets upset when the other kids don't understand him. He'll just scream instead of trying to say the word again."

Francisco Ramírez Domínguez stated: "Yo quiero que aprenda bien los dos idiomas, español e inglés. No quiero que se le quite el español, pero sí necesita hablar más claro."

Family priorities identified for this review period:
a) Increase intelligibility of Chuy's speech in both Spanish and English, particularly with unfamiliar listeners.
b) Reduce frustration-related tantrums at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center and at home.
c) Support bilingual language development so that Chuy continues to build Spanish alongside English.
d) Help Esmeralda Ramírez Castillo understand how to support her brother's communication at home.

4. PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT (SUMMARY OF EVALUATION RESULTS)

Birth History: Chuy was born at 36 weeks gestation via vaginal delivery. Apgar scores were 7 and 9 at one and five minutes. Birth weight was 5 lbs 8 oz. No NICU stay was reported.

Speech-Language: Evaluation on February 18, 2026 using the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5 Spanish) yielded an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 68 (2nd percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 64 (1st percentile), with a confidence interval of 58-74. Age equivalents fell at approximately 18 months for expressive language, against a chronological age at testing of 2;3. On the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), Chuy scored a standard score of 71 (3rd percentile). Speech intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners was estimated at 40% in connected speech.

Marisol Peña noted in session that Chuy produced "agua" as "[awa]," omitting the medial /ɣ/, and produced "ball" as "baw," final-consonant deletion consistent with the phonological pattern noted across both languages. Current articulation accuracy on trained target words is 8/10 (percent accuracy 80%) with moderate cues, an improvement from baseline.

Diagnosis: F80.2 — Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder (ICD-10). Supplemental diagnosis of R62.0 (delayed milestones) remains active per Dr. Ahmed Qureshi's referral.

5. OTHER AGENCIES AND RESOURCES INVOLVED

The family currently receives support from the following community agencies:

- Pinebrook County Department of Social Services (DSS): the family receives SNAP benefits and periodic case management through caseworker Tanya Burrell.
- Pinebrook County WIC Program: Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez continues nutrition counseling appointments for both Chuy and Esmeralda Ramírez Castillo.
- Pinebrook County Partnership for Children (local Smart Start partnership): provided a subsidy that allows Chuy to continue at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center.
- Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center: lead classroom teacher Keisha Lopez implements visual supports and modeling strategies recommended by the SLP.

Erica Hollis confirmed that no additional agency referrals are needed at this time, though the family may apply for respite care through Pinebrook County Department of Social Services if Dolores Castillo Vega's availability changes.

6. DEVELOPMENTAL DOMAINS SUMMARY

Gross/Fine Motor: Age-appropriate per physical therapist Hannah Choi, PT, who screened Chuy on August 14, 2026 and found no concerns warranting ongoing PT services.

Cognitive: Within normal limits per parent and teacher report; Keisha Lopez notes Chuy matches shapes and colors consistent with peers.

Social-Emotional: Chuy plays alongside his cousin José Luis Castillo Mendoza, called "Pepe," during family gatherings, though Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez notes increased frustration tantrums (2-3 per week) tied to communication breakdowns.

Adaptive/Self-Help: Age-appropriate; Chuy feeds himself and is beginning toilet training with support from Dolores Castillo Vega.

Occupational therapist Grace Whitfield, OTR/L, screened sensory regulation on August 14, 2026 and did not recommend OT services at this time, noting the tantrums appear communication-driven rather than sensory-based.

7. IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Chuy will increase expressive vocabulary in both Spanish and English to request wants and needs, reducing frustration-related behaviors.
Strategies: Use of Hanen-based strategies (It Takes Two to Talk) coached with Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez during home visits; bilingual modeling of two-word combinations; visual supports modeled after PECS principles introduced at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center by Keisha Lopez.
Progress: Chuy now uses 12 consistent word approximations across both languages, up from 4 at the initial IFSP. Caregiver report of daily requesting behavior improved from "rarely" to "several times daily."

Outcome 2: Chuy will improve speech sound production of final consonants and medial sounds to increase intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners.
Strategies: Cycles phonological approach targeting final consonant deletion patterns; home practice list of target words provided in both Spanish and English; moderate cueing level faded toward minimal cues as accuracy improves.
Progress: Accuracy on trained targets reached 8/10 (80%) with moderate cues, compared to 3/10 (30%) at baseline. Intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners estimated by parent report at 50%, up from 30%.

Outcome 3: The family will receive coaching to support bilingual language development and reduce stress related to communication breakdowns at home and at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center.
Strategies: Joint home visits with Marisol Peña and Erica Hollis to coach Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez and Francisco Ramírez Domínguez on bilingual modeling, expansion, and reducing direct correction. Collaboration call with Keisha Lopez monthly to align strategies between home and classroom.
Progress: Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez reports feeling "más tranquila" using the strategies, and Esmeralda Ramírez Castillo has begun modeling slow, clear speech for her brother as coached during a home visit on July 9, 2026.

New Outcome 4 (added this review): Chuy will use two-to-three word phrases in Spanish or English to protest or redirect, in place of screaming, across home and daycare settings.
Strategies: Visual choice board at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center; consistent bilingual phrase models ("quiero más," "all done") coached with both parents and Dolores Castillo Vega.

8. EARLY INTERVENTION SERVICES

Service: Individual speech-language therapy.
Provider: Marisol Peña, M.S., CCC-SLP, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC.
Location: Home-based, 142 Willow Bend Lane, Mill Creek.
Frequency/Duration: Two sessions weekly, 30 minutes each, individual treatment (CPT 92507).
Service dates this period: March 17, 2026 through September 22, 2026.
Evaluation/reassessment billed under CPT 92523 (speech sound production evaluation with language evaluation) on February 18, 2026 and again on August 14, 2026.

Service: Service coordination.
Provider: Erica Hollis, CDSA Piedmont Foothills.
Frequency: Monthly contact, with home visits quarterly; next contact scheduled for October 20, 2026.

Service: Developmental screening consultation (PT/OT, as needed).
Providers: Hannah Choi, PT; Grace Whitfield, OTR/L.
Frequency: As needed; no ongoing services recommended at this review.

Transportation and Natural Environment: All therapy is delivered in the family's home, consistent with the natural environment requirement. Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez confirmed no transportation barriers for appointments scheduled around her night-shift schedule at Ridgeline Poultry Processing.

Funding: Services are funded through CDSA Piedmont Foothills's state/federal Part C allocation; Medicaid is billed as secondary payor under Medicaid ID 803452219K.

9. NEXT STEPS AND SIGNATURES / FIRMAS

Next IFSP review scheduled: March 10, 2027 (annual review) with an interim contact by December 15, 2026 to monitor progress on Outcome 4.

The team, including Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez, Francisco Ramírez Domínguez, Erica Hollis, Marisol Peña, and Keisha Lopez (by phone), agreed to the outcomes and strategies above. Rosa Isela Castillo Ramírez stated in closing: "Gracias por explicarme todo en español también. Así entiendo mejor cómo ayudar a Chuy en la casa."

Mateo's mother, Lucía Rodríguez, brought him and remained in the waiting area; his older brother, Diego, did not attend today's visit. Mateo continues to receive early intervention services through the Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios para Familias Hispanas de Carolina del Norte (CDISFHCN), the regional agency coordinating his IFSP. His service coordinator, Marisol Peña, confirmed by phone (919-555-0142) that the annual IFSP review is scheduled for November 3, 2026, and that work continues toward Outcome 2. His case is tracked under Medicaid ID 784512093B and internal case ID TPS-04471.

Objective: Mateo demonstrated 8/10 accuracy (80%) producing final /k/ in single words during structured drill, up from 3 of 5 trials last session. The target word "cake" was produced as "[teɪ]" with mod cues and self-corrected once without prompting. Using PROMPT touch cues, medial /ɾ/ improved to 6/10 during a Cycles phonology task. The table below excerpts his ongoing progress log: Date 08/14/2026: Auditory Comprehension standard score 73-83 (95% CI); Date 09/18/2026: standard score 79-89; Date 10/09/2026: standard score 82-92, age equivalent 3;9–4;2, all on the PLS-5.
