text:
+ Name: Mateo Alejandro Vásquez Ponce ("Teo")
+ CA: 4;2 (DOB August 14, 2021)
+ Context: Comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation, conducted in home and reviewed with interpretation support from the clinician, who is bilingual
+ Examiner: Catalina M. Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist, Carolina Bright Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC
+ Date of Evaluation: September 22, 2026 and September 24, 2026
+ Location: family home, 482 Magnolia Grove Lane, Raleigh, NC 27610 (Wake County)
+ Referral Source: Agencia Regional de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (ARSDIP), Service Coordinator Ana M. Flores
+ Primary Language(s): Spanish (home), Spanish and English (daycare)
+ Medicaid ID: 748293615B
+ Record No.: LD-2026-00482

RESUMEN / SUMMARY

Mateo, conocido en casa como "Teo," is a Spanish-English bilingual boy, 4;2, referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by ARSDIP following a concern raised at his 4-year well-check by his pediatrician, Dr. Samuel Whitfield of Triangle Pediatric Partners. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez Nuñez, and his father, Hugo Vásquez Morales, report that Teo is "muy inteligente pero nadie le entiende" ("very smart but no one understands him"). This evaluation was completed to determine Mateo's current speech and language functioning across both languages and to guide eligibility for ongoing services through ARSDIP.

HISTORIA DE REFERENCIA / REASON FOR REFERRAL

Lucía reports that concerns about Teo's speech began around 2;0, when she noticed he was not combining words the way her daughter had at the same age. Hugo agreed, stating "él entiende todo, pero cuando habla, solo yo y su mamá le entendemos" (he understands everything, but when he talks, only his mom and I understand him). Mateo's daycare teacher, Ms. Lopez, at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, also raised concerns at a parent conference on June 3, 2026, noting that Teo frequently gestures instead of using words in the Ladybug Room, Ms. Lopez's classroom, and that peers sometimes ask "what did he say?" The family was referred to ARSDIP by Dr. Whitfield, and Ana M. Flores, Service Coordinator, completed the intake and coordinated this evaluation.

ANTECEDENTES / BACKGROUND HISTORY

Teo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez Nuñez and Hugo Vásquez Morales, his older sister, Camila Vásquez Rodríguez (age 7), and his paternal grandmother, Rosa Morales de Vásquez, who lives in the home and provides daytime childcare on days Teo is not at daycare. The family's primary language at home is Spanish, used by Lucía, Hugo, and Rosa. Camila attends second grade at Oakwood Elementary School, where her teacher, Mrs. Patel, has described her as "bilingual and doing great." Teo's maternal aunt, Elena Nuñez, visits on weekends and is described as Teo's "madrina" (godmother); she sometimes helps with pickups from daycare. The family also has a dog named Max, who Teo loves and frequently talks about.

HISTORIA MÉDICA Y DE NACIMIENTO / BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Lucía reports an uncomplicated pregnancy with Teo, carried to 38 weeks gestational age. He was delivered vaginally at WakeMed Raleigh Campus, weighing 6 lbs 14 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes respectively. There were no complications during delivery and no NICU stay. Mateo met early motor milestones within typical limits: sitting independently at 6 months, walking at 13 months. Lucía reports he said his first words around 14 months ("mamá," "papá," "agua") but did not begin combining two words until closer to 3;0, later than his sister, Camila, who combined words by 18 months. Teo passed his newborn hearing screening and has had no recent ear infections per report. He has had two rounds of tympanostomy tubes considered by Dr. Whitfield but not yet placed, as his most recent hearing screening on August 1, 2026 showed results within normal limits bilaterally. No history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness is reported. Hugo reports that he himself was "tardío para hablar" (a late talker) as a child but "se me fue arreglando solo" (it resolved on its own).

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The home language environment is predominantly Spanish. Lucía Rodríguez Nuñez works as a server at El Rancho Alegre Restaurant during the day and picks up evening shifts at el Servicio de Limpieza Carolina Clean (Carolina Clean Cleaning Service) several nights a week to supplement the family's income. Hugo Vásquez Morales works full-time at Carolina Fresh Poultry Processing Plant, and on weekends he works a second job with la Compañía de Construcción Triangle Builders (Triangle Builders Construction Company) doing framing and drywall. Because both parents work long hours, Rosa Morales de Vásquez, Teo's grandmother, provides much of his daytime care; she previously worked at la Finca Green Valley Produce (Green Valley Produce Farm) before retiring last year, and still helps there seasonally during harvest. Teo's aunt, Elena Nuñez, works at la Tienda Dollar Saver (Dollar Saver Store) and sometimes brings small toys for Teo and Camila. Lucía estimates Teo's exposure as roughly 80% Spanish and 20% English prior to starting daycare, with English exposure increasing since he began attending Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare five mornings a week. Lucía reports that her own English is "limitado pero me defiendo" (limited, but I manage), while Hugo reports feeling "más cómodo en español" (more comfortable in Spanish). Both parents stated a preference for Teo to remain bilingual and expressed concern that his unclear speech is present in both languages, not just one, which they find confusing.

HISTORIA EDUCATIVA / DAYCARE AND EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Teo has attended Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare since January 12, 2026, in the Ladybug Room under the supervision of Ms. Lopez. Ms. Lopez reports that Teo is social and enjoys playing with peers, particularly a classmate named Diego, but that other children sometimes have difficulty understanding his requests during play, prompting him to point or lead adults by the hand instead of using words. Ms. Lopez also noted that Teo participates in both English and Spanish circle time songs but is quieter during verbal turn-taking activities compared to peers his age. Lucía stated that Teo "se frustra cuando no lo entienden" (gets frustrated when people don't understand him) and has begun to have brief tantrums at daycare pickup when Ms. Lopez cannot understand his account of his day.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN / ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted over two sessions in the family home at 482 Magnolia Grove Lane, Raleigh, beginning at 9:30 AM on September 22, 2026 and at 10:00 AM on September 24, 2026. All testing and interviewing were conducted by Catalina M. Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, who administered items and instructions bilingually as appropriate. The following standardized and informal measures were used: the Spanish edition of the Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5 Spanish), the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), the Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) Morphosyntax subtest, an oral mechanism examination, a 15-minute conversational language sample coded with SALT conventions, and parent interview. Teo was cooperative throughout testing, though he required frequent redirection and benefited from short breaks with preferred toys, including a small truck he calls "tuck" (truck).

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS / TEST RESULTS

Preschool Language Scale-5, Spanish Edition (PLS-5 Spanish)
- Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 73 (4th percentile), 95% CI 65-80, age equivalent 2;9
- Expressive Communication: Standard Score 68 (2nd percentile), 95% CI 60-76, age equivalent 2;6
- Total Language Score: 70 (2nd percentile), 95% CI 63-77

PLS-5 administered in English (secondary administration for comparison):
- Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 77 (6th percentile)
- Expressive Communication: Standard Score 71 (3rd percentile)

Composite bilingual interpretation using conceptual scoring (best response across both languages per BESA guidelines) yielded an estimated functional language level in the low-average to below-average range overall, with expressive skills weaker than receptive skills in both languages.

Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax Subtest:
- Raw score 11/40, placing Teo below the clinical cutoff for his age range in both languages, with frequent omission of grammatical morphemes (plurals, verb tense markers) noted in both Spanish and English samples.

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3):
- Sounds-in-Words Standard Score 71 (3rd percentile), age equivalent 2;11
- Errors noted: final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for "cat"), stopping of fricatives (e.g., /t/ for /s/), gliding of liquids (e.g., [w] for /r/), and cluster reduction (e.g., "poon" for "spoon")

Speech sound production in Spanish was also sampled informally, with similar patterns noted, including substitution of /t/ for the trilled /r/ (producing "tojo" for "rojo") and inconsistent production of the tap /ɾ/ in medial position.

ANÁLISIS DE LA MUESTRA DE HABLA CONVERSACIONAL / CONVERSATIONAL SAMPLE ANALYSIS

During the SALT-coded sample, Teo's mean length of utterance was 2.3 morphemes, below expected range for his age in both languages. Utterances were frequently coded [EW] (end of word truncation) and [FP] (filler pause) due to frequent hesitations and sound-level breakdowns. Intelligibility was estimated at approximately 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 70% to familiar listeners (parents, grandmother) based on both direct observation and parent report. One notable exchange involved Teo narrating play with his dog: when asked what his dog was doing, he said "Max tun" (intending "Max run"), demonstrating final consonant deletion in a spontaneous, meaningful utterance. In another instance, when shown a picture of a red car, he said ""tojo cawo"" attempting "carro rojo" (red car) in reversed word order with multiple sound errors, illustrating both phonological and morphosyntactic difficulty across languages.

EXAMEN DEL MECANISMO ORAL / ORAL MECHANISM EXAMINATION

Oral structures were within normal limits for symmetry, strength, and range of motion. No evidence of tongue-tie, cleft, or craniofacial anomaly was observed. Diadochokinetic rates were mildly reduced for his age but adequate for the production demands of connected speech. Hearing was most recently screened within normal limits bilaterally on August 1, 2026.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS / CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, conversational sampling, and parent and teacher report, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and a concomitant speech sound disorder affecting both Spanish and English, his two languages of exposure. His difficulties are evident across languages rather than limited to one, which rules out a primary difference related solely to second-language acquisition; per BESA conceptual scoring guidelines, his performance falls below expectations even when the stronger response across languages is credited, consistent with a true bilingual language disorder rather than typical bilingual development. Lucía and Hugo's report that Teo "entiende todo" (understands everything) is only partially consistent with testing, which showed receptive scores also below age expectations, though stronger than his expressive scores. His speech sound errors, including final consonant deletion, stopping, gliding, and cluster reduction, are contributing significantly to his reduced intelligibility and are consistent with a phonological, rather than purely articulatory, pattern, affecting both of his languages. Diagnostic impressions are consistent with Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) and Phonological Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0).

This evaluation was billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).

RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo qualifies for ongoing speech-language therapy services based on standardized scores falling more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in multiple domains. It is recommended that services be provided bilingually, in Spanish and English, given the family's home language use and Teo's mixed language exposure.
2. Individual therapy is recommended 2 times per week, 30 minutes per session, targeting expressive morphosyntax (plurals, verb tense markers) and phonological patterns (final consonants, fricatives, liquids, clusters) in both languages, using a developmentally appropriate approach such as Cycles for phonology and naturalistic, play-based strategies such as Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" for language facilitation.
3. Coordination with Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare and Ms. Lopez is recommended to support carryover of target sounds and vocabulary in the classroom setting, including simple visual supports in the Ladybug Room.
4. The family is encouraged to continue supporting Teo's bilingual development at home; research consistently supports maintaining the home language alongside English rather than restricting input to one language.
5. Continued coordination with Dr. Samuel Whitfield at Triangle Pediatric Partners regarding hearing status is recommended, including follow-up if ear infections recur, given the mild history of fluctuating findings.
6. Reevaluation is recommended in approximately 6 months, or sooner if significant changes in communication skills are observed, to update eligibility documentation for ARSDIP services.
7. Ana M. Flores at ARSDIP will coordinate next steps for an IFSP meeting, tentatively scheduled for October 20, 2026, to review these findings with the family and establish outcomes.

RESUMEN FINAL / CLOSING SUMMARY

In summary, Mateo "Teo" Vásquez Ponce presents with a bilingual mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and phonological disorder affecting both Spanish and English. His difficulties are not attributable to typical second-language learning but represent a true communication disorder present across both of his languages. Lucía Rodríguez Nuñez and Hugo Vásquez Morales were both present for feedback on September 24, 2026 and expressed relief at having clearer answers, with Lucía stating "ahora sabemos que no estamos solos en esto" (now we know we are not alone in this). The family was provided with written and verbal recommendations in Spanish, and a referral packet will be sent to ARSDIP to initiate the IFSP process. Questions may be directed to Catalina M. Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP at catalina.reyes@carolinabrightslt.com or by phone at (919) 555-0142. Additional information about Carolina Bright Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC and its bilingual services is available at www.carolinabrightslt.com.

Respectfully submitted,

Catalina M. Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
2210 Battleground Avenue, Suite 140, Greensboro, NC 27408
Phone: (336) 555-0199 • Email: intake@piedmontpedispeech.com

Date of Report: September 29, 2026
Dates of Evaluation: September 15, 2026 and September 22, 2026

Child's Name: Mateo Andrés Hernández Cruz ("Teo")
Date of Birth: March 3, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;6
Record ID: LD-20394
Medicaid ID: 912837465B
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Pérez and Javier Hernández Morales
Home Address: 1420 Willowbrook Lane, Greensboro, NC 27405, Guilford County
Home Phone: (336) 555-0148
Parent Email: lucia.rodriguez82@example.com
Evaluator: Sarah Beth Collier, M.S., CCC-SLP
Interpreter Present: Rosa Delgado, certified medical interpreter
Referral Source: Dr. Michael Tran, pediatrician

Dear Lucía and Javier,

Querida familia, gracias por confiar en nosotros. Thank you for bringing Mateo in to see us. It was a joy getting to know your son over these two visits, and I want this letter to explain, in plain language, what we found and what we recommend. With the help of our interpreter, Rosa Delgado, we were able to talk through everything together, en inglés y en español, so that both of you felt comfortable asking questions. I hope this report reads less like a medical file and more like a conversation between us.

Motivo de la Evaluación / Reason for Referral

Lucía and Javier, you reached out to us because Mateo's preschool teacher, Miss Ana, noticed that other children were having trouble understanding him during circle time at Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center. You also told us, "a veces se frustra porque no lo entendemos" — sometimes he gets frustrated because we don't understand him — especially at home when he is trying to tell doña Lupe something important and she has to ask him to repeat himself two or three times. Dr. Michael Tran, his pediatrician, agreed that a full speech and language evaluation made sense given these concerns and referred your family to our clinic.

Historia del Desarrollo / Background and Developmental History

Mateo was born on March 3, 2022 at Moses Cone Hospital in Greensboro, following a pregnancy that Lucía described as mostly uncomplicated, though she did have some high blood pressure in the final weeks. He was born at 38 weeks gestational age, weighing 6 lbs 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9. There were no NICU stays and no feeding tube needs. Lucía shared that Mateo was a calm baby who nursed well, though she noted he had frequent ear infections between 8 months and 18 months, which led to ear tubes being placed when he was 20 months old. Since the tubes, both parents say his hearing seems much better, and he responds quickly when called.

Motor milestones were within typical limits: Mateo sat independently around 6 months, walked at 13 months, and currently runs, climbs, and jumps without difficulty. Both of his older siblings hit similar motor milestones, so Javier mentioned he wasn't especially worried about that side of things — "camina bien, corre bien, el problema es que no le entendemos lo que dice."

Mateo received Early Intervention services through Piedmont Triad CDSA starting around his second birthday, after a well-child visit flagged a speech delay. His service coordinator at the time helped the family work toward IFSP Outcome 2, which focused on functional communication at home, and IFSP Outcome 3, which focused on increasing his sound inventory. Lucía recalls that progress was slow but steady, and that the family was glad to have support in Spanish during those early visits, since at that point she felt most comfortable speaking to professionals in her first language.

Historia Familiar y del Lenguaje / Family and Language History

Mateo lives at home with his parents, Lucía and Javier; his older sister, Sol, who is 7; and his older brother, Diego, who is 10. His maternal grandmother, doña Lupe (whose full name is Guadalupe Torres), lives with the family several days a week and is Mateo's primary daytime caregiver on days he isn't at daycare. The family also has a dog named Max, whom Mateo loves to talk about, often saying "Max corre" when he wants to play fetch in the backyard.

Both Spanish and English are used daily in the home. Lucía speaks mostly Spanish with Mateo, while Javier code-switches depending on who is in the room — he might start a sentence in English and finish it in Spanish, especially when he's tired after a long shift. Doña Lupe speaks almost entirely in Spanish with Mateo, and his siblings, Sol and Diego, tend to speak English with him and with each other, since that is the language they use most at school. Lucía told us, "en la casa hablamos los dos idiomas, pero yo quiero que aprenda bien el español también, no quiero que se le olvide."

Both parents work long hours, which shapes the family's schedule significantly. Lucía trabaja en la planta de Carolina Fresh Poultry Processing, a chicken processing plant on the east side of town, where her shift often starts before sunrise. Javier works for Triad Construction Group, a construction company that sends him to job sites across the Triad, so his hours change from week to week — la compañía de construcción Triad Construction Group le asigna sitios distintos cada semana. On days when both parents are working, Mateo's aunt, Marisol Torres, sometimes helps out; she works at El Rancho Grande Restaurant, un restaurante donde trabaja de camarera algunas tardes, and can usually pick Mateo up if needed. An uncle on Lucía's side, Rogelio Torres, works at Deep Creek Dairy Farm — trabaja en una granja, Deep Creek Dairy Farm — and occasionally the whole extended family gathers there on weekends, which Mateo apparently loves because of the animals. Doña Lupe herself works part-time for Sparkle Clean Services, a cleaning company, trabaja medio tiempo para una empresa de limpieza, Sparkle Clean Services, on the days she isn't watching Mateo. Lucía also picks up occasional weekend shifts at a neighborhood store, Ramírez Grocery — la tienda de abarrotes Ramírez Grocery — to help with extra expenses.

This constellation of jobs and caregivers means that Mateo hears and uses language with many different people across the week, which is a real strength for his vocabulary and his social development, even though it also means his communication partners vary quite a bit in how well they understand him.

Mateo attends Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center four days a week, where his main teacher is Miss Ana. On Sunday mornings, Mateo also attends a children's program at the family's church, where his teacher is la maestra Carmen; Lucía mentioned that la maestra Carmen speaks only Spanish with the children, which Mateo seems to enjoy. The family anticipates that Mateo will begin kindergarten next fall at Oak Ridge Elementary School.

Mateo currently receives occupational therapy with Mr. Tom (full name Thomas Reyes) and physical therapy with Jennifer Boyd, both through a private outpatient clinic, focused primarily on fine motor coordination and mild low muscle tone. Both providers report that Mateo is cooperative and eager to please during sessions.

Horario de Sesiones Propuesto / Proposed Session Schedule

To make scheduling easier for your family given both of your work shifts, we would propose the following weekly pattern for individual speech therapy, pending openings in our calendar:

| Day | Start Time | Stop Time | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:30 AM | 10:15 AM | Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center, classroom pull-out |
| Wednesday | 3:45 PM | 4:30 PM | Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services clinic office |
| Friday | 9:30 AM | 10:15 AM | Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center, classroom pull-out |

We know doña Lupe can usually bring Mateo to the Wednesday clinic sessions, and the Monday and Friday sessions would happen right at daycare, so no extra driving would be needed on those days.

Resultados de las Pruebas / Test Results

During our two sessions, we used a combination of standardized testing, informal observation, and language sampling in both English and Spanish. Because Mateo is a bilingual learner, we administered formal measures in English, since that is the language of his current educational setting, but we gathered extensive informal information in Spanish as well, with support from Rosa Delgado, to avoid penalizing him for normal bilingual language patterns.

We administered the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), which looks at both understanding language (Auditory Comprehension) and using language (Expressive Communication).

| Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | 95% Confidence Interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 91 | 27th | 85-97 |
| Expressive Communication | 79 | 8th | 73-85 |
| Total Language Score | 83 | 13th | 78-88 |

These scores suggest that Mateo's understanding of language falls within the low-average range, while his ability to express himself in English is more significantly delayed, falling in the borderline-to-below-average range compared to same-age peers.

We also administered the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) to look specifically at his speech sound production.

| Measure | Score |
|---|---|
| GFTA-3 Standard Score | 72 |
| GFTA-3 Percentile Rank | 3rd |
| GFTA-3 Confidence Interval | 66-78 |

Mateo showed difficulty with several speech sounds that are typically mastered by his age, including /s/, /z/, /ɾ/ (the Spanish tapped r), and consonant clusters like /st/ and /bl/. He tends to simplify clusters (saying "tar" for "star") and sometimes substitutes [w] for /ɾ/ in Spanish words, which is a very common pattern for bilingual children his age and is not, by itself, concerning.

During articulation testing, we used a set of target words that included common nouns chosen for their sounds, such as "sapo," "silla," "luna," and "sol." When shown a picture of the sun and asked to name it, Mateo looked at the card, smiled, and said "sol," producing it clearly with only a mild distortion on the final consonant. He then giggled and added, in Spanish, "¡como mi hermana!" — like my sister — referring, of course, to his sister Sol. We thought this moment was worth including here, not because it affected the score (it did not; "sol" was scored simply as the target word for the /s/ and /l/ sounds), but because it shows how aware Mateo is of the connection between words and the people he loves, which speaks to his strong social and pragmatic skills.

In a separate drilling activity, Mateo was asked to imitate the word "sol" five times in a row with mod cues (a visual cue card plus a verbal model). He achieved 4 of 5 correct productions, which is a strong response to cueing and a good prognostic sign for therapy.

In our Spanish language sample, collected during a short play-based conversation with Rosa Delgado leading and me observing, Mateo used sentences of 3-4 words on average, with vocabulary appropriate for his age, including family-specific words like "abuela," "perro," and the name of his dog, "Max." He used Spanish grammar markers correctly most of the time, though he occasionally mixed English words into Spanish sentences — for example, saying "quiero el truck" instead of "quiero el camión." This kind of code-mixing is developmentally typical and expected in bilingual children and is not itself a sign of a language disorder.

Observaciones Clínicas / Clinical Observations

Throughout both sessions, Mateo was friendly, playful, and easy to redirect. He maintained eye contact, took turns in play, and used gestures and facial expressions effectively to support his spoken communication, which are all excellent pragmatic skills for his age. His main area of difficulty is clearly in speech sound production and in formulating longer, more complex sentences in English, which likely explains why unfamiliar listeners, like some of his classmates, have trouble understanding him.

We also want to note that Mateo's hearing, per the most recent audiological screening on file with Dr. Michael Tran, is within normal limits bilaterally, and no further hearing follow-up is indicated at this time.

Impresiones / Impressions

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and our clinical observations, Mateo presents with a speech sound disorder affecting several consonants and consonant clusters in both English and Spanish, alongside a mild-to-moderate expressive language delay in English. This diagnostic picture fits the ICD-10 code F80.1 (Expressive Language Disorder) along with F80.0 (Phonological Disorder). Given that Mateo is being raised bilingually, with ongoing, rich exposure to both Spanish and English, we do not believe that bilingualism itself is a cause of his difficulties; rather, he appears to show a true speech and language disorder present across both of his languages, which is the pattern we would expect to see if an English-only child presented similarly.

Mateo qualifies for speech-language therapy services based on standard scores falling 1.5 standard deviations or more below the mean on both the PLS-5 Expressive Communication subtest and the GFTA-3.

Recomendaciones / Recommendations

1. We recommend individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, targeting speech sound production (especially /s/, /z/, /ɾ/, and consonant clusters) and expressive language skills (sentence length, vocabulary diversity, and storytelling).

2. We recommend continuing to support both English and Spanish at home. Please continue speaking to Mateo in whichever language feels most natural to each of you — there is no need to limit Spanish at home in an effort to help his English; in fact, strong skills in Spanish will support his English development over time.

3. We recommend consultation between our clinic and Miss Ana at Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center to share simple strategies she can use during circle time, such as giving Mateo extra processing time and modeling target sounds without correcting him directly in front of peers.

4. We recommend continued coordination with Thomas Reyes (occupational therapy) and Jennifer Boyd (physical therapy), since combined therapy scheduling can sometimes be arranged on the same days to reduce the number of trips required for the family.

5. We recommend a follow-up hearing screening in approximately 6 months given his history of chronic ear infections, even though his most recent results were normal.

6. We recommend re-evaluation in approximately 12 months, or sooner if concerns increase, to monitor progress and adjust goals as needed.

Próximos Pasos / Next Steps

Lucía and Javier, our front desk team will reach out by phone to (336) 555-0148 within the next week to go over scheduling and insurance authorization using Medicaid ID 912837465B. If it's easier to reach you by email in the meantime, please feel free to write to us at intake@piedmontpedispeech.com, and we are also happy to have Rosa Delgado join any future phone calls so that everyone feels comfortable discussing next steps.

Gracias de nuevo por su confianza. It has been a privilege getting to know Mateo, and we look forward to supporting his growth, in both of his beautiful languages, in the months ahead.

Con cariño,

Sarah Beth Collier, M.S., CCC-SLP
Speech-Language Pathologist
Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC

La proxima cita sera el 18 de octubre de 2026 a las 3:30 pm en 4521 Hillgrove Road, Charlotte, NC 28213. Firmado, Carla Jimenez, M.S., CCC-SLP. Telefono de la clinica: (704) 555-0148. text:
INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y EL LENGUAJE

ENCABEZADO

- Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Rodríguez, a quien todos llaman "Teo"
- Fecha de nacimiento: June 25, 2022
- Edad cronológica al momento de la evaluación: 4;2
- Fechas de la evaluación: August 25, 2026 y August 27, 2026
- Fecha del informe: September 9, 2026
- Número de expediente médico (MRN): 00482913
- Número de Medicaid de Carolina del Norte: 804216573B
- Número de caso del CDSA: 2456-19
- Evaluadora: Mireya Santos Delgado, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla y el lenguaje bilingüe (inglés/español)
- Lugar de empleo de la evaluadora: Mountain Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
- Dirección de la clínica: 310 Maple Grove Avenue, Suite 204, Hendersonville, 28791
- Teléfono de la clínica: (828) 555-0147
- Correo electrónico de la evaluadora: msantos@mountainspeechpartners.com
- Sitio web de la clínica: www.mountainspeechpartners.com
- Pediatra que refiere: Dr. Samuel Kim
- Coordinadora de servicios del CDSA: Jennifer Boyd, correo jboyd@wnccdsa.org
- Agencia de intervención temprana: CDSA de las Tierras Altas Occidentales
- Escuela actual: Sunrise Avenue Elementary School, salón de Pre-Kínder
- Guardería anterior: Little Steps Daycare
- Dirección residencial: 142 Birchwood Lane, Hendersonville, Henderson County, 28792
- Teléfono de contacto de la familia: (828) 555-0192

MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA Y ANTECEDENTES

- Teo fue referido para esta evaluación por el Dr. Samuel Kim, su pediatra de cabecera, después de que su maestra de Pre-Kínder, la Sra. Diane Patterson, notara que el niño usa muy pocas palabras en comparación con sus compañeros y que con frecuencia señala en lugar de hablar.
- Su madre, Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paz, reporta que le preocupa que "Teo" todavía no forme oraciones completas y que extraños, incluida su niñera, Carmen Luna Reyes, a menudo no le entienden.
- Teo recibió servicios de intervención temprana del CDSA de las Tierras Altas Occidentales entre los 18 meses y los 3 años de edad, bajo un Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) que incluía el Resultado 1 (comunicación funcional), el Resultado 2 (alimentación) y el Resultado 3 (participación familiar).
- La evaluadora anterior durante ese periodo fue Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP, quien documentó un retraso moderado del lenguaje expresivo a los 26 meses.
- Al salir del CDSA por motivo de edad, el niño fue transferido al sistema escolar público y comenzó servicios de habla-lenguaje a través de la escuela, pero la familia solicita esta evaluación privada e independiente para obtener una segunda opinión y planificar el apoyo en el hogar.
- La evaluación se llevó a cabo en inglés y en español, dado que Teo escucha ambos idiomas en casa; la evaluadora es bilingüe y no fue necesario contratar un intérprete.

HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

- Mateo nació el June 25, 2022 en el Mission Regional Medical Center, en Asheville, Buncombe County, a las 35 semanas de gestación.
- El parto fue por cesárea de emergencia debido a sufrimiento fetal; el peso al nacer fue de 2,100 gramos (aproximadamente 4 libras, 10 onzas).
- Las calificaciones de Apgar fueron 6/10 al minuto y 8/10 a los cinco minutos.
- Teo permaneció 18 días en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales (UCIN) del Mission Regional Medical Center por dificultad respiratoria leve y problemas de alimentación.
- La neonatóloga a cargo fue la Dra. Patricia Owens; el pediatra de seguimiento después del alta fue el Dr. Samuel Kim.
- Durante su estancia en la UCIN, Teo requirió alimentación por sonda nasogástrica durante aproximadamente una semana antes de pasar a la alimentación oral completa.
- La madre, Lucía, reporta antecedentes de otitis media recurrente entre los 12 y los 30 meses de edad, con colocación de tubos de ventilación (miringotomía) a los 18 meses, realizada por el otorrinolaringólogo Dr. Benjamin Alvarado.
- No se reportan convulsiones, traumatismos craneales ni hospitalizaciones adicionales.
- El historial de vacunación está al día según el expediente del Dr. Kim.
- El diagnóstico médico actual incluye trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo (F80.2) y trastorno fonológico (F80.0), ambos documentados en el expediente escolar.
- El código de procedimiento utilizado para la evaluación de hoy es el 92523 (evaluación del habla y del lenguaje con interpretación del fonema).

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DEL LENGUAJE

- Teo vive principalmente con su madre, Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paz, y el esposo de ella, Marcos Villalta Osorio, en la dirección indicada arriba.
- También vive en el hogar su media hermana, Camila Villalta Rodríguez, de 6 años, hija de Lucía y Marcos.
- El padre biológico del niño, Édgar Cruz Montalvo, tiene custodia compartida y ve a Teo cada fin de semana; está casado con Rosa Pineda Gómez, quien también participa en el cuidado del niño.
- Édgar trabaja dos empleos para mantener la manutención: de día en la Smoky Mountain Construction Company, y de noche en segundo turno en la planta que la familia conoce solamente por sus siglas, "DPC"; nadie en la familia sabe ni usa el nombre completo de esa empresa.
- Lucía también trabaja dos empleos: por las mañanas en la Tienda de Variedades La Economía, y por las tardes y fines de semana en el Restaurante El Fogón Latino.
- Marcos trabaja en la Blue Ridge Family Farm, donde cuida animales y maneja maquinaria agrícola.
- Rosa trabaja en Servicios de Limpieza Estrella del Sur, limpiando oficinas durante las noches.
- Debido a los horarios de trabajo de ambos padres, la abuela materna, Alicia Paz Fernández, y la niñera, Carmen Luna Reyes, se turnan para cuidar a Teo y a Camila después de la escuela.
- La familia recibió anteriormente beneficios de WIC y actualmente mantiene contacto con Smart Start de Henderson County para servicios de alfabetización familiar.
- En el hogar se habla principalmente español con la madre, la abuela y la niñera, e inglés con el padre y la madrastra; Teo escucha una mezcla de los dos idiomas (bilingüismo simultáneo) desde el nacimiento.
- Lucía reporta que su propia familia tiene antecedentes de retraso del habla: un tío materno no habló oraciones completas hasta los 4 años y recibió terapia en la escuela primaria.
- Los primos de Teo, Valentina Cruz Soto y Josué Cruz Soto, viven cerca y juegan con él casi todos los fines de semana cuando visita a su padre.
- En casa de la madre hay un perro llamado Max, al que Teo adora; durante la sesión de evaluación mencionó varias veces a "Max" y produjo la frase "Max tomi agua" (por "Max toma agua"), con sustitución de /s/ por [t].
- En la escuela, sus compañeros de clase más cercanos son Liam Carter y Sofía Nguyen; ambos suelen traducir o repetir lo que Teo dice cuando los adultos no le entienden.
- En el grupo pequeño de lenguaje de la escuela también participan Ava Thompson y Noah Brooks.
- La maestra de Pre-Kínder es la Sra. Diane Patterson y el asistente de aula es el Sr. Marcus Davis.
- El terapeuta ocupacional de la escuela, Ashley Pratt, OTR/L, también atiende a Teo por dificultades leves de motricidad fina.
- La última revisión del IFSP, antes de la transición a servicios escolares, se llevó a cabo el July 14, 2024.

OBSERVACIONES DE CONDUCTA

- Teo se mostró amigable y cooperador durante ambas sesiones, que se realizaron de 9:00 a.m. a 11:30 a.m. el primer día y de 1:00 p.m. a 2:15 p.m. el segundo día.
- Mantuvo atención conjunta de manera consistente y respondió a su nombre y al apodo "Teo" sin dificultad.
- Usó gestos, señalar y palabras sueltas para comunicarse; combinó dos palabras en algunas ocasiones ("mas agua", "no queo") pero rara vez produjo oraciones de tres o más palabras.
- Se frustró levemente cuando no fue comprendido, golpeando la mesa una vez, pero se calmó rápidamente con apoyo verbal.
- Mostró buena imitación motora y disposición para repetir palabras modelo con claves verbales moderadas (mod cues).
- No se observaron conductas repetitivas significativas ni dificultades sensoriales que interfirieran con la tarea.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

- Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas en inglés y español, con observación clínica complementaria:

| Prueba / Subprueba | Puntaje estándar | Percentil | Edad equivalente / Rango |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5) – Comprensión Auditiva | SS 79 | percentil 8 | 2;6–3;0 |
| PLS-5 – Expresión Verbal | SS 73 | percentil 4 | 2;3–2;9 |
| PLS-5 – Puntaje Total del Lenguaje | SS 75 | percentil 5 | intervalo de confianza 68-82 |
| CELF Preschool-3 – Estructura del Lenguaje | SS 71 | percentil 3 | — |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | SS 65 | percentil <1 | 2;6–3;0 |
| Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5) | SS 85 | percentil 16 | — |

- En la PLS-5, subprueba de Comprensión Auditiva, Teo identificó correctamente 6 de 12 objetos y acciones solicitadas en español, y 5 de 12 en inglés.
- En la subprueba de Expresión Verbal, produjo frases de dos palabras de manera consistente, pero solo logró 2 de 10 oraciones de tres palabras solicitadas.
- El análisis fonológico basado en la GFTA-3 mostró los siguientes patrones de error:
  - Sustitución de /k/ por [t], como en "tasa" por "casa"
  - Reducción de grupos consonánticos, como en "lato" por "plato"
  - Sustitución de /r/ por [w], como en "wopa" por "ropa"
  - Omisión de consonantes finales en inglés, como en "ca" por "cat"
- La inteligibilidad del habla se estimó en aproximadamente 40% para oyentes desconocidos y 65% para familiares cercanos.
- Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, codificada con convenciones SALT, se observaron varias instancias de palabra incompleta marcadas como [EW].
- En la tarea de seguimiento de instrucciones de dos pasos, Teo logró 3 de 5 ensayos con claves mínimas (min cues) y 5 de 5 con claves máximas verbales (max verbal cues).
- Se evaluó también la praxis oral motora; no se identificaron signos de apraxia infantil del habla, aunque se observó baja precisión en los movimientos linguales rápidos.

IMPRESIONES

- Los resultados de esta evaluación son consistentes con un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo de moderado a severo (F80.2), junto con un trastorno fonológico moderado (F80.0), en ambos idiomas de Teo.
- El patrón de errores fonológicos y la baja inteligibilidad del habla afectan significativamente su capacidad de comunicarse con compañeros como Liam y Sofía, así como con adultos fuera del círculo familiar inmediato, incluida la niñera, Carmen.
- El perfil bilingüe de Teo no explica por sí solo el grado de retraso observado, dado que mostró dificultades similares en ambos idiomas; por lo tanto, no se trata únicamente de una diferencia relacionada con el aprendizaje de dos idiomas, sino de un verdadero trastorno del lenguaje.
- El apoyo familiar es sólido, pero los horarios de trabajo de Lucía y Édgar (ambos con dos empleos) limitan el tiempo disponible para practicar estrategias en casa; será importante involucrar también a Alicia y Carmen, quienes pasan tiempo significativo con el niño.
- Teo se beneficiaría de servicios continuos de terapia del habla y el lenguaje, con énfasis en intervención bilingüe y en estrategias de fonología funcional.

RECOMENDACIONES

- Continuar o aumentar los servicios de terapia del habla y el lenguaje a una frecuencia de dos sesiones individuales por semana, de 30 minutos cada una, con un enfoque bilingüe.
- Incorporar el enfoque de ciclos fonológicos (Cycles) para abordar los patrones de sustitución y reducción de grupos consonánticos identificados.
- Considerar estrategias del modelo Hanen y técnicas táctiles-cinestésicas tipo PROMPT para mejorar la precisión articulatoria y la participación familiar en el tratamiento.
- Coordinar con la terapeuta ocupacional, Ashley Pratt, y con la maestra, la Sra. Patterson, para mantener consistencia entre los entornos escolar y clínico.
- Solicitar una reunión del equipo del IEP en Sunrise Avenue Elementary School para revisar las metas actuales de lenguaje a la luz de estos resultados.
- Capacitar a los cuidadores principales, incluidos Lucía, Marcos, Alicia y Carmen, en estrategias simples de expansión del lenguaje durante las rutinas diarias, como la hora de comer y el baño.
- Fomentar actividades de juego estructurado con los primos Valentina y Josué, y con los compañeros Liam y Sofía, para practicar turnos conversacionales en un ambiente de baja presión.
- Reevaluar la inteligibilidad del habla y el progreso fonológico en seis meses, aproximadamente en March 9, 2027, utilizando medidas comparables a las administradas hoy.
- Mantener comunicación entre la clínica y la familia a través del correo msantos@mountainspeechpartners.com o del teléfono (828) 555-0147 para programar citas futuras.
- Se recomienda a la familia visitar el sitio web de la clínica, www.mountainspeechpartners.com, donde se encuentran materiales educativos bilingües para practicar en casa.

PLAN DE SEGUIMIENTO

- Esta evaluadora enviará copia de este informe a el Dr. Samuel Kim, a la coordinadora de servicios Jennifer Boyd, y al equipo escolar de Teo, previa autorización firmada por Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paz.
- Se programará una cita de seguimiento con la familia para revisar este informe en detalle, idealmente antes del October 1, 2026.
- Cualquier pregunta puede dirigirse a Mireya Santos Delgado en msantos@mountainspeechpartners.com o al (828) 555-0147, en Mountain Speech & Language Partners, PLLC.

Firmado electrónicamente,
Mireya Santos Delgado, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y el Lenguaje Bilingüe
Mountain Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
September 9, 2026

Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
2210 Kildaire Farm Road, Cary, NC 27518
Tel: (919) 555-0142 | Fax: (919) 555-0143

EVALUACIÓN DE HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Paciente: Mateo Hernández Cruz
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de agosto de 2021
Edad cronológica al momento de la evaluación: 4;2
Fecha de evaluación: 9 de octubre de 2025
N.º de expediente: LP-20395
N.º de Medicaid: 684213957B
Padres/tutores: Lucía Rodríguez (madre) y Daniel Hernández (padre)
Dirección del hogar: 142 Maple Ridge Court, Apex, NC 27502, Condado de Wake
Teléfono de contacto: (919) 555-0187
Correo electrónico: lucia.hernandez85@gmail.com
Escuela: Escuela Primaria Pine Hollow
Distrito escolar: Distrito Escolar de las Escuelas Públicas del Condado de Chatham
Maestra / salón: Srta. Patterson, salón de Pre-K n.º 4
Evaluadora: Carla Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla-lenguaje bilingüe español/inglés
Médico de cabecera: Dr. Alan Kim, Pediatría General
Coordinadora de servicios, CDSA del Triángulo: Diana Álvarez
Intérprete presente en la sesión: Rosa Fernández

S:

Entrevista clínica realizada con la madre, Lucía Rodríguez, el 9 de octubre de 2025 de 9:15 a.m. a 10:00 a.m., en la oficina de Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC. Refiere preocupación persistente por el lenguaje expresivo de su hijo Mateo, de 4;2 años, quien asiste a Pre-K en Escuela Primaria Pine Hollow, salón de la Srta. Patterson, dentro del Distrito Escolar de las Escuelas Públicas del Condado de Chatham. Madre reporta que Mateo usa principalmente gestos y palabras sueltas, con inteligibilidad reducida tanto para familiares como para desconocidos.

Hx de embarazo y parto: embarazo a término, sin complicaciones prenatales reportadas. Parto vaginal en Cary Regional Hospital el 14 de agosto de 2021. Edad gestacional al nacer 39 semanas. Peso al nacer 3,220 g. Apgar 8 al minuto 1 y 9 a los 5 minutos. No requirió ingreso a UCIN. Hitos motores dentro de límites normales (se sentó ~6m, caminó ~13m). Hx médica: sin convulsiones, sin cirugías, sin hospitalizaciones previas. Dos episodios de otitis media en el último año, tratados con antibiótico oral; madre no reporta tubos de ventilación. Audición evaluada por última vez en consulta de Dr. Alan Kim en marzo de 2025, resultado normal bilateral.

Hx familiar y de lenguaje: hogar bilingüe español-inglés; español predomina en casa, inglés en la escuela. Madre, Lucía Rodríguez, trabaja turno nocturno en Carolina Foods Processing, en Sanford, NC; padre, Daniel Hernández, trabaja en construcción con horario variable. Durante el día, Mateo queda al cuidado de su niñera, Marisol Gómez, quien habla solo español con él. Hermana mayor, Sol Hernández, de 7 años, le habla principalmente en inglés y reporta que a veces se frustra porque "no le entiende" a su hermano. Madre refiere que la abuela materna, Juana Pérez, vive aún en el pueblo de San Lucas Tolimán, Guatemala, y llama por videollamada casi todos los domingos; Mateo la saluda con gestos pero rara vez produce palabras durante esas llamadas. En casa hay un perro, Max, con quien Mateo juega e intenta imitar sonidos ("gua gua").

No hx previa de terapia de habla-lenguaje formal, aunque madre menciona que una amiga le recomendó el enfoque Hanen y el programa It Takes Two to Talk para estimulación en casa, que ha intentado seguir de manera informal viendo videos en línea. Madre reporta que Mateo disfruta jugar con su amigo Liam en la escuela, pero la Srta. Patterson ha notado que Mateo se aísla durante actividades de círculo cuando no logra hacerse entender.

Queja principal: producción limitada de palabras, omisión de consonantes finales, inteligibilidad reducida (~30% para desconocidos, ~60% para familia). Sin preocupaciones de comprensión reportadas por la madre; Mateo sigue instrucciones de 2 pasos en ambos idiomas.

O:

Evaluación realizada el 9 de octubre de 2025, de 9:15 a.m. a 11:30 a.m., con descanso de 10:30 a.m. a 10:40 a.m.. Administración bilingüe con apoyo de intérprete, Rosa Fernández, para confirmación de ítems en inglés. Niño cooperador, buen contacto visual, transiciones sin dificultad entre tareas. Nivel de atención adecuado para su edad.

Pruebas administradas:

Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), versión en español: Comprensión Auditiva, puntuación estándar 78 (7.º percentil); Expresión Verbal, puntuación estándar 65 (1.er percentil); Puntuación Total de Lenguaje 70 (2.º percentil), IC 95% 64-76. Edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo: 2;6–3;0.

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), subprueba Estructura de Oraciones: puntuación escalar 6 (9.º percentil); subprueba Vocabulario Expresivo: puntuación escalar 5 (5.º percentil).

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3): puntuación estándar 62 (1.er percentil), IC 95% 57-67. Proceso fonológico predominante: omisión de consonante final en el 85% de las palabras objetivo; frontalización de velares observada en 6 de 10 ítems; reducción de grupos consonánticos en 8/10 ítems.

Tabla de resultados resumida:

| Prueba | Área | Puntuación estándar | Percentil |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 | Comprensión Auditiva | 78 | 7.º |
| PLS-5 | Expresión Verbal | 65 | 1.er |
| CELF Preschool-3 | Estructura de Oraciones | 6 (escalar) | 9.º |
| CELF Preschool-3 | Vocabulario Expresivo | 5 (escalar) | 5.º |
| GFTA-3 | Articulación | 62 | 1.er |

Muestra de habla espontánea (15 minutos, juego libre con bloques y figuras de animales): longitud media de enunciado 1.8 palabras; inventario fonético consistente con /m, n, p, b, t, d, w/; ausencia de /k, g, s, ɾ/ en posición inicial y final. Produjo "pape" por "pan", "tete" por "leche", y al señalar una figura del sol dijo ""o"" como aproximación a "sol", target fonológico trabajado durante la sesión con mod cues táctiles-visuales, estilo PROMPT. Respondió a 8 de 10 preguntas de sí/no con gesto apropiado; produjo 3 de 5 combinaciones de dos palabras cuando se le dio modelo ("más agua", "no quiero").

Praxis oral motora dentro de límites normales; sin hallazgos sugestivos de apraxia del habla infantil. Estructuras orofaciales simétricas, movilidad adecuada de lengua y labios. Resonancia y voz dentro de parámetros normales.

A:

Mateo presenta un trastorno fonológico de moderado a severo con retraso concomitante en lenguaje expresivo, en el contexto de desarrollo bilingüe típico (sin evidencia de confusión por bilingüismo; patrones consistentes con trastorno primario de habla-lenguaje presentes en ambos idiomas). Perfil compatible con ICD-10 F80.1 (trastorno del desarrollo del lenguaje, tipo expresivo) y F80.0 (trastorno fonológico). Comprensión relativamente mejor conservada que expresión, patrón típico en este perfil. No se observan banderas rojas de trastorno del espectro autista; interacción social e intención comunicativa adecuadas dado el nivel de frustración esperado por limitación expresiva.

Pronóstico favorable con intervención intensiva temprana dado nivel de comprensión, cooperación en la sesión, y motivación familiar alta. Riesgo de impacto académico si no se aborda antes del ingreso a kindergarten, considerando calendario del Distrito Escolar de las Escuelas Públicas del Condado de Chatham.

P:

1. Se recomienda terapia de habla-lenguaje individual, 2 veces por semana, 45 minutos por sesión, CPT 92523 (evaluación) y CPT 92507 (tratamiento individual), facturado bajo Medicaid 684213957B.

2. Enfoque fonológico tipo Cycles para abordar procesos de omisión de consonante final y frontalización velar, con listas de palabras objetivo rotadas cada 4-6 semanas.

3. Incorporar estrategias de PROMPT para apoyo táctil-cinestésico en la producción de secuencias motoras del habla, dado el patrón de simplificación observado.

4. Entrenamiento a la familia en el modelo Hanen, usando el programa It Takes Two to Talk, con enfoque en expansión de enunciados y espera estructurada ("OWL"); se proveerá material en español a Lucía Rodríguez y Daniel Hernández.

5. Considerar sistema de comunicación aumentativa de respaldo tipo PECS si la frustración comunicativa persiste durante el próximo trimestre, para reducir conductas de evitación en el salón de la Srta. Patterson.

6. Protocolo Kaufman para apraxia del habla como plan alternativo si no se observa progreso adecuado en inteligibilidad tras 8-10 semanas de tratamiento con el enfoque actual.

7. Continuar seguimiento con Diana Álvarez, coordinadora de servicios en CDSA del Triángulo, para explorar elegibilidad de servicios adicionales en el hogar.

8. Se recomienda nueva evaluación auditiva de rutina con Dr. Alan Kim dado historial de otitis media recurrente.

9. Compartir resumen de resultados con Srta. Patterson para apoyo en el aula, incluyendo estrategias de modelado de lenguaje durante actividades de círculo y juego con compañeros como Liam.

Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) – Annual Review

FAMILY INFORMATION
Pt lives w/ mother Lucía Rodríguez, father Carlos Hernández, and older sister Valentina Hernández (age 6) at 482 Willowbrook Ln, Siler City, Chatham County, NC 27344. Family rents duplex, stable housing x2 yrs. Home language primarily Spanish; Valentina bilingual, often code-switches w/ pt during play. CG (mom) prefers Spanish for detailed discussion of pt's progress, comfortable w/ basic conversational English for scheduling. Dad Carlos works 2nd shift at Siler City Poultry Processing; mom works part-time cashier at Food Lion #2214 on 11th St. Babysitter Rosa Fernández (family friend, maternal aunt's neighbor) watches pt approx 3x/wk 8a-12p while mom works; Rosa reports pt "se frustra cuando no lo entiendo" (gets frustrated when she doesn't understand him). Pt also spends Sat afternoons w/ cousins Diego (age 5) and Camila (age 7) at maternal grandmother's home nearby; grandmother supervises all three children during visits. Family dog Rocky (lab mix, approx 3 yrs old) is a household fixture; pt reportedly imitates animal sounds w/ Rocky during play and will point to Rocky when wanting attention.

FAMILY CONCERNS / PRIORITIES (in family's own words, translated where noted)
Mom reports (orig. Spanish, documented 3 de marzo de 2025): "Teo no habla tanto como su hermana a esta edad. Dice pocas palabras y a veces se frustra y me pega o tira las cosas." (Translation: "Teo doesn't talk as much as his sister did at this age. He says few words and sometimes gets frustrated and hits me or throws things.") Mom also stated priority is that pt be understood by Rosa and by cousins Diego and Camila during play w/o mom interpreting every utterance. Dad's priority, shared by phone: pt follow 2-step directions at home w/o repeated cueing, and reduce tantrums during transitions (e.g. bath to bed). Family noted concern surfaced again el martes 4 de junio during a call w/ SC Brenda Michaels — mom reiterated frustration behaviors increasing at daycare dropoff, approx 3-4x/wk per teacher report.

DAILY ROUTINES
AM: wake approx 7a, breakfast w/ Valentina (cereal, typically same seat at table — routine helps pt transition), brief play w/ Rocky before daycare dropoff at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center (Siler City) by 8:15a. Pt in toddler room w/ teacher Ms. Karen Lopez and assistant Ms. Denise Boyd; classmates incl Ethan and Sofia reported as frequent play partners per daycare report, though parallel play predominates over interactive play currently. Midday nap 12:30p-2:30p. Lunch at daycare, snack at pickup. PM pickup by mom or Rosa approx 5p; dinner routine w/ whole family at table; bath (favorite routine, high engagement/vocalization per mom); bedtime book read in Spanish by mom, approx 7:30p-8p. Weekend routine incl Sat visits to grandmother's w/ cousins, outdoor play, and Sun church service where pt reportedly sits quietly w/ family.

OTHER AGENCIES / SERVICES INVOLVED
- Pediatrician: Dr. Angela Soto, Chatham Pediatric Associates, Siler City — last well visit 01/22/2025.

EVALUATION SUMMARY (current review)
Eval conducted by Marisol Delgado Vega, CCC-SLP, bilingual Spanish/English, of Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services. 03/10/2025 | PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | SS 73 | 4th | 68-78 | 1;8–2;0

Pt's overall composite falls in 73-83 range across measures, consistent w/ prior eval 09/16/2024 (SS 78, 69-87). Minimal change noted; continued delay in expressive domain, greater than receptive. Play-based observation: pt engaged in functional play w/ toy kitchen set, brief symbolic play ("feeding" stuffed animal), joint attention present but fleeting (approx 3-5 sec). Pt produced approx 15 intelligible single words consistently (Spanish-dominant), incl "agua", "mamá", "más"; English productions limited to "bye" and "up". Articulation informal sample: pt substituted /t/ for /k/ consistently (e.g. target "carro" produced "tawo"); stimulable for /k/ w/ mod cues in isolation, 3 of 5 trials correct. No oral-motor structural concerns noted. Hearing/vision WNL per records above.

Gestational hx: born 37 weeks gestation, birth weight 6 lbs 2 oz, Apgar 8/9. No NICU stay. Developmental milestones per mom: sat 6mo approx, walked 13 months approx — WNL for gross motor.

Outcome 3: Teo's family (esp. Lucía and Rosa) will report decreased frustration-related behaviors (hitting, throwing) during communication breakdowns, measured via caregiver log, by next review.

Outcome 4: Teo will produce /k/ correctly in isolation and in CV syllables w/ min cues in 8/10 trials across 2 consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Cycles approach targeting velar fronting pattern; home practice list of target words sent biweekly; CG to practice approx 5 min daily during bath or car time (naturalistic, low-pressure contexts).

Outcome 5: Teo will initiate joint attention (eye gaze + gesture) w/ peers incl Ethan and Sofia during structured daycare activities, 3 of 5 observed opportunities, by next review.
Strategies: daycare staff to set up parallel-play-to-interactive-play bridges (shared toy, turn-taking games); SLP to model w/ pt during home visits using sibling Valentina as peer model.

text:
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
Evaluación del Habla y Lenguaje / Speech-Language Evaluation Report

Clinician: Sarah Kowalski, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Employer: Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
Office Phone: (828) 555-0147
Email: skowalski@carolinabilingualslp.com
Website: www.carolinabilingualslp.com

Child's Name: Mateo Hernández Ruiz
Date of Birth: August 14, 2021
Chronological Age: 4;2
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Rodríguez
Address: Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601
Medicaid ID: NC8827461B
Referral Source: Piedmont CDSA
Interpreter Present: Yesenia Campos
Evaluation Date: February 19, 2026
Report Date: February 26, 2026

Razón de la Evaluación / Reason for Referral

Mateo Hernández Ruiz is a 4;2-year-old niño bilingüe referred for a comprehensive speech and language evaluation by Piedmont CDSA service coordinator Monica Teague due to limited intelligibility, reduced expressive vocabulary, and parent concern regarding Mateo's difficulty following multi-step directions in both English and Spanish. Mateo currently attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare four days a week, where his teacher, Miss Patricia Delgado, reports that he plays well with peers but often gestures instead of using words. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez, attended the evaluation with interpreter Yesenia Campos present for all case history and counseling portions. The session took place from 9:15 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. at our clinic office.

Historia de Nacimiento y Desarrollo / Birth and Medical History

According to Lucía Rodríguez, Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation via vaginal delivery, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 and a birth weight of 6 lbs, 14 oz. There were no complications during pregnancy or delivery. Lucía Rodríguez reported that Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Angela Whitfield, has followed him since birth and has not identified any significant medical concerns, though she referred the family to Piedmont CDSA at Mateo's 18-month well visit due to delayed babbling and limited word approximations. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening and a follow-up audiological evaluation in March 2023 confirmed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. He has a history of recurrent ear infections, with three documented episodes of otitis media between January 2024 and June 2024, treated with antibiotics; no tympanostomy tubes were placed. Mateo currently receives occupational therapy with Brittany Sorensen, OTR/L, for fine motor delays and physical therapy with Daniel Mackey, PT, DPT, for mild gross motor delays, both through Piedmont CDSA. His current IFSP, last reviewed on November 4, 2025, includes Outcome 2 targeting expressive communication across settings.

Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje / Family and Language History

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez, his older sister, Valentina Hernández Ruiz (age 7), and his maternal grandmother, Rosa, who provides childcare several afternoons a week. Mateo's father, Carlos Hernández, lives in a nearby town and has supervised visitation on weekends. Lucía Rodríguez shared, through interpreter Yesenia Campos, "Trabajo en el Harris Teeter de día y limpio oficinas de noche para RJS, por eso casi no tengo tiempo para jugar con él como quisiera." She works two jobs to support the household and reported feeling exhausted but committed to carrying out home practice recommendations whenever possible. Valentina frequently translates for Mateo with unfamiliar adults and reportedly speaks for him rather than waiting for him to communicate independently.

The home language environment is primarily Spanish, with Rosa speaking almost exclusively Spanish and Lucía Rodríguez using both Spanish and English depending on the listener. Lucía Rodríguez reported that Mateo's first words emerged around 18 months, later than Valentina's, and that his vocabulary growth has remained slow since. She stated, "Mateo entiende casi todo, pero cuando quiere decir algo, se frustra porque no le salen las palabras." During the clinical interview, Mateo pointed at the family dog and said "Rocky corre," demonstrating emerging two-word combinations in Spanish. At Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, Mateo is reportedly close with a classmate named Andrés, with whom he engages in parallel play but limited verbal exchange.

Resultados de las Pruebas / Test Results

Mateo was administered standardized assessments in both English and Spanish, with Yesenia Campos interpreting directions and eliciting Spanish responses under this clinician's direction. Behavioral observations suggested adequate attention and effort, though Mateo required frequent redirection and moderate verbal cues to remain on task during longer subtests.

Test / Subtest -- Standard Score -- Percentile -- Age Equivalent -- 95% CI

Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), Auditory Comprehension -- 78 -- 7th -- 2;6–3;0 -- 73–83

PLS-5, Expressive Communication -- 72 -- 3rd -- 2;3–2;9 -- 66–78

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-2 (CELF Preschool-2), Core Language Score -- 75 -- 5th -- 2;9–3;3 -- 69–81

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), Sounds-in-Words -- 68 -- 2nd -- 2;0–2;6 -- 61–75

On the GFTA-3, Mateo demonstrated multiple phonological processes consistent with his age, including final consonant deletion and fronting. He produced /k/ as [t] in word-initial position and substituted /ɾ/ with [d] medially, as in his production of "pe[d]o" for the target word "perro". Stimulability testing showed that Mateo could approximate /k/ correctly with max cues but reverted to his habitual pattern spontaneously. In connected speech sampled during play, intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners was estimated at 30%, improving to approximately 60% with context and gesture support.

Expressively, Mateo used primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations, such as "Rocky corre" and "más agua." He correctly answered 3 of 5 basic wh-questions in Spanish but struggled significantly with English equivalents, correctly answering only 1 of 5. Receptively, Mateo followed one-step directions reliably (8/10 trials) but had difficulty with two-step directions across both languages (4/10 trials). A sample utterance coded during language sample analysis included one word error, annotated as [EW], consistent with his reduced expressive vocabulary.

Oral-motor examination revealed adequate structure and function for speech production, with slightly reduced lingual lateralization that did not appear to significantly impact articulation. Diadochokinetic rates were mildly reduced but within functional limits for conversational speech.

Impresiones / Clinical Impressions

Based on standardized testing, parent report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, consistent with ICD-10 code F80.2, affecting both his Spanish and English language systems. His speech sound production also falls significantly below expected norms for his age, consistent with a moderate phonological disorder. These findings are not attributable to hearing loss, given his documented normal audiological results, nor fully explained by reduced exposure, as Mateo receives consistent language input in the home in Spanish and increasing exposure to English at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare. His difficulties appear to reflect a true language-learning disability affecting both languages roughly proportionally, rather than a language difference secondary to bilingual acquisition alone.

Mateo's limited intelligibility and reduced expressive output likely contribute to his increased frustration and reliance on Valentina to communicate for him, a pattern that may reduce his opportunities to practice independent verbal expression. Continued speech-language intervention is clinically indicated.

Recomendaciones / Recommendations

1. Mateo should receive individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, billed under CPT 92523, provided in both Spanish and English by a bilingual speech-language pathologist, to address expressive vocabulary, two-step direction following, and speech sound production.

2. This clinician recommends a Cycles phonological approach to target final consonant deletion and fronting patterns, alternating target sound classes across sessions to support generalization.

3. PROMPT techniques may be incorporated to provide tactile-kinesthetic cueing for Mateo's motor planning difficulties with /k/ and /ɾ/.

4. Given Mateo's reliance on gesture and his sister's interpreting on his behalf, introducing a structured augmentative system such as PECS during the initial phase of intervention may reduce communication frustration and support more independent requesting, with a planned fade as verbal output increases.

5. Parent coaching is strongly recommended. Given Lucía Rodríguez's demanding work schedule across two jobs, flexible scheduling and a brief, high-yield home program are essential. This clinician recommends Hanen-based strategies, specifically the It Takes Two to Talk program, adapted for bilingual delivery with support from interpreter Yesenia Campos as needed, so that Rosa and Lucía Rodríguez can both participate in brief coaching sessions during existing childcare hours.

6. A trial of the Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol is recommended to shape more complex syllable and word shapes, given Mateo's current reliance on simplified word forms.

7. Continued coordination with Dr. Angela Whitfield regarding recurrent otitis media history is recommended, along with ongoing collaboration with Brittany Sorensen, OTR/L, and Daniel Mackey, PT, DPT, to ensure a unified developmental approach across disciplines.

8. Piedmont CDSA service coordinator Monica Teague should update Mateo's IFSP to reflect updated present levels and to add specific speech-language goals under Outcome 2 and a new communication-focused outcome addressing independent verbal requesting.

9. Reassessment is recommended in approximately six months, or sooner if progress plateaus, to determine continued eligibility and appropriate frequency of services.

This clinician is available to discuss these findings further with the family, interpreter, or any member of Mateo's care team. Please direct questions to Sarah Kowalski, M.S., CCC-SLP, at skowalski@carolinabilingualslp.com or (828) 555-0147, or visit www.carolinabilingualslp.com for additional family resources in both English and Spanish.

Respetuosamente / Respectfully submitted,

Sarah Kowalski, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC

En cuanto a producción de sonidos, Mateo omite consistentemente /k/ y /g/ en posición inicial, sustituyéndolos por [t] y [d], y produce la palabra "agua" como "aba". Con claves táctiles y mod cues, logró producir /k/ aislado en 3 de 5 intentos. Codifiqué varias muestras con [EW] en el SALT por énfasis en palabra final poco clara.

Con base en estos resultados y en lo que ustedes compartieron hoy, propongo mantener los tres resultados actuales del IFSP con ajustes en las estrategias:

Resultado 1: Mateo usará al menos 10 palabras o aproximaciones consistentes para pedir objetos y actividades preferidas en el hogar y en el centro Burbujas y Risas.

Resultado 2: Mateo imitará sonidos consonánticos iniciales /k/, /g/ y /p/ en juego estructurado, con mod cues o menos, en 8 de 10 oportunidades.

Resultado 3: La familia reportará estrategias de comunicación aumentada (gestos, señas básicas) usadas en las rutinas diarias.

Seguiremos con sesiones dos veces por semana, los lunes y miércoles de 10:15 a.m. a 10:45 a.m., en el hogar, bajo el código 92523 con modificador GN. La próxima revisión está programada para el 2 de septiembre de 2025.

Hola Mariana:

Gracias por todo el trabajo. Queremos compartir algunas cosas desde nuestra perspectiva como familia.

Lo que más nos preocupa es que Mateo se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos. Anoche, 3 de marzo de 2025, a las 7:30 p.m., quería algo del refrigerador y empezó a llorar y a golpear la puerta porque no sabíamos qué pedía. Al final señaló el jugo. Esto pasa casi todos los días, a veces dos o tres veces entre 6:00 p.m. y 8:00 p.m., que es cuando toda la familia está en casa.

Su hermano mayor, Sebastián, de 7 años, a veces se adelanta y pide las cosas por él, y aunque eso ayuda en el momento, sentimos que no le da a Mateo la oportunidad de intentarlo. Mi suegra, Rosa Delgado, lo cuida los viernes mientras trabajamos, y ella usa muchos gestos con él, lo cual parece funcionar bien. Ella dice que entiende casi todo lo que él "dice" con señas improvisadas.

En el centro Burbujas y Risas, la maestra, Karla Soto, nos comentó el martes 4 de febrero de 2025 que Mateo prefiere jugar solo y que no busca a otros niños del salón, como Emilia o Dylan, para jugar. Sí reacciona cuando su amiguito Thiago le ofrece un juguete.

La rutina diaria es más o menos así: se despierta a las 6:45 a.m., desayuna con nosotros, llega al centro a las 8:00 a.m. y lo recogemos a las 5:15 p.m.. Cena entre 6:30 p.m. y 7:00 p.m., baño a las 7:45 p.m. y se duerme alrededor de las 8:30 p.m.. Nuestra perrita Luna siempre está con él durante el baño; le encanta salpicarla.

También queríamos mencionar que seguimos recibiendo apoyo de WIC y que la familia participa en el programa de Early Head Start para la evaluación de desarrollo general, aunque la terapia principal la recibimos de ustedes. Jorge también preguntó si Smart Start de Durham tiene algún recurso adicional para familias bilingües, porque alguien en su trabajo, en Distribuidores de Muebles Hernández (Distribuidores de Muebles Hernández), le mencionó un programa de lectura gratuito.

Una preocupación más: nuestro pediatra, el Dr. Andrés Villalobos, nos dijo en la cita del 20 de enero de 2025 que la audición de Mateo parece normal según la prueba más reciente, pero quería confirmar con usted si eso se documentó en el expediente del CDSA.

Estamos de acuerdo con los tres resultados que propone, pero quisiéramos agregar que la familia también practique en español e inglés, porque en casa hablamos sobre todo español, pero en el centro todo es en inglés.

Gracias de nuevo,
Lucía

Hola Lucía y Jorge:

Muchas gracias por compartir todo esto; es exactamente el tipo de información que necesitamos para que el IFSP refleje la vida real de Mateo.

Sobre la frustración en las tardes: vamos a incorporar en el Resultado 1 una estrategia específica de espera estructurada ("tiempo de espera" de 5 segundos) antes de que un adulto o Sebastián anticipen lo que Mateo quiere. Le pediré a Rosa que use las mismas señas que ya usa los viernes, porque es un gran punto de partida; podemos documentarlas como parte del vocabulario funcional del niño.

Hablaré directamente con la maestra Karla Soto en Burbujas y Risas el martes 11 de marzo de 2025 para observar la interacción con Thiago y pensar en cómo ampliar ese interés a otros niños del salón.

Sobre el bilingüismo: estoy totalmente de acuerdo. Añadiré al Resultado 3 que las estrategias de comunicación (gestos, señas básicas, aproximaciones verbales) se practiquen en ambos idiomas, y le pediré a la maestra que, cuando sea posible, también modele las palabras clave en español, ya que ella tiene formación bilingüe según me indicó Karla.

Sí, la evaluación auditiva del 20 de enero de 2025 del Dr. Villalobos ya está en el expediente del CDSA del Triángulo (referencia TR-2024-01187); se documentó como "audición dentro de límites normales bilateralmente". Confirmaré con Daniela Ortiz que también quede anotada en la sección de servicios médicos del IFSP.

En cuanto a Smart Start de Durham: voy a preguntarle a Daniela Ortiz si Manos Amigas tiene un enlace directo con ellos, porque sé que manejan un programa de lectura bilingüe para familias con niños de 0 a 5 años. Les aviso en cuanto tenga esa información.

Resultado 1: Mateo usará al menos 10 palabras o aproximaciones consistentes, en español o inglés, para pedir objetos y actividades preferidas, con un tiempo de espera estructurado de los adultos.

Mantenemos las sesiones los lunes y miércoles de 10:15 a.m. a 10:45 a.m. en el hogar, y agregaré una sesión de consulta mensual en Burbujas y Risas los terceros jueves del mes, de 1:00 p.m. a 1:30 p.m., comenzando el 20 de marzo de 2025.
