+ Name: Mateo Alejandro Fuentes Rivas (family calls him "Teo")
+ CA: 26 months
+ Context: Annual IFSP Review, Piedmont CDSA, Monroe office; meeting conducted bilingually (English/Spanish)

Summary: Mateo is a 26-month-old bilingual (Spanish-English) toddler referred to the NC Infant-Toddler Program after his pediatrician, Dr. Angela Chen, raised concerns about expressive language delay at a well-child visit on el martes 4 de junio de 2024 (06/04/2024). Initial eligibility evaluation confirmed a significant delay in expressive and receptive language. The Individualized Family Service Plan was written on July 22, 2024 and this annual review, held on 3 de marzo de 2025 (03/03/2025), updates present levels, family priorities, and service delivery for the coming year. Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez and Carlos Fuentes, his older sister Camila Fuentes Rodríguez (called "Cami"), and his maternal grandmother, Rosa Rivas, at 215 Pecan Grove Lane, Monroe, NC 28112. The family moved to Union County three years ago from Yarumela, a small village in Honduras where extended family still lives. Lucía can be reached by email at lucia.rodriguez84@gmail.com or by phone at (704) 555-0182.

FAMILY INFORMATION

Mother: Lucía Rodríguez, age 29, works the overnight shift at the Food Lion Distribution Center in Indian Trail. She speaks primarily Spanish at home and reports confidence in English for medical appointments but prefers Spanish for detailed conversations about Mateo's development.

Father: Carlos Fuentes, age 32, works as a machine operator at Charlotte Pipe and Foundry. He attends evening sessions when his schedule allows and participated in this review by phone from 9:15 AM to 9:45 AM... (correction: he joined by phone from 9:15 AM to 9:45 AM).

Sibling: Camila Fuentes Rodríguez, age 5, attends kindergarten and is described by the family as "Mateo's best helper," often modeling words for him during play.

Caregiver: Rosa Rivas, Mateo's maternal grandmother, lives with the family and provides afternoon childcare while Lucía sleeps before her shift. Rosa speaks only Spanish and is the primary communication partner during daytime hours.

The family's dog, Luna, is frequently mentioned as a motivator for requesting and labeling during play routines.

SERVICE COORDINATOR AND CDSA OFFICE

Service Coordinator: Jennifer Hayes, Piedmont CDSA, located at 1900 Skyway Drive, Suite 110, Monroe, NC 28110. Office phone: (704) 555-0199. Agency website: www.piedmontcdsa.org. Case record number: CDSA-2024-01837. Medicaid ID: NC847291635A.

Speech-Language Pathologist: Maria Santos, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual provider with Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services, authored this review following direct assessment and parent/caregiver report.

Occupational Therapist: Rachel Kim, OTR/L, also with Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services, contributed fine motor and feeding observations.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES (in the family's own words, translated where noted)

Lucía shared: "Me preocupa que Teo todavía no dice muchas palabras. Su hermana a esta edad ya hablaba mucho más." (Translation: "I worry that Teo still doesn't say many words. His sister was talking much more at this age.")

Carlos added, through the bilingual SLP: "I want him to be ready for school. I don't want him to fall behind like I did when I came to this country not knowing English."

Rosa reported that Mateo gets frustrated at mealtimes and sometimes throws food when he cannot ask for more water or more "agua."

Priorities identified by the family:
1. Increase Mateo's spoken vocabulary in both Spanish and English.
2. Reduce mealtime frustration by teaching functional requesting.
3. Prepare Mateo for the transition to preschool services before his third birthday.

DAILY ROUTINES

Morning: Mateo wakes around 7:00 AM, eats breakfast with Camila before she leaves for school, and is dropped at Little Sprouts Developmental Preschool by 8:30 AM, where his teacher, Debra Lopez, reports he engages in parallel play and is beginning to imitate peers, including his friend Sofia, during circle time.

Afternoon: Rosa picks him up at 3:30 PM and cares for him until Carlos returns from work around 5:45 PM. Snack time and outdoor play with Luna are daily highlights; the family reports Mateo says "Luna" clearly to call the dog, one of his most consistent words.

Evening: Bath routine at 7:00 PM, followed by a bilingual bedtime book routine led by Lucía, bedtime around 8:30 PM.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

- Union County WIC Program: provides nutritional support; next recertification appointment scheduled.
- Union County Department of Social Services: assisted the family with Medicaid enrollment.
- Smart Start of Union County: connected the family with the current childcare subsidy at Little Sprouts Developmental Preschool.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Communication: On the Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), administered in both English and Spanish, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (9th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 72 (3rd percentile). Age equivalents fell in the 14-16 months range against a confidence interval of 68-78. On the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, he demonstrated joint attention and requesting through gesture consistently but used only 3 of 10 targeted single words spontaneously (30%).

Mateo produces early-developing phonemes /p/, /b/, and /m/ consistently. He was observed to say "mamá," "más," and "up" with moderate cues, and imitated the target word "ball" with minimal cues during structured play.

Birth and medical history: Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestational age, weighing 6 lbs 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9. No significant medical history is reported. Working diagnosis code: F80.2 (Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder). Billed intervention code: 92523.

Adaptive/Fine Motor: Rachel Kim's observations on the Battelle Developmental Inventory-3 (BDI-3) placed fine motor skills within age expectations; no OT services are currently recommended.

IFSP OUTCOMES WITH STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 50 or more single words across settings to request, label, and comment, in Spanish and/or English, as reported by Lucía, Carlos, and Debra Lopez.
Strategies: Model target vocabulary during daily routines using Hanen "OWL" strategies (Observe, Wait, Listen); use PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cues to support bilabial and labiodental sound production; incorporate Luna and mealtime requests as natural motivators.

Outcome 2: Mateo will combine two words (e.g., "más agua," "more up") to reduce mealtime frustration, as reported by Rosa and observed by the SLP.
Strategies: Teach functional communication replacement for food-throwing using a simple core vocabulary board at home and at Little Sprouts Developmental Preschool; coach Rosa and Carlos on wait-time and expectant pause strategies during snack.

Outcome 3: The family will understand and participate in transition planning for Part B eligibility determination prior to Mateo's third birthday.
Strategies: Service coordinator Jennifer Hayes will schedule a transition conference at least 90 days before the birthday; family will visit the Union County Public Schools Exceptional Children's Preschool Program classroom at Marshville Elementary School, where Debra Lopez's colleague, Ms. Monica Brooks, runs the toddler transition classroom (Room 4).

SESSION SCHEDULE

| Day | Start | End | Service | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Speech-Language Therapy | Home: 215 Pecan Grove Lane, Monroe |
| Wednesday | 1:30 PM | 2:15 PM | Speech-Language Therapy | Little Sprouts Developmental Preschool, 420 Hawthorne Road, Monroe |
| Friday | 10:00 AM | 10:30 AM | Developmental Therapy Consult | Home: 215 Pecan Grove Lane, Monroe |
| Monthly, first Tuesday | 2:00 PM | 3:00 PM | Service Coordination | Piedmont CDSA, 1900 Skyway Drive, Suite 110, Monroe |

Transportation note: Rosa will transport Mateo to Little Sprouts Developmental Preschool on Wednesday sessions; Lucía or Carlos will be present for all home visits whenever possible given Lucía's overnight schedule.

INTERPRETER AND LANGUAGE SUPPORTS

All written materials are provided in Spanish and English. Maria Santos conducts sessions bilingually without need for a separate interpreter; however, when Jennifer Hayes conducts service coordination calls, a telephonic interpreter through the agency's language line is used if Lucía is unavailable.

TRANSITION PLANNING

As Mateo approaches his third birthday, the team discussed eligibility for Part B preschool services through Union County Public Schools. The family toured Marshville Elementary School on February 12, 2025 (02/12/2025) and met briefly with Ms. Monica Brooks. A formal transition conference is scheduled for April 9, 2025.

The family's extended support network includes relatives in Yarumela, who the parents report call weekly by video to speak with Mateo in Spanish, reinforcing home-language exposure.

SIGNATURES AND DATES

This IFSP review was completed collaboratively with the family on 3 de marzo de 2025. Present: Lucía Rodríguez (in person), Carlos Fuentes (by phone), Rosa Rivas (in person), Jennifer Hayes (service coordinator), Maria Santos (SLP, author). Next annual review due by March 3, 2026. Six-month review check-in scheduled for el martes 2 de septiembre de 2025 (09/02/2025).

For questions, contact Jennifer Hayes at Piedmont CDSA, (704) 555-0199, or visit www.piedmontcdsa.org for family resources in Spanish and English.

text:
Speech-Language Evaluation / Evaluación del Habla y Lenguaje

Child's Name: Mateo Hernández Ruiz
Date of Birth: August 14, 2021
Chronological Age: 4;2
Date of Evaluation: October 2, 2025
Evaluator: Rosa Fuentes, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Employer: Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC
Referring Provider: Dr. Amanda Ko, Lakeview Pediatrics – Hickory Campus
Case/Record ID: LD-48217-H
Medicaid ID: 209384716B
Address: 1442 Oakhurst Lane, Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601
Phone: (828) 555-0147
Email: lucia.hernandezruiz@carolinamail.net
Primary Languages in Home: Spanish and English (bilingual, Spanish-dominant)

Reason for Referral / Motivo de la Referencia

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by his pediatrician, Dr. Amanda Ko, following concerns raised by his mother, Lucía Ruiz Fernández, and his classroom teacher at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center. Mateo currently attends daycare in Ms. Lopez's room, the Caterpillar classroom, five days a week while his parents work. His father, Diego Hernández Morales, is employed at Catawba Furniture Works as a production supervisor, and his mother works part-time at Valley Fresh Market. Su mamá reports, "no entiendo por qué no habla como los otros niños de su edad," reflecting growing concern about Mateo's limited expressive vocabulary compared to his classmates, including Ava Thompson and Noah Pérez, who sit beside him during circle time.

Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestation via emergency cesarean section at Cedar Valley Health System – Mooresville Campus on August 14, 2021, following preterm labor. Birth weight was 4 lbs 6 oz with Apgar scores of 7 and 9 at one and five minutes. He spent 19 days in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Cedar Valley Health System – Mooresville Campus for respiratory distress and feeding support, during which time he received a swallow study (CPT 92611) that was unremarkable. Medical history is also significant for recurrent otitis media, with bilateral myringotomy tube placement performed at age 18 months by Dr. Felipe Navarro at Carolina Hearing & ENT Associates. A most recent audiological evaluation at that same practice on September 15, 2025 confirmed normal hearing bilaterally. Relevant diagnostic codes on file include ICD-10 F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and ICD-10 H65.19 (otitis media, resolved).

Family and Language History

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Ruiz Fernández and Diego Hernández Morales, and his older sister, Valentina Hernández Ruiz, who is in second grade. Family routines are conducted primarily in Spanish, though Mateo hears English daily at daycare and from his sister, who is more English-dominant after starting school. His maternal cousins, Emiliano Ruiz and Camila Ruiz, visit on weekends and speak mostly English, which Lucía Ruiz Fernández says sometimes frustrates Mateo because "él quiere jugar con ellos pero no le entienden." The family's regular babysitter, Blanca Osorio, cares for Mateo and Valentina Hernández Ruiz on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and reports similar concerns about limited expressive language at home. The family dog, Rocky, is a frequent topic of conversation, and Mateo often points and says "go" when Rocky runs in the yard, though he rarely combines words spontaneously.

The family was connected to Early Intervention services through Western Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency shortly after Mateo's NICU discharge, with ongoing case management provided by service coordinator Marcus Whitfield. The family also receives nutritional support through Catawba County WIC and was previously enrolled in Early Head Start before transitioning to Little Sprouts Early Learning Center. A referral to Catawba County Department of Social Services for housing assistance was made in March 2024, and the family has participated in parenting workshops through Smart Start of Catawba County.

Previous and Current Services

Mateo has received weekly speech-language therapy through Western Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency since age 26 months, using a combination of Hanen-based parent coaching and PROMPT techniques to target oral-motor placement and early word combinations. His most recent IFSP, developed on April 18, 2025, includes three active outcomes, reviewed quarterly with his service coordinator, Marcus Whitfield, and his parents.

IFSP Outcome Review

Outcome	Strategies	Progress	Date
Outcome 1: Mateo will use 2-word combinations to request desired items in Spanish and English	Parent modeling, Hanen-based "OWL" strategies, visual choice boards	Increased from 2/10 to 6/10 opportunities independent	July 14, 2025
Outcome 2: Mateo will imitate target phonemes /k/, /g/, and final consonants in single words	PROMPT tactile cueing, mod cues, drill-play with preferred toys	Produces /k/ in isolation with min cues; final consonants remain inconsistent	August 11, 2025
Outcome 3: Mateo will follow 2-step directions in structured and unstructured settings	Visual schedules, gesture pairing, bilingual direction-following tasks	3 of 5 trials correct with mod cues across settings	September 9, 2025

Behavioral Observations

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with testing materials, though he required frequent redirection to remain seated. He demonstrated functional play skills, stacking blocks and pretending to feed a toy dog, saying "Rocky comer" during the activity. Attention to task was variable, improving with movement breaks every 10 minutes. Testing was conducted bilingually, with instructions presented in both Spanish and English, and an interpreter, Gabriela Soto, present to support rapport-building and family communication during the feedback conference at 2:30 p.m.

Standardized Test Results

Test/Subtest	Score Type	Score	Confidence Interval	Date
Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), Spanish/English Edition – Auditory Comprehension	Standard Score	76	70-82	October 2, 2025
PLS-5 – Expressive Communication	Standard Score	68	62-74	October 2, 2025
PLS-5 – Total Language Score	Standard Score	71	66-76	October 2, 2025
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)	Standard Score	72	65-79	October 3, 2025
GFTA-3	Percentile	4th percentile	—	October 3, 2025
Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Test-4 (REEL-4), Spanish supplement	Age Equivalent	2;6–3;0	—	October 3, 2025

Articulation and Phonology

Single-word articulation testing in English revealed inconsistent production of word-final consonants and stopping of fricatives. Mateo produced /k/ correctly in word-initial position with min cues but substituted [t] for /k/ word-finally, saying "cat" as "cat" with the target "cat" reduced to "ca." In Spanish, he demonstrated difficulty with the tap /ɾ/, producing "pero" as "peo," consistent with typical developmental patterns but delayed relative to age expectations. During a home-language sample collected with his mother, Mateo was coded for mean length of utterance using SALT codes, including two instances of [EW] marking word-finding difficulty.

Language Sample

A 50-utterance language sample was collected in both languages during play with blocks and a toy kitchen. In English, Mateo's mean length of utterance was 1.8 morphemes, below the expected range for his age. In Spanish, his mean length of utterance was 2.1 morphemes. He used primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations such as "más agua" and "no quiero." He demonstrated limited use of grammatical morphemes in English, omitting plural -s and present progressive -ing consistently, while showing emerging use of Spanish gender agreement, correctly producing "la pelota" and "el perro" with 8/10 accuracy.

Teacher and Caregiver Input

Ms. Lopez, Mateo's classroom teacher at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, completed a classroom observation form noting that Mateo often watches peers rather than initiating interaction, and that he becomes frustrated when classmates such as Ava Thompson do not understand his gestures. His babysitter, Blanca Osorio, reported that he communicates more successfully at home with familiar routines but still relies heavily on pointing and single words. His father, Diego Hernández Morales, shared that extended family gatherings, including visits with cousins Emiliano Ruiz and Camila Ruiz, highlight the gap between Mateo's communication and that of same-age peers, saying, "se queda calladito mientras los otros hablan."

Impressions

Based on standardized testing, language sampling, and caregiver and teacher report, Mateo presents with a moderate expressive and receptive language delay affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a diagnosis of expressive-receptive language disorder (ICD-10 F80.2). His articulation skills are also delayed relative to age expectations in both languages, though patterns are consistent with typical bilingual development rather than a distinct articulation disorder. Given his NICU history, recurrent otitis media, and bilingual language exposure, his overall profile reflects a combination of biological risk factors and typical second-language acquisition patterns, though the magnitude of delay across both languages supports the need for continued intervention. Pragmatic skills, including initiation and turn-taking with peers, are emerging but remain below age expectations, contributing to social frustration observed both at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center and at home.

Recommendations

1. Continue weekly individual speech-language therapy through Western Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency, with continued use of Hanen and PROMPT strategies, transitioning gradually toward structured vocabulary expansion in both languages.
2. Incorporate bilingual language stimulation strategies at home, coached through parent training sessions with service coordinator Marcus Whitfield and SLP Rosa Fuentes, M.S., CCC-SLP.
3. Collaborate with Ms. Lopez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to implement visual supports and peer-mediated communication strategies within the Caterpillar classroom.
4. Repeat audiological monitoring annually at Carolina Hearing & ENT Associates given his history of recurrent otitis media.
5. Reassess IFSP outcomes at the next scheduled review on January 12, 2026, with updated standardized testing to track progress toward age-appropriate language skills in both Spanish and English.
6. Consider referral for a bilingual preschool language enrichment program, such as those supported through Smart Start of Catawba County, to supplement direct therapy services.

This evaluation and its recommendations were reviewed with the family in both Spanish and English during the feedback conference, with interpreter support provided by Gabriela Soto. Questions regarding this report may be directed to Rosa Fuentes, M.S., CCC-SLP at Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC, (828) 555-0193.

Report completed and signed electronically on October 6, 2025.

Rosa Fuentes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC

Centro de cuido: Centro de Cuido y Aprendizaje Arcoíris
Maestra principal: Maestra Ponce
Coordinadora de servicios: Daniela Ortiz Vásquez, Asociación de Coordinación de Servicios Tempranos del Piedmont (ACSTP)
Oficina CDSA asignada: Agencia de Servicios para el Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Brookhaven (CDSA de Brookhaven)
Pediatra: Dr. Andrés Villalobos

II. RAZÓN DE LA REMISIÓN

Mateo fue remitido para una reevaluación integral del habla y del lenguaje por su pediatra, el Dr. Villalobos, y por la coordinadora de servicios, Daniela Ortiz Vásquez, de ACSTP, como parte de la revisión anual de su Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP). Su madre, Blanca Paredes-Gómez, reporta que Mateo "habla como un bebé" para su edad y que frecuentemente es malentendido por adultos fuera de la familia. La última reunión de IFSP se realizó el 3 de marzo de 2026 en las oficinas de CDSA de Brookhaven; la presente evaluación informará la próxima reunión de revisión, programada para el 12 de noviembre de 2026.

III. HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO Y MÉDICA

Mateo nació a las 38 semanas de gestación por parto vaginal en el Centro Médico Regional de Brookhaven el 14 de agosto de 2022. Su peso al nacer fue de 3,200 gramos y sus puntuaciones de Apgar fueron 8 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. El embarazo fue descrito por la madre como "sin complicaciones", aunque reporta haber tenido hipertensión gestacional leve controlada sin medicamentos.

El historial médico es significativo por tres episodios de otitis media entre los 8 meses y los 2 años de edad, tratados con amoxicilina; no se colocaron tubos de ventilación. Un examen audiológico realizado el 6 de febrero de 2026 en el consultorio del Dr. Villalobos mostró audición dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos. No hay historial de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones prolongadas ni cirugías. Mateo alcanzó los hitos motores gruesos y finos dentro de rangos típicos (caminó a los 13 meses); los hitos de lenguaje se describen más adelante.

IV. HISTORIA FAMILIAR, SOCIAL Y DE EXPOSICIÓN A IDIOMAS

Mateo vive con sus padres, Blanca Paredes-Gómez y Esteban del Río, y sus dos hermanos mayores, Sol del Río Paredes (7 años) e Iker del Río Paredes (10 años), en una vivienda alquilada en Brookhaven. La abuela paterna, Rosario Londoño, vive con la familia y cuida a los niños varias tardes por semana mientras los padres trabajan.

La madre, Blanca Paredes-Gómez, sostiene dos empleos: durante el día trabaja en la caja del Supermercado La Cosecha, y por las noches limpia oficinas para una compañía de servicios que la familia conoce solo por sus siglas, RTS. El padre, Esteban del Río, trabaja a tiempo completo instalando techos para Techos y Construcciones Hermanos Ibarra. Debido a estos horarios, es frecuentemente la abuela Rosario quien lleva y recoge a Mateo del centro de cuido.

El idioma principal del hogar es el español; ambos padres y la abuela Rosario hablan español con Mateo casi exclusivamente. En el Centro de Cuido y Aprendizaje Arcoíris, Mateo está expuesto al inglés durante aproximadamente seis horas diarias desde los 18 meses de edad. Su maestra, Ponce, reporta que Mateo entiende instrucciones simples en inglés pero habla muy poco en ese idioma, prefiriendo señalar o usar gestos. Juega con regularidad con sus compañeros Emily y Josiah, aunque la maestra nota que estos niños a veces se frustran al no entenderlo.

Los padres describen a Mateo como "cariñoso pero terco" y reportan que en casa se comunica principalmente señalando, usando gestos y palabras sueltas en español, con un vocabulario estimado de menos de 50 palabras a los 3 años. No hay historial familiar reportado de trastornos del habla o del lenguaje en los hermanos; Sol y Iker tienen desarrollo típico según la madre.

V. PROCEDIMIENTOS Y RESULTADOS DE LA EVALUACIÓN

La evaluación se realizó en español, el idioma dominante del hogar, en dos sesiones el 23 de septiembre de 2026 y el 30 de septiembre de 2026, de 9:00 a.m. a 10:15 a.m. en la clínica. Se administraron los siguientes instrumentos estandarizados:

Prueba	Subprueba	Puntaje estándar	Percentil	Intervalo de confianza
PLS-5 Español	Comprensión auditiva	73	4	68-78
PLS-5 Español	Comunicación expresiva	71	3	65-77
GFTA-3 Bilingüe	Articulación	65	1	58-72
CELF Preescolar-2 Español	Estructura del lenguaje	70	2	64-76

En el PLS-5 Español, Mateo obtuvo un puntaje estándar de 73 en Comprensión auditiva (percentil 4) y de 71 en Comunicación expresiva (percentil 3), ambos en el rango deficiente. Logró identificar objetos y seguir instrucciones de dos pasos con 8/10 (80%) de precisión, pero tuvo dificultad marcada con conceptos relacionales y preguntas de "por qué".

En el GFTA-3 Bilingüe, su puntaje estándar de 65 (percentil 1) refleja un patrón consistente de errores fonológicos, incluyendo frontalización de sonidos velares (/k/ → [t]), simplificación de grupos consonánticos y omisión de consonantes finales. En el CELF Preescolar-2 Español, su desempeño en Estructura del lenguaje (puntaje estándar 70, percentil 2) mostró dificultad para formar oraciones de tres o más palabras y para usar marcadores verbales de tiempo.

VI. MUESTRA DE HABLA CONECTADA

Se obtuvo una muestra de habla espontánea de 50 enunciados durante juego dirigido. El objetivo fonético seleccionado para la evaluación fue la palabra "sol" (fonema inicial /s/); de forma coincidente, esta es también el nombre de la hermana de Mateo, Sol, quien estuvo presente en la segunda sesión. Al pedirle que nombrara la imagen del "sol", Mateo produjo [tol] en 7 de 10 intentos (70%), sustituyendo el fonema velar/sibilante por una oclusiva alveolar. Cuando se le preguntó por su hermana, señaló y dijo "Sol juega", demostrando que reconoce y usa el nombre correctamente en contexto referencial, aunque con la misma sustitución fonológica: "[tol] juega".

Con mod cues (modelado más indicación táctil), su precisión en la producción de /s/ inicial mejoró a 8/10 (80%). Se observó un patrón similar con otros objetivos: la palabra meta "casa" se produjo como [tata] en 3 de 5 intentos sin apoyo, mejorando a 4/5 con min cues. El análisis del proceso fonológico mostró frontalización en el 90% de las oportunidades y simplificación de grupos consonánticos en el 85% de las oportunidades, ambos por encima del rango esperado para su edad.

VII. IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Los hallazgos de esta evaluación, junto con el historial del desarrollo y los informes de los padres y la maestra, apoyan un diagnóstico de trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo con un trastorno fonológico concomitante (F80.2). El desempeño de Mateo en pruebas estandarizadas administradas en su idioma dominante, el español, cae consistentemente en el rango deficiente a muy deficiente en todas las áreas evaluadas, y sus patrones de error fonológico no son explicados por la exposición bilingüe normal, dado que persisten patrones atípicos (frontalización, omisión de finales) que superan lo esperado incluso para niños bilingües típicos de su edad.

La discrepancia entre la comprensión relativamente funcional del inglés a nivel social-conversacional, según reporta la maestra Ponce, y el desempeño deficiente en ambos idiomas en tareas estructuradas, sugiere un trastorno de base lingüística que afecta ambos sistemas lingüísticos, no simplemente una diferencia asociada al desarrollo bilingüe típico.

VIII. RECOMENDACIONES Y PLAN DE SERVICIOS

Se recomienda que Mateo continúe recibiendo terapia de habla y lenguaje individual a través del sistema de intervención temprana, con servicios bilingües en español e inglés cuando sea posible, y en español como idioma primario de instrucción dado que es el idioma dominante del hogar.

Servicio	Frecuencia	Duración	Proveedor	Código CPT
Terapia de habla y lenguaje individual	2x/semana	45 minutos	Mirta Elena Casares, CCC-SLP	92507
Evaluación de sonidos del habla (seguimiento)	1x	60 minutos	Mirta Elena Casares, CCC-SLP	92523

Los servicios se facturarán bajo el código 92507 (modificador GN) para las sesiones de intervención continua y 92523 para la próxima evaluación de seguimiento de sonidos del habla, programada para dentro de seis meses. Se recomienda continuar con un enfoque de ciclos fonológicos (Cycles) dirigido a los procesos de frontalización y simplificación de grupos consonánticos, junto con estrategias de expansión del lenguaje basadas en el modelo Hanen para apoyar el desarrollo sintáctico en el hogar.

Se recomienda además:

1. Continuar monitoreo audiológico anual dado el historial de otitis media recurrente.
2. Capacitar a la madre, Blanca Paredes-Gómez, y a la abuela, Rosario Londoño, en estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en el hogar, dada su disponibilidad limitada por los horarios laborales.
3. Coordinar con la maestra Ponce para reforzar vocabulario funcional en inglés dentro del aula del Centro de Cuido y Aprendizaje Arcoíris.
4. Reevaluar en un plazo de seis meses para medir progreso en comprensión y en producción fonológica, antes de la próxima reunión de IFSP programada para el 12 de noviembre de 2026.
5. Mantener comunicación activa con la coordinadora de servicios, Daniela Ortiz Vásquez, de ACSTP, y con CDSA de Brookhaven para asegurar la continuidad de los servicios bajo el IFSP vigente.

text:
CAROLINA BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
Comprehensive Speech-Language Evaluation / Evaluación Integral del Habla y Lenguaje

IDENTIFYING INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Pt. Name: José Alejandro Martínez Flores ("Pepe," también llamado "Pepito")
DOB: August 14, 2021   Age at eval: 4;2
Eval Date: October 2, 2026 and October 6, 2026   Report Date: October 11, 2026
Student ID #: RC-48217   Medicaid #: NC9284716K
Address: 1407 Juniper Branch Rd, Garnet Falls, NC 27529
Home Phone: (919) 555-0183   Cell (madre): (919) 555-0296
CG/Padre: Jesús Martínez Vega ("Chuy")
CG/Madre: Elena Flores Ramírez
Referral: Piedmont CDSA, service coordinator Teresa Núñez
School/District: Riverbend Elementary School, Pinecrest County Schools
Classroom Teacher: Ms. Dawson (Pre-K, afternoon session)
Clinician: Marisol Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (inglés/español)
Interpreter present 10/6 session: Ana Beltrán, certified medical interpreter
Clinic email: mcastillo@carolinabilingualspeech.com
Clinic website: www.carolinabilingualspeech.com

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE LA REFERENCIA

Pt. referred por Piedmont CDSA for re-evaluation prior to transition from Part C early intervention (previous IFSP Outcome 2, communication) to Part B preschool services at Riverbend Elementary School. CG reports concern re: pt's expressive language, intelligibility, y fluency of speech in both idiomas. Madre, Elena Flores Ramírez, states: "No le entendemos bien cuando está molesto, habla muy rápido y se le traban las palabras." Padre, Jesús Martínez Vega, added via interpreter that Pepe "gets frustrated when his sister Guadalupe doesn't understand him right away."

BACKGROUND / ANTECEDENTES

José (goes by Pepe at home, J.A. on some school paperwork) is a 4;2 y.o. male currently enrolled in Ms. Dawson's Pre-K classroom at Riverbend Elementary School, part of Pinecrest County Schools. He lives w/ both parents and older sister Guadalupe Martínez Flores (edad escolar, "Lupita" en casa) in Garnet Falls, Pinecrest County. Primary CGs during the day are the parents, with occasional help from paternal abuela, Rosa Ramírez, and a cousin, Juan "Juanito" Flores, who sometimes picks pt up after school. Family also reports a neighbor, Carmen, helps w/ babysitting on weekends b/c both parents' work schedules overlap approx 2x/week.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA PRENATAL Y PERINATAL

Madre reports pregnancy complicated by gestational hypertension; pt born 35 weeks gestation via emergency C-section at Carolina Pines Medical Center on August 14, 2021. Apgar scores 6 at 1 min and 8 at 5 min. Birth weight 4 lbs 11 oz. Pt admitted to Carolina Pines Medical Center NICU x 11 days for respiratory support and feeding difficulty; attending neonatologist was Dr. Adwoa Osei. Pediatrician of record since discharge is Dr. Farrukh Hassan at a clinic in Garnet Falls. Pt followed by ENT, Dr. Whitfield, for recurrent otitis media (approx 6 episodes between 8 months and 2;6); bilateral PE tubes placed March 3, 2023, removed February 19, 2025. No reported seizure history. Vision screened WNL per Dr. Hassan's last well-check. No current meds. Family denies hx of genetic syndrome; no other developmental dx on file except speech-language delay flagged at 18-month well-check.

FAMILY, LANGUAGE, AND WORK HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR, DE IDIOMA Y LABORAL

Home language mix is Spanish-dominant w/ increasing English exposure since pt started Pre-K. Madre, Elena Flores Ramírez, speaks primarily Spanish to pt; padre, Jesús Martínez Vega, code-switches depending on context. Sister Lupita speaks mostly English at home now, which CG reports sometimes frustrates pt b/c he wants her to respond en español. CGs estimate pt's input is approx 70% Spanish / 30% English at home, roughly reversed at school.

Work history es relevante para entender la disponibilidad de los padres para terapia y para "quién cuida a los niños." Padre, Chuy, trabajó antes en la fábrica de pollo Sanderson (processing plant, turno de noche) por approx 3 años; actualmente trabaja para la compañía de construcción Falcon (also written: he is employed by Falcon Construction Company) haciendo trabajo de techado y acabados, horario variable, a veces 6 días/semana. Madre, Elena, ha tenido varios trabajos: primero en la tienda El Mercado Latino (store, cajera), luego en el restaurante La Hacienda (waitress/server), con temporadas de verano trabajando en la finca Whitaker Farms (farm, cosecha de tomate) cuando Pepe era bebé. Currently madre works nights w/ un servicio de limpieza, Sparkle Clean Cleaning Service, cleaning offices in Garnet Falls and Millbrook. Both parents report their combined schedule makes it difícil attend daytime appts; most sessions have been scheduled late afternoon or Saturdays.

EDUCATIONAL AND SOCIAL HISTORY / HISTORIA EDUCATIVA Y SOCIAL

Pt attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Center from approx 18 months to 3;0, then transitioned into the Pinecrest County Schools Pre-K program at Riverbend Elementary School under Ms. Dawson. Teaching assistant in the room, Mr. Ortiz, also bilingual, reports pt is "social, le gusta jugar, pero cuando se frustra habla muy rápido y nadie le entiende." Classroom observation (9:15 a.m. to 9:50 a.m. on October 2, 2026) noted pt initiating play w/ peers Ava and Marcus during centers; pt used gestures + short phrases to request materials ("more block," "quiero eso"). One peer, Ava, was observed repeating pt's utterances back incorrectly, suggesting limited peer intelligibility outside home.

School SLP consult note from Ms. Keene (school-based SLP) indicates pt was flagged during universal screening September 15, 2026 for unintelligible speech and short utterance length relative to peers.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

Eval conducted across 2 sessions (approx 90 min total) in a combo of English y español, per family preference and clinician's bilingual proficiency. Interpreter Ana Beltrán present session 2 to confirm accuracy of Spanish-language scoring decisions and to support CG interview. Procedures included caregiver interview, standardized testing (admin bilingually where normed, English-only where required), speech sample analysis, oral mech exam, and classroom observation.

Tests Administered:
- Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Phonology subtests
- Test of Narrative Language-2 (TNL-2) (informal, English)
- Speech and language sample, approx 150 utterances, analyzed w/ SALT; relevant codes incl. [EW] and [RP]
- Oral-peripheral exam

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Pt separated easily from CG, engaged readily w/ clinician and interpreter. Attention mod-to-good w/ structured tasks; required occasional redirection during unstructured play. Intelligibility in connected speech estimated at approx 60% in known context, dropping to approx 35-40% in unknown context, per both English and Spanish samples. Pt frequently self-corrected w/ mod cues when a word wasn't understood ("otra vez, otra vez") and would attempt gestural backup when verbal repair failed.

TEST RESULTS

PLS-5 (English edition):
Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 76 (CI 70-82), 5th percentile, age equiv. 2;9-3;1
Expressive Communication: Standard Score 71 (CI 65-77), 3rd percentile, age equiv. 2;6-2;11
Total Language Score: 72 (CI 67-77), 3rd percentile

PLS-5 (Spanish edition, administered by clinician, native-fluent):
Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 82, 12th percentile
Expressive Communication: Standard Score 78, 7th percentile
Total Language Score: 79, 8th percentile

BESA Morphosyntax Index: 81 (below average range for bilingual peers)
BESA Phonology composite: 74

GFTA-3: Standard Score 68, 2nd percentile. Errors noted across both languages incl. stopping of fricatives, cluster reduction, and gliding of liquids. Examples: target "casa" produced as "tasa"; target "plato" produced as "pato"; target "spoon" produced [pu:n]; target /r/ in Spanish inconsistently produced as /ɾ/ vs tap omitted entirely.

Summary Score Table (abbreviated):

| Measure | Domain | SS/Percentile |
|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 (EN) | Total Language | 72 / 3rd |
| PLS-5 (ES) | Total Language | 79 / 8th |
| GFTA-3 | Articulation | 68 / 2nd |
| BESA | Morphosyntax | 81 / below avg |
| BESA | Phonology | 74 / below avg |

ORAL-PERIPHERAL EXAM

WNL structurally; no overt oral-motor weakness noted. Slightly reduced DDK rate on multisyllabic sequences (approx 2 reps/sec on "pataka," below age expectation). No nasal emission observed. Dentition mixed, no notable malocclusion impacting speech.

LANGUAGE SAMPLE ANALYSIS

MLU in Spanish sample: 3.1 morphemes. MLU in English sample: 2.8 morphemes. Both below expected range for 4;2. Pt used primarily SVO constructions, limited use of subordinate clauses, frequent omission of articles in English ("want ball" instead of "I want the ball") and occasional gender agreement errors in Spanish ("el casa" for "la casa"). Narrative retell task (TNL-2, informal) showed pt could sequence 2-3 events w/ mod cues but struggled w/ causal connectors ("porque," "because"). Pt quoted spontaneously during play: "el perro come" and "more juice please" — both age-appropriate semantically but reduced in grammatical complexity.

FLUENCY

CG report and clinician observation both note occasional rapid, "trabado" speech pattern during excitement, w/ sound/syllable repetitions (approx 3-5% of syllables in connected speech during high-arousal play). This appears tied to word-finding struggle rather than a primary stuttering dx at this time; recommend monitoring, not formal fluency dx. No secondary behaviors (no tension, no eye blinking) observed.

IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Pepe presents w/ a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10: F80.2), evident across both his languages, consistent w/ a primary language impairment rather than a language difference attributable solely to bilingual exposure. Speech sound disorder (ICD-10: F80.0) also present, impacting intelligibility in both English and Spanish w/ similar error patterns across languages, supporting a true phonological disorder rather than typical bilingual phonological variation. Concomitant mild dysfluency features noted but do not currently meet criteria for a primary fluency disorder; recommend re-screen in 6 months.

Given bilingual presentation in both languages at comparably depressed levels, this pattern supports a language disorder construct rather than a language-difference/second-language-acquisition explanation. Family's language model is rich and appropriate; no evidence that reduced input or recent language exposure accounts for the magnitude of delay observed.

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES

1. Pt qualifies for and is recommended for individual speech-language therapy services, 2x/week, 30 min sessions, bilingual provider preferred given home language dominance.
2. Recommend continuation of services in both English and Spanish rather than English-only, to support home-school language continuity and avoid loss of Spanish as pt's dominant home language.
3. Therapy approach to incorporate Cycles phonological approach for speech sound errors, and Hanen-based strategies for CG coaching to support expressive language at home. PROMPT techniques may be considered as adjunct given motor-based articulation patterns observed.
4. Recommend coordination between Riverbend Elementary School SLP (Ms. Keene) and classroom teacher Ms. Dawson to support classroom-based language modeling and peer communication strategies, including structured peer pairing (e.g., with classmate Marcus, who has shown patience w/ pt's communication attempts).
5. CG training recommended re: expansion strategies, bilingual input strategies, and reducing rate of adult speech during high-demand communication moments to model slower rate for pt.
6. Recommend hearing re-screen given hx of chronic otitis media; refer back to Dr. Whitfield if any concern for recurrence.
7. Re-evaluate in approx 12 months or per Pinecrest County Schools IEP timeline, whichever is sooner, to monitor fluency pattern and continued progress across both languages.
8. Family may contact clinic at mcastillo@carolinabilingualspeech.com or visit www.carolinabilingualspeech.com for scheduling, bilingual handouts, and CG coaching resources.

Billing codes this visit: CPT 92523 (speech sound production w/ evaluation of language comprehension and expression), CPT 92521 (fluency eval, screening only, not billed as primary dx).

Case coordination note sent to Piedmont CDSA service coordinator Teresa Núñez for transition planning to Part B services at Riverbend Elementary School; copy also routed to pediatrician Dr. Hassan's office per release signed by Elena Flores Ramírez on October 2, 2026.

Report prepared and reviewed by Marisol Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual clinician, Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC. Interpreter services for CG interview provided by Ana Beltrán, certified medical interpreter. Questions re: this report may be directed to Marisol Castillo at mcastillo@carolinabilingualspeech.com or (919) 555-0410.

REASON FOR REVIEW
This annual IFSP review was conducted for Mateo, a 2;6-year-old Spanish/English bilingual toddler enrolled in the Piedmont Foothills CDSA under the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program. The meeting was held at the family's home at 418 Willowbend Court in Hickory, Catawba County. Service coordinator Patricia Nguyen attended in person, and interpreter Marisol Delgado joined by phone to support communication with Mateo's mother, Lucía Ramírez. Clinician Hannah Okafor presented assessment findings and proposed outcomes for the coming year.

PARTICIPANTS PRESENT
Lucía Ramírez (mother), Carlos Fernández (father, joined by speakerphone from work), Patricia Nguyen (service coordinator), Hannah Okafor (speech-language pathologist), Marisol Delgado (interpreter), and Rosa Ramírez (maternal grandmother and regular caregiver, attending to support the family and provide routine information).

FAMILY BACKGROUND
Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Ramírez; his father, Carlos Fernández; and his older sister, Sol, age 5. The family also relies on regular support from Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Ramírez, who provides childcare two afternoons a week while Lucía Ramírez prepares for her shift. Mom works nights at Catawba Valley Medical Center as a certified nursing assistant, and Dad works days installing cabinetry for Foothills Custom Woodworks. The family's dog, Canela, is frequently referenced by Mateo during play-based sessions and appears to motivate spontaneous vocalization. The household is warm and supportive, with extended family nearby who regularly interact with Mateo in both languages.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES
In the family's own words, shared through interpreter Marisol Delgado: "Queremos que Mateo pueda decir lo que necesita sin frustrarse. En la guardería lo entienden poco porque mezcla español e inglés, y en casa a veces solo yo lo entiendo," said Lucía Ramírez. She added, "Su hermana Sol habla por él, y no quiero que se acostumbre a eso." Carlos Fernández shared a similar concern by phone: "I want him to talk to his cousins without getting upset when they don't understand him."

The family's top priorities, as agreed at the meeting, are: (1) increasing Mateo's intelligibility in both languages so that extended family and daycare staff can understand him without Sol interpreting; (2) decreasing frustration-related tantrums when he is not understood; and (3) building home routines that support bilingual language growth without pressuring Mateo to favor one language over the other. The family also expressed interest in strategies they can use consistently between Lucía Ramírez's nursing shifts and Rosa Ramírez's caregiving hours.

DAILY ROUTINES
Mateo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with his father before Carlos Fernández leaves for work. He attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, where classroom teacher Brenda Collier reports he engages well in gross motor play but frequently relies on gesture and pointing to request items from peers and staff. Rosa Ramírez picks him up most afternoons and supervises homework time for Sol alongside free play for Mateo. In the evenings, Lucía Ramírez prepares dinner while Sol watches Mateo during independent play before leaving for her overnight shift; bath and bedtime routines begin around 7:30 p.m., with books read in both Spanish and English. On weekends, the family often visits Rosa Ramírez's home nearby, where cousins Diego and Valentina play with Mateo in a mixed-language environment that the family reports he enjoys but sometimes finds overwhelming.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED
The family currently receives nutritional support through WIC and has been referred to Smart Start of Catawba County for a developmental playgroup to increase peer exposure. Lucía Ramírez reported an open case with Catawba County DSS related to a pending housing assistance application, unrelated to Mateo's early intervention services but noted here for coordination purposes. Primary medical care is provided by Dr. Angela Weiss at Catawba Valley Pediatrics, who referred the family for evaluation after noting significant expressive language delay at the 24-month well-child visit.

DEVELOPMENTAL STATUS / ASSESSMENT SUMMARY
Direct assessment was completed using the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), administered bilingually with items credited in either language per examiner's manual guidelines. Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 79 (8th percentile), falling within the 73-83 confidence interval, and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), within the 65-77 confidence interval. Age-equivalent scores placed receptive skills at 20 months and expressive skills within the 16-18 month range, against a chronological age of 2;6. A supplemental nonverbal cognitive screening yielded an age equivalent within 2;6–3;0, consistent with age-level nonverbal reasoning and contrasting with the more significant expressive delay. Parent report using the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories estimated an expressive vocabulary of approximately 45 words across both languages combined. Oral-motor examination was within normal limits, and hearing screening passed bilaterally on August 14, 2026.

Phonetic inventory in Spanish included /p/, /m/, /n/, and /a/, with inconsistent production of /s/ and /t/ in word-initial position. During structured play, Mateo was stimulable for the target word "sol" with moderate cues, producing an approximation transcribed as [ʔo] in 2 of 10 trials and improving to 6 of 10 trials following tactile cueing modeled on PROMPT principles. This target was chosen for its phonetic simplicity and everyday functional relevance, distinct from the name of his sister, Sol; the family confirmed during the session that the word was understood as referring to the sun, not to Sol herself.

PRESENT LEVELS OF FUNCTIONING
Mateo communicates primarily through gesture, single-word approximations, and vocalizations. He follows simple one-step directions in context (8 of 10 trials) but struggles with directions outside routine context (3 of 10 trials). He imitates two- to three-word phrases inconsistently and shows emerging turn-taking skills during structured play. Social engagement with Diego and Valentina is positive, though Mateo becomes frustrated and occasionally drops to the floor or hits when peers or adults misunderstand his requests. Classroom observation by Brenda Collier corroborates these patterns, noting improved engagement when visual supports are available.

OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES
Outcome 1: Mateo will increase expressive vocabulary to 75 words across English and Spanish combined, as measured by parent log and direct observation, within six months. Strategies include modeling and expansion techniques drawn from Hanen's It Takes Two to Talk program, which Lucía Ramírez and Rosa Ramírez will practice during daily routines with coaching from Hannah Okafor every two weeks.

Outcome 2: Mateo will combine two words to request preferred items in at least 8 of 10 opportunities across settings. Strategies include a core vocabulary board supplemented by PECS-based exchange for daycare transitions, with visual supports introduced at home and shared with Brenda Collier for classroom consistency.

Outcome 3: Mateo will reduce frustration behaviors, including hitting and dropping to the floor, to no more than 2 episodes per session by increasing functional communication attempts. The team will track phonological progress using the Cycles approach alongside behavior charts shared between home and Little Sprouts Early Learning Center.

Outcome 4: Lucía Ramírez and Carlos Fernández will report increased confidence supporting bilingual language development, as measured by a parent confidence survey administered at each review. Service coordinator Patricia Nguyen will provide a Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol home-practice guide translated into Spanish and will follow up on the Smart Start of Catawba County playgroup referral by October 15, 2026.

TRANSITION PLANNING
Because Mateo will turn three in April 2027, the team briefly discussed transition planning. Patricia Nguyen will initiate the required referral to the local school district's preschool exceptional children's program no later than January 12, 2027, and a transition conference will be scheduled closer to Mateo's third birthday. The family was informed that services under this IFSP continue uninterrupted until that process concludes.

SERVICE DELIVERY
Speech-language therapy will continue twice weekly for 30-minute sessions in the home setting, provided by Hannah Okafor through Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners under CPT code 92526, authorized through Piedmont Foothills CDSA. Developmental therapy continues biweekly through a separately contracted provider. Service coordination visits occur quarterly, with the next scheduled for December 10, 2026. For general program information, the family was directed to www.ncei.org.

SIGNATURES AND CONSENT
This IFSP review was completed and discussed with the family on September 22, 2026. Lucía Ramírez and Carlos Fernández consented verbally to continued services, with written consent to follow by mail. The next annual review is scheduled for March 22, 2027, with an interim six-month check-in scheduled for March 20, 2027. Questions may be directed to Patricia Nguyen at the Piedmont Foothills CDSA office, or to clinician Hannah Okafor at hokafor@carolinapedstherapy.com.

Bridges Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
412 Owen Drive, Suite 220, Fayetteville, NC 28304
Tel: (910) 555-2847 · Fax: (910) 555-2848 · intake@bridgespeds-slp.com

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Date of Evaluation: September 8, 2026
Date of Report: September 15, 2026

Child/Niño: Mateo Hernández Cruz ("Mateo")
Date of Birth: July 3, 2022
Chronological Age: 4;2
Medicaid ID: 784215963B
Record No.: SLP-2026-00417

Parents/Padres: Lucía Rodríguez (madre), Carlos Hernández (padre)
Home Address: 118 Camden Road, Spring Lake, Cumberland County, NC 28390
Contact: (910) 555-3391 · lucia.rodriguez82@fakemail.com

Interpreter: Yolanda Pacheco, certified medical interpreter, present for the full session.
Clinician: Jennifer Alvarez-Pratt, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish) speech-language pathologist, Bridges Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Referral Source: Dr. Priya Nair, Carolina Pines Pediatric Associates

RAZÓN DE REFERRAL / REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred by su pediatra, Dr. Priya Nair of Carolina Pines Pediatric Associates, for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation due to concern about limited expressive vocabulary and reduced speech intelligibility in both English and Spanish. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez, reported, "Mateo entiende todo, pero cuando habla, solo yo y su papá le entendemos más o menos." His father, Carlos Hernández, added that strangers "really can't understand him at all, even when he tries in English."

ANTECEDENTES DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICOS / BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 32 weeks gestational age at Carolina Pines Regional Medical Center, Fayetteville Campus on July 3, 2022, weighing 3 lbs, 9 oz at birth. Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. He spent 19 days in the Level III NICU at Carolina Pines Regional Medical Center for respiratory distress and feeding support, per mother's report and the discharge summary she brought to this visit.

Mateo failed his newborn hearing screening bilaterally and was referred for diagnostic audiology at Sandhills Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology, where repeat testing at 4 months adjusted age showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. He has since had recurrent otitis media, with fluctuating mild conductive loss documented on tympanometry; bilateral pressure-equalization tubes were placed on March 12, 2024 by Dr. Samuel Okafor, ENT, at Sandhills Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology. No ear infections or drainage have been reported since tube placement. A recheck is scheduled for November 4, 2026.

Mateo receives occupational therapy with Brianna Walsh, OTR/L, and physical therapy with Michael Chen, PT, DPT, both through early intervention coordinated by Sandhills CDSA. His service coordinator is Denise Fowler. Current IFSP goals include fine motor planning (IFSP Outcome 2) and gross motor coordination (IFSP Outcome 3); the most recent IFSP review was held on June 2, 2026.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The family's home language is Spanish. Lucía Rodríguez reported, "en casa hablamos puro español, pero cuando llega del daycare empieza a mezclar inglés." English exposure comes primarily through Sunshine Bilingual Daycare in Spring Lake, NC, which Mateo has attended since January 2025, and through his older sister, Luz Hernández Cruz, age 7, who is in second grade and speaks both languages fluently. Luz often translates for her brother at home, telling her mother, "Mateo quiere jugo, no leche," when his requests are unclear to others.

Lucía Rodríguez works at Sandhills Produce Distributors and Carlos Hernández works in roofing for Cape Fear Roofing & Construction. The family reports strong support from Mateo's maternal grandmother, Marisol Cruz, who provides childcare two days a week and speaks only Spanish with him. Mateo's daycare teacher, Ms. Angela Ferris, reports he plays well with peers, including his frequent playmate Dylan Boyd, but that other children "sometimes just stop trying" to understand him and play alongside him instead of with him.

SESSION SCHEDULE / HORARIO DE SESIONES

| Day | Start | Stop | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Bridges Pediatric, Fayetteville office |
| Wednesday | 2:30 PM | 3:15 PM | Sunshine Bilingual Daycare classroom |
| Friday | 10:15 AM | 11:00 AM | Home visit, Spring Lake, NC |

Sessions were co-treated once monthly with Brianna Walsh, OTR/L, to address joint attention and feeding-related oral motor goals.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

Testing was conducted in a combination of English and Spanish with Yolanda Pacheco interpreting for parent interview and family-directed caregiver report measures. Standardized tools administered included the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions; the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3); and the Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Phonology subtests. Informal measures included a parent-report inventory, language sample analysis coded with SALT, and structured play-based observation.

RESULTADOS / TEST RESULTS

| Measure | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 5th | 68–84 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 71 | 3rd | 63–79 |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | 72 | 3rd | 65–79 |
| GFTA-3 Standard Score | 65 | 1st | 58–72 |
| BESA Morphosyntax | 70 | 2nd | 61–79 |

Age-equivalent range on the PLS-5 Expressive Communication subtest fell between 2;6–3;0, and GFTA-3 performance corresponded to an age equivalent of 2;9–3;3.

On conversational language sample analysis, Mateo produced mean length of utterance of 2.8 morphemes, below expectations for his chronological age. Errors coded [EW] (error word) occurred on 34% of multiword utterances, most consistent with morphological omissions in both languages (e.g., omission of plural -s, article drop in Spanish).

Articulation testing revealed a moderate phonological disorder affecting both languages. Mateo demonstrated fronting of velars (target /k/ produced as [t]), final consonant deletion, and gliding of liquids, substituting [w] for /ɾ/ in Spanish words such as "pe[w]o" for "pe/ɾ/o" (perro). Speech was approximately 30% intelligible to unfamiliar listeners in connected speech, improving to 65% with context and mod cues. When asked to name a picture of a dog, he said "guau-guau" rather than attempting the target word, and on a structured imitation task he produced "tato" for the target "carro" with max cues.

Receptive vocabulary and following of two-step directions in both languages fell within the low range but were relatively stronger than expressive skills, consistent with a mixed receptive-expressive presentation weighted toward expressive deficits.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS / CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Mateo presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and a moderate phonological disorder affecting both English and Spanish, consistent with a true bilingual language impairment rather than typical second-language acquisition patterns; errors were present and comparable across both languages rather than confined to the non-dominant language, which rules out typical bilingual variation as the sole explanation. His history of prematurity, NICU stay, and recurrent otitis media are relevant contributing factors but do not fully account for the magnitude of delay observed.

Jennifer Alvarez-Pratt, M.S., CCC-SLP, diagnostic impressions:
- F80.2 Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder
- F80.0 Phonological disorder
- H90.3 Sensorineural hearing loss, bilateral, resolved (history, per audiology record)

RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for continued speech-language intervention under his IFSP. Recommend individual bilingual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 45-minute sessions, targeting expressive morphosyntax, phonological patterns, and functional vocabulary in both languages.
2. Continue co-treatment with occupational therapy (Brianna Walsh) monthly to support joint attention during structured tasks.
3. Incorporate Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies for caregiver coaching with Lucía Rodríguez and Carlos Hernández, and PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing to target motor placement for fronted and glided sounds.
4. Continue audiology monitoring given history of recurrent otitis media; recheck scheduled November 4, 2026 at Sandhills Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology.
5. Share strategies with Ms. Angela Ferris at Sunshine Bilingual Daycare to support peer interaction and reduce reliance on gestural communication with classmates such as Dylan Boyd.
6. Reassess in six months or at next IFSP review, whichever is sooner, to monitor progress toward IFSP Outcome 2 and consider adding a communication-specific outcome.
7. Billing: services coded under CPT 92523 (speech sound and language evaluation) for today's visit; ongoing treatment to be billed under CPT 92507.

This evaluation was conducted with interpreter support from Yolanda Pacheco to ensure full parental participation. Results were shared verbally with Lucía Rodríguez and Carlos Hernández at the conclusion of testing, and a written summary will be forwarded to Dr. Priya Nair and Sandhills CDSA with signed parental consent.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Alvarez-Pratt, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Bridges Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC

INFORME DE REVISIÓN DEL PLAN INDIVIDUALIZADO DE SERVICIOS PARA LA FAMILIA (IFSP)
CDSA del Triángulo, Programa de Infantes y Niños Pequeños de Carolina del Norte

Fecha de la reunión de revisión: 2 de octubre de 2026
Hora de inicio: 9:30 a.m.
Lugar: oficina de CDSA del Triángulo, Durham, Carolina del Norte

Niño: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez
Fecha de nacimiento: 3 de marzo de 2023 (edad actual 3;7)
Número de expediente: NC-IFSP-048213
Número de Medicaid: 9087654321A
Dirección: 142 Maple Creek Lane, Durham, Carolina del Norte, 27703, Condado de Durham

Padres/tutores: Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paz (madre) y Jorge Luis Flores Mendoza (padre)
Hermanos en el hogar: Sol Flores Rodríguez (7 años) y Diego Flores Rodríguez (10 años)
Otros miembros del hogar: la abuela materna, Carmen Paz, quien cuida a Mateo las tardes que sus padres trabajan

Coordinadora de servicios: María Fernanda Ortiz, CDSA del Triángulo
Teléfono de la coordinadora: (919) 555-0137
Correo electrónico de la coordinadora: maria.ortiz@cdsatriangulo.example.org

Terapeuta del habla y lenguaje que redacta este informe: Mariana Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Terapias Integrales Carolina, PLLC
Sitio web de la práctica: www.terapiascarolina-slp.com

I. HISTORIA Y ANTECEDENTES

Mateo nació prematuro, a las 32 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 1,580 gramos y un puntaje de Apgar de 6 al minuto y 8 a los cinco minutos. Pasó 19 días en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales del Blue Ridge Health – Children's Hospital, Mountainview Campus, donde recibió apoyo respiratorio y alimentación por sonda durante la primera semana. Después del alta, fue seguido de cerca por su pediatra, la Dra. Andrea Solís, en la Clínica Pediátrica Blue Ridge Health, Mountainview Campus, quien a los dieciocho meses refirió a la familia al CDSA del Triángulo debido a un retraso notable en el lenguaje expresivo y el balbuceo limitado.

Por historial de otitis media recurrente, Mateo fue evaluado en el Carolina Hearing & Balance Center, Hillsborough Campus mediante timpanometría y audiometría conductual. Los resultados mostraron audición dentro de límites normales bilateralmente (0-20 dB en todas las frecuencias probadas), aunque se recomendó vigilancia continua dado el patrón de infecciones del oído medio. Se colocaron tubos de ventilación en ambos oídos en enero de 2025.

Mateo asiste de lunes a viernes al centro preescolar El Jardín de las Luciérnagas, donde su maestra, Patricia Gómez, reporta que interactúa con sus compañeros Emmanuel y Valentina durante el juego libre, principalmente mediante gestos y sonidos, con lenguaje verbal limitado comparado con sus compañeros de la misma edad.

II. PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (en sus propias palabras)

La madre, Lucía, compartió: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Mateo no nos dice lo que quiere, solo señala o llora. Queremos que pueda pedir las cosas con palabras antes de empezar el kínder."

El padre, Jorge, agregó: "A veces en la casa su hermana Sol le entiende mejor que nosotros. Él tiene su propio modo de hablar y solo ella lo descifra. Nos gustaría que nosotros también pudiéramos entenderle sin necesitar traductora."

La abuela, Carmen, añadió durante la reunión: "Cuando lo cuido en las tardes, él se frustra mucho si no entiendo lo que quiere. A veces llora hasta que llega su mamá."

La familia también expresó preocupación por la transición a servicios escolares cuando Mateo cumpla tres años, y por continuar recibiendo apoyo en español, ya que es el idioma principal del hogar y el único idioma que se habla en casa con los abuelos.

III. RUTINAS DIARIAS DE LA FAMILIA

Lucía trabaja medio tiempo limpiando habitaciones en el Hotel Sierra Vista, y Jorge trabaja en construcción con Techos y Estructuras del Triángulo. Entre semana, Mateo se despierta a las 6:45 a.m., desayuna con sus hermanos Sol y Diego, y la abuela Carmen lo lleva al El Jardín de las Luciérnagas a las 8:00 a.m.. Durante el almuerzo, usa principalmente las manos y señala las imágenes de comida en un tablero de comunicación que la maestra Patricia Gómez preparó.

Por las tardes, después de recogerlo a las 4:30 p.m., la familia juega en el patio con la perra de la familia, Nube, antes de la cena. El baño es a las 7:00 p.m. y durante esa rutina Mateo suele producir aproximaciones de palabras como "agua" cuando quiere que le echen más agua tibia. Se duerme hacia las 8:30 p.m. después de que su hermana Sol le lee un cuento corto.

Los fines de semana, una vecina, Rosa Delgado, a veces les da transporte a las citas médicas cuando el carro de la familia no funciona. La familia también visita el parque del vecindario, donde Mateo observa a otros niños jugar pero rara vez se integra sin que un adulto lo acompañe.

IV. AGENCIAS Y PROVEEDORES INVOLUCRADOS

Además del CDSA del Triángulo, la familia recibe beneficios de WIC del Condado de Durham y participa en el programa Smart Start del Condado de Durham, que les proporcionó materiales de lectura bilingüe. El Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Durham ayuda con la solicitud y renovación de Medicaid. El equipo de intervención temprana incluye a la terapeuta física Laura Jiménez y al terapeuta ocupacional Kevin Nguyen, ambos de Terapias Integrales Carolina, PLLC.

Para contactar a la familia: teléfono de la casa (919) 555-0137, celular de la madre 919-555-0198, celular de la abuela (919) 555.0245. El padre tiene familia en Honduras y comparte el número de contacto de emergencia de su hermano, +504 9988-7766, para casos en los que la familia viaje durante el verano. También puede escribirse a la familia al correo lucia.flores84@example.com. La línea general del CDSA del Triángulo es 1-800-555-0199.

V. RESUMEN DE EVALUACIÓN Y NIVELES ACTUALES

La evaluación más reciente, realizada el 15 de abril de 2026, utilizó las Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), versión en español. Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 68 (percentil 2) en Comunicación Expresiva y una puntuación estándar de 79 (percentil 8) en Comunicación Auditiva, con un intervalo de confianza de 73-83. Su edad equivalente en comunicación expresiva fue 18 meses, comparada con su edad cronológica de 3;7.

En el inventario de sonidos, Mateo omite consonantes finales y sustituye /r/ por [w]; por ejemplo, produce "uela" en lugar de "rueda". Durante las sesiones de articulación, practica la palabra meta "sol" junto con "silla" y "sapo" para trabajar el fonema /s/ en posición inicial; es importante notar que esto coincide con el nombre de su hermana, Sol, lo cual a veces causa confusión cuando la familia practica en casa y Mateo mira hacia ella en lugar de repetir la palabra. Produjo "sol" con claves mínimas en 4 de 5 intentos durante la última sesión, mejora notable comparada con 1 de 5 hace tres meses.
