text:
PIEDMONT CROSSING HEALTH SYSTEM — HICKORY CAMPUS
Piedmont Crossing Health System — Hickory Campus is referred to throughout this report simply as the health system campus.
Pediatric Rehabilitation Services • Speech-Language Pathology
Comprehensive Bilingual Speech-Language Evaluation

IDENTIFYING INFORMATION

Child's Name: Mateo Hernández-Soto ("Teo")
Date of Birth: April 8, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;6
Primary Home Language: Spanish
Secondary Language: English
Dates of Evaluation: October 2, 2025 and October 6, 2025
Date of Report: October 9, 2025
Mother: Lucía Rodríguez Soto
Father: Andrés Hernández Vega
Sibling: Camila Hernández Soto, age 7
Examiner: M.R. Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Interpreter: J. Ortiz, Spanish-English Medical Interpreter
Referring Physician: Dr. Priya Shah, Foothills Pediatric Partners
Service Coordinator: Denise Faulk, Catawba County Children's Developmental Services Agency
Medicaid ID: 704582913B
Case/Referral ID: CDSA-22841
Address on File: 1148 Startown Road, Hickory, NC 28602

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo is a 4;6-year-old bilingual (Spanish-English) boy who was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by his pediatrician, Dr. Priya Shah of Foothills Pediatric Partners, following parent and teacher concern about limited intelligibility, reduced expressive vocabulary in both languages, and difficulty following multi-step directions in the classroom. Mateo currently attends Sunshine Bilingual Daycare and Preschool four days per week, where his lead teacher, Ms. Karen Pruitt, reports that he is often quiet during circle time, relies heavily on gesture and pointing, and has been observed to withdraw from group activities when he cannot make himself understood. A classmate, Dylan, frequently repeats Mateo's requests aloud so that other children can understand him, and another classmate, Ava, has started imitating some of his sound substitutions, which concerns Ms. Karen Pruitt.

Mateo was previously enrolled in Early Intervention services through Catawba County Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA) from June 2022 through April 2024, under IFSP Outcome 2, and was discharged at age 3 with continued mild expressive language delay noted at the time of discharge. This evaluation was requested to update eligibility documentation for continued services and to determine whether Mateo qualifies for speech-language therapy through the Exceptional Children's program at Sunshine Bilingual Daycare and Preschool and/or through outpatient services at Piedmont Crossing Health System — Hickory Campus. Parents report that their primary goals are for Mateo to be understood by unfamiliar listeners and to be ready for kindergarten entry in fall 2026.

BACKGROUND AND RECORD REVIEW

Records reviewed prior to this evaluation included CDSA Early Intervention evaluation and IFSP documents dated July 2022 through April 2024; a hearing screening report from Carolina Ear, Nose and Throat and Audiology Associates, Lenoir Office dated September 18, 2025; and a daycare progress note authored by Ms. Karen Pruitt dated September 22, 2025. No prior speech-language evaluation reports from an outpatient setting were available for review, as Mateo's only previous assessments occurred through Early Intervention.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 36 weeks gestational age via emergency cesarean section at Catawba Valley Medical Center in Hickory, NC, weighing 4 lb 11 oz (2,126 grams) at birth. Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. He required a 9-day stay in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Catawba Valley Medical Center for respiratory support and phototherapy for jaundice, and was discharged home in stable condition. Mother, Lucía Rodríguez Soto, reports an otherwise uncomplicated pregnancy until the onset of preterm labor at 35 weeks, with no reported substance use, infections, or gestational diabetes.

Following NICU discharge, Mateo was followed for prematurity-related monitoring by Dr. Priya Shah at Foothills Pediatric Partners through early childhood, with developmental milestones for gross motor and fine motor skills reported as age-appropriate. Parents report a significant choking episode at 14 months of age requiring an emergency room visit to Catawba Valley Medical Center, after which Mateo underwent a modified barium swallow study that was within normal limits, and no feeding therapy was recommended at that time.

Mateo has a history of recurrent otitis media, with bilateral myringotomy tube placement at 18 months performed by Dr. Grace Alford at Carolina Ear, Nose and Throat and Audiology Associates, Lenoir Office. The tubes extruded naturally by age 3, and he has had no further ear infections requiring intervention since that time. Most recent audiological evaluation at the same practice on September 18, 2025 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally, with normal tympanometry and no middle ear effusion noted at that visit. Mateo's current medications include a daily children's multivitamin; he has no known drug allergies and is up to date on routine immunizations per his most recent well-child visit. Family medical history is significant for a maternal uncle with a reported history of late talking that resolved without formal intervention, and a paternal cousin, Diego, who currently receives speech services through his school in Morganton, NC.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Soto; his father, Andrés Hernández Vega; his older sister, Camila Hernández Soto (age 7); and his maternal grandmother, Rosa Soto Martínez, at 1148 Startown Road, Hickory, NC 28602. The family also keeps a dog named Rex, of whom Mateo is reportedly very fond and with whom he frequently initiates play and attempts verbal communication.

Lucía Rodríguez Soto was born and raised in the village of El Rosario, Yoro, Honduras, and immigrated to the United States in 2016; her family's home there remains at Barrio El Progreso, Calle Principal, El Rosario, Yoro, Honduras, where Rosa Soto Martínez's sister, Marta Soto Martínez, still lives and with whom the family maintains regular video calls. Andrés Hernández Vega was born in Hickory, NC and works as a shift supervisor at Carolina Furniture Works. Lucía Rodríguez Soto works part-time as a receptionist at Hickory Dental Group.

Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home among Mateo, Lucía Rodríguez Soto, and Rosa Soto Martínez, while Andrés Hernández Vega alternates between Spanish and English with the children, estimated by parent report at roughly 70% Spanish and 30% English overall language input in the home. Camila Hernández Soto is reported to be fully bilingual and often serves as a language model and informal interpreter for Mateo at home and in community settings such as medical appointments and store visits. Rosa Soto Martínez cares for Mateo and Camila Hernández Soto after daycare and school three days per week while both parents are at work, and speaks only Spanish with the children.

Lucía Rodríguez Soto reports that Mateo's babbling was delayed compared to Camila Hernández Soto's at the same age, with first words emerging around 22 months in Spanish and first two-word combinations around 30 months. English exposure began at 26 months when Mateo started attending Sunshine Bilingual Daycare and Preschool. Prior to that, from March 2022 to July 2023, Mateo attended a smaller home daycare operated by a family friend, Yesenia Portillo, before transitioning to his current center.

EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Mateo has attended Sunshine Bilingual Daycare and Preschool since July 2023, currently in the four-year-old classroom with Ms. Karen Pruitt as lead teacher and Ms. Brianna Coggins as assistant teacher. Both report that Mateo is social and affectionate with peers but becomes frustrated when unable to make himself understood, occasionally resulting in pushing or grabbing toys from classmates, including Dylan and Ava. He enjoys building with blocks, watching videos about trucks, and playing outside during recess. Ms. Karen Pruitt's most recent progress note, dated September 22, 2025, indicates that Mateo follows one-step directions reliably but requires repetition and gestural support for two-step directions, and that his English vocabulary use in the classroom lags noticeably behind his Spanish vocabulary use at home.

Previous developmental assessment through CDSA at 18 months using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale and the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition indicated expressive language skills at the 11–13 month level against a chronological age of 18 months, with receptive language and cognitive skills within age expectations at that time. A follow-up CDSA assessment at 30 months again using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition showed continued expressive language delay with an age equivalent of 20–22 months, prompting continuation of services until discharge at age 3.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS AND LANGUAGE SAMPLE

Across both evaluation sessions, conducted at Piedmont Crossing Health System — Hickory Campus, Mateo separated easily from his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Soto, and engaged readily with the examiner, M.R. Castillo, and interpreter, J. Ortiz. The first session began at 9:30 a.m. and concluded at 11:00 a.m.; the second session was held from 1:00 p.m. to 2:15 p.m.. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of approximately 15 minutes before requiring a sensory break. Oral-motor examination was within normal limits for structure and function, with adequate lip closure, tongue mobility, and diadochokinetic rate for alternating movements.

A spontaneous language sample was collected in both Spanish and English during play-based tasks with toy cars, animal figures, and a picture book. Mateo's mean length of utterance in words was calculated at 2.4 in English and 2.8 in Spanish, both below age expectations. During a play-based segment, Mateo pointed to the family dog in a photograph and said "Lex run," which parents confirmed was his typical pronunciation of the dog's actual name. Transcript coding included several instances of unintelligible utterances marked [EW] where word boundaries could not be determined by either examiner, consistent with his reduced overall intelligibility.

Mateo's speech was moderately intelligible to an unfamiliar listener in both languages, estimated at approximately 60% intelligibility in connected speech, improving to approximately 85% intelligibility for known context and single words. He demonstrated a mild-moderate phonological disorder characterized by final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for /kat/, "cat"), cluster reduction (e.g., "poon" for /spun/, "spoon"), and gliding of liquids (e.g., /w/ for /ɾ/ in Spanish words such as "pewo" for /peɾo/, "perro"). Stimulability testing showed that Mateo could produce target sounds with mod cues in isolation but not consistently in connected speech. Pragmatically, Mateo demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking for his age, and used gesture effectively to compensate for limited verbal output, though his range of communicative functions was reduced relative to typically developing peers.

STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENT RESULTS

The following English-language and Spanish-language measures were administered across both sessions. Scores reflect Mateo's performance relative to monolingual normative samples, as no bilingual norms exist for several measures; results are interpreted with this limitation in mind, and all Spanish-language administration and scoring were conducted or verified by M.R. Castillo, who is bilingual, with interpretation support from J. Ortiz for parent interview portions only.

Test/Subtest | Date Administered | Standard Score | 95% Confidence Interval | Percentile Rank | Age Equivalent

Preschool Language Scale-5, Spanish-English Bilingual Edition, Auditory Comprehension | October 2, 2025 | 78 | 73–83 | 7th | 2;9–3;2

Preschool Language Scale-5, Spanish-English Bilingual Edition, Expressive Communication | October 2, 2025 | 72 | 66–78 | 3rd | 2;4–2;9

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3, Sounds-in-Words | October 6, 2025 | 68 | 61–75 | 2nd | not reported

Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5, English Form | October 6, 2025 | 82 | 76–88 | 12th | 3;1–3;6

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3, Spanish Supplemental Screener | October 6, 2025 | not standardized | not applicable | not applicable | not reported

A dynamic assessment task incorporating mediated learning strategies was also administered on October 6, 2025 to differentiate language disorder from language difference. Mateo showed modifiability of moderate cueing level with new vocabulary tasks, requiring mod cues to generalize a newly taught label across three trials, a pattern more consistent with a true language disorder than with a language difference secondary to bilingual exposure alone.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on parent and teacher report, record review, and today's assessment, Mateo presents with a bilingual (Spanish-English) mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and a moderate speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility in both languages, consistent with a primary language impairment rather than a language difference secondary to bilingual exposure alone, given that delays are present and comparable across both of Mateo's languages. His scores on the Preschool Language Scale-5 fell in the moderately delayed range for Auditory Comprehension (78, 73–83) and Expressive Communication (72, 66–78), with Expressive Communication falling further below age expectations than Auditory Comprehension, a pattern consistent with his early history of expressive language delay documented by CDSA using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale and the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition.

Articulation testing with the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 placed his sounds-in-words performance in the severely delayed range (68, 61–75), consistent with clinical observation of final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and gliding of liquids affecting both English and Spanish phoneme inventories. English receptive vocabulary as measured by the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 fell in the low-average range (82, 76–88), suggesting a relative strength in single-word vocabulary recognition compared to connected language use and expressive output.

These findings are consistent with Mateo's reported history of prematurity, NICU stay, recurrent otitis media with documented conductive involvement prior to tube placement, and an early expressive language delay first identified at 18 months. His current audiological status, confirmed within normal limits as of September 18, 2025 at Carolina Ear, Nose and Throat and Audiology Associates, Lenoir Office, supports that his current language and speech sound difficulties are not attributable to an active hearing loss, though his otologic history remains a relevant factor to monitor given known associations between recurrent otitis media and speech sound disorder. Mateo meets criteria for speech-language therapy services under North Carolina's Exceptional Children's program eligibility category of Speech-Language Impairment, and continued monitoring of his hearing is recommended given his history.

For billing and documentation purposes, this evaluation is coded under ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and ICD-10 F80.0 (phonological disorder), and under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) with modifier -59 applied to distinguish the combined evaluation from separately billed interpreter services.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo should receive speech-language therapy services a minimum of two times per week for 30-minute sessions, targeting phonological processes (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, gliding) and expressive language skills (sentence structure, vocabulary, narrative skills) in both Spanish and English, ideally delivered or directly supported by a bilingual provider.

2. Therapy should incorporate a combination of the Cycles approach for phonological intervention and Hanen-based strategies to support Lucía Rodríguez Soto and Andrés Hernández Vega in facilitating language development during daily routines at home, with written materials provided in both Spanish and English.

3. A referral is recommended to Smart Start of Catawba County for family support services and a possible slot in a tuition-assistance program to continue Mateo's enrollment at Sunshine Bilingual Daycare and Preschool, where consistent peer language models and a bilingual classroom environment are likely to support continued progress.

4. Classroom staff, including Ms. Karen Pruitt and Ms. Brianna Coggins, should be provided with a brief in-service on supporting Mateo's communication, including allowing extra response time, modeling full phrases rather than single words, and encouraging Mateo to use words rather than gesture when he is capable of doing so.

5. Continued audiological monitoring is recommended given Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media; a repeat audiological evaluation is recommended in 6 months or sooner if parents or teachers note signs of hearing difficulty, to be scheduled through Carolina Ear, Nose and Throat and Audiology Associates, Lenoir Office.

6. This report and its recommendations should be shared with Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Priya Shah at Foothills Pediatric Partners, and with the family's current service coordinator, Denise Faulk at Catawba County Children's Developmental Services Agency, to support continuity of care and eligibility documentation.

7. Given Mateo's reduced intelligibility and associated peer frustration noted in the classroom, a brief consultation with the school counselor is recommended to support his social-emotional adjustment and to monitor for any ongoing behavioral concerns related to communication frustration.

8. Family members, including Rosa Soto Martínez, should be encouraged to continue rich Spanish-language exposure at home, as strong first-language skills support, rather than hinder, second-language development; home language should not be discouraged in favor of English-only strategies.

9. Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately 12 months, or sooner based on clinical progress, to monitor Mateo's response to intervention across both languages and to reassess eligibility for continued services.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Mateo. Please contact the undersigned with any questions regarding this report or its recommendations.

Respectfully submitted,

M.R. Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Piedmont Crossing Health System — Hickory Campus
Pediatric Rehabilitation Services

Scores in the 65-81 standard score range and percentile ranks below 5th percentile across domains confirm continued eligibility for NC ITP services. Gap between receptive and expressive skills has narrowed slightly since last review (prior Expressive SS 60-68 CI) but remains clinically significant. Phonological pattern of final consonant deletion is developmentally appropriate for age equivalent but limits intelligibility given chronological age 3;6.

Pragmatic skills (joint attention, turn-taking) remain emerging and are impacting group participation at daycare, consistent with family-reported difficulty following directions among peers. No new medical concerns identified; feeding history resolved, hearing/vision WNL, supports ongoing primary diagnosis of expressive-receptive language disorder rather than sensory etiology.

Family's stated priorities align well with current outcomes; recommend continuing Outcome 1 and 2, revising strategies for Outcome 2 given new daycare context, and adding a transition-related outcome ahead of third birthday.

Outcome 1 (continued): Mateo will use 2-word combinations to request and comment across home and daycare settings.
Strategies: modeling expansion ("up" to "more up"), parallel talk during routines, abuela and parents coached in expectant waiting and choice-giving during meals/play. Daycare staff at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to receive handout on cueing hierarchy (min/mod/max cues).

Outcome 2 (continued, revised strategy): Mateo will follow 1- and 2-step directions with decreasing visual support in group settings.
Strategies: visual schedule introduced at daycare transitions, pairing verbal direction with gesture fading over 4-week increments, coordination with daycare lead teacher.

Outcome 3 (new): Family will have information needed to plan for transition from NC ITP to preschool services or continued community supports by age 3.
Strategies: service coordinator Megan Price to provide transition packet, discuss potential Early Head Start placement, coordinate timing with Guilford County DSS subsidy renewal so childcare continuity is not disrupted during transition window.

P:
Continue direct SLP services, 2x weekly, 30 minutes, home/daycare settings, through contracted provider Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Partners. Continue OT consult services 1x monthly per existing plan; next OT note due from K.S. by November 1, 2026.

Service coordination activities: Megan Price to follow up on Guilford County DSS subsidy renewal paperwork by October 20, 2026; confirm continued Guilford County WIC enrollment at next nutrition check-in December 2, 2026; share Early Head Start waitlist update with family by November 15, 2026.

Next 6-month review scheduled April 6, 2027. Annual IFSP review scheduled October 5, 2027, contingent on continued eligibility. Transition planning conference to be scheduled no later than 90 days prior to third birthday, per NC ITP timeline, target window opening January 12, 2027.

Family education provided today: cueing hierarchy handout (min/mod/max cues) reviewed in English, key phrases translated to Spanish for abuela's use at home. Family given SLP direct line 336-555-0211 and office email intake@piedmontpedsllc.org for scheduling questions; CDSA general line remains (336) 555-0101.

No change to transportation or interpreter needs at this time; family continues to decline formal interpreter services, noting mother is comfortable in both languages for clinical visits. Consent for continued services reviewed and signed by Lucía Rodríguez Martínez and Jorge Hernández at today's visit.

Plan reviewed with family verbally; copy of updated IFSP to be mailed to home address within 10 business days per NC ITP procedure, with electronic copy available on request through Triad Regional CDSA family portal.

PIEDMONT PEDIATRIC THERAPY ASSOCIATES, PLLC — Charlotte, NC 28205
Speech-Language Pathology Evaluation / Evaluación del Habla y Lenguaje
Phone: (704) 555-0148  Fax: (704) 555-0149  Email: intake@piedmontpedsslp.com

CONFIDENTIAL — BILINGUAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION

Client / Niño: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Ramírez (called Teo at home)
Date of Birth: February 9, 2023   Chronological Age at Evaluation: 2;8
Gestational Age at Birth: 32 weeks   Birth Weight: 3 lbs, 11 oz   Apgar Scores: 4 and 7
Evaluation Date(s): September 22, 2026 and September 24, 2026
Report Date: October 1, 2026
Medicaid ID: 907442318B   CDSA Case ID: CDSA-2026-11872
Referral Source: Dr. Anita Kowalski, pediatrician, Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital – Steele Creek Campus
Service Coordinator: Marisol Peña, Mecklenburg County CDSA Office
Interpreter Present: [X] Yes [ ] No — Yesenia Gutiérrez, certified medical interpreter
Clinician: Rachel Odom, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual provider, Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC

Setting of Evaluation: [X] Home  [ ] Clinic  [ ] Daycare
Language(s) Used in Session: [X] English [X] Spanish (mixed/code-switched)
Primary Language in Home: [X] Spanish [ ] English [ ] Both equally

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA

Mateo ("Teo") was referred by Mecklenburg County CDSA Office following a developmental screening completed by his service coordinator, Marisol Peña, at a routine Early Head Start home visit on August 14, 2026. Concerns were noted regarding limited expressive vocabulary, unclear speech, and difficulty following two-step directions in either language. His mother, Lucía Cruz Ramírez, reports that Teo "no habla casi nada todavía, solo unas pocas palabras" ("he barely talks yet, just a few words") and expressed worry that he is "behind" compared to his older sister, Valentina ("Vale"), age 6.

This evaluation was conducted to determine eligibility for Part C early intervention services through Mecklenburg County CDSA Office and to make recommendations regarding speech-language therapy.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE ANTECEDENTES

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Cruz Ramírez; his father, Jesús Cruz Hernández (called "Chuy" by the family); his sister Valentina; and his paternal grandmother, Rosa Hernández ("abuela Rosa"), who provides childcare during the day. The family resides at 4218 Tuckaseegee Road, Apt. 3B, Charlotte, NC 28208, in Mecklenburg County.

Lucía works two jobs: a day shift stocking produce at a grocery store and an evening shift doing contract cleaning. She also works occasional weekend shifts for CATS as a part-time bus terminal attendant. Jesús ("Chuy") works full-time in commercial roofing. Both parents report significant fatigue and limited time for appointments, and Lucía stated, "Entre los dos trabajos y la niña, se me hace difícil venir a todas las citas" ("Between the two jobs and the girl, it's hard for me to make it to all the appointments").

The family has received services through WIC since Mateo's infancy and currently receives case management through DSS for housing assistance. Mateo was enrolled briefly in Smart Start's subsidized childcare program but was withdrawn in June 2026 due to a lapse in paperwork; he currently attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center three days per week, where his teacher, Ms. Patterson, has also expressed concern about his limited verbal output in the classroom. Ms. Patterson noted that Teo tends to point and grunt rather than use words, and that he gets frustrated when peers like Jayden and Mikayla don't understand what he wants.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA MÉDICA Y DE NACIMIENTO

Mateo was born at 32 weeks gestation via emergency cesarean section at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center due to maternal preeclampsia. Birth weight was 3 lbs, 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 4 and 7 at one and five minutes. He required resuscitation at delivery and spent 41 days in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center's NICU, with a secondary transfer for a brief period to the Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital NICU for evaluation of suspected necrotizing enterocolitis, which resolved without surgical intervention.

Per maternal report and available discharge summaries, Mateo required supplemental oxygen for approximately 6 weeks and had a diagnosis of chronic lung disease of prematurity (ICD-10 P27.1). He passed his newborn hearing screening in the right ear but did not pass in the left ear and was referred for diagnostic audiology. Follow-up testing at Atrium Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Carmel Campus at 4 months corrected age showed mild conductive hearing loss in the left ear, attributed to middle ear effusion, which has since resolved per repeat testing at 18 months. Dr. Sanjay Patel, the audiologist, recommended ongoing monitoring given Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media.

Lucía reports Mateo has had five documented ear infections since age 8 months, with tympanostomy tubes placed at Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital on March 11, 2025 (CPT 69436). No further surgeries are reported. Current medications: none. No known allergies. Vision was screened as within normal limits at his most recent well-child visit.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

The home language is primarily Spanish. Abuela Rosa, who cares for Mateo on weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., speaks only Spanish to him. Lucía and Jesús ("Chuy") are both bilingual and report mixing English and Spanish at home, especially when speaking with Valentina ("Vale"), who is in kindergarten and increasingly English-dominant. Lucía described the home as "un poquito de todo — a veces le hablo en español, a veces en inglés, y la Vale le habla mitad y mitad" ("a little of everything — sometimes I speak to him in Spanish, sometimes in English, and Vale speaks to him half and half").

Lucía reports that Mateo's first words emerged around 18 months, later than Valentina's, and that his current vocabulary includes approximately 15-20 words across both languages, including "mamá," "papá," "agua," "no," "más," and "perro." She reports he uses these words inconsistently and often reverts to pointing, pulling, or vocalizing without clear words. He reportedly calls the family dog, a chihuahua mix, by pointing and saying "wo-wo" rather than her actual name, Canela. During the home visit, Mateo pointed at the dog and said "wo wo go" when Canela ran past him, which the clinician interpreted as an attempt at "Canela, go" or possibly "there goes the dog."

No other family members are reported to have histories of speech, language, or hearing disorders, though Jesús reports he himself was "un poco lento para hablar" (a little slow to talk) as a child and did not receive services.

The family previously received a home visit from an Early Head Start educator, Brianna Tolliver, who provided developmental activities but was unable to address speech-specific concerns and recommended the current referral.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo presented as a social, affectionate child who readily engaged with the examiner and interpreter, Yesenia Gutiérrez, within the first ten minutes of the session. He demonstrated good eye contact, shared enjoyment through smiling and laughing, and engaged in brief joint attention around toys, particularly a set of stacking cups and a toy truck. Attention to structured tasks was variable, requiring frequent redirection and the use of preferred items (a ball) as motivators. Mateo used gestures (pointing, reaching, pulling adults' hands) as his primary means of communication throughout much of the session, supplementing with occasional single words and a few consistent vocal approximations.

STANDARDIZED AND INFORMAL ASSESSMENT RESULTS

The following measures were administered in both English and Spanish, with items presented bilingually and credit given for a correct response in either language where applicable, per standard bilingual assessment protocol.

Test/Measure                                   | Domain                        | Score/Result
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale       | Receptive & Expressive Lang.  | Age equivalent 12-14 months
Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 (Bayley-4), Language subtests | Receptive Communication | Scaled score 4 (1st percentile)
Bayley-4, Expressive Communication      | Expressive Communication      | Scaled score 3 (<1st percentile)
Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5), Spanish form | Receptive Vocabulary | Standard score 68 (2nd percentile), CI 62-74
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | Articulation (English stimulus) | Raw score not interpretable due to limited verbal output; informal sampling only
Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), Spanish-English Bilingual Edition | Auditory Comprehension | Standard score 71 (3rd percentile)
PLS-5 Bilingual Edition                       | Expressive Communication      | Standard score 65 (1st percentile)
PLS-5 Bilingual Edition                       | Total Language Score          | Standard score 66, age equivalent 14-16 months

Informal Spanish Language Sample: In a 20-minute play-based sample conducted primarily in Spanish, Mateo produced 11 intelligible single words and 2 two-word combinations ("más agua," "no no"). Mean length of utterance could not be reliably calculated given the low overall utterance count; estimated MLU is approximately 1.1 morphemes.

Informal English Language Sample: During a brief 10-minute sample in English with the examiner, Mateo produced 4 intelligible single words ("ball," "no," "up," "go") with no two-word combinations observed.

Oral-Motor/Speech Sound Observations: Informal stimulability testing suggested Mateo can approximate /m/, /p/, /b/, and /n/ with min cues, but has difficulty with /k/, /g/, and most fricatives. When attempting to say "gato" (cat), he produced [da], substituting an alveolar stop for the velar /ɡ/. When attempting "perro," he produced something close to [pedo], omitting the trilled /r/ entirely. Vowel production appeared age-appropriate in both languages.

Hearing/Audiology Status: Per most recent audiogram from Atrium Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Carmel Campus, dated July 8, 2026, hearing is within normal limits bilaterally. Tympanometry was normal bilaterally at that visit as well, suggesting resolved middle ear status at present, though continued monitoring is recommended given history.

Oral-Peripheral Examination: Structures and function of the lips, tongue, hard and soft palate, and jaw appeared within normal limits for age. No evidence of overt oral-motor dysfunction, though reduced lingual-palatal contact was observed during attempts at /k/ and /g/ sounds.

Play and Social Communication: Mateo engaged in functional and emerging symbolic play (feeding a stuffed animal, pushing a truck and making car sounds), consistent with roughly 18-month developmental expectations. He demonstrated some protodeclarative pointing but limited protoimperative pointing combined with eye gaze shifting, and did not consistently combine gesture with vocalization to request.

IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Mateo presents with a significant delay in both receptive and expressive language skills across English and Spanish, consistent with a diagnosis of Developmental Language Disorder, affecting both languages rather than reflecting typical bilingual second-language acquisition patterns. His delay is evident on standardized measures in his dominant language (Spanish) as well as in informal English sampling, ruling out the possibility that scores reflect limited English exposure alone. Scores across the PLS-5 Bilingual Edition, PPVT-5 Spanish form, and Bayley-4 Language subtests fell consistently in the 1st to 3rd percentile range, indicating delays of approximately 12-16 months below chronological age expectations.

Mateo's history of prematurity, NICU stay, and early conductive hearing loss are all known risk factors contributing to his current language delay, though his hearing has since normalized. His limited expressive vocabulary, reliance on gesture, and emerging but inconsistent speech sound production (particularly difficulty with velars and liquids in both languages) are consistent with his overall language profile and are not attributable to oral-motor dysfunction or current hearing loss.

Given Mateo's age, the severity of his delay, and his risk history, he meets eligibility criteria for Part C early intervention services through Mecklenburg County CDSA Office under the established condition/informed clinical opinion pathway as well as the standard deviation criteria for his age.

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES

1. Mateo is recommended for speech-language therapy services at a frequency of 2 times per week for 45-minute sessions, delivered bilingually or with interpreter support, focusing on both receptive and expressive language in Spanish (home-dominant language) with English exposure incorporated as appropriate for daycare/community participation.

2. Recommend development of an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) through Mecklenburg County CDSA Office, with Marisol Peña continuing as service coordinator. Suggested IFSP Outcome 1: Mateo will use 2-word combinations to request and comment across settings. Suggested IFSP Outcome 2: Mateo will follow simple one-step directions without gestural cues in both languages.

3. Recommend continued coordination with Little Sprouts Early Learning Center and Ms. Patterson to incorporate language-facilitation strategies (modeling, expansion, wait time) into classroom routines, and to monitor for ongoing social frustration with peers.

4. Recommend therapy incorporate a Hanen-based caregiver coaching model, given Lucía's and Jesús's limited availability for frequent clinic visits; home-based or telehealth-supported caregiver coaching sessions may improve consistency of carryover despite the family's demanding work schedules. Consider brief, high-yield strategies that abuela Rosa, as primary daytime caregiver, can also implement given her central role in Mateo's daily routine.

5. Recommend referral back to Audiology at Atrium Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Carmel Campus for a recheck in 6 months given history of recurrent otitis media, to rule out recurrence of conductive loss that could further impact language development.

6. Recommend repeat speech-language reevaluation in 6 months to monitor progress and adjust the IFSP as needed, including repeat administration of the PLS-5 Bilingual Edition and informal language sampling in both languages.

7. Recommend continued connection with WIC and exploration of renewed Smart Start childcare subsidy eligibility to support consistent daycare attendance, which provides valuable peer language models and routine.

8. Recommend caregiver education regarding the benefits of continued bilingual exposure; no recommendation to reduce or eliminate Spanish in the home. Research consistently supports that bilingual exposure does not cause or worsen language disorders, and Mateo's needs are best met by strengthening language in both English and Spanish concurrently.

This evaluation was conducted using a combination of standardized tools and informal, play-based assessment, with input from Mateo's parents, interpreter, service coordinator, and daycare teacher. Results should be interpreted within the context of Mateo's medical and linguistic history. Please contact this office at (704) 555-0148 or rodom@piedmontpedsslp.com with any questions regarding this report.

Respectfully submitted,

Rachel Odom, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC
License No. NC-SLP-19887

2. Que disminuyan los comportamientos de frustracion (morder, empujar) relacionados con la comunicacion.
3. Que la familia, incluyendo a doña Lupe, aprenda estrategias para apoyar el lenguaje en casa.
4. Preparar a Majo para la transicion al preescolar en el otono de 2026.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Majo vive con su mama, su papa y su hermano Sol en una casa en Kernersville. Entre lunes y miercoles, Majo pasa el dia con su abuela, doña Lupe, quien vive a dos cuadras y la recoge a las 7:30 a.m.. Los martes y jueves, Majo asiste a la guarderia Pequenos Pasos Bilingual Daycare, en el salon de Miss Ana, de las 8:00 a.m. a las 3:00 p.m..

En la manana, la familia tiene una rutina de desayuno en la que Majo senala lo que quiere comer. A la hora del bano, a Majo le gusta jugar con su patito de goma mientras su hermano Sol canta canciones. Por las noches, la madre lee libros con dibujos y Majo intenta nombrar los animales.

La familia tambien mencionó que la mascota de la casa, un perro llamado Toby, ayuda a motivar a Majo a usar palabras como "agua" cuando le quiere dar agua al perro. Los fines de semana, la familia visita a menudo a los abuelos y Sol juega con Majo en el patio.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

La familia recibe apoyo nutricional de WIC en la oficina de Winston-Salem. Una trabajadora de caso de DSS del Condado de Forsyth tambien hace seguimiento de la familia por motivos no relacionados con este IFSP. La familia participa en un grupo de juego de Smart Start los viernes.

Para el proximo ano escolar, la coordinadora de servicios, Yesenia Ortiz, ayudara a la familia a solicitar servicios de preescolar publico a traves de Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Schools. La familia tiene la esperanza de que Majo pueda asistir a Kernersville Elementary School, en el salon de intervencion temprana de la maestra Carmen.

RESULTADOS DEL IFSP CON ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Majo combinara dos palabras para pedir, comentar o rechazar, en espanol o ingles, en 8 de 10 oportunidades observadas durante actividades de rutina.

Estado actual: En la evaluacion con el PLS-5, forma en espanol, Majo obtuvo una puntuacion estandar de 76 en Comunicacion Auditiva (percentil 5) y 79 en Comunicacion Expresiva (percentil 8), con un intervalo de confianza de 70-82. Produce combinaciones de dos palabras en aproximadamente 3 de 10 oportunidades, principalmente con claves mod cues.

Estrategias: Se usara el enfoque Hanen, especificamente el programa It Takes Two to Talk, para entrenar a la madre y a doña Lupe en tecnicas de expansion de lenguaje durante las rutinas diarias. Tambien se incorporaran elementos de PROMPT para apoyar la produccion motora de palabras como "agua" y "mas", que actualmente produce como [a] y [ma].

Resultado 2: Majo disminuira los comportamientos de frustracion (morder, empujar) usando un sistema de comunicacion funcional, con una reduccion del 50% en la frecuencia reportada por la familia y por Miss Ana en la guarderia.

Estrategias: Se introducira un sistema basado en PECS (sistema de comunicacion por intercambio de imagenes) con tarjetas de "mas", "ayuda" y "terminar". La guarderia Pequenos Pasos Bilingual Daycare usara las mismas tarjetas que la casa para dar consistencia.

Resultado 3: Dado el patron fonologico de Majo de omitir consonantes finales (observado en "ga" por "gato" y "pa" por "pan"), se trabajara la produccion de consonantes finales usando el enfoque de Cycles, con meta de 70% de precision en palabras monosilabicas durante sesiones estructuradas.

Resultado 4: Para apoyar la generalizacion de vocabulario basico, se considerara el uso de materiales del programa Kaufman si Majo no muestra progreso suficiente con las estrategias anteriores en un periodo de 3 meses.

FECHAS Y HORARIO DE SERVICIOS

Terapia de habla y lenguaje: dos sesiones por semana, los lunes y miercoles a las 10:00 a.m., en la casa de la familia, provistas por Diana Lopez.

Fisioterapia: una sesion quincenal, los jueves a las 2:00 p.m., provista por Mark Sullivan.

Coordinacion de servicios: visitas mensuales de Yesenia Ortiz, con la proxima visita programada para el 9 de abril de 2026.

Fecha de inicio de los servicios actualizados: 20 de marzo de 2026
Fecha de la proxima revision del IFSP: 10 de septiembre de 2026

La familia firmo su consentimiento para continuar los servicios segun lo descrito arriba. Se les entrego una copia en espanol de este IFSP y los numeros de contacto de la oficina del CDSA, (336) 555-0199, y del correo cdsa.piedmonttriad@example.org, en caso de preguntas.

Resumen de la Familia / Family Summary

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez and Javier Fernández, and his older sister, Camila (3;8), in Garner. His grandmother, doña Lupe, helps with child care three days a week while his parents work. The family is bilingual; Lucía and doña Lupe speak mostly Spanish at home, while Javier mixes both languages, and Mateo is developing both.

Javier trabaja en Triangle Construction Co., una empresa de construcción cerca de Clayton, desde hace dos años. Before that, he worked at Carolina Poultry Processing, a poultry processing plant also near Clayton. Lucía trabaja medio tiempo en la tienda Ahorra Mart en Garner; anteriormente trabajó de mesera en El Sabor Restaurant, a restaurant on Fayetteville Road. Doña Lupe limpia casas con Sparkle Clean Services, a cleaning service based in Raleigh. The family's tío Mario trabaja en Vance Family Farm, a tobacco and produce farm near Four Oaks, and sometimes drives Mateo to therapy when the parents work late.

Preocupaciones y Prioridades Familiares / Family Concerns and Priorities

During the home visit on September 25, 2026, Lucía shared, in her own words: "Mateo entiende todo, pero no nos dice lo que quiere. He points, he grunts, pero no usa palabras. Eso nos frustra a todos, especially at mealtime." Javier added, "At daycare they say he screams when he can't tell them what he wants. Queremos que hable antes de empezar preschool."

Lucía also said, "Doña Lupe me dice que en la casa él dice más palabras en español que en inglés con ella, pero con la maestra Carmen casi no habla nada." The family's top priorities, as stated by Lucía and Javier, are: (1) more spoken words in both languages, (2) fewer tantrums related to communication breakdown, and (3) strategies the family and Lupe can use consistently, "algo fácil que todos podamos hacer igual."

Rutinas Diarias / Daily Routines

Mateo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Camila before Lucía drops both children at Little Learners Daycare by 7:45 a.m.. He attends the toddler room with la maestra Carmen, who reports he prefers solitary play near the block area. Twice a week, a CDSA-contracted early intervention provider from the Little Learners Program arrives at the daycare at 10:00 a.m. for a 30-minute session embedded in circle time, per the SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS section below — note this is a separate program from the daycare itself, despite the similar name, and this has caused scheduling confusion twice this quarter.

On the days doña Lupe cares for him, Mateo naps around 1:00 p.m. and plays outside in the late afternoon. The family receives food support from Wake County WIC, and Lucía attends occasional parenting workshops through Wake Smart Start. Camila is enrolled at Triangle Early Head Start, and the family's open case with Wake County DSS (unrelated to this referral) is being closed this month per Miss Ana's last contact note.

Dinner is around 6:00 p.m., and Javier usually gets home from Triangle Construction Co. by 5:30 p.m.. Bedtime routine includes a bath and a short book, "siempre el mismo libro," per Lucía, around 8:00 p.m..

Historia del Nacimiento y Médica / Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestation at Cedar Ridge Regional Hospital on August 14, 2024, weighing 4 lbs 2 oz, with Apgar scores of 6 and 8. He spent 18 days in the NICU for respiratory distress (ICD-10 P22.0) and was followed by neonatologist Dr. Patel. His pediatrician, Dr. Nguyen, referred him to Piedmont CDSA at 14 months for expressive language delay. Occupational therapist Mr. Tom has also followed Mateo since the initial evaluation for mild sensory-seeking behaviors noted during feeding.

Resultados de la Evaluación / Assessment Results (Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, administered September 18, 2026)

Interaction-Attachment	34	24-27 months	within normal limits
Pragmatics	28	18-21 months	mild-moderate delay
Gesture	30	20-23 months	mild delay
Play	33	22-25 months	within normal limits
Language Comprehension	31	19-22 months	moderate delay
Language Expression	22	13-16 months	significant delay

Mateo produced approximately 35 words combined across both languages per parent report, including "agua," "más," and "up," but no two-word combinations were observed. He used jargon and pointing to request. Receptively, he followed one-step directions in Spanish 8 of 10 trials and in English 6 of 10 trials, consistent with a bilingual child whose dominant input language is Spanish.

Resultados y Estrategias / Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 2-word combinations in Spanish and English to request and comment during daily routines, increasing from a baseline of 0 to 10 spontaneous combinations per session by the next review.
Strategy: Family and doña Lupe will model expansion ("quiero agua," "más leche") using mod cues during meals and bath time. SLP will coach using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, reviewed with Lucía and Javier in both languages.

Outcome 2: Mateo will reduce frustration-related tantrums from an average of 5 per day to 2 per day by using a gesture or word to request instead.
Strategy: Introduce a core board with 8 high-frequency words/images (agua, más, ayuda, terminar) at home and at Little Learners Daycare; la maestra Carmen and doña Lupe trained on min cues prompting hierarchy on September 30, 2026.

Outcome 3: Mateo will increase single-word vocabulary from 35 to 75 words across both languages, tracked by parent log, by April 2027.
Strategy: Weekly direct SLP sessions using PROMPT touch cues for bilabial and alveolar sounds, pairing target words in both languages ("pato"/duck); embedded consultation at Little Learners Program twice weekly.

María José Castillo Fuentes — Bilingual Speech-Language Evaluation

**EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN**

Child's Name / Nombre de la niña: María José Castillo Fuentes (called MJ by family, Majo by her little brother)
Date of Birth: April 9, 2022
Age at Evaluation: 3;6
Medicaid ID: 784302915B
Case ID (CDSA): NC-CDSA-00471Q
Evaluation Date: October 2, 2026
Report Date: October 9, 2026
Evaluator: Hannah Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Clinician
Employer/Clinic: Carolina Bilingual Speech Therapy, PLLC
Interpreter: not needed; evaluation conducted directly in English and Spanish by evaluator
Referral Source: Dr. Anjali Patel, pediatrician, Central Regional CDSA
Address: 118 Rosada Lane, Durham, Durham County, NC 27703
Phone: (919) 555-2048

**Reason for Referral / Motivo de la Remisión**

María José was referred by Central Regional CDSA service coordinator Denise Alford following concerns raised at her September 14, 2026 Part C eligibility meeting. Her mother, Carmen Fuentes Díaz, reported that MJ "no habla casi nada en inglés, y en español le cuesta también" ("she barely speaks any English, and in Spanish it's also hard for her"). Carmen noted that at home the family speaks mostly Spanish, but María José attends an English-immersion preschool, El Nido de Colibríes, five days a week while Carmen works.

**Background Information / Información de Antecedentes**

María José lives with her mother, Carmen Fuentes Díaz; her father, Eduardo Castillo Pérez; her younger brother, Sol (18 months); and her maternal grandmother, Rosa, who moved in with the family in January 2026 to help with childcare. Rosa speaks only Spanish and is María José's primary caregiver on weekends. Carmen works nights stocking shelves at the Harris Teeter distribution center on Angier Avenue, and Eduardo works days in landscaping. Because of their schedules, Rosa and Sol spend the most daytime hours with María José when she is not at school.

The family was connected to WIC shortly after MJ's birth and currently receives support from the Durham County Partnership for Children, which helped subsidize her enrollment at El Nido de Colibríes. Carmen stated, "Sin esa ayuda, no hubiera podido pagar la escuela" ("Without that help, I wouldn't have been able to pay for school").

**Birth and Medical History / Historia Médica y del Nacimiento**

María José was born at 38 weeks gestation at Duke Regional Hospital via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. Carmen reported no complications during pregnancy or delivery. MJ passed her newborn hearing screening and has had no history of chronic ear infections, though she had one episode of otitis media at 14 months treated with antibiotics. There is no history of hospitalization beyond birth. Her pediatrician, Dr. Anjali Patel of Duke Children's Primary Care, confirmed age-appropriate gross motor milestones but noted delayed expressive language at the 24-month well-child visit.

Family medical history is significant for a maternal uncle, Tío Beto, who reportedly had a speech delay as a child and did not begin talking in full sentences until age 4. No other family history of hearing loss, autism, or developmental disability was reported.

**Family and Language History / Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje**

Language exposure in the home is predominantly Spanish. Carmen and Eduardo both report speaking Spanish 90% of the time at home, with occasional English words mixed in for things like colors and numbers. Rosa speaks exclusively Spanish with María José and Sol. Carmen described a mixed approach: "Yo le hablo en español, pero a veces se me sale el inglés porque en el trabajo todo es en inglés" ("I speak to her in Spanish, but sometimes English slips out because at work everything is in English").

María José began attending El Nido de Colibríes at 30 months of age, where instruction is conducted primarily in English with limited Spanish support. Her teacher there, Maestra Yolanda Benítez, reported that MJ is quiet in the classroom and tends to play alongside peers rather than engage verbally, though she responds to simple English directions like "sit down" and "line up." A classmate, Danna, was described by Maestra Yolanda as MJ's "best little friend," and the two are often seen holding hands at pickup.

Carmen reported that María José's first words emerged around 16 months in Spanish ("mamá," "agua," "no"), but vocabulary growth has been slow since then. She currently combines two words occasionally in Spanish ("más agua," "no quiero") but rarely produces two-word combinations in English. Carmen also shared that MJ calls her little brother "Sol" clearly but struggles to name most other family members or common objects consistently in either language.

**Educational History**

María José has attended El Nido de Colibríes, located at 2240 Holloway Street, Durham, NC, since April 2025. The center was recommended to the family by their service coordinator at Central Regional CDSA as a program with some bilingual staff support, though Maestra Yolanda is currently the only Spanish-speaking staff member in MJ's classroom. The family also considered a nearby program, Casa de Sueños Early Learning, but chose El Nido de Colibríes due to proximity to Carmen's workplace.

**Assessment Procedures**

María José was assessed in both English and Spanish across two sessions, September 25, 2026 and October 2, 2026, at the family's home. Standardized and informal measures were administered bilingually, with scoring following dual-language administration guidelines. MJ was cooperative throughout both sessions, though she required frequent breaks and responded best to play-based tasks involving toy animals and a favorite stuffed rabbit she calls "Coneja."

**Test Results / Resultados de las Pruebas**

| Measure | Domain | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scales–5 (Spanish Edition) | Auditory Comprehension | 78 | 7th | 2;4 |
| Preschool Language Scales–5 (Spanish Edition) | Expressive Communication | 72 | 3rd | 2;1 |
| PLS-5 | Total Language Score | 74 | 4th | 2;2 |
| Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) | Morphosyntax (Spanish) | 82 | 12th | — |
| BESA | Morphosyntax (English) | 68 | 2nd | — |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation–3 | Sound Production | 85 | 16th | — |

Confidence interval for the PLS-5 Total Language Score was 69-79 (95% confidence). On an informal Spanish language sample, María José produced 3 of 5 target consonant clusters correctly, substituting /t/ for /tr/ in words like "tren," produced as "ten". In English, she produced the word "ball" as [bɔ], omitting the final consonant.

Oral mechanism examination was within normal limits. Hearing screening (pure tone, bilateral) was passed at 20 dB HL across frequencies.

**Clinical Impressions / Impresiones Clínicas**

Results indicate a language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a primary language impairment rather than second-language acquisition alone, given that María José's scores fall well below expected ranges even in her dominant language (Spanish). Her expressive skills are notably weaker than her receptive skills in both languages, and she demonstrates reduced mean length of utterance relative to same-age bilingual peers. Articulation errors are mild and likely to resolve with typical development or minimal intervention, but language delay is the primary concern.

María José meets criteria for Developmental Delay under the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program eligibility guidelines (DSM-5-TR code F80.9, unspecified developmental language disorder; ICD-10 code F80.9). CPT code for the bilingual evaluation performed was 92523 with modifier -59.

Family and caregiver mix of languages, while rich and loving, has resulted in some inconsistency in modeling, which likely contributes to but does not fully explain MJ's delay. Rosa reported, "Ella entiende todo, pero no me dice casi nada" ("She understands everything, but she barely tells me anything"), which is consistent with the receptive-expressive gap observed during testing.

**Recommendations / Recomendaciones**

1. María José qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention services under Central Regional CDSA's Infant-Toddler Program, two sessions weekly, 30 minutes each, in a bilingual service delivery model.
2. Intervention should target vocabulary growth, two- and three-word combinations, and morphosyntactic development in both Spanish and English, using play-based and naturalistic approaches such as Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies.
3. Family coaching should include Carmen, Eduardo, and Rosa, given their shared caregiving roles, with written home strategies provided in Spanish.
4. Continued coordination with El Nido de Colibríes and Maestra Yolanda Benítez is recommended to support classroom language modeling and reduce reliance on nonverbal communication strategies.
5. Referral to Durham County Partnership for Children for possible additional subsidized hours of bilingual preschool programming, given documented benefit of increased language exposure.
6. Re-evaluation in 6 months to monitor progress toward IFSP outcomes and determine continued eligibility.
7. Hearing should be rescreened annually given history of one prior ear infection; no current referral to audiology is needed at this time.

**IFSP Outcomes Review**

Outcome	Strategies	Progress	Date
María José will combine 2-3 words in Spanish to request desired items	Modeling, expansion, wait time during play with Rosa and Carmen	Emerging; uses "más agua" and "no quiero" consistently	10/02/2026
María José will follow 2-step directions in English at El Nido de Colibríes	Visual cues, consistent routines with Maestra Yolanda	Limited progress; follows 1-step directions only	10/02/2026
María José will increase single-word vocabulary across both languages to 150+ words	Bilingual labeling, shared book reading at home and school	Partial progress; approximately 90 words documented	10/02/2026
María José will reduce final consonant deletion in English words	Articulation drills, auditory bombardment	Not yet addressed; recommended for next IFSP cycle	10/02/2026
Family will receive bilingual home strategies from service coordinator	Written materials, monthly check-ins with Denise Alford	Ongoing; materials provided in Spanish at last visit	09/14/2026

**Service Coordination Note**

Denise Alford will schedule the next IFSP review meeting for April 2027, coinciding with María José's upcoming transition planning as she approaches her third birthday eligibility window for the local education agency. The family has been informed of their right to request an earlier review if concerns increase, and contact information was provided: Central Regional CDSA, main line (919) 555-7731, email intake@centralregionalcdsa.example.org.

**Evaluator's Summary Statement**

María José Castillo Fuentes presents with a bilingual developmental language disorder affecting both her receptive and expressive skills in Spanish and English, with expressive language most significantly impacted. She is a warm, engaged child who benefits from consistent routines, visual support, and the rich bilingual environment her family already provides. With targeted bilingual intervention and continued family and caregiver involvement, including from Rosa and her little brother Sol, MJ is expected to make meaningful progress in both languages.

Respectfully submitted,

Hannah Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Speech Therapy, PLLC
License #NC-SLP-30182
(919) 555-4420

Child Name: Mateo Alejandro Vargas Cruz
Preferred Name: Teo
Date of Birth: November 14, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;10
Evaluation Dates: September 22, 2026 and September 24, 2026
Report Date: September 29, 2026
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Vargas Rodríguez (mother), Esteban Cruz Molina (father)
Referring Provider: Dr. Patricia Nguyen, Carolina Pediatric Associates
Primary Language(s): Spanish (home), English (daycare)
Evaluator: Ana Beltrán, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Clinic/Program: Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services
Clinic Phone: (919) 555-0237
Clinic Website: www.carolinabilingualslp.com
Record/Case #: SLP-2026-0847
Medicaid ID: 784552913A
Home Address: 214 Holly Ridge Lane, Apex, NC 27502
Family Phone: (919) 555-0184
Family Email: lucia.vargas84@gmail.com
Service Coordinator: Mónica Flores, Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE LA REMISIÓN

Teo was referred by Dr. Patricia Nguyen at Carolina Pediatric Associates for a bilingual speech-language evaluation following parent and teacher concern about limited intelligibility in both Spanish and English, reduced expressive vocabulary, and delayed sentence structure. Lucía Vargas Rodríguez reported, "Casi nadie afuera de la familia le entiende a Teo cuando habla" ("Almost no one outside the family understands Teo when he talks"). The classroom teacher at Little Learners Daycare, Ms. Jennifer Hodges, echoed this concern in a written note sent home on August 11, 2026.

Teo was previously enrolled in early intervention through Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency from March 2023 through November 2024, when he aged out of Part C services. He is currently receiving private speech-language therapy twice weekly and occupational therapy once weekly through Little Learners Program in Cary. This evaluation was requested to update diagnostic impressions and determine continued medical necessity for CPT 92523 and CPT 92522 services.

BACKGROUND / ANTECEDENTES

Teo lives at home with his mother, Lucía Vargas Rodríguez; his father, Esteban Cruz Molina; and his older sister, Sol Vargas Cruz, age 8;3. His maternal grandmother, Carmen Molina, lives nearby and provides after-school childcare for both children three days a week. Lucía Vargas Rodríguez works part-time as a receptionist, and Esteban Cruz Molina is employed in construction with Triangle Framing Solutions. The family receives support through the WIC nutrition program and reports stable housing.

Teo attends Little Learners Daycare five days a week from 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM. His lead teacher is Ms. Jennifer Hodges, and his classroom assistant is Ms. Marisol Peña, who is bilingual and often supports Teo during transitions. Lucía Vargas Rodríguez described two close friends in the classroom, Jack and Ava, noting that Teo plays well with them but mostly uses gestures rather than words.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Teo was born at 32 weeks gestation at Riverstone Medical Center in Raleigh following preterm labor. Birth weight was 3 lbs, 10 oz (approximately 1,650 grams), and Apgar scores were 4 and 7 at 1 and 5 minutes. He was admitted to the NICU at Riverstone Medical Center for five weeks due to respiratory distress and feeding difficulty, under the care of neonatologist Dr. Robert Kim. Obstetric delivery was managed by Dr. Sandra Ellis.

Per maternal report, Teo required supplemental oxygen for the first 10 days of life and had a nasogastric tube for feeding support for approximately three weeks. He passed his newborn hearing screening bilaterally prior to discharge on December 19, 2021. Pediatric follow-up has been ongoing with Dr. Patricia Nguyen since January 2022.

Medical history is otherwise significant for recurrent otitis media, with six documented episodes between 18 months and 3 years of age. He underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on June 2, 2024, performed by Dr. Omar Haddad, ENT. Tubes extruded spontaneously by February 2025, and his most recent hearing screening, conducted at this evaluation, showed pass bilaterally at 20 dB HL across frequencies.

Teo's diagnostic history includes ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and ICD-10 F80.4 (speech and language development delay due to hearing loss), assigned following his November 14, 2024 IFSP review. No seizure history, no known allergies, and no current medications were reported.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

The home language is primarily Spanish. Lucía Vargas Rodríguez reported, "En casa hablamos español casi siempre, pero Sol le habla más en inglés porque así aprendió en la escuela" ("At home we speak Spanish almost always, but Sol speaks to him more in English because that is how she learned it at school"). Esteban Cruz Molina communicates with Teo in a mix of Spanish and English depending on the activity, and extended family, including the paternal grandmother in Durham, speak exclusively Spanish with him during visits.

Lucía Vargas Rodríguez estimated that Teo produces roughly 50 intelligible words total across both languages, with greater use of nouns than verbs. She reported first words around 18 months and noted that two-word combinations did not emerge until approximately 3;0. She stated, "Antes pensábamos que era solo porque es bilingüe, pero ahora con Sol vemos que no es igual" ("Before we thought it was only because he is bilingual, but now comparing him with Sol we see it's not the same").

Sol is described as typically developing and attends Holly Ridge Elementary School. There is no reported family history of speech, language, or learning disability on either side, though Carmen Molina mentioned that a cousin, Rosa Molina, received speech therapy as a young child in Mexico.

DAYCARE AND THERAPY SCHEDULE / HORARIO ESCOLAR Y TERAPÉUTICO

Teo currently receives speech-language therapy and occupational therapy through Little Learners Program, distinct from his daycare, Little Learners Daycare, though the family notes the similar names cause occasional confusion when scheduling. His occupational therapist is Jake Thompson, OTR/L. Current weekly schedule:

| Day | Start Time | Stop Time | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 3:30 PM | 4:15 PM | Little Learners Program, Cary office |
| Wednesday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Home visit, 214 Holly Ridge Lane |
| Friday | 1:00 PM | 1:45 PM | Little Learners Daycare |

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES / PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Assessment was conducted bilingually by the undersigned, who is fluent in both English and Spanish; no interpreter was required. Procedures included parent interview, classroom observation, standardized testing in both languages, a spontaneous language sample coded in SALT format, oral mechanism examination, and a hearing screening. Lucía Vargas Rodríguez was present for both sessions and provided informal translation checks for home vocabulary.

RESULTS / RESULTADOS

Standardized Testing

| Measure | Domain | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CELF Preschool-2 | Core Language Score | 78 | 7th percentile | 73-83 | 3;2 |
| CELF Preschool-2 | Receptive Language Index | 81 | 10th percentile | 76-86 | 3;4 |
| CELF Preschool-2 | Expressive Language Index | 74 | 4th percentile | 68-80 | 2;9 |
| PLS-5 Spanish Edition | Auditory Comprehension | 71 | 3rd percentile | 65-77 | 2;6–3;0 |
| PLS-5 Spanish Edition | Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd percentile | 62-74 | 2;4 |
| GFTA-3 | Sounds-in-Words | 82 | 12th percentile | 77-87 | — |
| MB-CDI (Spanish, parent report) | Vocabulary Checklist | — | 9th percentile | — | 26 months |

Articulation and Phonology

Oral mechanism examination revealed adequate structure and mobility for speech; no evidence of apraxia was noted. In single-word testing, Teo produced word-final consonant deletion and cluster reduction across both languages. He substituted /t/ for /k/ in initial position (e.g., ""tasa" for "casa"") and devoiced final /g/ (e.g., ""pego" for "perro"" with final consonant omitted). He produced /ɾ/ inconsistently, achieving the target in 3 of 10 trials with moderate cues. In English, he substituted [w] for /l/ (e.g., ""wion" for "lion"") and demonstrated stimulability for isolated /k/ with minimal cues in 8/10 attempts.

Connected speech intelligibility was estimated at 60% to familiar listeners and 30% to unfamiliar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

Language Sample

A 20-minute spontaneous language sample was collected during structured play with Teo and Lucía Vargas Rodríguez, then rescored by SALT convention. Mean length of utterance was 1.8 morphemes in English and 2.1 morphemes in Spanish, both below expected range. One representative utterance was coded [EW] for an English-word intrusion during a Spanish utterance ("quiero [EW] car"). Teo relied heavily on single words and gestures, producing few two- and three-word combinations.

Receptive and Social Communication

During classroom observation at Little Learners Daycare, Teo followed one-step directions reliably but required repetition or gesture for two-step directions. He engaged in parallel play with Jack and Ava and initiated joint attention using pointing and eye gaze more often than verbal bids. Ms. Jennifer Hodges reported that Teo becomes frustrated when peers do not understand him, occasionally resulting in pushing or walking away.

Hearing

Pure-tone screening passed bilaterally at 20 dB HL for 1000, 2000, and 4000 Hz.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Teo presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a true bilingual language impairment rather than typical second-language acquisition. This impression is supported by below-average performance across both home and school language measures, history of prematurity and recurrent otitis media, and converging parent and teacher report. Co-occurring speech sound disorder affecting both languages is also present, with difficulty at the phoneme level in /k/, /g/, /ɾ/, and /l/.

Lucía Vargas Rodríguez shared, "Nos preocupa que empiece kínder el año que viene y nadie le entienda" ("We worry that he will start kindergarten next year and no one will understand him"), underscoring the family's concern about school readiness. Esteban Cruz Molina added, "Queremos que siga hablando español en casa, pero también que le vaya bien en inglés en la escuela" ("We want him to keep speaking Spanish at home, but also do well in English at school"), which was incorporated into recommendations below.

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES

1. Continue bilingual speech-language therapy twice weekly through Little Learners Program, targeting both Spanish and English expressive language, syntax, and the identified phoneme targets, with ongoing coordination between Ana Beltrán and classroom staff at Little Learners Daycare.
2. Continue occupational therapy with Jake Thompson, OTR/L to address frustration tolerance and fine motor skills supporting communication.
3. Reconvene the IFSP/educational team, including Service Coordinator Mónica Flores of Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency, to review IFSP Outcome #3 and determine eligibility for preschool exceptional children's services prior to kindergarten entry.
4. Encourage continued use of Spanish at home while introducing targeted English vocabulary through shared book reading, using PROMPT-informed cueing strategies modeled during today's session.
5. Repeat audiological monitoring in six months given history of recurrent otitis media.
6. Family should contact the clinic at (919) 555-0237 or lucia.vargas84@gmail.com to schedule the next progress review, tentatively planned for March 2027.

Report prepared by Ana Beltrán, M.S., CCC-SLP
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services
www.carolinabilingualslp.com
