PIEDMONT PEDIATRIC THERAPY ASSOCIATES, PLLC
142 Willow Bend Lane, Suite 204, Cary, NC 27511
Tel: (919) 555-0148 | Fax: (919) 555-0149
Informe de Evaluación del Habla y Lenguaje / Speech-Language Evaluation Report

Client/Cliente: Mateo del Río
Date of Birth/Fecha de Nacimiento: February 14, 2022
Chronological Age/Edad: 4;2
Medicaid ID: AB482913650C
Record #: LDR-2026-0417
Evaluation Date/Fecha de Evaluación: April 17, 2026
Report Date: April 24, 2026
Parent/Guardian: Ana Fernández-Soto (madre), Carlos del Río (padre)
Clinician/Clínica: Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP

Setting of Evaluation:
[X] Home  [ ] Daycare  [ ] Clinic
Referral Source:
[ ] Pediatrician  [X] Early Intervention Service Coordinator  [ ] Parent Self-Referral
Interpreter Used:
[ ] Yes  [X] No (bilingual clinician conducted session in English and Spanish)

Reason for Referral / Motivo de Consulta

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech and language evaluation by his service coordinator, Marisol Vega, of the Centro Regional de Desarrollo y Servicios para la Primera Infancia del Piedmont (CDSPI), following a concern raised at his 4;2 well-child visit on March 3, 2026 by his pediatrician, Dr. Patel. His mother, Ana Fernández-Soto, reported, "No le entiendo casi nada de lo que dice, and his cousins can't understand him either." She noted that Mateo mixes English and Spanish within the same sentence and frequently gestures instead of speaking when frustrated. CDSPI opened a case for Mateo on January 9, 2026 under IFSP outcome #2, targeting functional communication across home and daycare settings.

Background / Antecedentes

Mateo lives with his parents, Ana Fernández-Soto and Carlos del Río, and his older brother, Diego, age six, in Cary. His maternal grandmother, Rosa Fernández, lives nearby and provides afternoon childcare three days a week, picking Mateo up from daycare around 3:00 PM. The family also has a dog, Luna, whom Mateo is reportedly very attached to; his mother shared that he once said "Luna agua" when the dog was thirsty, combining a target noun with a two-word utterance.

Mateo attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare on weekdays from 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM. His lead teacher, Ms. Ortiz, reports that he plays well alongside peers but rarely initiates verbal exchanges. His classroom aide, Mr. Fuentes, echoed this, noting that Mateo prefers parallel play and will point rather than ask for items. One classmate, Noah, has reportedly taken a liking to Mateo and often tries to include him in group games, though Mateo's limited verbal output makes turn-taking difficult.

Birth and Medical History / Historia Médica y de Nacimiento

Mateo was born at 39 weeks gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery at WakeMed Cary Hospital. Birth weight was 7 lbs 4 oz; Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. His mother reported no complications during pregnancy or delivery. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening and has had no subsequent hearing concerns; a tympanometry performed by Dr. Patel's office on November 12, 2025 was within normal limits bilaterally. He has had three ear infections since birth, the most recent resolving without need for tubes.

Developmental milestones were reportedly met within normal limits for gross and fine motor skills; Mateo walked at 13 months. His mother noted first words emerged around 18 months but that vocabulary growth has been slower than that of his brother, Diego, at the same age. No history of seizures, head trauma, or significant illness was reported. Vision was last screened at 4;0 and was within normal limits.

Family and Language History / Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje

The home language environment is mixed. Ana Fernández-Soto reported that she and Rosa Fernández speak primarily Spanish with Mateo, while Carlos del Río and Diego often speak English, particularly during homework or screen time. Ana Fernández-Soto estimated the home language exposure as roughly 60% Spanish and 40% English, consistent with simultaneous bilingual exposure since birth. She reported no family history of speech or language disorders on her side, though she mentioned that her own brother "tardó en hablar pero se le resolvió solo" (was a late talker but resolved on his own). Carlos del Río reported no known family history of communication disorders.

Ana Fernández-Soto described Mateo's communication at home: "Dice palabras sueltas, pero no hace oraciones. He'll say 'quiero jugo' but then just points for everything else." She reported that Mateo understands both languages well but produces far less than he comprehends, and that he sometimes mixes languages mid-sentence, such as saying "no quiero that one." Both parents expressed concern that his limited intelligibility is affecting his confidence, noting he has started to whine or point rather than attempt words he has struggled with before.

Behavioral Observations / Observaciones Conductuales

Mateo presented as a friendly, engaged child who separated easily from his mother and transitioned into the evaluation room without difficulty. Eye contact and joint attention were within normal limits. Play skills were age-appropriate; he engaged in symbolic play with a toy kitchen set, feeding a stuffed rabbit and saying "más" when requesting more pretend food. Attention to task was adequate across the session, with brief redirection needed during the final ten minutes.

Mateo's speech was characterized by multiple sound substitutions and omissions that reduced overall intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners. In connected speech, approximately 60% of his utterances were intelligible to this examiner, who is a fluent Spanish-English bilingual listener; his mother estimated intelligibility to unfamiliar adults at closer to 30-40%.

Assessment Results / Resultados de la Evaluación

The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both English and Spanish, as appropriate, using the family's reported dominant language for each task.

Measure                                  Domain                          Score                    Percentile
Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5) Spanish Edition   Auditory Comprehension       Standard Score 82       12th percentile
PLS-5 Spanish Edition                            Expressive Communication      Standard Score 71       3rd percentile
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)  Sounds-in-Words              Standard Score 68       2nd percentile
Khan-Lewis Phonological Analysis-3               Phonological Processes       Standard Score 65       1st percentile

Mateo's expressive and receptive scores on the PLS-5 fell within the moderately to severely delayed range, with a notable gap favoring comprehension over production, consistent with his parents' report. On the GFTA-3, he demonstrated consistent phonological processes including final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and fronting of velars, producing /t/ for /k/ and /d/ for /g/ across word positions. For example, he produced "tat" for the target word "cat" and "do" for "go."

A Spanish phonological probe revealed similar patterns, with consistent deletion of syllable-final consonants and reduced accuracy producing the tap /ɾ/ in medial position, as in "pe-o" for "perro." Stimulability testing showed that with mod cues, Mateo could approximate /k/ in isolation with 8/10 accuracy, but this did not generalize to the word level without max cues, where accuracy dropped to 30%. On a 20-item single-word articulation probe administered informally in English, he achieved 8/10 accuracy on word-initial sounds and 3/10 on word-final sounds, an overall accuracy of approximately 55% across positions.

A language sample was collected during structured play and transcribed using SALT conventions. Mean length of utterance was 1.4 morphemes, below expectations for his age; several utterances were coded [EW] for unintelligible word-level productions. His mother reported that her own estimate of his functional vocabulary is roughly 80 words across both languages combined, well below typical expectations for a bilingual four-year-old.

Session Schedule / Horario de Sesiones

Day         Start Time        Stop Time         Location
Monday      9:00 AM       9:30 AM        Clinic – Room 2, Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates
Wednesday   3:30 PM       4:00 PM        Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, consultation room
Friday      9:00 AM       9:30 AM        Clinic – Room 2, Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates

Sessions will be billed under CPT code 92507 (individual speech-language treatment) following this initial evaluation, billed under CPT code 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression). Diagnosis coding will reflect ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder).

Impressions / Impresiones

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) with a co-occurring speech sound disorder affecting both his English and Spanish phonological systems. His difficulties appear consistent across both languages, which supports a true disorder rather than a typical bilingual language difference. His receptive skills, while also delayed, remain relatively stronger than his expressive skills, suggesting he understands significantly more language than he can produce.

Mateo's reduced intelligibility, estimated at 30-40% with unfamiliar listeners, is likely contributing to his increasing frustration and reliance on gesture rather than verbal attempts, as described by both Ana Fernández-Soto and his teacher, Ms. Ortiz. His strong play skills, joint attention, and social engagement with peers such as Noah are notable strengths that should support therapy progress.

Diagnostic impression supports continued eligibility for speech-language services through CDSPI under his existing IFSP, as well as initiation of direct speech-language therapy through this clinic to address both expressive language and speech sound production in both languages.

Recommendations / Recomendaciones

1. Individual speech-language therapy, twice weekly for 30 minutes per session, focusing on phonological awareness, word-final consonant production, and expansion of expressive vocabulary and sentence structure in both English and Spanish.
2. Continued home language stimulation strategies, coached for Ana Fernández-Soto and Carlos del Río, using a Hanen-based "It Takes Two to Talk" framework adapted bilingually.
3. Collaboration with Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare staff, including Ms. Ortiz and Mr. Fuentes, to reinforce target sounds and encourage verbal requesting during classroom routines.
4. Coordination with CDSPI service coordinator Marisol Vega regarding updated IFSP outcomes and frequency of services.
5. Referral to occupational therapy, Jennifer Boyd, OTR/L, for a brief consultation regarding oral-motor function and feeding, given mild reports of picky eating that may warrant monitoring.
6. Re-evaluation in 6 months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan, including repeat administration of the PLS-5 Spanish Edition.
7. Follow-up with pediatrician Dr. Patel to rule out any additional contributing medical factors, including recurrent otitis media history.

Mateo's family was counseled extensively on the distinction between bilingual language difference and true language disorder, and both parents verbalized understanding and expressed strong motivation to participate in home carryover activities. Ana Fernández-Soto specifically requested that materials be provided in Spanish when possible, which this clinician will coordinate with the family moving forward.

This evaluation and report were completed by Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist, licensed in the state of North Carolina. Questions regarding this report may be directed to (919) 555-0148 or ljimenez@piedmontpediatricspeech.com.

_________________________________
Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC

- Birth weight was recorded as 2,100 grams (4 lb 10 oz), and Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes.
- Teo was admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at WakeMed Health & Hospitals – Raleigh Campus NICU for a stay of approximately three weeks due to prematurity and respiratory distress.
- Daniela Soto reports that Teo required supplemental oxygen during the NICU stay but did not require a feeding tube at discharge.
- Developmental milestones were reportedly mildly delayed: Teo sat independently at 9 months, walked at 17 months, and said his first words around 20 months.
- Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with at least five documented ear infections between 12 and 30 months of age.
- Teo was seen by Dr. Samuel Patel, audiologist, at Duke Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Duke Raleigh Campus on February 11, 2026.
- That audiologic evaluation documented mild conductive hearing loss in the left ear, attributed to persistent middle ear effusion, with normal hearing in the right ear.
- Bilateral tympanostomy tube placement was performed by an ENT surgeon affiliated with Duke Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Duke Raleigh Campus on March 4, 2026.
- Daniela Soto reports no infections or ear drainage since the tube placement, and a recheck is scheduled for November 2026.
- No history of seizures, head trauma, or significant illness aside from the above is reported.
- Teo is followed for routine pediatric care by Dr. Amanda Chen at WakeMed Pediatric Specialists – North Raleigh Campus, with well-child visits current through June 2026.
- Teo currently receives occupational therapy with Katie Reyes, OTR/L, and physical therapy with Brian Moyer, PT, DPT, both through the CDSA-coordinated early intervention team.
- Katie Reyes notes mild fine motor delays affecting utensil use and pencil grasp; Brian Moyer reports gross motor skills are now within age expectations following six months of physical therapy.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

- Teo lives at home with his mother, Daniela Soto; his father, Ricardo Hernández; and his older sister, Camila Hernández ("Cami").
- The family's household dog, Rocky, is frequently mentioned by Teo during play and in spontaneous speech samples.
- Daniela Soto was born in Veracruz, Mexico, and reports Spanish as her first and dominant language; she speaks limited English.
- Ricardo Hernández was born in Guadalajara, Mexico, and reports functional but non-fluent English, used primarily at work.
- Ricardo Hernández works as a network technician at Cisco Systems, where meetings are conducted in English.
- Daniela Soto works part-time as a dental assistant at Cary Family Dental, a position that requires basic conversational English.
- The home language is estimated at 90% Spanish and 10% English, primarily driven by Cami's use of English learned at school.
- Teo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Delgado, provides childcare two days per week while Daniela Soto is at work; she speaks only Spanish with Teo.
- Rosa Delgado reports that Teo understands her instructions well but that his spoken responses are often unintelligible to her as well.
- Daniela Soto reports that Teo's receptive language in Spanish is stronger than his expressive language in either language.
- No other family members in the home report speech, language, or learning concerns, though Daniela Soto notes that her own brother was "a late talker" as a child.
- Cami is described as verbal and talkative, frequently speaking for Teo or interpreting his requests for adults, which the family was counseled to reduce.
- During the interview, conducted with Marisol Vega interpreting for Daniela Soto, the family indicated a strong preference for continued services in Spanish, with English support introduced gradually.

EDUCATIONAL AND DAYCARE HISTORY

- Teo has attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Center since January 2024, currently enrolled four days per week in Ms. Lopez's room.
- The daycare program is conducted primarily in English, with limited Spanish support provided by a bilingual aide.
- Ms. María Lopez reports that Teo participates in circle time and follows simple routines but rarely initiates verbal interaction with classmates.
- Teo's closest peer relationship at daycare is with Sofia Ramirez, who reportedly assists him by fetching items he points to rather than waiting for a verbal request.
- Ms. Lopez has implemented visual supports and modeled simple phrases in the classroom at the recommendation of the early intervention team.
- No formal preschool special education evaluation has yet been completed, as Teo remains under Part C services pending this evaluation and the upcoming IFSP review.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS AND ORAL MECHANISM EXAMINATION

- Teo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the examiner and the interpreter throughout the session.
- Attention and engagement were adequate for standardized testing, with brief breaks offered approximately every fifteen minutes.
- Teo demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during structured and unstructured play.
- No unusual sensory behaviors, repetitive movements, or atypical social communication patterns were observed during this session.
- Oral mechanism examination revealed symmetrical facial structure, adequate lip and tongue strength and range of motion, and no evidence of structural abnormality.
- Dentition was within normal limits for age; no overt signs of tongue-tie or craniofacial anomaly were noted.
- Diadochokinetic rates were judged mildly reduced for age but within functional limits for connected speech production.

ASSESSMENT TOOLS ADMINISTERED

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish and English editions, administered in both languages with interpreter support
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool, Third Edition (CELF Preschool-3), selected subtests, English
- Spontaneous language sample, approximately 100 utterances, analyzed using SALT (Systematic Analysis of Language Transcripts)
- Oral mechanism examination
- Informal bilingual phonological screening in Spanish and English
- Parent and teacher interview and questionnaire review

TEST RESULTS

PLS-5 (Spanish Edition)

- Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 78, 9th percentile, 95% confidence interval 73-83
- Expressive Communication: Standard Score 70, 2nd percentile, confidence interval 65-75
- Total Language Score: Standard Score 73, 4th percentile
- Age Equivalent, Auditory Comprehension: 2;9
- Age Equivalent, Expressive Communication: 2;3

PLS-5 (English Edition)

- Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 71, 3rd percentile
- Expressive Communication: Standard Score 65, 1st percentile
- Total Language Score: Standard Score 67, 1st percentile

Composite Bilingual Interpretation

- Using the higher score obtained across both languages for each domain, consistent with bilingual scoring guidelines, Teo's best-performance composite falls at Standard Score 76 overall, in the moderately delayed range.
- This pattern reflects a true language impairment present across both languages rather than a language difference attributable to bilingual exposure alone.

GFTA-3 Results

- Raw Score: 38; Standard Score: 72; Percentile Rank: 3rd percentile
- Sounds-in-Words subtest revealed consistent error patterns affecting both English and Spanish phoneme inventories.

CELF Preschool-3 Selected Subtests (English)

- Sentence Structure: Scaled Score 5, 5th percentile
- Word Structure: Scaled Score 6, 9th percentile
- Expressive Vocabulary: Scaled Score 4, 2nd percentile

SPEECH SOUND PRODUCTION AND INTELLIGIBILITY

- Connected speech intelligibility was judged at approximately 50% for unfamiliar listeners and 80% for familiar listeners, consistent with parent report.
- Consistent phonological processes included final consonant deletion, fronting of velars, and cluster reduction, observed in both Spanish and English samples.
- Teo produced /k/ as [t] in word-initial position in English, saying "tookie" for "cookie" and "tat" for "cat."
- In Spanish, Teo substituted /ɾ/ with [d] in medial position, producing "pedo" for "perro," though no dog-related confusion was noted in context.
- During play, Teo pointed at the family dog in a photograph and said "Rocky due," an apparent attempt at "Rocky runs," omitting the final consonant cluster.
- When shown a family photo, Teo pointed to his sister and said "Cami go," demonstrating early two-word combination with consistent final consonant deletion on "go" for "going."
- Gliding of liquids was noted, with /r/ and /l/ both realized as [w] in English, for example "wabbit" for "rabbit" and "yewwow" for "yellow."
- Stimulability testing showed that Teo could approximate /k/ in isolation with moderate cues, achieving 6 of 10 correct productions, but the target did not generalize to the word level without continued maximal cues.
- Target word probes for /s/ clusters showed 3 of 10 correct productions in English and 4 of 10 in Spanish, both below age expectations.
- Repetition of multisyllabic words resulted in syllable deletion, for example ""nana"" for "banana" and ""puter"" for "computer."
- Overall phonological inventory is reduced relative to age expectations in both languages, consistent with a phonological disorder rather than an isolated articulation disorder.

LANGUAGE SAMPLE ANALYSIS

- Mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLU-m) was calculated at 2.1, falling well below the expected range of 3.0-4.0 for his age.
- SALT analysis coded frequent omission of grammatical morphemes, tagged [EW] for word-level errors and [EO] for omissions throughout the transcript.
- Teo relied heavily on single-word utterances and two-word combinations, with only occasional three-word utterances observed, such as "Cami no go," intended to mean that his sister should not leave.
- Pronoun use was inconsistent, with frequent omission of subject pronouns and substitution of "me" for "I" in English utterances.
- Spanish utterances showed similarly reduced grammatical complexity, with verb conjugation errors and omission of articles noted throughout the sample.
- Narrative and sequencing skills could not be formally assessed due to limited expressive output but appeared emerging based on gesture-supported storytelling about a recent family outing.
- Pragmatic skills, including requesting, commenting, and protesting, were present but frequently achieved through gesture or vocalization rather than words.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

- Teo presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with F80.2.
- Speech sound production is significantly impaired in both languages, consistent with a phonological disorder, F80.0, rather than a language difference secondary to bilingual exposure.
- History of recurrent otitis media with effusion, H65.93, and documented mild conductive hearing loss likely contributed to delayed phonological development, though the current presentation exceeds what hearing history alone would explain.
- Language and speech sound deficits are present across both of Teo's languages, confirming a true impairment rather than typical second-language acquisition or dialectal variation.
- Reduced intelligibility, limited MLU, and inconsistent grammatical morpheme use place Teo at significant risk for continued academic and social-emotional impact without intervention.
- Family engagement is a strength: Daniela Soto and Ricardo Hernández are motivated, consistent with home practice recommendations from the early intervention team, and responsive to coaching from Katie Reyes and Brian Moyer.
- Continued coordination between this practice, Duke Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Duke Raleigh Campus, and Dr. Amanda Chen's office is recommended given the medical complexity of this case.

RECOMMENDATIONS

- Teo qualifies for and is recommended to receive individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, billed under 92507, with bilingual service delivery in Spanish and English.
- Therapy should prioritize phonological process remediation using a Cycles approach, targeting final consonant deletion and velar fronting as initial targets in both languages.
- Incorporation of minimal pairs treatment is recommended to establish the /k/-/t/ and /ɾ/-/d/ contrasts identified during testing.
- A core vocabulary and early grammar program informed by Hanen principles, specifically It Takes Two to Talk, is recommended to coach Daniela Soto and Ricardo Hernández in naturalistic language facilitation strategies at home.
- PROMPT techniques are recommended as a tactile-kinesthetic support for articulatory placement, given Teo's reliance on visual and gestural cues during stimulability testing.
- Continued audiological monitoring is recommended through Duke Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Duke Raleigh Campus, with the scheduled recheck in November 2026 prioritized given the history of conductive hearing loss.
- Continued coordination with occupational therapy (Katie Reyes) and physical therapy (Brian Moyer) is recommended to address overlapping fine motor needs that may affect augmentative gesture use and classroom participation.
- Continued use of a qualified Spanish interpreter, such as Marisol Vega, is recommended for all family meetings, including the upcoming IFSP review on September 3, 2026.
- Daycare staff, including Ms. Lopez, should continue to model simple two- to three-word phrases in English during classroom routines and should coordinate with the family regarding core vocabulary targets used in therapy.
- The family is encouraged to continue structured home practice in Spanish, including supported turn-taking with Cami rather than allowing her to speak on Teo's behalf.
- Rosa Delgado should be included in home-practice coaching sessions when feasible, given her significant caregiving role two days per week.
- It is recommended that IFSP Outcome #3 be revised at the upcoming review to reflect updated speech intelligibility targets based on these results, and that IFSP Outcome #2 be continued with updated expressive language benchmarks.
- Re-evaluation of speech and language skills is recommended in approximately six months, or sooner if progress toward IFSP outcomes is not observed, to determine continued eligibility and appropriate transition planning as Teo approaches preschool special education eligibility age.
- This report and its recommendations should be shared with Dr. Amanda Chen and the Wake County CDSA service coordination team, Monica Alvarado, to support integrated service planning.

Report prepared by Jennifer Walsh, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist, Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services, with interpretation provided by Marisol Vega throughout the evaluation and parent interview.

INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y DEL LENGUAJE

**Nombre del niño:** Mateo Alejandro Fuentes Ramírez (conocido como "Teo")
**Fecha de nacimiento:** 14 de febrero de 2024
**Edad cronológica en la evaluación:** 2;8 (edad corregida 2;6)
**Fecha de la evaluación:** 30 de septiembre de 2026
**Hora de la cita:** 9:30 a.m.
**Fecha del informe:** 11 de octubre de 2026
**Lugar de la evaluación:** domicilio de la familia, 214 Oakmist Lane, Garner, NC 27529, Condado de Wake
**Número de expediente:** CDSA-2026-04871
**Número de Medicaid:** 987654321B
**CDSA remitente:** Centro de Desarrollo y Servicios para la Primera Infancia del Área de Piedmont (en adelante "el CDSA de Piedmont")
**Coordinadora de servicios:** Yolanda Pérez Martínez, de la Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios para la Primera Infancia del Triángulo (en adelante "la Agencia del Triángulo")
**Terapeuta evaluadora:** Katherine A. Byrd, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Terapia Pediátrica Bilingüe de Carolina, PLLC
**Teléfono de la clínica:** (919) 555-0148
**Correo electrónico:** kbyrd@terapiapediatricabilingue.com
**Sitio web:** www.terapiapediatricabilingue.com
**Pediatra:** Dr. James Whitfield

---

**1. MOTIVO DE LA REFERENCIA**

Mateo fue remitido al CDSA de Piedmont para una evaluación del habla y del lenguaje después de que su madre, Lucía Ramírez Torres, expresara preocupación por el retraso en la comunicación de su hijo durante una cita de rutina en el WIC, el Programa Especial de Nutrición Suplementaria para Mujeres, Infantes y Niños. La consejera de nutrición del programa WIC recomendó una derivación inmediata al CDSA al observar que Mateo no producía palabras reconocibles a los 2;4.

Poco después, la maestra de la guardería de Teo, la Srta. Ana López, del Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pasitos Felices, confirmó la preocupación. Informó que Mateo se comunicaba principalmente por medio de gestos y gruñidos, mientras que su compañero de salón, Liam, de edad similar, ya combinaba dos o tres palabras. Una amiga cercana de la familia, Patricia Gómez, quien había usado los servicios del Smart Start del Condado de Wake con su propio hijo, animó a Lucía Ramírez Torres a comunicarse con el CDSA de Piedmont sin demora.

La familia también participa en el Programa Early Head Start del condado, y su trabajadora social de allí coordinó el papeleo inicial junto con la coordinadora de servicios, Yolanda Pérez Martínez, de la Agencia del Triángulo.

**2. HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO MÉDICO**

Mateo Alejandro Fuentes Ramírez nació en el WakeMed Cary Hospital el 14 de febrero de 2024, a las 34 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 2,100 gramos (4 libras 10 onzas). Sus puntuaciones de Apgar fueron 7 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. Permaneció en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales durante 11 días por dificultad respiratoria leve, sin complicaciones neurológicas documentadas.

Su pediatra, el Dr. James Whitfield, ha realizado seguimiento regular del desarrollo desde el alta hospitalaria. En una cita reciente con el Dr. James Whitfield, la familia utilizó los servicios de la intérprete médica Carmen Solís, ya que el padre, Diego Fuentes Castillo, prefiere recibir información médica complicada en español. No se reportan antecedentes de pérdida auditiva; una prueba de audición neonatal y una evaluación audiológica de seguimiento a los 18 meses resultaron dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos.

Lucía Ramírez Torres reporta que el embarazo estuvo marcado por hipertensión gestacional leve, controlada con medicación desde la semana 28. No hubo exposición conocida a alcohol, tabaco ni sustancias durante el embarazo. Los hitos motores gruesos de Mateo se alcanzaron dentro de rangos esperados para su edad corregida: se sentó sin apoyo a los 7 meses y caminó de forma independiente a los 16 meses. Sin embargo, los hitos de comunicación se han retrasado de forma notable: no balbuceó con consonantes variadas hasta después de los 14 meses, y a la fecha de esta evaluación su vocabulario expresivo se limita a aproximadamente 6 palabras aproximadas y varios gestos convencionales.

El pediatra derivó previamente a Mateo al Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Wake (DSS) para explorar apoyos adicionales de vivienda y nutrición, dado que la familia reportó inestabilidad habitacional temporal el año pasado. El DSS confirmó la elegibilidad continua de la familia para asistencia alimentaria y remitió el caso de vuelta al CDSA de Piedmont para los servicios de intervención temprana.

**3. HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y LINGÜÍSTICA**

Mateo vive con su madre, Lucía Ramírez Torres (29 años), quien trabaja como cajera en Food Lion en Cary, NC; su padre, Diego Fuentes Castillo (32 años), empleado en la planta de Perdue Farms en Garner, NC; su hermana mayor, Camila Fuentes Ramírez, de 5 años, quien asiste a la Escuela Primaria Aversboro; y su abuela materna, Rosa Castillo Díaz, quien vive con la familia y ayuda con el cuidado diario de los niños. Una niñera de confianza, Marisol Vega, cuida a Mateo tres días por semana mientras sus padres trabajan. La familia también tiene un perro llamado Rocky, con quien Mateo disfruta jugar en el patio trasero.

El español es el idioma principal del hogar; se habla español aproximadamente el 90% del tiempo entre todos los miembros de la familia. Diego Fuentes Castillo comprende inglés de forma funcional por su trabajo, pero prefiere el español en el hogar. Camila Fuentes Ramírez es bilingüe emergente gracias a su escolarización en inglés, y a menudo traduce frases simples para Mateo durante el juego. La abuela, Rosa Castillo Díaz, habla únicamente español y es la cuidadora principal durante las horas de la tarde.

Según Lucía Ramírez Torres, no hay antecedentes familiares conocidos de trastornos del habla o del lenguaje, aunque un tío paterno fue "tardío para hablar" según la familia. Mateo no ha asistido a servicios de intervención temprana previamente, aunque la familia completó una evaluación de desarrollo informal hace seis meses a través del Programa Early Head Start, la cual sugirió retraso en el área de comunicación y motivó la derivación formal actual.

**4. PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN**

La evaluación se llevó a cabo en el hogar de la familia durante una sesión de 90 minutos, con la participación activa de Lucía Ramírez Torres y observación parcial de Rosa Castillo Díaz. Se administraron los siguientes instrumentos estandarizados, complementados con observación clínica directa, muestra de lenguaje espontáneo y entrevista estructurada a los padres:

- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4)
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5)

Esta evaluación integral se facturó bajo el código 92523 (evaluación de la producción de sonidos del habla con evaluación de la comprensión y expresión del lenguaje). Se recomendó previamente el código 92507 para el tratamiento continuo una vez establecida la elegibilidad.

Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, se registraron las producciones de Mateo utilizando transcripción fonética. Produjo el sonido /k/ correctamente en 8/10 ensayos (80% de precisión) en posición inicial de palabra, pero sustituyó el sonido /ɾ/ por [w] de forma consistente, como en su intento de decir "carro", que produjo como "cawo". También dijo "agua" de forma clara al pedir de beber, y se observó que imitaba la palabra "más" con claves moderadas (mod cues) de la evaluadora.

**5. RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS ESTANDARIZADAS**

| Prueba | Área evaluada | Puntuación | Percentil / Rango | Edad equivalente |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Comprensión del lenguaje | — | — | 14-16 meses |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Expresión del lenguaje | — | — | 12-14 meses |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Interacción-Apego | — | — | 26-28 meses |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 | Sonidos del habla | 62 | 1er percentil | — |
| Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition | Cognición (escala) | 8 | 25 | — |
| Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition | Comunicación (compuesto) | 76 (71-83, IC del 95%) | 5to percentil | — |
| Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition | Vocabulario receptivo | 70 | 2do percentil | — |

En la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, el área de Interacción-Apego se ubicó dentro de límites apropiados para la edad, lo cual indica fortalezas relativas en el vínculo social y la atención conjunta con sus cuidadores. Sin embargo, las áreas de Comprensión del lenguaje y Expresión del lenguaje mostraron retrasos significativos, de aproximadamente 12-16 meses por debajo de su edad cronológica corregida.

En el Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 62, correspondiente al 1er percentil, lo cual refleja un inventario fonético marcadamente reducido en comparación con sus pares. Sus errores incluyeron sustitución de deslizamientos por líquidas (por ejemplo, /ɾ/ por [w]) y omisión de consonantes finales en aproximadamente 3 de 5 intentos.

En el Bayley-4, su desempeño cognitivo se ubicó dentro de límites bajos-promedio, con una puntuación escalar de 8 (25 percentil), mientras que el compuesto de comunicación fue significativamente bajo, con una puntuación de 76 (71-83).

En el Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition, obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 70 (2do percentil), lo cual confirma un retraso considerable en el vocabulario receptivo, consistente con los hallazgos de las demás pruebas.

**6. OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES**

Durante la sesión, Mateo se mostró activo, curioso y receptivo al juego interactivo con la evaluadora. Mantuvo contacto visual apropiado y participó en turnos de juego simbólico simple, como alimentar a un muñeco y empujar carritos por el suelo mientras decía "vrum" repetidamente. No se observaron conductas repetitivas atípicas ni dificultades sensoriales significativas durante la evaluación.

Se notó frustración leve cuando no pudo comunicar sus deseos verbalmente; en esos momentos, recurrió a tomar la mano de su madre, Lucía Ramírez Torres, y llevarla hacia el objeto deseado. Esta estrategia comunicativa no verbal, aunque funcional, confirma el retraso expresivo documentado en las pruebas estandarizadas.

**7. IMPRESIONES DIAGNÓSTICAS**

Con base en los hallazgos estandarizados, la historia del desarrollo y la observación clínica directa, Mateo Alejandro Fuentes Ramírez presenta un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo, consistente con el código F80.2 del CIE-10, acompañado de un trastorno fonológico concomitante que afecta la inteligibilidad de su habla. Sus habilidades sociales y de interacción se consideran una fortaleza relativa y un punto de apoyo importante para la intervención.

Dado el patrón de retraso observado en ambos idiomas del entorno (con exposición predominante al español), no se considera que el bilingüismo del hogar sea la causa del retraso; más bien, Mateo presenta un retraso verdadero que se manifiesta en su idioma dominante.

**8. RECOMENDACIONES**

1. Se recomienda que Mateo sea elegible para servicios de intervención temprana bajo la Parte C a través del CDSA de Piedmont, con terapia de habla y lenguaje individual dos veces por semana, sesiones de 30 minutos, facturadas bajo el código 92507.

2. Se recomienda un modelo de coaching para los padres basado en el enfoque Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk"), para fortalecer las estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en el hogar, dirigido principalmente a Lucía Ramírez Torres y a la abuela, Rosa Castillo Díaz, quienes pasan más tiempo con Mateo durante el día.

3. Para abordar los errores fonológicos, se sugiere incorporar el enfoque de Cycles una vez que el niño demuestre mayor estabilidad en su inventario de sonidos consonánticos.

4. Si no se observa un progreso verbal funcional en un plazo de 3 meses, se recomienda considerar un sistema de comunicación aumentativa de respaldo, como el enfoque PECS, para apoyar la comunicación funcional mientras se desarrolla el habla.

5. Para los errores motores del habla si se identifican en sesiones futuras, podría considerarse el enfoque PROMPT como complemento.

6. Se recomienda establecer el Resultado 1 del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (PIFS) enfocado en aumentar el vocabulario expresivo funcional, y el Resultado 2 enfocado en mejorar la inteligibilidad del habla en contextos familiares y de la guardería.

7. Se recomienda consulta continua con la maestra de la guardería, Srta. Ana López, del Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pasitos Felices, para asegurar la generalización de las estrategias en el aula.

8. Se recomienda seguimiento continuo con el pediatra, Dr. James Whitfield, y re-evaluación audiológica anual dado el historial de dificultad respiratoria neonatal.

9. Se recomienda una revisión del PIFS en 6 meses, programada para el 15 de abril de 2027, para medir el progreso respecto a los objetivos establecidos.

10. La coordinadora de servicios, Yolanda Pérez Martínez, de la Agencia del Triángulo, continuará supervisando la coordinación entre el CDSA de Piedmont, el DSS, WIC y el Programa Early Head Start para asegurar la continuidad de los servicios familiares.

**9. RESUMEN**

Mateo Alejandro Fuentes Ramírez es un niño de 2;8 años, bilingüe emergente de hogar predominantemente hispanohablante, que presenta retrasos significativos en el lenguaje receptivo y expresivo, así como un trastorno fonológico concomitante, consistente con el código F80.2. Se recomienda inicio inmediato de servicios de intervención temprana a través del CDSA de Piedmont, con participación activa de la familia y coordinación continua entre las agencias involucradas.

---

Respetuosamente sometido,

Katherine A. Byrd, M.S., CCC-SLP

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) — Annual Review

Child: Mateo de la Cruz Fuentes
Date of Birth: June 14, 2024
ITP Record ID: 4487621
Medicaid ID: 784215663B
CDSA Office: CDSA of the Piedmont, Asheboro, North Carolina
Service Coordinator: Denise Alvarado, (336) 555-0198
IFSP Review Date: October 3, 2026
Previous IFSP Date: April 7, 2026
Next Review Due: April 3, 2027

This review was prepared by Hannah Whitfield-Osei, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist with Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language, PLLC, in consultation with the family, the service coordinator, and the IFSP team. Interpretation support during the family interview was provided by Marisol Peña, contract interpreter through CDSA of the Piedmont.

FAMILY INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Fuentes-Molina, and his father, Javier de la Cruz, at 214 Hollyridge Lane, Asheboro, North Carolina 27203. The family's home phone number is (336) 555-0142, and Lucía's email is lfuentesmolina@gmail.com. Javier's cell number is (336) 555-0176.

Mateo's older sister, Sol de la Cruz Fuentes, is 6 years old and attends first grade at Guy B. Teachey Elementary School. Sol often translates informally for her brother when he gestures instead of speaking, which the family and this clinician have discussed as both a strength and a pattern to watch.

Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Fuentes, lives with the family three days a week and provides childcare while Lucía works. Rosa immigrated to the United States from Aldea Las Minas, near Huehuetenango, Guatemala, where Mateo's great-aunts and cousins still live. Lucía reports that Rosa speaks almost exclusively Spanish with Mateo and that this has been an important source of language modeling at home.

Javier works at Mountain Valley Poultry in Siler City and is frequently unavailable for sessions scheduled after 4:00 PM. The family has asked that therapy stay on weekday mornings whenever the schedule allows, so that both parents can participate in home-visit coaching.

Mateo's primary care physician is Dr. Priya Anand at UNC Health Randolph. The family also receives nutrition support through Randolph County WIC and has been connected to parenting resources through Smart Start of Randolph County. Randolph County DSS arranged interpreter services for the initial intake appointment.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES, IN THE FAMILY'S OWN WORDS

During the review interview, Lucía shared, "Mateo no me dice lo que quiere, solo señala y llora." She explained that her biggest worry is that Mateo still cannot combine words and becomes frustrated both at Rosa's care and at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center.

Javier added that he wants Mateo "to be able to tell us hurts, hungry, more — the words he needs at home," and noted that bedtime has become harder because Mateo cannot explain what he wants and ends up crying instead.

Sol told this clinician, unprompted, that she wishes her brother "could just say my name instead of pulling my shirt." The team used this comment to shape one of the strategies below.

The family's priorities for this review period are: (1) functional communication across English and Spanish at home, at Rosa's care, and at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center; (2) reducing frustration-related tantrums tied to unmet communication attempts; and (3) coaching Sol and Rosa on simple cues they can use with Mateo during daily routines.

DAILY ROUTINES

Mateo wakes around 6:30 AM and eats breakfast with Sol before she leaves for school. On Monday through Thursday, he attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center on West Pritchard Street in Asheboro from 8:00 AM to 3:30 PM. His classroom teacher, Carla Nguyen, reports that Mateo points and pulls adults' hands rather than requesting verbally, and that two classroom peers, Emma and Liam, often hand him toys before he asks, which may be reducing his opportunities to practice requesting.

On Fridays, Mateo stays home with Rosa, who reports a similar pattern of pointing and crying rather than using words, especially around snack time. The family's dog, Rocky, greets Mateo at the door each afternoon, and Lucía notes this is one of the few times Mateo reliably vocalizes without prompting ("dog," "wo").

Bath and bedtime routine happens around 7:45 PM, led mostly by Lucía in Spanish and by Javier in English on the nights he is home before 8:00 PM. The family reports this transition is the most frequent site of tantrums during the week.

EVALUATION SUMMARY

Mateo was seen for annual assessment on September 22, 2026 at a chronological age of 26 months (2;2). The Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), administered in a bilingual Spanish/English format, yielded an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 78 (7th percentile), age equivalent 17-19 months, and an Expressive Communication standard score of 73 (4th percentile), age equivalent 14-16 months. The Total Language Score fell within the range 73-83, consistent with a moderate delay affecting both languages roughly equally.

On the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories (CDI), Spanish-language comprehension corresponded to an age equivalent range of 2;6–3;0, while production fell well below this range, with a vocabulary checklist total of 18 words produced consistently across settings.

Oral-motor examination was within normal limits, with no structural concerns noted. Mateo used 2 of 15 single words consistently during the session ("mamá," "agua," "no") and paired gestures with vocalizations in 8/10 opportunities. He independently produced /m/, /a/, and /n/ but omitted final consonants, so the target word "pan" was produced as "pa." Stimulability for /t/ and /k/ was present with max cues, decreasing to mod cues by the end of the session.

Hearing was last screened on July 15, 2026 following a course of treatment for recurrent otitis media; ICD-10 code H66.90 was documented at that visit, and otoacoustic emissions screening was billed under CPT 92587 with modifier -59. Results were within normal limits bilaterally.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 37 weeks gestation by scheduled cesarean delivery, with a birth weight of 5 lbs 12 oz and Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. There is no other significant medical history beyond the recurrent ear infections noted above. Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Priya Anand, has not raised additional medical concerns affecting communication development.

RECOMMENDED STRATEGIES

The team recommends continued individual speech-language therapy combined with caregiver coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies and PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing for emerging consonant sounds. Aided language stimulation with a core-vocabulary board was introduced during this review and will continue at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center and at home. Carla Nguyen has agreed to prompt peers Emma and Liam to wait for Mateo to request rather than anticipating his needs.

IFSP OUTCOMES — REVIEW SUMMARY

Outcome	Strategies	Progress	Date
Outcome 1: Mateo will use 2-word combinations to request and comment across home, Rosa's care, and Little Sprouts Early Learning Center.	PROMPT cueing and Hanen "OWL" (Observe, Wait, Listen) strategies modeled for Lucía, Javier, and Rosa in both Spanish and English during home visits.	Increased from 0/10 to 6/10 opportunities for spontaneous 2-word combinations ("más agua," "no quiero"). Emerging; not yet met.	October 3, 2026
Outcome 2: Mateo will use a word or gesture-plus-word combination to request a break instead of tantrumming, across 3 settings.	Core-vocabulary board introduced at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center and at home; functional communication training paired with brief planned ignoring of tantrum behavior.	Tantrum frequency decreased from an average of 7 per day to 3 per day per caregiver report; requesting with the board occurred in 4 of 5 observed opportunities. Partially met.	October 3, 2026
Outcome 3: Mateo will produce final consonants in single words with mod cues in structured play.	Cycles phonological approach targeting final consonant deletion, with weekly probe words reviewed with the family.	Accuracy improved from 10% to 45% of probe words across two consecutive sessions. Progressing toward criterion.	October 3, 2026
Outcome 4: Sol and Rosa will use at least 2 simple communication cues (point-and-wait, offering a choice) daily with Mateo.	Caregiver coaching session held with Sol present, modeling point-and-wait and choice-offering during a snack routine.	Rosa reports using the cues "most days"; Sol demonstrated both cues independently during the coaching session. Met for this period; continue to monitor generalization.	October 3, 2026

SESSION SCHEDULE

Day	Start	Stop	Location
Monday	9:00 AM	9:45 AM	Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, Asheboro
Wednesday	10:15 AM	11:00 AM	214 Hollyridge Lane, Asheboro (home visit)
Friday	1:30 PM	2:15 PM	CDSA of the Piedmont therapy room, Asheboro

Sessions are conducted jointly by this clinician and, when scheduling allows, Marisol Peña for interpretation support during caregiver coaching components. The family has requested that the Wednesday home visit remain in place specifically so that Rosa and Sol, who is present after early dismissal on Wednesdays, can take part directly.

TRANSITION AND FOLLOW-UP

Because Mateo will turn three on June 14, 2027, the team briefly discussed transition planning. Denise Alvarado will initiate the transition conference process no later than January 14, 2027, six months prior to Mateo's third birthday, as required under the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program timelines. The family was given written information about preschool special education referral and local Head Start options, and Lucía asked that any future paperwork be provided in both English and Spanish.

The team also discussed Mateo's eligibility redetermination, which will occur at the next annual evaluation. No changes to eligibility category are anticipated given the consistency of standard scores across this review and the prior evaluation on March 2, 2026, when the Auditory Comprehension standard score was 74 and the Expressive Communication standard score was 69.

TEAM SIGNATURES AND PARTICIPATION

This IFSP review was completed with the participation of Lucía Fuentes-Molina and Javier de la Cruz (parents), Rosa Fuentes (grandmother and caregiver), Sol de la Cruz Fuentes (sibling, present for part of the meeting), Denise Alvarado (service coordinator, CDSA of the Piedmont), Marisol Peña (interpreter), and Hannah Whitfield-Osei (bilingual speech-language pathologist, Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language, PLLC). Carla Nguyen from Little Sprouts Early Learning Center provided written input but was not present at the meeting.

The family indicated agreement with the outcomes, strategies, and schedule described above. A copy of this review, along with the updated schedule, was provided to Lucía and Javier in Spanish and English on the date of this review.

Next contact: Hannah Whitfield-Osei will call the family at (336) 555-0142 by October 10, 2026 to confirm the Wednesday home-visit time continues to work with Rosa's schedule, and Denise Alvarado can be reached at (336) 555-0198 or by email at denise.alvarado@cdsapiedmont.org with any questions about the transition timeline.

END OF REVIEW DOCUMENT

text:
+ Nombre: Mateo Hernández Silva ("Teo")
+ CA: 2;3
+ Contexto: Revisión semestral del IFSP (Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia) realizada en el hogar de la familia el 14 de septiembre de 2026, con interpretación simultánea en español e inglés. Participantes: la madre Daniela Silva Ponce, el padre Jorge Hernández Ruiz, la coordinadora de servicios Patricia Gómez de la Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Durham (ASDIC), y la patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP, contratada por Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services.

Resumen: Mateo es un niño de 2;3 años, bilingüe receptivo (español/inglés), referido por retraso significativo en el habla y el lenguaje expresivo. La evaluación más reciente confirma un diagnóstico de F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo). La familia solicita servicios continuos de terapia del habla y lenguaje dos veces por semana, apoyo en el hogar y coordinación con la guardería. Este informe documenta la información familiar, las prioridades de la familia, las rutinas diarias, las agencias involucradas, los resultados actuales de desarrollo y los resultados (outcomes) del IFSP con sus estrategias.

INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR

Mateo vive con su madre, Daniela Silva Ponce; su padre, Jorge Hernández Ruiz; su hermana mayor, Camila, de 5 años; y su abuela materna, Rosa Ponce, quien cuida a los niños algunas tardes. La familia reside en 412 Avery Pines Court, Durham, Condado de Durham, código postal 27703. El número de teléfono de contacto principal es (919) 555-0148 y el correo electrónico de la familia es dsilvaponce26@gmail.com. La madre, Daniela, trabaja medio tiempo como asistente administrativa en Triangle Auto Parts Distribution; el padre, Jorge, trabaja turnos variables en Carolina Freight Logistics. En casa, la familia tiene un perro llamado Rocky, al cual Mateo adora y menciona con frecuencia durante las sesiones.

Mateo nació a las 38 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 3,100 gramos y un Apgar de 8/9. No hubo complicaciones perinatales reportadas. La familia indica que Mateo comenzó a caminar a los 13 meses, dentro de los parámetros esperados, pero el lenguaje expresivo se ha retrasado de forma notable en comparación con el de su hermana Camila a la misma edad.

COORDINACIÓN DE SERVICIOS Y OFICINA DEL CDSA

La coordinadora de servicios asignada es Patricia Gómez, de la ASDIC, ubicada en 2200 Chalmette Drive, Suite 110, Durham. El número de caso con la agencia es ASD-2026-30487. Patricia puede ser contactada al (919) 555-0271 o por correo electrónico a pgomez@asdic-nc.org. El número de identificación de Medicaid de Mateo es NC487201635B. La ASDIC supervisa la elegibilidad continua del niño bajo la Parte C y revisa este IFSP cada seis meses, con la próxima revisión programada para el 12 de marzo de 2027.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (EN SUS PROPIAS PALABRAS)

La madre, Daniela, expresó: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Mateo no puede decirnos lo que quiere. Solo señala o grita, y a veces se frustra mucho y empieza a llorar. Su hermana Camila a esta edad ya hablaba en oraciones completas, y la comparación nos asusta un poco." Añadió: "Queremos que él pueda pedir las cosas, aunque sea con pocas palabras, para que no se frustre tanto en casa ni en la guardería."

El padre, Jorge, comentó: "Yo trabajo turnos rotativos, así que no siempre estoy en las sesiones, pero cuando estoy en casa trato de jugar con él y repetir las palabras que la terapeuta nos enseña. Lo que más queremos es que Mateo pueda decir 'mamá' y 'papá' claramente, y que pueda decir el nombre del perro, porque ahora solo dice algo como '[EW] oco' cuando quiere jugar con Rocky."

Durante la observación directa, Mateo produjo varios enunciados espontáneos documentados por la terapeuta. Al ver a su hermana entrar al cuarto, dijo "más Camila" pidiendo que ella se quedara jugando con él. Cuando el perro ladró afuera, Mateo señaló la puerta y dijo "Rocky fuera." Más adelante, al pedir agua, produjo una aproximación de la palabra con sustitución fonológica: dijo "agua" como "awa", omitiendo el sonido /g/. La familia reportó que estas producciones de dos palabras son típicas en casa, pero que su inteligibilidad sigue siendo baja fuera del contexto familiar, estimada por los padres en aproximadamente 30% para oyentes desconocidos.

Las prioridades de la familia, en orden de importancia, son: (1) aumentar el vocabulario funcional expresivo de Mateo en ambos idiomas; (2) reducir las conductas de frustración relacionadas con la comunicación; (3) apoyar la transición a un salón de clases más estructurado el próximo año escolar.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Mateo asiste a la guardería Pequeños Soñadores Daycare de lunes a viernes, de 7:30 a.m. a 5:00 p.m.. Su maestra principal es la Sra. Marisol Ortiz, quien reporta que Mateo juega bien en paralelo pero rara vez inicia intercambios verbales con sus compañeros, incluido su amigo cercano Diego, de 2 años, con quien comparte mesa durante la merienda de las 9:15 a.m..

La rutina típica en casa incluye desayuno a las 6:45 a.m., recogida de la guardería alrededor de las 5:30 p.m., tiempo de juego con Camila y Rocky hasta la cena a las 6:30 p.m., baño a las 7:15 p.m. y rutina de sueño que comienza a las 7:45 p.m.. La familia indica que los momentos de mayor comunicación espontánea ocurren durante el baño y antes de dormir, cuando Mateo está más relajado y produce más intentos verbales.

Las sesiones de terapia del habla y lenguaje se realizan los martes y jueves, de 10:00 a.m. a 10:45 a.m., en el hogar de la familia, con la asistencia frecuente de la abuela, Rosa Ponce, cuando los padres no pueden estar presentes.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

La familia recibe apoyo nutricional del programa WIC del Condado de Durham, y la madre, Daniela, indicó que la nutricionista asignada ha sido útil para hablar sobre las texturas de alimentos y la aversión sensorial leve de Mateo. La familia también ha sido referida al Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Durham (DSS) para evaluar elegibilidad de asistencia de vivienda, y participa en talleres de crianza ofrecidos por Smart Start del Condado de Durham.

El pediatra de Mateo, el Dr. Esteban Méndez, de Duke Children's Primary Care Clinic, realizó la referencia inicial a la ASDIC después de notar el retraso de lenguaje durante la visita de los 24 meses. No se han identificado preocupaciones auditivas; una prueba de audición realizada el 2 de junio de 2026 resultó normal bilateralmente.

NIVELES ACTUALES DE DESARROLLO (RESULTADOS DE EVALUACIÓN)

La evaluación comprensiva más reciente, realizada el 18 de agosto de 2026, incluyó los siguientes instrumentos administrados de forma bilingüe con apoyo de intérprete:

La Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale ubicó a Mateo en un nivel de lenguaje receptivo equivalente a 18-20 meses y un nivel de lenguaje expresivo equivalente a 14-16 meses, indicando un retraso significativo en ambos dominios, más marcado en el área expresiva.

En las Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4), Mateo obtuvo una puntuación compuesta de comunicación receptiva de 76 (percentil 5) y una puntuación compuesta de comunicación expresiva de 70 (percentil 2), ambas dentro del rango deficiente. Las habilidades motoras gruesas y finas estuvieron dentro de límites normales, con puntuaciones compuestas de 95 y 91 respectivamente.

El Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) arrojó una puntuación estándar de 72 (intervalo de confianza 65-79), percentil 3, reflejando un inventario fonético reducido para la edad. Se observaron procesos fonológicos de omisión de consonante final y reducción de grupos consonánticos. Los fonemas /s/, /k/ y /ɾ/ estuvieron ausentes del repertorio espontáneo observado.

El Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5), administrado en español con normas de referencia apropiadas, arrojó una puntuación estándar de 74, equivalente de edad de 19 meses, consistente con los hallazgos de la Rossetti.

En muestras estructuradas de denominación, Mateo identificó correctamente objetos familiares con 8/10 aciertos cuando se le dio una opción de dos imágenes, pero su producción espontánea de dos palabras combinadas ocurrió solo en 3 de 15 oportunidades observadas durante una muestra de juego de 20 minutos, equivalente a 20%.

RESULTADOS DEL IFSP CON ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Mateo combinará dos palabras de forma espontánea para solicitar objetos o acciones deseadas en el 80% de las oportunidades observadas en el hogar y en la guardería, durante tres sesiones consecutivas. Estrategias: modelado con expansión lingüística usando el enfoque Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk"); los padres recibirán entrenamiento para seguir el interés comunicativo de Mateo y expandir sus intentos verbales en ambos idiomas; uso de claves mod cues (señalamiento visual más modelo verbal) durante el juego dirigido.

Resultado 2: Mateo producirá de forma precisa los sonidos /k/ y /s/ en posición inicial de palabra en el 70% de los intentos, usando palabras funcionales como "casa" y "sopa", con apoyo de claves táctiles-cinestésicas del enfoque PROMPT. Estrategias: práctica estructurada con min a mod cues según respuesta; generalización en rutinas de comida y baño; refuerzo de la familia en casa mediante juego con Rocky y objetos preferidos.

Resultado 3: La familia aumentará su confianza y conocimiento de estrategias de comunicación en el hogar, según lo reportado en una escala de autoevaluación familiar, pasando de un nivel bajo a un nivel moderado-alto en un período de seis meses. Estrategias: visitas domiciliarias quincenales con la coordinadora de servicios Patricia Gómez; materiales bilingües proporcionados por Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP; coordinación con la maestra Marisol Ortiz en Pequeños Soñadores Daycare para alinear estrategias de aula y hogar; uso del programa de comunicación por intercambio de imágenes (PECS) como apoyo visual complementario en momentos de alta frustración.

FECHAS Y CÓDIGOS DE SERVICIO

El IFSP inicial fue desarrollado el 15 de marzo de 2026, con la primera revisión semestral completada el 14 de septiembre de 2026, según se documenta en este informe. La próxima revisión está programada para el 12 de marzo de 2027, y la evaluación anual completa deberá realizarse antes del 15 de marzo de 2027 para mantener la elegibilidad continua bajo la Parte C.

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Client Name: Juan Carlos Ramírez Soto (called "Juanito" at home)
Date of Birth: August 14, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Sex: Male
Case/Record #: 2026-0417-JR
Medicaid ID: 544872193A
Evaluation Dates: October 6, 2026 and October 8, 2026
Report Date: October 11, 2026
Referring Provider: Dr. Amara Chen, pediatrician
Service Coordinator: Nadia Fournier, Piedmont CDSA
Interpreter: Marisol Peña, certified medical interpreter

Referral Source:

[X] Spanish  [X] English  [ ] Other

[X] Yes  [ ] No

BACKGROUND AND REASON FOR REFERRAL

Juanito is a 4;2-year-old bilingual boy who was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Amara Chen following a well-child visit on September 2, 2026, at which his mother, Guadalupe Ramírez (known to family and friends as "Lupita"), expressed concern that Juanito's expressive language had not progressed at the same rate as that of his older sister, Luz Ramírez Soto, at a comparable age. Lupita reported that Juanito currently uses mostly single words and a small number of two-word combinations in both Spanish and English, that unfamiliar listeners frequently cannot understand him, and that he has begun to show frustration and occasional tantrums when he cannot make himself understood at home or at the grandmother's apartment where he spends weekdays.

Juanito's father, Jesús Soto (called "Chuy" by the family), works full time as a line supervisor at Ferrum Steel Fabrication in Concord and was present for the second evaluation session on October 8, 2026. He reported similar concerns and noted that Juanito is "easier to understand in Spanish than in English, but even in Spanish he mixes up his sounds." Both parents denied any family history of autism but reported that a paternal cousin received speech services as a toddler. The family lives at 132 Sendero Lane, Concord, NC 28025, in Cabarrus County.

Juanito previously received early intervention services through an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) coordinated through Piedmont CDSA from March 2024 through August 2025, exiting Part C eligibility shortly after his third birthday. His most recent IFSP outcomes, Outcome 2 (expressive vocabulary growth) and Outcome 3 (functional play and joint attention), were reported by his former early-intervention speech therapist, Hannah Oduya, M.S., CCC-SLP, as "partially met" at his exit visit. No records of standardized testing from that period were available for this report; the family was unable to locate the final IFSP summary.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Juanito was born at 39 weeks gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery at CaroMed Women's Hospital in Charlotte. Birth weight was 7 lbs 4 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lupita reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care; she denied tobacco, alcohol, or substance use during pregnancy. Juanito was discharged home with his mother on day two of life and has had no NICU admissions.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with 6 documented episodes between 8 months and 24 months of age, managed with antibiotics. Bilateral myringotomy with tympanostomy tube placement (CPT 69436) was performed on February 11, 2024 by Dr. Rebecca Alvord, pediatric ENT. Tubes remain in place per the family's report, and Juanito's most recent hearing screening, conducted at Charlotte ENT & Audiology Associates on June 3, 2026, indicated bilateral hearing within normal limits with Type A tympanograms bilaterally. No current audiology concerns were reported.

Juanito reached gross and fine motor milestones within normal limits: sat independently at 6 months, walked independently at 13 months. Feeding history is unremarkable aside from mild picky eating; parents deny any oral-motor feeding concerns, choking, or aspiration history. He is up to date on immunizations per his pediatrician, Dr. Amara Chen. No history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness was reported. Vision was last screened at 4 years and was within normal limits.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The household is bilingual Spanish-English. Lupita reported that Spanish is the primary language spoken at home between herself, her mother, and the children, while Chuy speaks a mix of Spanish and English with Juanito depending on context. Juanito's grandmother, Rosa Hernández, who cares for him on weekdays while his parents work, speaks almost exclusively Spanish with him and reports that he is "más tranquilo" (calmer) and somewhat more intelligible in Spanish than in English. Rosa Hernández lives in the same household and is described by the family as Juanito's primary daytime caregiver.

Juanito's older sister, Luz Ramírez Soto, age 7, is enrolled in second grade and is reportedly fully bilingual with age-appropriate language skills in both languages. Lupita stated that Luz Ramírez Soto often "translates" for her brother with unfamiliar adults and sometimes finishes his sentences for him, a pattern this clinician discussed with the family as something to monitor, since it may reduce Juanito's opportunities for independent communication attempts.

Extended family involved in Juanito's care include a paternal aunt, Paz Soto, who provides occasional weekend childcare, and a cousin close in age, William Soto (called "Will" by the family), with whom Juanito plays most weekends. Parents reported that Juanito is more verbal and animated when playing with Will than in most other settings. The family also has a dog, Max, whom Juanito frequently references in play; during the home observation he was heard saying "Max go" while pointing toward the back door.

Juanito briefly attended Sunshine Beginnings Daycare in Concord between January 2025 and May 2025, where his lead teacher, Ms. Keisha Johnson, reportedly expressed concerns about his intelligibility relative to same-age peers in the classroom. The family withdrew him from Sunshine Beginnings Daycare for financial reasons and he has remained in home-based care with Rosa Hernández since that time. He is not currently enrolled in any preschool or Pre-K program, though Lupita indicated interest in enrolling him at Little Explorers Preschool in Concord for the coming school year pending the outcome of this evaluation.

DEVELOPMENTAL AND EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Parents report that Juanito said his first words around 18 months, later than his sister, who reportedly said first words around 11 months. He began combining two words around 3;0, significantly later than typical milestones for either language. Current expressive output per parent report includes an estimated 75-100 intelligible single words, with inconsistent two-word combinations such as "más agua" ("more water") and "go car."

Socially, Juanito is described as affectionate, sociable with familiar adults, and increasingly withdrawn with unfamiliar listeners when he is not understood. Chuy reported that Juanito has begun hitting or throwing toys "when nobody understands him," which both parents attribute to communicative frustration rather than a primary behavioral concern. Play skills were reported as age-appropriate, including pretend play with toy vehicles and simple turn-taking games with Will and Luz Ramírez Soto.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

During both evaluation sessions, Juanito separated easily from his caregivers and engaged readily with this clinician and with Marisol Peña, the interpreter, using a combination of gesture, single words, and some jargon. Attention to task was adequate for structured testing with frequent breaks and preferred toys (cars, blocks) used as reinforcement. Juanito demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking in play-based tasks. Intelligibility was judged to be fair in known context and poor out of context, consistent with parent report. No atypical behaviors suggestive of autism spectrum disorder were observed during this evaluation; however, given his communicative frustration, continued monitoring of social-emotional development was recommended.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

The following formal and informal measures were administered across both languages as appropriate, with interpretation support from Marisol Peña for Spanish-language administration and family interview:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish and English editions
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Expressive One-Word Picture Vocabulary Test, Fourth Edition (EOWPVT-4), Spanish-Bilingual Edition
- Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Test, Third Edition (REEL-3) parent questionnaire
- Spontaneous language sample (English and Spanish), approximately 50 utterances each
- Oral-peripheral examination
- Parent/caregiver interview and clinical observation

TEST RESULTS

Receptive and Expressive Language (PLS-5, Spanish-English administration):

| Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 5th | 2;9 |
| Expressive Communication | 71 | 3rd | 2;6 |
| Total Language Score | 72 | 3rd | 2;7 |

Confidence intervals (95%) were 70-82 for Auditory Comprehension and 65-77 for Expressive Communication, placing both domains within the moderately-severely delayed range relative to same-age peers in both languages.

Expressive Vocabulary (EOWPVT-4, Spanish-Bilingual Edition):
Standard Score 68, Percentile Rank 2nd, Age Equivalent 2;8. Juanito was credited for responses given in either language, per bilingual scoring guidelines.

Articulation (GFTA-3):
Raw Score 34, Standard Score 73, Percentile Rank 4th. Sound errors noted included final consonant deletion, stopping of fricatives, and gliding of liquids. Specific error patterns included substitution of [w] for /ɾ/ (e.g., "wojo" for "rojo"), deletion of final consonants (e.g., "ga" for "gato"), and stopping of /s/ to [t] in word-initial position. In English, he produced "tar" for "car" and "poon" for "spoon," consistent with the same error patterns across both languages, supporting a phonological rather than purely articulatory basis.

Caregiver Report (REEL-3):
Receptive Language Age Equivalent 2;10; Expressive Language Age Equivalent 2;4; Combined Language Age Equivalent 2;7, consistent with direct testing.

Oral-Peripheral Examination:
Structures and function of the lips, tongue, hard and soft palate, and jaw were within normal limits for speech. No evidence of structural abnormality, dysarthria, or apraxic features was observed. Diadochokinetic rates were age-appropriate.

Language Sample Analysis:
In the English sample, Juanito produced primarily single-word and two-word utterances, with 3 of 20 utterances containing three or more words. In the Spanish sample, he produced a comparable mean length of utterance, with 4 of 20 utterances at three or more words, and demonstrated slightly higher intelligibility, estimated at 65% in context compared with 55% in English. He required moderate cues to produce target words during structured tasks and minimal cues during preferred play-based activities. Target word "agua" was elicited with min cues and produced as "[EW] awa," reflecting a glide substitution for the medial consonant.

SUMMARY AND CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Juanito presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, accompanied by a moderate phonological disorder characterized by consistent, language-independent error patterns (final consonant deletion, stopping, gliding). His difficulties are not attributable to hearing loss, oral-motor structural impairment, or bilingual language exposure alone; his error patterns and language scores are depressed relative to typical bilingual peers in both of his languages, which supports a true language disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition variability. His sociable affect, intact play skills, and appropriate joint attention argue against an autism spectrum disorder at this time, though continued monitoring of behavior related to communicative frustration is warranted.

Diagnostic impressions, for coding purposes, correspond to ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and ICD-10 F80.0 (phonological disorder). This evaluation was billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Juanito is recommended for speech-language therapy twice weekly, bilingual Spanish-English service delivery, for an initial period of 12 weeks with re-evaluation of progress at that time.
2. Treatment approaches recommended for this case include Hanen (It Takes Two to Talk) coaching for caregivers to increase responsive language strategies in the home, PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing to address the motor-based components of his sound errors, and the Cycles approach for phonological pattern remediation given the consistency of his error patterns across both languages.
3. Given his limited expressive output and frustration behaviors, introduction of a modified PECS (Picture Exchange Communication System) visual support at home is recommended as a bridge strategy to reduce communicative frustration, to be faded as verbal output increases.
4. If expressive vocabulary growth remains slow despite direct treatment, a trial of the Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol is recommended to target motor planning for multisyllabic word production.
5. Caregiver training, including Rosa Hernández and both parents, in home-based strategies consistent with It Takes Two to Talk principles is strongly recommended, given that Rosa Hernández serves as the primary daytime caregiver.
6. Family is encouraged to continue exposing Juanito to both Spanish and English rather than restricting either language, as bilingual exposure is not contributing to his disorder and dual-language input supports long-term outcomes.
7. Continued collaboration with Dr. Amara Chen regarding monitoring of middle ear status is recommended given history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement.
8. Re-evaluation of behavioral/social-emotional functioning is recommended if frustration-related behaviors increase or if autism spectrum features emerge, with referral to Dr. Priya Mehta, developmental pediatrician, as needed.
9. Family should contact Piedmont CDSA service coordinator Nadia Fournier regarding possible continued service coordination support given the family's prior Part C involvement, even though Juanito has aged out of Part C eligibility.

Sessions will be conducted in both Spanish and English as appropriate to the activity, with Marisol Peña available by phone for interpretation support during the Wednesday home visits as needed. The family was advised that the Monday clinic slot may shift to accommodate Chuy's work schedule at Ferrum Steel Fabrication, and the clinic will confirm any changes by phone at (704) 555-0188 or email at ramirez.familia2022@mailbox.com.

This report, along with a recommendation for continued bilingual speech-language therapy, was discussed in detail with Lupita and Chuy at the conclusion of the second evaluation session. Both parents verbalized understanding and agreement with the recommendations above and signed consent for treatment to begin. A copy of this report has been provided to the family and, with signed release, will be forwarded to Dr. Amara Chen and to Piedmont CDSA.
