SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Client: Mateo Hernández
Date of Birth: June 14, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Evaluation Dates: August 11, 2025 and August 18, 2025
Report Date: August 25, 2025
Parents/Guardians: Lucía Hernández and Carlos Hernández
Home Address: 4821 Persimmon Ridge Lane, Bramblewood, NC 28605
Home Phone: (828) 555-0271
Medicaid ID: 724815903B
Case/Record #: 4471-SLP
Primary Language(s) of the Home: Spanish and English
Referral Source: Dr. Nadia Patel, pediatrician, and Catawba County CDSA
Evaluator: Jennifer Álvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (Spanish/English)

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Patel at his well-child visit on July 2, 2025 due to parent and teacher concern regarding limited intelligibility and short sentence length in both Spanish and English. Mateo currently receives early intervention services through Catawba County CDSA under IFSP Outcome 2, and his service coordinator requested an updated bilingual evaluation to inform the upcoming six-month review. Mateo's parents, Lucía and Carlos Hernández, also report that his teacher at Little Oaks Preschool, Ms. Lopez, has noted that Mateo is sometimes difficult to understand during circle time in Ms. Lopez's room and tends to point or gesture rather than use words with peers.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestation at Piedmont Regional Health System – Riverside Campus, weighing 5 lb 4 oz (2,380 g), with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. He spent 18 days in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at Piedmont Regional Health System – Riverside Campus for respiratory support and feeding difficulties related to prematurity. His mother, Lucía Hernández, reports no other significant complications during the NICU stay and that Mateo was discharged home in stable condition.

Mateo has a history of recurrent otitis media beginning around 8 months of age, with at least six documented ear infections prior to his second birthday. He was referred to Piedmont Regional Health System Pediatric ENT & Audiology – University Campus, where he was evaluated by Dr. Samuel Ortiz, pediatric otolaryngologist, and underwent bilateral myringotomy with tympanostomy tube placement at age 22 months. Audiologic testing conducted at that same campus by Dr. Erin Choi, audiologist, most recently on March 3, 2025, showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally, with normal tympanometry. Carlos reports that Mateo has not had an ear infection since the tubes were placed and that his hearing is now considered normal by Dr. Choi's team.

Developmental milestones were reported as mildly delayed. Mateo sat independently at 8 months, crawled at 10 months, and walked independently at 17 months. Lucía reports that his first words emerged around 20 months, later than his older sister, and that word combinations did not appear consistently until closer to 3;6.

Family and Language History

Mateo lives at home with his parents, Lucía and Carlos Hernández, and his older sister, Sol Hernández, age 7. Lucía was born in Honduras and is a native Spanish speaker; Carlos was born in Hickory and is bilingual, though he reports feeling more comfortable in English for technical or work-related conversation. Lucía reports that approximately 70% of the language spoken in the home is Spanish, with English used increasingly by Sol and, to a lesser extent, by Mateo, since starting preschool.

Mateo's maternal grandmother, doña Lupe, cares for him two to three afternoons a week while his parents work and speaks almost exclusively Spanish with him. Carlos works at Ridgeline Furniture Manufacturing, and Lucía recently began part-time work at Sunrise Senior Living. A family friend and neighbor, Mr. Tom, occasionally drives Mateo to therapy appointments when both parents are working.

Prior to enrolling at Little Oaks Preschool, Mateo attended Los Pollitos Learning Cottage from age 18 months to 3;8, where his primary teacher was Miss Ana. Lucía reports that Miss Ana frequently commented that Mateo seemed to understand more than he could express, and that he often became frustrated when peers at Los Pollitos Learning Cottage could not understand his requests. Mateo has a close friend from that program, Diego, whom the family still sees occasionally on weekends. The family also has a dog, Luna, who Lucía says Mateo talks to frequently at home, often in single words or short phrases.

Sol is reportedly a strong student at Cedar Run Elementary and sometimes helps interpret for Mateo when he is not understood by English-speaking peers. Lucía and Carlos both expressed hope that Mateo will continue developing both languages and did not want him discouraged from using Spanish at home.

Educational and Early Intervention History

Mateo was referred to Catawba County CDSA at age 2;4 following parent concern about limited vocabulary. His service coordinator, Marisol Peña, has coordinated services including developmental therapy and, more recently, speech-language therapy delivered in the home and at Little Oaks Preschool. Mateo's current IFSP includes IFSP Outcome 1 (functional communication across settings) and IFSP Outcome 2 (increased intelligibility in connected speech). This evaluation was requested to update present levels of performance ahead of the IFSP review scheduled for September 15, 2025.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

Mateo was evaluated across two sessions, totaling approximately 2 hours 15 minutes, in a combination of English and Spanish, with instructions and stimuli presented in each child's dominant response language per item. Jennifer Álvarez, the evaluating clinician, is fully bilingual and administered all measures without the need for interpretation. Lucía Hernández was present for both sessions and provided case history information and a language sample context; Carlos Hernández joined briefly during the second session.

Assessment included the following: parent interview, review of records from Catawba County CDSA and Little Oaks Preschool, oral mechanism examination, hearing screening review, standardized testing in both languages, dynamic assessment of phonology and morphosyntax, spontaneous language sampling, and classroom-based observation at Little Oaks Preschool in Ms. Lopez's room on August 14, 2025.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and testing materials. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks, requiring occasional redirection ("Mateo, mira aquí") but no significant off-task behavior. Rapport was established quickly, and Mateo appeared to enjoy turn-taking games. He used a mix of single words, gestures, and short phrases in both languages to communicate, and his intelligibility was estimated at approximately 40-50% to an unfamiliar listener in connected speech, improving to 70-80% with context. He required moderate cues to produce multi-word utterances consistently and minimal cues to repair unintelligible productions when a model was provided.

TEST RESULTS

Receptive and Expressive Language

Mateo was administered the Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition, Spanish-English Bilingual Edition (PLS-5), with items presented in the child's stronger language of response for each item set, consistent with conceptual scoring procedures.

| Measure | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% Confidence Interval | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12th | 76–88 | 3;2–3;8 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 79 | 8th | 73–85 | 2;9–3;3 |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | 78 | 7th | 72–84 | — |

Results suggest expressive and receptive language skills falling in the below-average to moderately delayed range relative to same-age monolingual norms. Given Mateo's simultaneous bilingual exposure, conceptual scoring (crediting a concept if demonstrated in either language) was used to reduce the risk of over-identifying a disorder based on language difference alone.

Bilingual Phonology and Morphosyntax

To further distinguish language difference from language disorder, the Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) was administered.

| Subtest | Score | Percentile | 95% Confidence Interval | Severity Rating |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BESA Phonology, English | 6 | 9th | 4–8 | Moderate |
| BESA Phonology, Spanish | 7 | 16th | 5–9 | Mild-Moderate |
| BESA Morphosyntax, English | 5 | 5th | 3–7 | Moderate-Severe |
| BESA Morphosyntax, Spanish | 8 | 25th | 6–10 | Mild |

Performance across both languages on the BESA, particularly the morphosyntax subtests, suggests a language disorder affecting both languages rather than a language difference alone, as deficits were present even in Mateo's stronger language, Spanish.

Articulation and Phonology

The Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) was administered in English, supplemented by informal Spanish phonology sampling.

| Measure | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% Confidence Interval | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | 81 | 10th | 75–87 | 3;0–3;6 |

Mateo demonstrated the following phonological patterns across both languages: final consonant deletion (e.g., "mas" for /mas/ produced as [ma]), stopping of fricatives (e.g., /s/ realized as [t]), and gliding of liquids (e.g., /ɾ/ realized as [w] in words such as "carro", produced as [kawo]). During single-word probing, Mateo was asked to name a picture of the sun and produced the target word "sol" as [tol], consistent with the stopping pattern noted above; this target was selected for its word-initial /s/ and was unrelated to any family member's name. He also produced "casa" as [kata] and "sopa" as [topa], further supporting a consistent fricative-stopping pattern rather than an isolated error.

Oral Mechanism and Hearing

Oral mechanism examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech production, with adequate range of motion, strength, and coordination of the lips, tongue, and jaw. No signs of dysarthria or apraxia of speech were noted; errors were consistent with a phonological process disorder rather than a motor speech disorder. Hearing was reported as within normal limits per the most recent audiologic evaluation at Piedmont Regional Health System Pediatric ENT & Audiology – University Campus on March 3, 2025, and a hearing screening conducted informally during this evaluation raised no new concerns.

Language Sample Analysis

A 50-utterance spontaneous language sample was collected during free play with Lucía and during structured play with the examiner. Mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLU-m) was calculated separately by language.

| Context | MLU-m | Range |
|---|---|---|
| Spanish (with Lucía) | 2.8 | 2.1–3.4 |
| English (with examiner) | 2.3 | 1.7–2.9 |

Grammatical morphemes frequently omitted in English included third-person singular -s, past tense -ed, and auxiliary "is" (e.g., "Mateo go house" coded as [EW] for an early-word-order error in the sample). In Spanish, Mateo showed inconsistent use of grammatical gender agreement and frequent omission of articles. Pragmatically, Mateo used gesture to supplement verbal requests in 8 of 10 observed communicative attempts and initiated joint attention appropriately with both the examiner and his mother.

Classroom Observation

During a 30-minute observation at Little Oaks Preschool in Ms. Lopez's room, Mateo was observed during circle time and center-based play. Ms. Lopez reported that Mateo participates willingly but is often not understood by peers, including his classmate Diego, and will sometimes abandon an attempt to communicate rather than repeat himself. Mateo was observed to use primarily English at school, reserving Spanish for interactions with the examiner and briefly with Ms. Lopez, who is also bilingual.

IMPRESSIONS

Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and a phonological process disorder affecting both English and Spanish, consistent with ICD-10 codes F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (phonological disorder). Deficits were observed across both languages and across multiple measures, including conceptually scored standardized testing, bilingual criterion-referenced measures, and naturalistic language sampling, supporting a true language disorder rather than a language difference attributable to bilingual or dialectal variation. Mateo's history of chronic otitis media and NICU stay, along with his family history of later-emerging language in Sol per parent report, are considered contributing but not sole explanatory factors, as Mateo's current profile is more significantly delayed than typical bilingual acquisition patterns would predict at 4;2.

Mateo's strengths include good attention, strong nonverbal communication and gesture use, willingness to engage in structured tasks, and responsiveness to cueing, all of which are favorable prognostic indicators. Family involvement, including support from Lucía, Carlos, doña Lupe, and Sol, is a significant strength and should be leveraged in treatment planning.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo is recommended for individual speech-language therapy twice weekly for 30-minute sessions (CPT 92507), to be delivered bilingually, targeting both phonological and morphosyntactic goals across English and Spanish.
2. Continued coordination with Catawba County CDSA and service coordinator Marisol Peña is recommended to update IFSP Outcome 1 and IFSP Outcome 2 to reflect current present levels and to add a specific phonological goal targeting word-final consonants and fricatives in both languages.
3. A phonological awareness and articulation treatment approach, incorporating principles from Cycles phonological remediation, is recommended given Mateo's consistent, patterned error types.
4. Caregiver training is recommended for Lucía, Carlos, and doña Lupe using a Hanen-based coaching model (e.g., "It Takes Two to Talk") to support language stimulation strategies in the home across both languages.
5. Collaboration with Ms. Lopez at Little Oaks Preschool is recommended to support peer-directed communication strategies in the classroom, including structured peer supports during center time with classmates such as Diego.
6. Continued audiologic monitoring is recommended given Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media; a repeat hearing screening is suggested at Mateo's next well-child visit with Dr. Patel, with referral back to Piedmont Regional Health System Pediatric ENT & Audiology – University Campus if any regression in hearing status is suspected.
7. Home practice targeting word-initial and word-final /s/ is recommended using meaningful, high-frequency words, including the target word "sol" (sun), given its functional relevance and clear phonetic contrast; families should be advised that this target refers to the word for "sun" and is unrelated to any family member's name.
8. Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and determine continued eligibility for services, with results to be shared with Catawba County CDSA at the scheduled IFSP review.

This evaluation and these recommendations were discussed with Lucía Hernández and Carlos Hernández on August 25, 2025. Please contact the undersigned with any questions regarding this report.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Álvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

basado en los resultados de esta evaluación bilingüe mateo hernández cruz presenta un trastorno mixto de lenguaje receptivo-expresivo con un componente significativo de trastorno fonológico del habla estos hallazgos están presentes en ambos idiomas español e inglés lo cual confirma que no se trata simplemente de una diferencia dialectal o de exposición bilingüe normal sino de un verdadero trastorno de comunicación

6. se recomienda revisión del plan de tratamiento en 90 días con reevaluación formal en aproximadamente 6 meses fecha tentativa de reevaluación march 2027

7. PAINF debe ser notificado de estos resultados para determinar elegibilidad continua de servicios bajo intervención temprana parte c la coordinadora brenda ingram fue contactada el september 24, 2026 y recibirá copia de este informe

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) — Six-Month Review

Child: Mateo Flores Rodríguez ("Teo")
DOB: 04/02/2024   Age at review: 2;6
Child ID: NC-ITP-88214   Medicaid #: 914772630A
Address: 1420 Sardis Lane, Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, NC 28270
Home phone: (704) 555-0148
Mother: Lucía Rodríguez, cell (704) 555-0162
Father: Javier Flores, cell (704) 555-0179
Service Coordinator: Brenda Walsh, Piedmont Regional CDSA, Charlotte Office
CDSA phone: (704) 555-0120   CDSA email: bwalsh@piedmontregionalcdsa.org
CDSA website: www.piedmontregionalcdsa.org
Initial IFSP: November 14, 2024   Review date: May 9, 2026
Interpreter: Marisol Nuñez (Spanish, in person)
SLP: Ana Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners
SLP email: ana.castillo@carolinapedstherapy.com

BACKGROUND / HISTORIA MÉDICA

Pt born 34 wks gestation at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center – Dilworth Campus, Level III NICU, 04/02/2024, b/c maternal preeclampsia. Birth wt 4 lbs 1 oz, Apgar 6/8. Teo spent approx 3 wks in the NICU, d/c'd 04/23/2024 per neonatologist Dr. Anil Patel. Mother Lucía Rodríguez reports pt had feeding tube x 10 days, "no quería comer, lloraba mucho" (did not want to eat, cried a lot). Pediatrician Dr. Sarah Kim at Atrium Health Pineville Pediatric Associates followed closely for weight gain thru approx 9 mo. No other significant hx; hearing screen passed at birth, repeat screen ordered at 18 mo 2/2 parental concern re: speech delay.

ENT/AUDIOLOGÍA

Teo seen 02/11/2026 at Duke Health Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Matthews Campus for f/u audiologic eval, ordered by Dr. Robert Chen (ENT). Audiologist Dr. Lindsey Moore completed VRA (visual reinforcement audiometry); results WNL bilaterally, no hx of recurrent OM reported by CG. Tympanometry type A bilaterally. No surgical intervention recommended. Father Javier Flores drove pt to appt, arrived 9:40 AM, seen 10:00 AM–10:45 AM.

FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES / PREOCUPACIONES DE LA FAMILIA

Reviewed w/ Lucía Rodríguez and Javier Flores via interpreter Marisol Nuñez. Mother states, "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no usa palabras, solo señala y grita cuando quiere algo" (what worries me most is that Teo doesn't use words, he just points and screams when he wants something). She added "en la guardería dicen que se frustra mucho, pero en casa yo lo entiendo casi todo" (at daycare they say he gets very frustrated, but at home I understand him almost everything). Father reports concern is mainly "que hable en las dos idiomas, inglés y español, para la escuela" (that he speak in both languages, English and Spanish, for school). Family priority remains functional communication at home and daycare; CG also requested more strategies for mealtime, as pt "avienta la comida cuando está frustrado" (throws food when he's frustrated).

Family resources: maternal grandmother Rosa Delgado lives nearby and provides care approx 3 days/wk while parents work; sitter Yolanda Pérez covers evenings 2x/wk. Older sister Camila Flores (5 yo) attends kindergarten and is described as "muy paciente con su hermanito" (very patient with her little brother) per mother. Family dog, Luna, is a favorite motivator during home practice per report.

DAILY ROUTINES / RUTINAS DIARIAS

Wake approx 7:00 AM; breakfast w/ CG Rosa Delgado at home. Daycare drop-off at Little Explorers Daycare & Preschool by 8:15 AM; pick-up by mother Lucía Rodríguez or father Javier Flores approx 5:30 PM. Teacher Jennifer Thompson reports pt plays alongside peers, esp Emma and Josue, but uses mostly gestures; 1:1 support offered during circle time. Lunch at daycare 11:30 AM; nap 12:30 PM–2:00 PM. Dinner at home approx 6:00 PM, bath 7:00 PM, bed 7:30 PM. Mother notes bedtime routine incl. 2-3 books, mix of English/Spanish; pt enjoys pointing to pictures and vocalizing. Weekend routine less structured; family attends iglesia (church) Sun mornings where Teo is often w/ Rosa Delgado in the nursery.

OTHER AGENCIES / OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

Family receives WIC benefits thru Mecklenburg County WIC (nutrition support, formula supplement to 18 mo). Smart Start of Mecklenburg County provided one-time childcare subsidy referral 01/2025. No DSS involvement reported. Pt is not enrolled w/ any other EI provider at this time. Neighbor Carmen occasionally drives Lucía Rodríguez to appts when father Javier Flores is at work; father employed full-time at Carolina Logistics Group, mother works part-time at Sunrise Cleaning Services, schedule variable.

ASSESSMENT RESULTS / RESULTADOS DE LA EVALUACIÓN

Standardized and informal measures re-administered to track progress toward outcomes. Administered in clinic by Ana Castillo, bilingual administration w/ parent report supplementing direct testing per best practice for sequential bilingual toddlers.

Date | Measure | Score | CI | Percentile
05/02/2026 | PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | SS 73 | 68-79 | 4th
05/02/2026 | PLS-5 Expressive Communication | SS 65 | 60-71 | 1st
05/02/2026 | REEL-3 (Spanish form) | SS 70 | 64-76 | 2nd
11/08/2024 | PLS-5 Expressive Communication | SS 58 | 52-64 | <1st

Progress noted in expressive SS from 58 to 65 over 6 mo interval, still below avg range (avg 85-115). Informal bilingual lang sample (50 utterance SALT sample, both langs combined) yielded MLU 1.4 morphemes; most utterances single-word or unintelligible vocalization coded [EW]. Oral mech exam WNL; no concerns for structural etiology. Dx consistent w/ expressive lang delay, ICD-10 F80.1; CPT code for eval 92523, modifier GN.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Receptive: pt follows 1-step directions approx 7/10 trials w/ mod cues (gestural + visual); understands significantly more than he produces per parent report, consistent w/ expressive-receptive gap typical of toddlers w/ expressive delay.

Expressive: approx 10 words/approximations noted across both langs: "mamá," "agua" (approximated [awa]), "up," "more," "no," "Luna" (dog's name, approximated [una] — note: here the target itself is the pet's name, marked below). When attempting Luna's name pt produces [una], omitting initial consonant /l/. Pt attempted "pelota" (ball) → [bota], substitution of /p/ for /b/ and deletion of medial syllable. Phonetic inventory limited to approx 8 consonants incl /m/, /b/, /n/, /d/; stimulable for /k/ in isolation w/ max cues.

During session 04/28/2026 (clinic, 3:15 PM–4:00 PM), pt used PECS-style picture exchange to request "más galletas" independently 3 of 5 opportunities, a notable gain from baseline 0/5 at IFSP start. Pragmatics: eye contact variable, joint attention emerging w/ mod cues, some protesting behaviors (throwing, screaming) when communication breaks down, consistent w/ parent-reported mealtime frustration above.

Social-emotional: pt interacts w/ sister Camila Flores frequently at home; CG Rosa Delgado reports pt "se ríe mucho con su hermana" (laughs a lot with his sister). At daycare, teacher Jennifer Thompson notes improved tolerance for group activities over past 3 mo.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Teo will use 15 functional words/word approximations across English and Spanish to request and comment, observed by CG during 3 consecutive home visits.
Strategies: Modeling target words in both langs during daily routines (meals, bath, play); CG trained in Hanen "OWL" (Observe, Wait, Listen) strategy during 02/2026 coaching session; continue PECS picture exchange at home and daycare; SLP to provide bilingual word list to Jennifer Thompson at Little Explorers Daycare & Preschool for consistency across settings.

Outcome 2: Teo will combine 2 words ("more juice," "mamá up") in 4 of 5 opportunities across 2 consecutive sessions, to support emerging syntax in both langs.
Strategies: Expansion technique (adult repeats + adds 1 word to child's utterance); PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing during artic/motor planning practice for CV and CVC shapes; continue following child's lead per Hanen principles; home practice log reviewed at each session.

Outcome 3: Family will report decreased mealtime frustration behaviors (throwing, screaming) from current baseline of approx 4-5x/week to 1-2x/week or fewer, measured by parent log.
Strategies: Teach CG to offer 2 visual choices at mealtime rather than open-ended questions; model simple requesting phrases ("quiero más," "all done") paired w/ gesture; coordinate w/ pediatrician Dr. Sarah Kim re: any feeding/sensory concerns if behaviors persist past 3 mo; SLP to check in w/ family by phone at 6-wk mark.

SERVICE DELIVERY

Direct SLP services continue 1x/wk, 30 min, in home, provided by Ana Castillo thru Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners. Session example 05/05/2026: arrived 4:00 PM, began 4:05 PM (brief delay, CG finishing phone call w/ Brenda Walsh re: review paperwork), ended 4:35 PM. CG Lucía Rodríguez present for full session, implemented modeling strategy independently 2x w/o prompt from SLP — positive sign for carryover. Service coordination visits by Brenda Walsh quarterly; next SC visit scheduled 08/11/2026.

Transition planning: family informed that pt will transition from Infant-Toddler Program services around 36 mo per state guidelines; SC Brenda Walsh to begin transition conference planning approx 90 days prior to 3rd birthday. Family verbalized understanding; mother asked clarifying question re: preschool options, referred to Mecklenburg County Schools Exceptional Children's Division for future eval request.

SIGNATURES

Reviewed and agreed to by:

Lucía Rodríguez, Mother — Date: 05/09/2026
Javier Flores, Father — Date: 05/09/2026
Ana Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP — Date: 05/09/2026
Brenda Walsh, Service Coordinator, Piedmont Regional CDSA, Charlotte Office — Date: 05/09/2026

Next review scheduled: November 9, 2026. Questions prior to next review may be directed to SLP at ana.castillo@carolinapedstherapy.com or CDSA at (704) 555-0120 / www.piedmontregionalcdsa.org.

215 Hillsboro Street, Pittsboro, NC 27312

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Ramírez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: January 14, 2024
Age at Evaluation: 2;8
Gestational Age at Birth: 37 weeks
Evaluation Date(s): October 3, 2026
Report Date: October 6, 2026
Evaluator: Jennifer Alvarado-Pike, M.S., CCC-SLP (bilingual English/Spanish)
Referral Source: Dinora Castellanos, Service Coordinator, Children's Developmental Services Agency of the Triangle
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Fernanda Ramírez Mejía (mother), Carlos Alberto Flores Ortiz (father)
Home Address: 1427 Holly Grove Lane, Siler City, NC 27344 (Chatham County)
Medicaid ID: 800473921B
Insurance Member ID: WCB48217305
NC ITP Child ID: ITP-2025-10483
Record/Authorization Number: AUTH-2026-003871

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo ("Teo") is a 2;8-year-old bilingual Spanish/English-speaking boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation as part of his annual Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) review through the Children's Developmental Services Agency of the Triangle. Teo was initially referred to the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program at 14 months of age after a developmental screening completed at the Chatham County Health Department flagged delays in expressive language. He has been enrolled in early intervention services since May 20, 2025, when his initial IFSP was developed, and received a six-month review on November 18, 2025. This evaluation was requested by his service coordinator, Dinora Castellanos, to update present levels of functioning and determine continued eligibility and goal direction ahead of his transition planning meeting. Lucía and Carlos report ongoing concern that Teo's expressive vocabulary, in both Spanish and English, remains well below that of same-age peers, and that he is difficult to understand even by familiar listeners.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Birth and Medical History

Teo was born on January 14, 2024 at 37 weeks gestation via scheduled cesarean section at UNC Rex Hospital in Raleigh, NC, following a pregnancy complicated by gestational hypertension. Birth weight was 5 lbs 14 oz. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. He required a brief stay in the special care nursery for monitoring of transient respiratory distress but was discharged home with his mother on day three of life. Lucía reports no additional complications during the pregnancy aside from the hypertension, which was managed with medication.

Teo's early medical history is notable for recurrent otitis media, with his pediatrician, Dr. Michael Osei, documenting six episodes between 8 months and 22 months of age. He underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on June 12, 2025 at UNC Children's Hospital, after which his parents report a noticeable improvement in his responsiveness to sound and attention to speech, though expressive language gains have been slower to follow. A diagnostic audiological evaluation completed on July 8, 2025 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally following tube placement. Teo has no known history of seizures, significant head trauma, or hospitalization beyond the newborn period and the tube placement procedure. He is not currently on any medications. His immunizations are reported as up to date per Dr. Osei's records.

Developmental milestones were reported as mildly delayed in the gross motor domain, with independent walking achieved at 16 months, and more significantly delayed in communication. Carlos reports that Teo did not produce his first recognizable words, in either language, until approximately 20 months, and that his vocabulary growth since has been slow and inconsistent. Fine motor and self-care skills are reported as age-appropriate by both parents and by his current classroom teacher.

Family and Language History

Teo lives with both parents, his older sister Valentina Flores Ramírez (age 6), and his maternal grandmother, Rosa Mejía, who moved in with the family in January 2026 to help with childcare while both parents work full time. The family's pet, a mixed-breed dog named Max, is also in the home and is frequently mentioned by Teo during play. Teo's maternal aunt, Carmen Ramírez Mejía, lives nearby in Siler City and provides occasional babysitting on weekends.

Lucía and Carlos both immigrated to the United States from La Esperanza, Intibucá, Honduras, a small mountain village, approximately eight years ago, prior to Teo's birth. Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home; Carlos reports limited conversational English, while Lucía is more comfortable in English due to her workplace. Extended family, including Teo's paternal grandparents, remain in La Esperanza, and the family communicates with them regularly by phone and video call. Valentina is reported to be functionally bilingual, having acquired English rapidly after starting kindergarten, and frequently serves as a language model and informal interpreter for Teo at home.

Lucía works as a server at El Jalisco Mexican Restaurant in Pittsboro, typically six shifts per week, including evenings. Carlos is employed with Flores Construction Company, a small residential framing crew that he co-owns with his brother; within the family, the business is more often referred to by its Spanish-order name, Compañía de Construcción Flores. His work frequently requires early mornings and occasional travel to job sites outside Chatham County. Given both parents' work schedules, Rosa provides the majority of daytime care for Teo on days he is not at daycare, and the family reports that most of Teo's language input across the week is in Spanish.

The family receives support from several community resources. They have been enrolled with the Chatham County WIC Program since Teo's infancy and receive nutrition supplementation and counseling. Lucía also reports past involvement with the Chatham County Department of Social Services for food assistance (SNAP) during a period of reduced work hours in 2024. The family was connected to Chatham County Partnership for Children by their service coordinator, which helped enroll Teo in a subsidized childcare slot and provided a referral to Early Head Start.

Educational History

Teo has attended the Early Head Start center located at Siler City on West Second Avenue since March 3, 2025, attending five days per week from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.. His classroom teacher, Patricia Núñez, reports that Teo is social and affectionate with peers and adults but is frequently misunderstood due to unclear speech, and that he has begun to show frustration, including hitting and throwing toys, when he is not understood. Patricia reports that Teo has formed a particular friendship with a classmate, Liam, with whom he engages in parallel and some interactive play, primarily nonverbal or through gesture.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted in both English and Spanish by a bilingual, bicultural speech-language pathologist across two sessions: a parent interview and direct assessment session on October 3, 2026, and a classroom observation at Early Head Start on October 6, 2026. Standardized assessment, informal language sampling, oral-motor examination, and parent/teacher report via questionnaire were used to evaluate Teo's current speech and language functioning relative to same-age peers, with consideration of his bilingual language exposure and dialectal features of Honduran Spanish. Testing was conducted with instructions and stimuli presented in both languages as appropriate to each measure, and parent report instruments (the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale interview form) were completed primarily in Spanish with Lucía and Carlos, translated by the evaluator.

Standardized Tests Administered:
- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4) — Language and Cognitive subtests
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish and English editions

TEST RESULTS

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale

The Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale was completed via structured parent interview and direct observation of play-based interaction. Results are reported as age-equivalent ranges across developmental categories.

| Category | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|
| Interaction-Attachment | 26–28 months |
| Pragmatics | 20–22 months |
| Gesture | 18–20 months |
| Play | 22–24 months |
| Language Comprehension | 16–18 months |
| Language Expression | 12–14 months |

Teo's performance on the Rossetti indicates that receptive and expressive language skills fall significantly below chronological age expectations, with expressive language showing the most marked delay, roughly 12–14 months behind his chronological age of 2;8.

Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition

| Scale | Standard Score | 95% CI | Percentile | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cognitive | 85 | 79–91 | 16th | Low Average |
| Receptive Language | 76 | 70–82 | 5th | Below Average |
| Expressive Language | 68 | 62–74 | 2nd | Extremely Low |
| Fine Motor | 94 | 87–101 | 34th | Average |
| Gross Motor | 88 | 81–95 | 21st | Below Average |

Teo's Cognitive composite falls within the low average range, suggesting that his overall nonverbal problem-solving and cognitive skills are comparatively stronger than his language scores. His Expressive Language subtest score of 68 (62–74, 2nd percentile) reflects a significant and disproportionate delay relative to his cognitive skills and relative to his Receptive Language score.

Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (English)

Teo obtained a standard score of 82 (76–88, 12th percentile), with an age equivalent of 2;9–3;0. Given that Teo receives the majority of his language input in Spanish, this score should be interpreted with caution, as the PPVT-5 is normed on monolingual English-speaking children and may underrepresent his conceptual vocabulary knowledge across both languages.

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (English and Spanish stimuli)

Teo obtained a standard score of 70 (64–76, 2nd percentile) on the Sounds-in-Words subtest. Error patterns were consistent across both languages and included final consonant deletion, fronting of velars (substituting /t/ for /k/, as in "tasa" for "casa"), stopping of fricatives, and cluster reduction (e.g., "pato" for "plato"). Stimulability testing showed Teo was able to approximate the target /k/ with moderate cues in isolation but not in words. Speech intelligibility was judged to be approximately 40% with unfamiliar listeners and 65% with familiar listeners, within connected speech, consistent across both of Teo's languages.

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (Spanish/English)

| Subtest | Standard Score | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 73 | 67–79 |
| Expressive Communication | 65 | 59–71 |
| Total Language Score | 68 | 62–74 |

Teo's Total Language Score of 68 falls within the significantly delayed range, with Expressive Communication representing a notable area of relative weakness compared to Auditory Comprehension.

Oral-Motor and Speech Mechanism Examination

Oral-motor structures were judged to be within normal limits for structure and symmetry. Teo demonstrated adequate lip closure, tongue lateralization, and jaw stability for age. No signs of apraxia of speech were noted; however, inconsistent sound substitutions across repeated productions of the same word (e.g., "dada," "gaga," and "baba" for "vaca" across three trials) raise some concern and warrant monitoring for motor planning difficulty as his language system develops further.

Language Sample

A 20-minute play-based language sample was collected in Spanish with Lucía present and in English with the evaluator, Jennifer Alvarado-Pike, and analyzed using SALT conventions. Teo's mean length of utterance was 1.4 morphemes in Spanish and 1.2 morphemes in English. Utterances were predominantly single-word, with occasional two-word combinations (e.g., "más agua," "Max no"). Several utterances were coded [EW] for error of word form, and unintelligible utterances were marked [*] at a rate of roughly 3 of 10 utterances. Teo used gesture, including pointing and pulling Lucía's hand toward desired objects, to supplement limited verbal output.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized assessment, parent and teacher report, and direct observation, Teo presents with a significant mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, with expressive language functioning substantially below both his receptive language and his nonverbal cognitive skills, across both of his languages, Spanish and English. His speech sound production also falls significantly below age expectations, with error patterns that are consistent cross-linguistically, supporting a true speech sound disorder rather than a pattern attributable solely to typical second-language phonological transfer or dialectal variation within Honduran Spanish.

The relative consistency of Teo's delays across both of his languages indicates that his difficulties reflect a genuine language impairment rather than a difference attributable to bilingual language exposure alone. His cognitive skills, which fall within the low average range, are notably higher than his language scores, further supporting the presence of a specific language impairment rather than a global developmental delay. The combination of reduced intelligibility, limited expressive vocabulary, and emerging behavioral frustration (hitting, throwing toys when not understood, as reported by Patricia Núñez) suggests that Teo's communication difficulties are beginning to affect his social-emotional functioning and peer interactions at Early Head Start, including his developing friendship with Liam.

Teo continues to meet eligibility criteria for ongoing early intervention services under the North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program, given standard scores more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean across multiple domains of communication. Given his upcoming third birthday, transition planning toward preschool special education services (Part B, Section 619) should begin promptly, in coordination with his service coordinator, Dinora Castellanos.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo should continue to receive speech-language therapy services at a frequency of at least two 45-minute sessions per week, provided by a bilingual speech-language pathologist or with the support of a qualified Spanish interpreter, with a focus on both receptive and expressive language in Spanish, his primary home language, with concurrent support for English given his daycare environment.

2. Therapy should incorporate a combination of approaches, including Hanen-based parent coaching strategies and the PROMPT approach to support motor planning for speech production, given Teo's inconsistent sound substitution patterns.

3. A home program should be developed collaboratively with Lucía, Carlos, and Rosa, given her significant role in Teo's daily care, with materials and strategies provided in Spanish to maximize carryover, including modeling expansion of Teo's one-word utterances into two- and three-word combinations.

4. Continued collaboration with Early Head Start staff, including Patricia Núñez, is recommended to support classroom-based communication strategies and to monitor Teo's frustration-related behaviors, which appear linked to communication breakdown.

5. Referral for a transition evaluation to determine eligibility for preschool special education services (Part B) is recommended, to be initiated by Children's Developmental Services Agency of the Triangle in coordination with the local school district, well in advance of Teo's third birthday.

6. Re-evaluation of speech and language skills is recommended in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and adjust goals as needed, or sooner if significant changes in communication or behavior are observed by caregivers or teaching staff.

7. Continued audiological monitoring is recommended given Teo's history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement, with re-evaluation if any changes in hearing sensitivity or attention to sound are noted by caregivers or Dr. Osei.

8. The family should continue to be connected with available community resources, including the Chatham County WIC Program and Chatham County Partnership for Children, to support continued access to subsidized childcare and nutritional services as Teo transitions between programs.

This evaluation was conducted and this report was prepared by Jennifer Alvarado-Pike, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist, of Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Associates, PLLC. Please contact our office at (919) 542-7788 or info@carolinabilingualslp.com with any questions regarding this report or recommendations.

Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC (TBSLT)
Comprehensive Bilingual Speech-Language Evaluation / Evaluación Integral de Habla y Lenguaje

Employer (Legal Name): Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC    Also Known As: Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language    Abbreviation: TBSLT
Clinic Office: 4420 Kildaire Farm Road, Suite 112, Cary, NC 27518    Clinic Phone: (919) 555-0271    Clinic Email: intake@trianglebilingualslt.com

Child's Name: Mateo de la Cruz Fernández (called "Teo" at home)    Date of Birth: April 18, 2023    Chronological Age: 3;6
Medicaid ID: NC88231407B    Case ID: PCDSA-04521    Evaluation Date: October 6, 2026
Mother: Lucía Fernández-Ortiz    Father: José de la Cruz Soto ("Pepe")
Home Address: 214 Walnut Grove Lane, Apex, NC 27502    County: Wake County
Home Phone: (919) 555-0148    Mother's Cell: (919) 555-0193
Referring Pediatrician: Dr. Priya Patel    Referring Agency: Piedmont CDSA    Service Coordinator: Brenda Johnson
Interpreter Present: Marisol Vega    Occupational Therapist: Sarah Whitfield, OTR/L    Physical Therapist: Kevin O'Brien, PT, DPT
Evaluating Clinician: Daniela Fuentes-Marín, M.S., CCC-SLP    Employer: TBSLT
Evaluation Start Time: 9:15 AM    Evaluation End Time: 11:30 AM    Location: 214 Walnut Grove Lane, Apex (home visit)

Reason for Referral

Teo was referred by Dr. Priya Patel at his 36-month well-child visit due to limited expressive vocabulary in both English and Spanish, frequent use of gestures to communicate, and difficulty following two-step directions in either language. Piedmont CDSA opened the case on March 2, 2025 and assigned Brenda Johnson as service coordinator. This evaluation was requested to update Teo's Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) ahead of his annual review, scheduled for November 14, 2026, and to determine continued eligibility for TBSLT services under Piedmont CDSA authorization.

Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje / Family and Language History

Teo vive con su mamá, Lucía Fernández-Ortiz, su papá, José de la Cruz Soto ("Pepe"), y dos hermanos mayores: Guadalupe de la Cruz Fernández, a quien todos llaman "Lupita," de seis años, y Jesús de la Cruz Fernández, apodado "Chuy," de ocho años. La abuela paterna, Carmen Soto, cuida a Teo tres días a la semana mientras los padres trabajan. Lucía Fernández-Ortiz works at Blue Ridge Furniture Company on the assembly line, and José de la Cruz Soto works for Apex Landscaping Co. as a crew supervisor.

The family reports that Spanish is the primary language spoken at home, roughly 80% of the time, with English used increasingly since Teo began attending Little Sprouts Early Learning Center in January 2026. "Lucía Fernández-Ortiz dice que en la casa hablamos puro español con los niños, pero Lupita y Chuy le hablan a Teo en inglés a veces porque así les sale más fácil desde la escuela." The grandmother, Carmen Soto, speaks only Spanish with Teo and reports that he understands more than he says: "entiende todo lo que le digo, pero contesta poquito." At Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, his teacher, Amanda Lopez, communicates with him primarily in English and notes that he often watches his classmate Juan Pablo Ríos, nicknamed "Juanito," and imitates his play rather than initiating language himself.

Lucía Fernández-Ortiz reports that Teo's older siblings, Lupita and Chuy, were both bilingual by age 3;0 and did not show similar delays. She described feeling "preocupada" because "Teo se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos, y a veces se pega o llora." The family's dog, Rocky, is a frequent topic of Teo's spontaneous speech; during the home visit he pointed at the dog and said "Rocky corre," demonstrating a two-word combination that the family reports is typical of his current output.

Current Session Schedule

Day         Start Time    Stop Time    Location
Monday      9:00 AM      9:45 AM     Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, Apex
Wednesday   2:30 PM      3:15 PM     home, 214 Walnut Grove Lane, Apex
Friday      10:15 AM     11:00 AM    TBSLT office, 4420 Kildaire Farm Road, Cary

Sessions on Monday and Friday are co-treated with Sarah Whitfield, OTR/L, who addresses fine motor and sensory regulation goals concurrently. Kevin O'Brien, PT, DPT, sees Teo separately on Tuesdays at 1:00 PM for gross motor goals related to his history of low tone.

Birth and Medical History

Teo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Cary Valley Medical Center via scheduled cesarean delivery. Birth weight was 6 lbs 4 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lucía Fernández-Ortiz reported an uncomplicated pregnancy aside from gestational hypertension managed with medication. Teo remained in the hospital for two days and was discharged home with his mother.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with five documented episodes between 8 and 24 months of age. Dr. Priya Patel placed bilateral tympanostomy tubes on September 12, 2024, and the family reports improvement in responsiveness to sound since the procedure, though tubes extruded naturally by June 2026 and have not been replaced. A hearing screening conducted at Piedmont CDSA on July 30, 2026 showed results within normal limits bilaterally. Teo has no history of seizure, head injury, or hospitalization beyond birth. He is not currently taking any medications. Family history is notable for a maternal uncle who "no hablaba hasta los cuatro años" per report, though no formal diagnosis is documented. José de la Cruz Soto denies any personal or family history of autism, intellectual disability, or genetic syndromes.

Developmental milestones were reported as follows: sat independently at 6 months, walked independently at 15 months, first words (in Spanish) around 18 months ("mamá," "agua," "no"), and two-word combinations emerging only in the past three months. Kevin O'Brien, PT, DPT, has followed Teo since February 2025 for mild generalized low tone, which the family and Sarah Whitfield feel may also affect oral-motor control and contribute to reduced speech intelligibility.

Educational and Early Intervention History

Teo has received speech-language services through Piedmont CDSA, delivered by TBSLT clinicians, since his initial IFSP was signed on February 18, 2025. He began attending Little Sprouts Early Learning Center three days a week in January 2026 under his teacher, Amanda Lopez. Amanda Lopez reports that Teo follows classroom routines well but rarely uses words to request items, instead pulling adults by the hand or pointing. She has observed him attempting to play alongside Juanito during free play but struggling to join ongoing games verbally.

Assessment Procedures

This evaluation included formal and informal measures, parent and caregiver interview through interpreter Marisol Vega, a language sample in both English and Spanish, and direct observation during structured and unstructured play. All test administration and scoring followed standardized procedures with adaptations for bilingual administration as outlined in each test manual. Daniela Fuentes-Marín administered items in both languages across two separate presentations, crediting a correct response in either language per bilingual scoring guidelines.

Test Results

Measure                                          Score Type           Score         Percentile      Age Equivalent
Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish     Auditory Comprehension   Standard Score 76    5th        2;4
PLS-5 Spanish                                    Expressive Communication  Standard Score 71    3rd        2;1
PLS-5 Spanish                                    Total Language Score     73           4th        —
Rosetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale            Interaction-Attachment   Age equivalent 24-27 months  —   —
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)   Sounds-in-Words     Standard Score 68    2nd        —
MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories (CDI), Spanish/English short form   Vocabulary Checklist   total 112 words produced   —   —

Confidence intervals for the PLS-5 scores fell within 73-83 for Total Language at the 90% confidence level. Teo's performance places him in the moderately delayed range for both receptive and expressive language relative to same-age bilingual peers.

During the language sample, Teo produced a mean length of utterance of 1.4 morphemes in English and 1.6 morphemes in Spanish, consistent with typical single-word to early two-word combinations for a child his age range of 2;0 to 2;6 rather than his chronological age of 3;6. He used approximately 35 different words across both languages during a 20-minute sample, achieving a type-token ratio considered low for his age.

Articulation and Phonology

Teo demonstrated the following sound production patterns, consistent with normal second-language-acquisition influence as well as a phonological delay beyond what is accounted for by bilingual exposure alone:

Final consonant deletion was observed in both languages, for example producing "pa" for "pan" and "ga" for "gato". Cluster reduction was noted, with /s/ blends simplified, as in "apo" for "sapo". He substituted [w] for /ɾ/ in words such as "Rocky uega" (intended "Rocky juega"), and substituted [t] for /k/ in word-initial position, as in "tasa" for "casa." These patterns persisted across minimal pair probes with moderate (mod) cues and did not resolve with maximum (max) cues on roughly half of attempts, suggesting a phonological component beyond typical crosslinguistic transfer. His intelligibility was estimated at 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners within shared context.

Oral-Motor and Feeding Observations

Oral-motor examination revealed adequate structure with mildly reduced tone, consistent with Kevin O'Brien's findings on PT evaluation. Teo demonstrated age-appropriate diadochokinetic rates for a 3-year-old and no overt signs of dysphagia. Lucía Fernández-Ortiz reported no feeding concerns, noting "come de todo, no es quisquilloso," though she noted occasional drooling during focused play, which Sarah Whitfield has also observed and is monitoring as part of OT goals.

Social Communication and Play

Teo engaged readily with Daniela Fuentes-Marín and Marisol Vega during the session, making eye contact, taking turns in simple cause-and-effect toys, and showing joint attention when a preferred toy (a toy dump truck) was introduced. He demonstrated requesting through pointing and vocalizing but rarely combined gesture with a word. When his sister Lupita was mentioned, he looked toward the door and said "Lupe," approximating her name, which the family confirmed is typical. He showed brief pretend play, feeding a stuffed animal and saying "come," a single-word production judged appropriate for a feeding script. No concerning repetitive behaviors, restricted interests, or significant sensory aversions were observed beyond the mild tactile sensitivities already being addressed by Sarah Whitfield in OT.

Parent and Caregiver Report

Through interpreter Marisol Vega, Lucía Fernández-Ortiz completed a structured interview covering communication milestones, behavior, and family priorities. She stated, "lo que más queremos es que Teo pueda decirnos lo que necesita sin frustrarse, y que pueda jugar con Juanito y los otros niños en la guardería." José de la Cruz Soto added that he wants his son to be ready for Pre-K "hablando los dos idiomas, como sus hermanos," referring to Lupita and Chuy. The grandmother, Carmen Soto, who was present for part of the home visit, expressed concern about Teo's behavior when frustrated, noting he has begun biting his own hand, a behavior not previously reported to Dr. Priya Patel and flagged for follow-up at his next pediatric visit.

Teacher input was gathered by phone from Amanda Lopez prior to the evaluation. She reported that Teo participates in circle time but does not yet answer simple "wh-" questions verbally, instead pointing or shrugging. She noted growth in his willingness to approach Juanito during outdoor play over the past month, which the family and clinical team view as a positive sign for continued peer-mediated intervention strategies.

Impressions

Based on standardized testing, language sampling, parent and teacher report, and direct observation, Teo presents with a moderate expressive and receptive language delay affecting both Spanish and English, alongside a moderate phonological disorder affecting intelligibility in both languages. His scores fall more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in both languages, which, combined with error patterns that do not fully resolve with cueing and persist across both languages, support a diagnosis beyond what would be expected from typical bilingual language development alone. His ICD-10 diagnostic impression is F80.9 (Developmental disorder of speech and language, unspecified) with a secondary impression of F80.0 (Phonological disorder). Relevant CPT codes for today's evaluation include 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) and 96110 (developmental screening, with scoring) for the CDI checklist, modifier -59 appended to reflect the distinct procedural service.

Teo's mild low tone, noted by Kevin O'Brien and Sarah Whitfield, likely contributes to reduced oral-motor precision underlying some articulation errors, supporting continued interdisciplinary collaboration. His strong social engagement, joint attention, and responsiveness to both languages are significant strengths and predict a favorable response to continued intervention, particularly peer-mediated approaches given his emerging interest in Juanito and classroom participation.

Recommendations

1. Continue individual speech-language therapy through TBSLT under Piedmont CDSA authorization, two to three sessions weekly, addressing IFSP Outcome 2 (functional communication) and IFSP Outcome 3 (speech sound production), using a bilingual, family-centered model.
2. Incorporate Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies into parent coaching for Lucía Fernández-Ortiz and José de la Cruz Soto, with interpreter Marisol Vega present for coaching sessions as needed, to increase responsive communication opportunities across both languages at home.
3. Introduce PROMPT-based tactile-kinesthetic cueing to target oral-motor placement for final consonants and the /ɾ/ and /k/ substitution patterns noted above, coordinating with Sarah Whitfield given the oral-motor and tone overlap.
4. Continue co-treatment sessions with occupational therapy (Monday and Friday, per the schedule above) and physical therapy with Kevin O'Brien to support postural stability during seated language tasks.
5. Collaborate with Amanda Lopez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to implement peer-mediated communication strategies during free play with Juanito and other classmates, including modeling simple requesting phrases in both languages.
6. Refer concerns regarding self-injurious behavior (hand-biting when frustrated) to Dr. Priya Patel for medical follow-up and behavioral consultation as appropriate, with results to be shared with the IFSP team prior to the November 14, 2026 review.
7. Re-administer the PLS-5 Spanish and GFTA-3 in approximately six months to monitor progress and inform continued eligibility determination through Piedmont CDSA.
8. Provide the family with bilingual home strategies handout, reviewed with Lucía Fernández-Ortiz and José de la Cruz Soto through interpreter Marisol Vega, emphasizing expansion of two-word combinations and reduction of gesture-only communication.

This report was prepared by Daniela Fuentes-Marín, M.S., CCC-SLP, on behalf of Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC (TBSLT), and reviewed with Lucía Fernández-Ortiz and José de la Cruz Soto in Spanish through interpreter Marisol Vega on October 6, 2026. A copy has been forwarded to Dr. Priya Patel, Brenda Johnson at Piedmont CDSA, and the family for inclusion in Teo's IFSP record, Case ID PCDSA-04521.

Email: patricia.gomez@carolinabilingual.org

Evaluation date: September 2, 2025

2. SERVICE COORDINATION

Jennifer Stokes, the family's service coordinator through Piedmont Regional CDSA, convened this annual review with Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Carlos Reyes Ibarra on October 8, 2026 at 9:30 AM. Patricia Gómez conducted the session in Spanish and English per the family's preference, with Jennifer Stokes taking notes in English. The family's pediatrician, Dr. Amanda Chen, and the program's audiologist, Dr. Robert Kim, were consulted by phone but did not attend in person.

3. FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES — PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA

La mamá, Lucía Rodríguez Flores, shared: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Mateo no me dice lo que quiere. Él solo señala y hace sonidos, pero no usa palabras como su hermano Diego a esa edad." She continued in English, "At home he says things like, 'Rocky no' when the dog barks, or he'll point and say 'Diego go' when his brother leaves the room, but he doesn't combine many other words."

Carlos Reyes Ibarra added, "En la guardería dicen que se frustra mucho. Quiero que pueda decirle a su maestra qué necesita, not just cry or grab things."

The family's priorities, in their own words, include: (1) "que hable más para que no se frustre," (2) that Mateo be understood by his grandmother, Rosa Martínez, who provides afternoon childcare, and (3) that services continue in both languages so Mateo does not lose Spanish "porque es la lengua de la familia."

4. PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Birth history: Mateo was born at 39 weeks gestation via cesarean delivery, birth weight 3,400 grams, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9.

Mateo was assessed using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale and the Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), administered bilingually by Patricia Gómez. On the PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension subtest, Mateo earned a standard score within 73-83 (confidence interval), placing him at the 9th percentile, with an age equivalent of 2;6–3;0. Expressive Communication fell lower, with an age equivalent range of 1;8–2;0.

A diagnosis consistent with ICD-10 code F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) was confirmed. Articulation sampling showed Mateo produces /b/, /m/, and /p/ consistently, but substitutes [w] for /ɾ/ in words like "carro" → "[kawo]." Spontaneous productions sampled during the session included "Rocky agua" (wanting water for the dog) and "mamá arriba," both coded [EW] for emerging word combinations.

With mod cues, Mateo imitated two-word combinations in 8/10 trials (80% accuracy); without cues, accuracy dropped to 3 of 5 trials.

5. DAILY ROUTINES / RUTINAS DIARIAS

Mateo wakes around 7:00 AM and is cared for by his grandmother, Rosa Martínez, until he attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center in the afternoons, where his teacher, Ms. Lopez, reports similar frustration during snack time and circle time. His brother Diego, age 8, plays with him after school and often "translates" his wants to their parents. The family dog, Rocky, is a frequent motivator during play-based routines; Lucía Rodríguez Flores noted Mateo will attempt new words to ask for Rocky's leash or food.

6. OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

The family receives nutrition support through WIC and has been connected to Alamance County DSS for housing assistance. Mateo was previously enrolled in Early Head Start before transitioning to Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, and the family participates in parenting workshops through Alamance Smart Start. Jennifer Stokes coordinates information sharing across WIC, Alamance County DSS, and Piedmont Regional CDSA with the family's written consent.

7. OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Mateo will use two- to three-word combinations in Spanish and English to request and comment during daily routines, increasing from current baseline to 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive sessions.
Strategy: Use Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies; family-coached sessions bilingually by Patricia Gómez; incorporate Rocky and Diego as motivating communication partners.

Outcome 2: Mateo will increase intelligibility of early-developing consonants in both languages, moving from [w] substitutions toward accurate /ɾ/ production in at least 8/10 trials with min cues.
Strategy: PROMPT-informed tactile cueing during snack and play routines; collaboration with Ms. Lopez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to reinforce target sounds.

Outcome 3: Family will report increased confidence identifying Mateo's communication attempts at home and at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, as measured by parent interview at next review.
Strategy: Monthly coaching visits in the home at 214 Maple Hollow Drive; written strategies provided in Spanish and English; consultation with grandmother Rosa Martínez during a portion of each visit.

8. SERVICES AND SERVICE DATES

Speech-language therapy (individual), billed under CPT 92507, twice weekly, beginning October 15, 2025 and continuing through this review.
Speech-language evaluation services, billed under CPT 92523, completed September 2, 2025.

Client Name: María José Fuentes Rivera (called "Chabela" and sometimes "MJ" at home)  DOB: September 14, 2023  Age at Evaluation: 2;11

Evaluator: Marisol Hernández-Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual SLP  Agency: Alamance-Caswell CDSA  Employer: Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

Address: 418 Overbrook Road, Burlington, Alamance County, NC 27215  Phone: (336) 555-0148  Email: mhernandez@piedmontbilingualslp.com

NC Medicaid ID: 9802345671A  Insurance Member ID: BCBSNC-884512309  NC ITP Child ID: ITP-2024-003871  Authorization #: AUTH-55021-RJ

Evaluation Date: August 18, 2026  Report Date: August 22, 2026  Referral Source: Dr. Robert Kim, UNC Children's Clinic of Burlington  Service Coordinator: Ana Gutiérrez

CPT Code: 92523  ICD-10: F80.2  Modifier: GN

**Reason for Referral / Motivo de la Referencia**

María José, known to her family as "Chabela," was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Robert Kim after her mother, Guadalupe Rivera Soto — "Lupita" to family — reported during a well-child visit that Chabela "no habla casi nada" compared to her cousin Mateo Rivera Soto, known as "Teo," who is the same age. Lupita stated, in Spanish, "ella solo señala y hace gestos, casi no dice palabras," which the clinician translated as the child mostly points and gestures rather than using words. The family lives in Burlington and receives services through the Alamance-Caswell CDSA under the NC Infant-Toddler Program. Chabela currently attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare four days a week while her parents work.

**Birth and Medical History / Historia Médica y de Nacimiento**

Guadalupe Rivera Soto reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with routine prenatal care beginning at 10 weeks gestation. Chabela was born at 38 weeks gestational age via vaginal delivery at Alamance Regional Medical Center on September 14, 2023. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. No NICU stay was required. Lupita reported no history of ear infections requiring tubes, though Chabela had "dos infecciones de oído" (two ear infections) treated with antibiotics around 18 months of age. Hearing was last screened at June 3, 2026 and passed bilaterally. There is no reported history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness. Chabela's pediatrician, Dr. Robert Kim, noted no concerns on recent growth charts but deferred to this evaluation for language concerns. The family denies any genetic syndromes or known hearing loss in extended family, though Lupita mentioned that her own brother, Marcos Rivera, "tardó en hablar" (was a late talker) as a toddler.

**Family and Language History / Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje**

Chabela lives at home with her mother, Guadalupe Rivera Soto ("Lupita"); her father, José Luis Fuentes Delgado ("Pepe"); her older brother, Jesús Fuentes Rivera ("Chuy"), age 7; and her younger brother, Juan Fuentes Rivera ("Juanito"), age 18 months. The family dog, Max, also lives in the home; Lupita noted that Chabela will point at Max and say something close to "pa" when he barks, though she does not yet attempt his name clearly.

The home language environment is predominantly Spanish, with English introduced primarily through Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare and through Chuy's homework and television shows. Lupita reported that she speaks "casi siempre en español" with Chabela, while Pepe mixes "un poco de inglés y español" depending on fatigue after long shifts. Pepe works second shift at a poultry processing plant, Carolina Fresh Poultry, and often describes his schedule as "trabajo en la planta de empaque" (he works at the packing plant), referring to la planta de Carolina Fresh Poultry. Lupita works part-time in the kitchen of a local restaurant, El Compadre Mexican Restaurant, which she calls "el restaurante donde trabajo" — el restaurante El Compadre — three evenings a week.

Extended family plays a large role in childcare and language exposure. Chabela's maternal grandmother, Rosa Soto, helps watch the children on weekends and works for a cleaning company, Manos Limpias Cleaning Service; Rosa often describes her job as working at "el servicio de limpieza," referring to el servicio de limpieza Manos Limpias. Chabela's paternal grandfather, Ernesto Fuentes, works seasonally on a farm, Green Valley Farm, outside Graham, and her paternal grandmother, Carmen Delgado, works at a small grocery, La Economía, which the family refers to as "la tienda La Economía." Chabela's uncle (tío), Marcos Rivera, works for a construction company, Triángulo Construction Company, and often brings Teo along on weekends to play with Chabela and Chuy; the family calls his employer "la compañía de construcción Triángulo."

Lupita reported that Chabela's first words emerged around 14 months, consistent with "mamá" and "papá," but that vocabulary growth has since stalled. She estimated Chabela's current expressive vocabulary at fewer than 20 words across both languages, with most productions being single words rather than combinations. Receptively, Lupita and Pepe both feel Chabela "entiende todo" (understands everything), following simple directions in Spanish such as "trae tus zapatos" and responding to her name and to Chuy's and Teo's names. No family history of autism was reported, though Lupita mentioned that a cousin's son was "diagnosticado con autismo" at a CDSA in another county.

**Assessment Procedures / Procedimientos de Evaluación**

This evaluation was conducted in the home by Marisol Hernández-Vega in both English and Spanish, with primary interactions occurring in Spanish per family preference. Procedures included parent interview, standardized assessment, informal language sampling, oral-motor examination, and observation of play-based interaction with Lupita and briefly with Chuy. Chabela was cooperative for most of the session but required frequent breaks and preferred toys over picture-based tasks. A brief spontaneous language sample was collected and transcribed using SALT conventions; several utterances were coded [EW] where Chabela used an exact word repetition rather than a novel combination. Dynamic assessment techniques, including mod cues and max cues to elicit imitated word attempts, were used throughout to assess learnability.

Oral-motor examination revealed adequate structure and function for speech, with slightly reduced lingual lateralization noted but no feeding concerns reported by the family. Chabela produced the target word "agua" as ["aba"] and "más" as ["ma"] during the sample, both with moderate cues. She attempted the word "perro" (referring to Max) as ["peo"], omitting the final consonant cluster.

**Test Results / Resultados de las Pruebas**

Standardized and informal measures were administered in both languages where normed and appropriate. Results are summarized below.

Test/Measure                    Domain                          Date Administered           Standard Score / Index        Percentile        95% CI
Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish   Auditory Comprehension    August 18, 2026    72    3rd    65-79
PLS-5 Spanish           Expressive Communication  August 18, 2026    58    1st    51-65
PLS-5 Spanish           Total Language Score      August 18, 2026    63    1st    57-69
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale   Interaction-Attachment    August 19, 2026    age equivalent 20 months    N/A    N/A
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale   Pragmatics                August 19, 2026    age equivalent 22 months    N/A    N/A
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)   Sounds-in-Words   August 20, 2026    70    2nd    61-79
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) Semantics   Receptive/Expressive Semantics    August 20, 2026    76    5th    68-84

On the PLS-5 Spanish, Chabela obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 72 (3rd percentile, 95% CI 65-79) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 58 (1st percentile, 95% CI 51-65), yielding a Total Language Score of 63 (1st percentile, 95% CI 57-69), administered on August 18, 2026. On the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, administered August 19, 2026, Chabela functioned at an age equivalent of 20 months for Interaction-Attachment and 22 months for Pragmatics, both notably below her chronological age of 2;11. Articulation testing via the GFTA-3 on August 20, 2026 yielded a standard score of 70 (2nd percentile, 95% CI 61-79), with final consonant deletion and cluster reduction noted as primary error patterns, consistent with phonological processes commonly observed at this age but occurring at a higher rate than expected. Phoneme-level probes showed inconsistent production of /s/, /ɾ/, and final /n/, with Chabela substituting [w] for /ɾ/ in medial position. Semantic skills assessed via the BESA on August 20, 2026 showed a standard score of 76 (5th percentile, 95% CI 68-84).

Informal observation during a short cooperative play sequence with Chuy showed that Chabela followed his lead nonverbally in 8 of 10 turn-taking opportunities but initiated verbal requests in only 2 of 10 opportunities, usually relying on pointing or pulling Chuy's hand. When Chuy said "dile 'más' a tu hermana" (tell her "more"), Chabela produced "ma" with minimal cues, suggesting stimulability for simple CV word attempts.

**Impressions / Impresiones**

Chabela presents with a moderate to severe expressive language delay and a mild-to-moderate receptive language delay, affecting both Spanish and emerging English, consistent across formal measures and informal observation. Her PLS-5 Spanish scores fall well below age expectations (Total Language Score 63, 1st percentile), and her limited expressive vocabulary, inconsistent word combinations, and reliance on gesture support this impression. Articulation findings on the GFTA-3 (standard score 70) indicate a co-occurring phonological disorder, with error patterns (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, [w] for /ɾ/ substitution) that are somewhat atypical in frequency for age 2;11, even accounting for typical bilingual developmental variation.

Given that Chabela is being raised in an environment where Spanish is the dominant input language, with English introduced primarily through Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, her delays appear to reflect a true language disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition patterns, as deficits are present across both languages and in nonlinguistic pragmatic domains (Rossetti age equivalents of 20 and 22 months). Chabela's stimulability for word approximations with moderate and minimal cues is a positive prognostic sign.

Family strengths include strong engagement from both Lupita and Pepe, consistent routines involving extended family such as Rosa Soto and cousin Teo, and a supportive sibling, Chuy, who already scaffolds Chabela's communication attempts. Barriers to progress include both parents' demanding work schedules — Pepe's shifts at Carolina Fresh Poultry and Lupita's evening hours at El Compadre Mexican Restaurant — which limit availability for weekday appointments, though weekend sessions may be feasible given Rosa's and Marcos's involvement in childcare.

**Recommendations / Recomendaciones**

1. Chabela is eligible for ongoing early intervention services through the Alamance-Caswell CDSA under the NC Infant-Toddler Program, and an IFSP review should be scheduled to add or revise relevant outcomes, including IFSP Outcome 2 (expressive vocabulary growth) and IFSP Outcome 3 (speech sound intelligibility).

2. Direct bilingual speech-language therapy is recommended at a frequency of two times per week, 30 minutes per session, using a combination of Hanen-based coaching for caregivers and PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing to support word approximations and sound shaping.

3. Caregiver coaching sessions should include both Lupita and Pepe when possible, and may be scheduled around their work availability; weekend sessions involving Rosa Soto as a secondary caregiver are encouraged given her regular role in childcare.

4. A phonological approach such as Cycles is recommended to target final consonant deletion and cluster reduction patterns identified on the GFTA-3.

5. Continued monitoring of receptive language and pragmatic skills is recommended given Rossetti age equivalents below chronological age; referral for occupational therapy consultation may be considered if attention and play skills do not progress alongside language gains.

6. The family should continue speaking Spanish at home, as bilingual input does not cause language disorders and supports Chabela's relationships with Lupita, Pepe, Rosa Soto, and extended family including Ernesto Fuentes and Carmen Delgado.

7. Coordination with Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare staff, including Miss Ashley Combs and Maestra Yesenia Ortiz, is recommended to ensure consistent vocabulary targets across home and daycare settings.

8. A follow-up hearing screening is not indicated at this time given the passed screening on June 3, 2026, but should be repeated if language progress stalls despite intervention.

9. This report and its findings should be shared with Dr. Robert Kim at UNC Children's Clinic of Burlington and with service coordinator Ana Gutiérrez for inclusion in Chabela's IFSP record under ITP-2024-003871.

10. Re-evaluation is recommended in 6 months to monitor progress toward IFSP outcomes and determine continued eligibility.

Thank you to the family for their openness and participation. Lupita and Pepe were both engaged throughout the session, and their insight into Chabela's communication at home, including her interactions with Chuy, Juanito, and cousin Teo, was invaluable to this evaluation.

Report prepared by: Marisol Hernández-Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP  License #: SLP-NC-22841  Date: August 22, 2026
