INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y EL LENGUAJE

Nombre del niño/a:	Mateo Alejandro Vásquez Flores ("Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento:	14 de marzo de 2022
Edad actual al momento de la evaluación:	4;7
Sexo:	Masculino
Idiomas del hogar:	Español (primario), inglés (secundario)
Número de identificación NC ITP:	NC-ITP-00457821
Número de Medicaid:	MA9284017B
Número de identificación del seguro (member ID):	BCBS-NC-774215690
Número de expediente / autorización:	AUTH-2026-003871
Fecha de la evaluación:	6 de octubre de 2026
Lugar de la evaluación:	Oficina del Centro de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA Piedmont)
Coordinadora de servicios:	Marisol Guzmán Herrera, de la Red de Apoyo Familiar de Carolina del Norte (Family Support Network of NC)
Evaluadora:	Patricia Jiménez Solano, M.S., CCC-SLP, Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language, PLLC

INFORMACIÓN DE CONTACTO

Relación	Nombre	Teléfono	Correo electrónico
Madre	Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paredes	(336) 555-0148	lucia.rodriguezparedes@gmail.com
Padre	Carlos Andrés Vásquez Morales	(336) 555-0193	cvasquezmorales@outlook.com
Dirección:	1428 Willowbrook Lane, Greensboro, NC 27406
Condado:	Condado de Guilford

MOTIVO DE REFERIDO

Mateo, conocido en casa como "Teo", fue referido al Centro de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA Piedmont) por su pediatra, el Dr. Manuel Ortega Castillo, de la clínica pediátrica afiliada al Moses Cone Hospital, debido a preocupaciones sobre el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y la claridad del habla. La familia también fue apoyada por el Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Guilford (DSS Guilford) y por la oficina local de WIC del Condado de Guilford durante la solicitud de servicios de intervención temprana. Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paredes, madre de Mateo, reportó que su hijo usa pocas palabras en comparación con otros niños de su edad y que, cuando habla, es difícil entenderle incluso para personas que lo conocen bien.

La evaluación fue solicitada para determinar la elegibilidad de Mateo para servicios continuos bajo el Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP, por sus siglas en inglés) y para actualizar las metas existentes.

ANTECEDENTES DEL DESARROLLO Y LA HISTORIA MÉDICA

Mateo nació a las 38 semanas de gestación en el Moses Cone Hospital en Greensboro, con un peso al nacer de 3,150 gramos y puntajes de Apgar de 8 y 9 al primer y quinto minuto, respectivamente. El embarazo fue descrito por Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paredes como sin complicaciones significativas, aunque mencionó un episodio de presión arterial elevada durante el tercer trimestre que fue monitoreado sin intervención adicional.

El desarrollo motor grueso de Mateo fue reportado dentro de los parámetros típicos: caminó de forma independiente a los 13 meses. Sin embargo, los hitos del lenguaje se retrasaron: sus primeras palabras reconocibles no aparecieron hasta aproximadamente los 22 meses, y la combinación de dos palabras no se observó de manera consistente hasta cerca de los 3 años.

A los 26 meses de edad, Mateo fue evaluado por un audiólogo, el Dr. Brian Whitfield, en el Brenner Children's Hospital, quien documentó una audición dentro de límites normales bilateralmente mediante timpanometría y audiometría conductual. No se han reportado infecciones de oído recurrentes ni colocación de tubos de ventilación. El historial médico es, por lo demás, sin eventos relevantes; no hay diagnósticos genéticos ni neurológicos conocidos. El código ICD-10 actualmente asociado al expediente es F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo), pendiente de confirmación tras esta evaluación.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo vive con sus padres, Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paredes y Carlos Andrés Vásquez Morales, y sus dos hermanos: Diego Vásquez Rodríguez, de siete años, y Camila Vásquez Rodríguez, de dos años. Según la familia, el español es el idioma predominante en el hogar, usado en aproximadamente el 80% de las interacciones diarias, mientras que el inglés se introduce principalmente a través de la televisión, la guardería y las interacciones con Diego Vásquez Rodríguez, quien asiste a la escuela primaria en inglés.

La abuela materna, Rosa Paredes de Rodríguez, vive con la familia de lunes a viernes y ayuda con el cuidado de los tres niños mientras los padres trabajan. Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paredes trabaja como asistente de enfermería en Cone Health, y Carlos Andrés Vásquez Morales trabaja en producción en Mohawk Industries. Debido a los horarios laborales de ambos padres, una niñera de confianza, Yesenia Torres Luna, también cuida a Mateo algunas tardes y refuerza las actividades de lenguaje sugeridas por la terapeuta.

El padre, Carlos Andrés Vásquez Morales, nació y se crio en la Aldea El Rosario, cerca de La Esperanza, en el departamento de Intibucá, Honduras, y mantiene contacto frecuente con familiares allí, incluyendo a los primos de Mateo, Valentina Flores Paredes y Esteban Flores Paredes, con quienes habla por videollamada casi semanalmente. La familia reporta que estas llamadas son una fuente importante de exposición al español y que Mateo disfruta mostrarles a sus primos su perro, Toby, durante las llamadas.

No se reportan antecedentes familiares de trastornos de lenguaje, aprendizaje o audición en ninguna rama de la familia.

PARTICIPACIÓN COMUNITARIA Y APOYO DE AGENCIAS

La familia ha recibido apoyo coordinado de varias agencias comunitarias. La oficina de Smart Start del Condado de Guilford conectó a la familia con recursos de cuidado infantil de calidad cuando Mateo tenía dos años, y posteriormente la familia fue referida al programa Early Head Start local, aunque Mateo no fue inscrito debido a la lista de espera. En su lugar, asiste actualmente al Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy, un centro de cuidado infantil bilingüe en Greensboro.

La maestra principal de Mateo en el salón de preescolar es la Sandra Lopez Mejía, y la asistente de maestra es Karen Diaz. Ambas han reportado que Mateo se frustra cuando sus compañeros no entienden lo que intenta comunicar. Entre sus compañeros de clase se encuentran Ethan Caldwell y Sofia Marín, con quienes Mateo juega regularmente durante el tiempo de recreo, aunque la interacción verbal es limitada.

La Partnership for Children del Condado de Guilford también ha apoyado a la familia con información sobre subsidios de cuidado infantil, y el DSS Guilford facilitó la renovación de la cobertura de Medicaid de Mateo el año pasado.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

La evaluación se llevó a cabo completamente en español, el idioma dominante de Mateo, con observación informal de su desempeño en inglés durante actividades de juego libre. Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas y medidas informales:

- Preschool Language Scale-5 Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
- Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, transcrita y analizada usando convenciones SALT
- Observación clínica estructurada y entrevista con los padres

Durante la sesión, Mateo estuvo acompañado inicialmente por su madre, Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paredes, y se mostró cooperador tras un breve período de adaptación. La evaluadora, Patricia Jiménez Solano, es bilingüe certificada y administró todas las pruebas directamente en español sin necesidad de interpretación adicional.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS ESTANDARIZADAS

Prueba	Subprueba	Puntaje estándar	Percentil	Intervalo de confianza
PLS-5 Spanish	Comprensión Auditiva	76	5	68-84
PLS-5 Spanish	Comunicación Expresiva	71	3	63-79
PLS-5 Spanish	Puntaje Total del Lenguaje	72	3	65-79
GFTA-3	Sonidos en Palabras	79	8	71-87

Los resultados de la PLS-5 Spanish indican un retraso significativo tanto en el lenguaje receptivo como expresivo, con un desempeño notablemente más débil en el área expresiva. La edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo se ubicó entre 2;6 y 3;0, lo cual representa un retraso de aproximadamente dos años con respecto a su edad cronológica de 4;7.

ANÁLISIS DEL HABLA

Durante la evaluación de articulación con el GFTA-3, Mateo mostró varios patrones de simplificación fonológica típicos de un desarrollo fonológico atrasado, incluyendo:

- Frontalización de velares: /k/ y /g/ frecuentemente producidos como [t] y [d]
- Simplificación de grupos consonánticos, por ejemplo "tren" producido como "ten"
- Sustitución del fonema vibrante /ɾ/ por [l] en posición intervocálica

Durante el juego libre, Mateo llamó a su perro mientras jugaba, diciendo "Toby co-e" (simplificación de "corre"), demostrando la simplificación de grupos consonánticos descrita anteriormente. En otro momento, señaló una foto y dijo "nene" para referirse a sí mismo, y repitió "mamá" y "agua" de forma clara durante la merienda.

Su inteligibilidad general fue estimada en aproximadamente 40% para oyentes desconocidos y 65% para oyentes familiares, basándose en el análisis de la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo.

MUESTRA DE LENGUAJE ESPONTÁNEO

La muestra de lenguaje espontáneo de Mateo reveló una longitud media de enunciado (MLU, por sus siglas en inglés) de 2.1 morfemas, considerablemente por debajo de lo esperado para su edad. Se observaron principalmente enunciados de una y dos palabras, con uso limitado de morfología gramatical, incluyendo omisión frecuente de artículos y marcadores de plural. Se codificaron varios enunciados como [EW] (palabra exacta) en el análisis SALT para documentar producciones espontáneas específicas.

Durante tareas de nombrar imágenes con apoyo visual, Mateo respondió correctamente en 6 de 10 ensayos con mod cues (claves moderadas), y en 3 de 10 de forma independiente. Con max cues (claves máximas), el porcentaje de respuestas correctas aumentó al 90%.

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES Y SOCIALES

Mateo se mostró sociable y motivado durante la sesión, buscando aprobación de la evaluadora, Patricia Jiménez Solano, y de su madre, Lucía Fernanda Rodríguez Paredes, después de completar tareas. No se observaron conductas repetitivas, dificultades sensoriales significativas ni problemas de atención conjunta. Mantuvo contacto visual apropiado y respondió a su nombre de manera consistente.

Según el reporte de la madre, en casa Mateo se comunica principalmente señalando, usando gestos y produciendo aproximaciones de palabras, y se frustra cuando su hermana menor, Camila Vásquez Rodríguez, no logra entenderlo. Su hermano mayor, Diego Vásquez Rodríguez, frecuentemente interpreta por él ante otros adultos, lo cual puede estar reduciendo las oportunidades de Mateo de practicar la comunicación independiente.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, el análisis del habla, la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo y la observación clínica, Mateo presenta un retraso significativo en el desarrollo del lenguaje receptivo y expresivo, con un retraso expresivo de mayor magnitud, junto con un trastorno fonológico que afecta su inteligibilidad general. Estos hallazgos son consistentes con un diagnóstico de trastorno del lenguaje y del habla (ICD-10 F80.2) y respaldan la continuación de servicios de intervención temprana bajo el IFSP.

Es importante notar que, dado que el español es el idioma dominante y primario del hogar, los déficits observados en ambos idiomas no pueden atribuirse a una exposición limitada al inglés o a bilingüismo normal, sino que reflejan un trastorno primario del lenguaje.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda que Mateo continúe recibiendo terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, con una frecuencia de dos sesiones semanales de 45 minutos cada una, administrada en español como idioma primario de intervención.

2. Se recomienda el uso del enfoque Hanen para apoyar la participación de los padres y maximizar las oportunidades de lenguaje en el entorno natural del hogar.

3. Para el componente de intervención fonológica, se recomienda el enfoque Cycles dirigido a los procesos fonológicos identificados, incluyendo la frontalización de velares y la simplificación de grupos consonánticos.

4. Se recomienda introducir estrategias de apoyo visual tipo PECS como complemento temporal mientras se fortalece el lenguaje verbal expresivo, particularmente durante momentos de frustración comunicativa.

5. Se recomienda incorporar técnicas del enfoque PROMPT para apoyar la producción motora del habla, dado el patrón de errores articulatorios observado.

6. Se recomienda coordinar con la maestra, Sandra Lopez Mejía, y la asistente, Karen Diaz, en el Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy, para reforzar las metas de lenguaje dentro del salón de clases.

7. Se recomienda educar a la familia, incluyendo a la abuela, Rosa Paredes de Rodríguez, y a la niñera, Yesenia Torres Luna, sobre estrategias de lenguaje modelado para usar de manera consistente en casa.

8. Se recomienda una reevaluación en seis meses para medir el progreso hacia los objetivos del IFSP, específicamente el Objetivo 1 (comunicación funcional de necesidades básicas) y el Objetivo 2 (inteligibilidad del habla en oraciones cortas).

CÓDIGOS DE FACTURACIÓN

Los servicios de evaluación descritos en este informe se facturaron bajo el código CPT 92523 (evaluación de habla y producción de sonidos del habla con evaluación de lenguaje), con el código de autorización AUTH-2026-003871 asociado al expediente de Mateo.

PRÓXIMOS PASOS

Este informe será compartido con el equipo del IFSP, incluyendo a la coordinadora de servicios Marisol Guzmán Herrera de la Red de Apoyo Familiar de Carolina del Norte (Family Support Network of NC), con el Dr. Manuel Ortega Castillo, y con el personal del Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy, previa autorización firmada de los padres. La reunión del equipo del IFSP está programada para el 3 de noviembre de 2026 en las oficinas del Centro de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA Piedmont).

TAHEEL PEDIATRIC THERAPY ASSOCIATES
Tarheel Pediatric Therapy Associates  Bilingual Outpatient Speech-Language Services
118 Sweetgum Court, Suite 4, Hickory, NC 28601  Phone: (828) 555-0192  Fax: (828) 555-0193

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Child's Name: Mateo Andrés Fernández ("Teo")  Date of Birth: August 9, 2021  Chronological Age: 4;2
Case/Record #: LD-48217  Medicaid ID: 998213467B
Date of Evaluation: October 2, 2026  Session: 9:00 AM–11:10 AM
Parent/Guardian: Ana Sofía Fernández (madre)  Diego Fernández (padre)
Address: 142 Willow Bend Lane, Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601
Phone: (828) 555-0471  Email: anasofiafernandez21@gmail.com
Referring Pediatrician: Dr. Rajesh Patel
Interpreter: Marisol Reyes, Certified Spanish Language Interpreter
Service Coordinator: Denise Shull, Piedmont CDSA
Evaluator: Carmen Delgado-Ruiz, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Setting: Manzanita Kids Academy (classroom observation) and Tarheel Pediatric Therapy Associates (clinic testing)

MOTIVO DE LA REMISIÓN / REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Rajesh Patel following concerns raised at Mateo's 4-year well-child visit regarding limited intelligibility and reduced sentence length in both English and Spanish. His mother, Ana Sofía Fernández, reported, "No le entendemos casi nada cuando habla rápido" ("We can hardly understand him when he talks fast"). Additional concerns were raised by his lead teacher, Ms. Holloway, at Manzanita Kids Academy, who noted that Mateo often gestures instead of using words to request items during circle time and snack time, y que "se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos."

This evaluation was coordinated through Piedmont CDSA at the request of service coordinator Denise Shull, who has followed the family since January 2024. Marisol Reyes served as the certified Spanish-language interpreter for portions of the parent interview conducted primarily en español.

ANTECEDENTES / BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his parents, Ana Sofía Fernández and Diego Fernández; his older sister, Camila (7 years); and his infant brother, Leo (9 months), at 142 Willow Bend Lane, Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601. His maternal grandmother, Rosa Martínez, lives with the family three days a week and helps with after-school childcare for Camila while Ana Sofía Fernández works evening shifts at Carolina Poultry Processing. Diego Fernández works in residential framing for Vega & Sons Framing and is often away from home before 6:30 AM and after 6:00 PM. A part-time babysitter, Yesenia Ortiz, watches Mateo on Saturday mornings so Ana Sofía Fernández can attend church.

The family dog, Chispa, is reportedly a favorite of Mateo's; during the home-language sample his mother reported he often says "Chispa corre" when the dog runs through the yard. Mateo's enrollment at Manzanita Kids Academy is subsidized through Smart Start of Catawba County.

HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA / BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Pinecrest Women's Hospital in Hickory, NC on August 9, 2021, via scheduled cesarean delivery due to breech presentation. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Ana Sofía Fernández reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care through WIC.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with 6 documented episodes between 8 and 24 months of age, treated with bilateral tympanostomy tube placement on March 3, 2023 by Dr. Melissa Okafor, ENT. Hearing was most recently screened within normal limits bilaterally per report from Dr. Rajesh Patel's office dated June 14, 2026; given the extensive otitis media history, a comprehensive audiological evaluation is recommended below rather than screening alone.

Developmental milestones were reported as follows: sat independently at 6 months, walked independently at 14 months, and first words were reported around 18 months in Spanish ("agua," "más"), followed by what the family described as a plateau. Diego Fernández noted that Mateo "casi no hablaba hasta los dos años" ("hardly spoke until he was two"). Feeding history is unremarkable; Ana Sofía Fernández denied any history of swallowing difficulty, significant reflux, or oral-motor feeding concerns, though she noted Mateo remains a picky eater and prefers pureed textures for some foods beyond what is typical for his age.

Mateo currently receives occupational therapy through Piedmont CDSA with Jennifer Kowalski, OTR/L, weekly, addressing fine motor and self-feeding goals under IFSP outcome #3. He also receives physical therapy with Brian Sutter, PT, DPT, biweekly, addressing gross motor coordination under IFSP outcome #2. No prior speech-language services have been provided.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home. Ana Sofía Fernández and Diego Fernández both grew up in Mexico and report feeling "más cómodos hablando español en casa" ("more comfortable speaking Spanish at home"). English is used primarily outside the home, particularly at Manzanita Kids Academy, where instruction is delivered in English by Ms. Holloway and her classroom assistant, Señora Ibarra, who provides some Spanish support during transitions and mealtimes.

Family history is significant for a maternal uncle who, per report, "no hablaba bien de niño pero ahora habla normal" ("didn't speak well as a child but speaks normally now"), and a paternal cousin with a diagnosed speech sound disorder. Ana Sofía Fernández denied family history of hearing loss, autism, or intellectual disability.

Mateo attends Manzanita Kids Academy five days per week from 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM. His best friend there, Josiah, reportedly helps him point to pictures during centers and "habla por él" (speaks for him) when other children do not understand him. Another classmate, Nico, was mentioned by Ms. Holloway as a peer Mateo "empuja cuando está frustrado" ("pushes when frustrated"), typically during transitions between activities.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN Y OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES / ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Assessment occurred across two sessions: September 25, 2026 (1:00 PM–2:30 PM) and October 2, 2026 (9:00 AM–11:10 AM), both conducted in a quiet therapy room at Tarheel Pediatric Therapy Associates. A supplemental classroom observation was completed at Manzanita Kids Academy on September 29, 2026, 10:15 AM–10:45 AM, during free play and circle time.

The following instruments were administered:

- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (administered in Spanish with Marisol Reyes interpreting instructions)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4), Language subtests
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5), English administration
- Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), bilingual Spanish/English edition
- Spontaneous language sample (English and Spanish), analyzed in part using SALT conventions

Mateo separated easily from Ana Sofía Fernández and transitioned into the therapy room readily on both days. Rapport was established quickly, and he was cooperative for most tasks, though attention decreased toward the end of each session, requiring frequent breaks and mod cues to return to task. He used a mix of single words and two-word combinations across both languages ("more please," "quiero agua"), with intelligibility estimated at 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners in connected speech.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS / TEST RESULTS

Test (Subtest)                                    Date Administered              Score                      Percentile        95% CI
Rossetti – Interaction-Attachment         September 25, 2026    SS 78             7th      70-86
Rossetti – Pragmatics                     September 25, 2026    SS 71             3rd      63-79
GFTA-3 – Sounds-in-Words                  October 2, 2026       SS 68             2nd      60-76
Bayley-4 – Receptive Communication        October 2, 2026       Scaled Score 6    9th      4-8
Bayley-4 – Expressive Communication       October 2, 2026       Scaled Score 5    5th      3-7
PPVT-5                                    October 2, 2026       SS 74             4th      67-81
PLS-5 – Auditory Comprehension             September 25, 2026   SS 70             2nd      62-78
PLS-5 – Expressive Communication           September 25, 2026   SS 65             1st      58-72
PLS-5 – Total Language Score               September 25, 2026   SS 66             1st      59-73

Articulation error analysis revealed gliding of liquids (/r/ → [w]), fronting of velars (/k/ → [t]), and final consonant deletion, consistent across both languages. Mateo produced "wabbit" for the target "rabbit" and "tasa" for the target "casa" (house), demonstrating a pattern of velar fronting present in both languages. This cross-linguistic pattern supports a true phonological disorder rather than a typical second-language transfer pattern.

Expressive language sample measures (English): Mean Length of Utterance (MLU) of 2.1 morphemes, total communication units 42, type-token ratio 0.38. Spanish sample measures: MLU 2.4 morphemes, total communication units 38, type-token ratio 0.41.

IMPRESIONES / IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0) and a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) affecting both English and Spanish. Scores fell consistently in the below-average to well-below-average range across both receptive and expressive domains in both languages, indicating a true bilingual language impairment rather than a language difference secondary to dual-language exposure. His difficulties with intelligibility, sentence length, and vocabulary are present across both languages, with his history of recurrent otitis media considered a likely contributing factor to early language acquisition delays.

Ana Sofía Fernández shared, "Nos preocupa que no lo entiendan en la escuela" ("we worry that he won't be understood at school"), and this concern is clinically supported by today's findings. Mateo's current profile places him at risk for continued academic and social difficulty without intervention, particularly given the upcoming transition out of early intervention.

Mateo continues to meet criteria for ongoing early intervention services through Piedmont CDSA and is expected to transition to preschool exceptional children's services through the local school district prior to kindergarten entry. Coordination between Denise Shull, the family, and Manzanita Kids Academy staff will be important during this transition period.

RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Continue individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, targeting phonological processes (velar fronting, gliding, final consonant deletion) and expressive language (sentence expansion, vocabulary growth) in both English and Spanish.

2. Refer for a comprehensive audiological re-evaluation given the extensive history of recurrent otitis media; coordinate with Dr. Rajesh Patel and Dr. Melissa Okafor regarding scheduling.

3. Continue coordination with Jennifer Kowalski, OTR/L and Brian Sutter, PT, DPT to integrate speech-language goals with existing IFSP outcomes #2 and #3.

4. Provide classroom-based strategies for Ms. Holloway and Señora Ibarra at Manzanita Kids Academy, including visual supports, modeling of expanded utterances, and bilingual vocabulary reinforcement during daily routines.

5. Family training in home-language strategies, including modeling target sounds during daily routines and mealtimes; Ana Sofía Fernández and Diego Fernández should continue reading nightly in Spanish, with emphasis on labeling and expanding Mateo's utterances rather than correcting them directly.

6. Trial of the PROMPT approach to address motor-speech planning, alongside continued Hanen-based caregiver coaching strategies already introduced during prior home visits by the early intervention team.

7. Continue bilingual exposure at home and in the community; discourage any recommendation to reduce Spanish exposure, as current evidence does not support a one-language-only approach for children with language disorders in bilingual households.

8. Re-evaluate in approximately 6 months or at the next IFSP review, tentatively scheduled for April 2, 2027.

This report was discussed with the family in Spanish with interpretation support from Marisol Reyes, and a written summary will be provided to the family in both English and Spanish. Please direct questions to Carmen Delgado-Ruiz, M.S., CCC-SLP at Tarheel Pediatric Therapy Associates, (828) 555-0192, or cdelgadoruiz@tarheelpeds.com.

Respectfully submitted,

Carmen Delgado-Ruiz, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

Daily Session Note

October 9, 2026, 2:15 PM. Mateo del Río was seen for a 45-minute individual speech-language session at Tar Heel Pediatric Therapy Services in Cary, NC. Interpreter Yesenia Alvarado-Pineda supported Spanish-English interpretation for the family throughout. Mateo's mother, Rosa del Río, reported he slept well and had no illness this week. His father, Héctor de la Cruz, works en la fábrica de muebles Hickory Furniture Plant, and Rosa works at the Piggly Wiggly grocery store, tienda de abarrotes. Mateo's stepfather info was not discussed today; his aunt, Carmen de la Cruz, who sometimes picks him up, works at una lavandería de limpieza, Sparkle Clean Services.

Mateo (age 4;2) continues to work on expressive language and articulation goals from his IFSP (Outcome 2). On admission, his PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension standard score was 73-83 (confidence interval), with age equivalent 2;6–3;0. Today's informal probe showed improved two-step direction following, 8/10 trials correct with min cues. He produced the target word "truck" as "tʌk" with stimulability for /tr/ cluster at 3 of 5 attempts using mod cues. He imitated his pet rabbit's name clearly, saying "Pepper hop," with no articulation breakdown noted.

Mateo attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare three mornings weekly; his teacher there, Ms. Fuentes, reports he is using more two-word combinations in Spanish with peers, including his classroom friend Diego Santos-Marrero. Mateo's older sister, Valentina del Río, often practices sounds with him at home per Rosa's report.

Coordination continues with his pediatrician, Dr. Sandra Whitfield, regarding a recent ENT referral for suspected fluid buildup; OT Brian Kowalczyk and PT Marisol Yáñez both see Mateo weekly through the same agency. Case coordination with CDSA of the Triangle service coordinator Latasha Jenkins confirmed the next IFSP review is scheduled for November 14, 2026. Medicaid authorization on file (ID 987654321A) covers services through December 31, 2026; record number LD-20394 was verified at intake.

Clinically, Mateo presented with mild phonological process patterns consistent with ICD-10 code F80.0, and today's session used CPT code 92507 with modifier GN. Cycles approach targeting fronting and final consonant deletion was used, alongside PROMPT tactile cueing for jaw stability during bilabial production. He achieved 70% accuracy on /k/ and /g/ in word-initial position, a notable gain from last month's 45% baseline.

Family was coached on home practice strategies using the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" framework, with Rosa demonstrating good carryover of modeling techniques. Héctor was unable to attend due to his shift at the plant but will review the home program notes sent via the parent portal. Next session scheduled for October 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM; family can reach the clinic at (919) 555-0142 with questions. Overall, Mateo continues to show steady progress toward his articulation and receptive language goals, and this clinician recommends continued twice-weekly individual therapy with ongoing bilingual interpreter support to maximize family engagement and generalization across home and daycare settings.

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN — SIX-MONTH REVIEW

CDSA Office: Piedmont Triad CDSA, serving Alamance County
Record Number: AT-2025-04871
Medicaid ID: 889204517A
Initial IFSP Date: 12 de marzo de 2025
Review Date: 9 de octubre de 2025 (10/09/2025)

Child: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodriguez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: March 3, 2024
Chronological age at review: 19 months
Address: 118 Cedar Hollow Lane, Burlington, Alamance County, NC 27217
Home Phone: (336) 555-0142

Mother: Lucia Rodriguez Garcia
Father: Jesus Flores Delgado ("Chuy")

FAMILY COMPOSITION AND EMPLOYMENT

Teo lives with both parents and two siblings in a rented home in Burlington. His older brother, Jose Flores Rodriguez ("Pepe"), is 6 years old and attends elementary school nearby. His younger sister, Valentina Flores Rodriguez, is 4 months old. Teo's paternal grandmother, Guadalupe Delgado Martinez ("Lupita"), lives with the family and provides most of his daytime care. A cousin, Juan Carlos Flores Lopez ("Juanito"), who is 5 years old, visits on weekends and plays with Teo in the backyard with the family's dog, Rocky.

Lucia Rodriguez Garcia currently works as a cook at the Restaurante El Sabor Latino (in English, the El Sabor Latino Restaurant) in downtown Burlington, and during the summer months she also works picking produce at Granja Sunrise (the Sunrise Farm) outside of Elon. Before taking the restaurant job, she worked for several years at the Tienda La Esperanza (the La Esperanza Store), also in Burlington. Chuy works full time for the Compania de Construccion Garcia (the Garcia Construction Company) and previously spent about two years at the Planta de Aves Carolina (the Carolina Poultry Plant) in Mebane before that company reduced its shifts.

SERVICE COORDINATION

Service Coordinator Hannah Whitfield of Piedmont Triad CDSA coordinated this review. Hannah Whitfield can be reached at (336) 555-0987 or hwhitfield@piedmonttriadcdsa.org. The family's bilingual Spanish interpreter, Rosa Fernandez, was present for the entire meeting, which was held at the family's home on el martes 4 de junio... correction, the review meeting was held on 10/09/2025 at 9:00 a.m. This report was prepared by Daniela Castillo-Ortiz, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist with Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC, who can be reached at (336) 555-0276 or dcastillo@carolinabilingualtherapy.com.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

When asked about her priorities for Teo, Lucia Rodriguez Garcia said, in Spanish, "Queremos que Teo pueda decir lo que necesita sin frustrarse tanto." Rosa Fernandez interpreted this as, "We want Teo to be able to say what he needs without getting so frustrated." She added that at home Teo points and grunts, and that Pepe often speaks for him, which worries her because she wants Teo to use his own words. Chuy said, "Yo quiero que aprenda ingles y espanol los dos, porque aqui en la casa hablamos espanol pero afuera todo es ingles." He is concerned that Teo is behind in both languages compared to Pepe at the same age. Lupita shared that she has noticed Teo getting more frustrated lately, sometimes throwing himself on the floor when he cannot make himself understood, and she asked for ideas she can use during the day while the parents are at work.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Teo was born at 34 weeks gestation at Alamance Regional Medical Center on March 3, 2024, weighing 4 lbs 1 oz. His Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. He was admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Alamance Regional Medical Center for 11 days for respiratory support and feeding difficulty. His attending neonatologist was Dr. Samuel Brightwater, and his outpatient pediatrician since discharge has been Dr. Adaeze Okafor at Alamance Regional Medical Center's pediatric clinic. Teo passed his newborn hearing screening in both ears before discharge, and a repeat audiologic evaluation on 11/14/2024 confirmed normal hearing bilaterally. There is no history of chronic ear infections, though Lupita reported one episode of otitis media around 14 months of age that resolved with a course of antibiotics prescribed by Dr. Okafor. Current diagnosis codes on file include ICD-10 F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and ICD-10 P07.3 (other preterm infant, history of).

DAILY ROUTINES

On a typical day, Teo wakes around 7:00 a.m. and eats breakfast with Lupita while his parents leave for work. Lucia Rodriguez Garcia leaves for the El Sabor Latino Restaurant by 7:30 a.m., and Chuy leaves for whatever job site the Garcia Construction Company has him on that week, sometimes as early as 6:45 a.m. Lupita takes Teo and his baby sister to Little Sprouts Daycare and Learning Center three mornings a week so Teo can have peer interaction, dropping him off around 9:00 a.m. and picking him up at 1:00 p.m. At daycare his lead teacher is Ms. Keisha Lopez, and he has one close friend there, Sofia, with whom he shares toys and snacks. On the days he stays home, Lupita follows a simple routine of outside play, lunch, and a nap from about 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. Pepe gets home from school around 3:15 p.m. and often plays trucks with Teo on the living room floor. Dinner is usually around 6:30 p.m., after Chuy and Lucia Rodriguez Garcia get home from work, and Teo's bedtime routine, including a bath and two books, begins around 8:00 p.m.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

The family receives nutrition support through the Alamance County WIC Program and has an open case with the Alamance County Department of Social Services for food assistance. Lucia Rodriguez Garcia reported that a caseworker there, referred to only as "the lady from DSS," helped the family apply for Medicaid for Teo and his sister. Pepe previously attended a program through Alamance-Burlington Early Head Start before starting kindergarten, and the family learned about Piedmont Triad CDSA services through a flyer from the Alamance Partnership for Children Smart Start office, which Lupita picked up during a visit for diaper vouchers.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT: COMMUNICATION

Teo was assessed using the PLS-5 (Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition) in both English and Spanish, with scores based on his stronger responses in either language per bilingual assessment protocol. His Auditory Comprehension standard score was 76 (5th percentile), and his Expressive Communication standard score was 71 (3rd percentile), both falling in the range of 70-79. His receptive age equivalent fell within 16-18 months, while his expressive age equivalent fell within 12-14 months. Spontaneous language sample analysis showed a mean length of utterance of one word, with an expressive vocabulary estimated at approximately 35 words across both languages combined, including Spanish words such as "agua," "mas," and "nene," and English words such as "ball" and "up." He produced the target word for truck as "tuck" with mod cues, and attempted "perro" (dog) as "[EW]" when unintelligible, pointing instead to Rocky. He imitated the phoneme /p/ in isolation 4 of 5 trials but was stimulable for /b/ only 1 of 5 trials with max cues. He followed one-step directions in Spanish 8/10 trials and in English 5/10 trials, suggesting stronger comprehension in his home language at this time. He used gestures, including pointing and reaching, for the majority of his communicative attempts, estimated at 80% of observed interactions during the session.

OUTCOME 1: Functional Communication

Teo will use 2-3 word combinations in Spanish and English to request desired items and activities, as measured by caregiver report and direct observation, with moderate cueing or less.

Strategies: Daniela Castillo-Ortiz will coach Lupita and Lucia Rodriguez Garcia in using the Hanen "OWL" strategies (Observe, Wait, Listen) during daily routines such as snack time and bath time. The family will be encouraged to model short phrases in whichever language feels most natural, rather than translating.

OUTCOME 2: Expressive Vocabulary Growth

Teo will increase his expressive vocabulary to 75 words across both languages combined, as measured by a parent-report vocabulary checklist completed monthly.

Strategies: Use of core vocabulary boards during daycare transitions at Little Sprouts Daycare and Learning Center, coordinated with Ms. Keisha Lopez, paired with repeated, functional modeling of target words during play with Pepe and Sofia.

OUTCOME 3: Reducing Frustration-Related Behavior

Teo will use a gesture or vocal approximation to request help or a break before engaging in floor-dropping behavior, in 3 of 5 observed opportunities.

Strategies: Introduce a simple two-picture choice board at home and at daycare; Daniela Castillo-Ortiz will model this during the next two home visits and provide Lupita with a laminated version for daytime use.

SERVICES

Speech-language therapy, direct and consultative, CPT 92523 and CPT 92507, one 45-minute session weekly in the home, provided by Daniela Castillo-Ortiz, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC, beginning March 20, 2025 and continuing through this review.

Developmental therapy consultation, provided by Rachel Kim, once monthly, focusing on play-based routines coordinated with speech-language goals.

Next IFSP review scheduled for el martes 10 de marzo de 2026 (03/10/2026), with annual IFSP update due by March 12, 2026.

Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Área del Piedmont (CDSA del Piedmont)
Oficina de Greensboro, condado de Guilford
Expediente/ID de caso: PT-2024-00892
Medicaid #: 804552913A

Niño: Mateo Alejandro Vásquez Fernández ("Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de marzo de 2024
Edad cronológica en esta revisión: 2;7 (edad corregida 2;5 por prematuridad)
Fecha de la revisión del IFSP: 9 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del IFSP inicial: 2 de mayo de 2024

Coordinadora de servicios: Yesenia Campos, Programa de Coordinación de Servicios Infantiles de Piamonte (PCSI Piamonte)
Tel. oficina: (336) 555-0199
Correo: yesenia.campos@pcsipiamonte.org

Terapeuta del habla y lenguaje: Marisol Herrera Díaz, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingüe español-inglés
Empresa: Terapias Bilingües del Piedmont, PLLC
Tel.: 336-555-0162

**S:**
Mamá Lucía Fernández Morales y papá Carlos Vásquez Ortiz presentes en la reunión junto con la coordinadora Yesenia Campos. Abuela materna Rosa Morales de Fernández cuida a Teo de lunes a viernes mientras los padres trabajan y participó por teléfono desde el inicio de la sesión.

Mamá refiere, en sus propias palabras: "Mateo entiende casi todo lo que le decimos en español e inglés pero no nos dice lo que quiere, solo señala y llora." Agrega: "Me preocupa que empiece el programa Head Start el año que viene y no lo entiendan los maestros, porque en la casa a veces le hablamos en español y a veces en inglés y no sé si eso lo confunde." Papá añade: "Queremos que hable oraciones completas antes de los tres años, como su prima en Monterrey."

Prioridades de la familia para esta revisión, tal como las expresó mamá:
1. "Que Teo me diga 'más agua' o 'quiero eso' en vez de llorar."
2. "Que ya no le dé tanto coraje cuando no lo entendemos."
3. "Que esté listo para la escuela cuando cumpla tres años."

Rutina diaria: Teo se despierta alrededor de las 6:30 a.m., desayuna con su abuela Rosa y su hermana Camila Vásquez Fernández antes de que ella salga para la escuela. Mamá trabaja de noche en el Centro de Distribución de Amazon en Kernersville y duerme la mayor parte de la mañana; papá trabaja de día instalando pisos y llega a casa hacia las 5:30 p.m.. La cena familiar es hacia las 6:00 p.m. y mamá reporta que Teo señala su plato y hace sonidos para pedir más comida, pero rara vez usa una palabra reconocible; el baño es a las 7:30 p.m. y durante este momento imita el sonido del agua pero no palabras. Se acuesta hacia las 8:15 p.m. después de que su hermana Camila le lee un libro de imágenes, rutina que ambos disfrutan según mamá.

Teo asiste al centro Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pasitos Felices los martes y jueves de 9:00 a.m. a 1:00 p.m. mientras la abuela hace mandados; su maestra ahí, la Srta. Robles, reporta que Teo juega al lado de otros niños pero rara vez se acerca a jugar con ellos, con la excepción de su compañerito Diego, con quien comparte carritos sin hablar. Otra niña del grupo, Valentina, a veces le ofrece juguetes y Teo responde con una sonrisa pero no con palabras.

La familia vive en 742 Calle Maple, Apto. 3B, Greensboro, NC 27401, en el condado de Guilford. Mascota: perro pequeño llamado Max que Teo señala y dice "guau" cuando lo ve. La familia viajó en julio pasado a visitar a parientes en Monterrey; mamá reporta que durante el viaje Teo estuvo expuesto principalmente a español y que a su regreso pareció usar más gestos, no palabras nuevas.

La familia también recibe apoyo del Departamento de Servicios Sociales del condado de Guilford (DSS de Guilford) para cuidado infantil subsidiado, y mamá asiste mensualmente a citas de WIC por el embarazo actual (28 semanas de gestación; hermana menor en camino). El pediatra de Teo, Dr. Andrea Lin, en Clínica Pediátrica de Greensboro (210 Avenida Elm, Greensboro), lo vio en su chequeo de los 30 meses el 28 de septiembre de 2026 y no encontró preocupaciones médicas nuevas, pero refirió a audiología por precaución dado el retraso de lenguaje.

La familia llama casi cada domingo a la bisabuela de Teo, Esperanza Morales, que vive en Tegucigalpa, Honduras, al número +504 2234-5678; mamá reporta que Teo reconoce su voz y dice ""Mama Pancha"" (apodo cariñoso) cuando ve su foto en el teléfono, aunque no siempre lo dice durante la llamada misma.

**O:**
Administré el Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale y partes del PLS-5 (Preschool Language Scale-5, edición en español) durante dos sesiones, el 30 de septiembre de 2026 y el 7 de octubre de 2026, en el hogar de la familia, de 10:00 a.m. a 11:00 a.m. ambas veces.

Historia de nacimiento (de expediente médico compartido por Dr. Andrea Lin): Teo nació a las 32 semanas de gestación, peso al nacer 1,790 gramos, Apgar 6/9. Egresó de la unidad neonatal después de 18 días. Historia de alimentación: succión débil en el período neonatal, resuelta hacia los 4 meses; transición a sólidos sin complicaciones a los 7 meses.

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale: Interacción-Apego dentro de límites esperados para edad corregida; Lenguaje Receptivo equivalente a edad de 18-20 meses; Lenguaje Expresivo equivalente a edad de 12-14 meses; Gestos equivalente a 16-18 meses; Juego equivalente a 14-16 meses.

PLS-5 (subpruebas administradas en español, con apoyo visual): Comprensión Auditiva puntaje estándar 73-83 (percentil 4-13), edad equivalente 2;0–2;4. Comunicación Expresiva puntaje estándar 62-72 (percentil 1-3), edad equivalente 1;2–1;6. Rango de edad equivalente combinado 14;0–18;0 meses.

Comparado con la evaluación previa del 3 de abril de 2026, donde Comunicación Expresiva fue 55-65 (percentil 1), hay mejora leve pero el niño permanece 2–3 desviaciones estándar por debajo de la media para su edad corregida.

Muestra de habla espontánea (50 minutos, hogar y juego libre): 8 palabras diferentes usadas espontáneamente: ""más"", ""agua"" (producido ""aba""), ""mamá"", ""papá"", ""no"", ""arriba"" (producido también ""aba"", homófono con agua), ""perro"" (señala a Max y dice ""guau""), ""abre"". No combina dos palabras espontáneamente; con modelo y mod cues combinó ""más agua"" 2 de 5 intentos.

Inventario fonético limitado a vocales, nasales /m/, /n/, oclusivas /p/, /b/, y glotal /h/; ausencia de /k/, /g/, /t/, /d/, /f/, /s/ y líquidas /l/, /ɾ/. Estructura silábica predominante CV y VCV; omisión consistente de consonante final y reducción de grupos consonánticos.

Comprensión de vocabulario: señala correctamente 9 de 12 objetos familiares nombrados (biberón, pelota, zapato, etc.); sigue instrucciones de un paso 4 de 5 ensayos; de dos pasos 1 de 5.

Juego simbólico: etapas tempranas presentes (alimenta a muñeca, empuja carrito haciendo sonido ""bbb""); no observado juego secuenciado de 2-3 pasos.

Examen oral-motor: simetría facial adecuada; tono ligeramente bajo en labios y mejillas; babeo mínimo residual observado durante juego concentrado; sin preocupaciones estructurales evidentes.

Observación en Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pasitos Felices el 1 de octubre de 2026 de 9:15 a.m. a 9:45 a.m.: Teo se comunicó principalmente con gestos y vocalizaciones no específicas durante círculo; la Srta. Robles reporta que usa un dispositivo de comunicación con imágenes de forma inconsistente en el aula y pide apoyo adicional de modelado para el personal.

Terapia ocupacional: Brittany Hughes, OTR/L, reporta en nota compartida del 3 de octubre de 2026 que Teo muestra búsqueda sensorial oral consistente con posible hipotonía oral leve; recomienda continuar monitoreo conjunto y considerar estrategias de alimentación.

Resumen de servicios desde el IFSP inicial: 46 sesiones de habla-lenguaje completadas entre 2 de mayo de 2024 y 30 de septiembre de 2026; 18 sesiones de terapia ocupacional en el mismo período.

Códigos de facturación de esta sesión: 92523 (evaluación habla-lenguaje), 92507 (terapia individual), modificador GN. Diagnóstico: F80.1 (trastorno del lenguaje expresivo), F80.2 (trastorno mixto receptivo-expresivo).

**A:**
Teo presenta retraso significativo de lenguaje expresivo con retraso leve-moderado de lenguaje receptivo, consistente con los hallazgos de la evaluación inicial de 2 de mayo de 2024 pero con progreso mensurable, aunque lento, dado el nivel de intervención actual. El perfil es congruente con las preocupaciones de la familia: comprensión relativamente fuerte frente a producción muy limitada explica la frustración y las rabietas descritas por mamá. El inventario fonético restringido y el patrón silábico CV/VCV son consistentes con apraxia leve del habla infantil a vigilar, aunque no se confirma diagnóstico formal en esta visita; se recomienda seguimiento si el progreso con el vocabulario no acelera en los próximos 3 meses.

La discrepancia entre comprensión y expresión, junto con el uso emergente de gestos y el inicio de combinación de dos palabras con apoyo, indica buena respuesta a la intervención con modelo y a los cues de PROMPT introducidos en la sesión pasada. Dada la transición que se acerca al programa preescolar, es prioritario aumentar el vocabulario funcional y la intencionalidad comunicativa antes de los 36 meses.

El bilingüismo del hogar no es una barrera para el progreso; se orienta a la familia que mantener ambos idiomas apoya, no retrasa, el desarrollo de lenguaje, y que la exposición mixta observada durante el viaje a Monterrey es normal y beneficiosa a largo plazo.

El progreso en el gateo gestual y el juego simbólico temprano apoya que las bases cognitivas y sociales están presentes para avanzar en lenguaje expresivo con apoyo intensivo. La hipotonía oral leve identificada por Brittany Hughes puede contribuir al inventario fonético restringido y amerita coordinación continua entre disciplinas. Se mantiene elegibilidad para servicios de Intervención Temprana del Programa de Infantes y Niños Pequeños de Carolina del Norte bajo la categoría de retraso establecido.

**P:**
Continuar sesiones de terapia del habla y lenguaje 2 veces por semana, 30 minutos cada una, en el hogar, a través de Terapias Bilingües del Piedmont, PLLC, con Marisol Herrera Díaz, CCC-SLP, bilingüe.

Resultado/Meta 1 del IFSP: Teo combinará 2-3 palabras para pedir, rechazar y comentar en al menos 4 de 5 oportunidades observadas, en español y/o inglés, para 9 de abril de 2027.
Estrategias: modelado de lenguaje aumentado (técnica de expansión), enfoque Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" para los padres, tiempo de espera de 5 segundos, uso de apoyo visual tipo PECS en el hogar y en Pasitos Felices.

Resultado/Meta 2 del IFSP: Teo producirá de forma espontánea un inventario de al menos 30 palabras funcionales (actualmente 8) para 9 de abril de 2027.
Estrategias: cues de PROMPT táctil-kinestésicas para apoyar /p/, /b/, /m/ en posición inicial; rutinas de juego repetitivas con pausas estratégicas; coordinación con abuela Rosa y mamá para generalizar vocabulario meta ("más", "abre", "ayuda") en las comidas y el baño.

Resultado/Meta 3 del IFSP: Disminuir la frecuencia de rabietas relacionadas con frustración comunicativa de un promedio de 5-6 por día a 1-2 por día, según registro de los padres, para 9 de enero de 2027.
Estrategias: enseñar gesto/signo funcional para "más" y "ayuda" como puente hacia el habla; reforzar cualquier intento verbal antes de atender la rabieta; colaboración con terapia ocupacional (Brittany Hughes, OTR/L) sobre regulación sensorial.

Resultado/Meta 4 del IFSP (nueva, agregada en esta revisión): Mejorar el tono y la coordinación oral-motora para apoyar producción de consonantes finales en al menos 3 de 5 intentos estructurados, para 9 de julio de 2027.
Estrategias: ejercicios oral-motores breves integrados en juego, coordinados con Brittany Hughes; práctica de palabras meta con consonante final en contexto de alimentación y merienda; seguimiento conjunto cada 6 semanas.

Coordinación de servicios: la coordinadora Yesenia Campos del PCSI Piamonte continuará facilitando la elegibilidad de Medicaid, el transporte a citas cuando se necesite, y la referencia a evaluación de posible apraxia infantil con un segundo especialista bilingüe si no hay progreso fonético para la próxima revisión. Se mantiene la consulta conjunta trimestral con terapia ocupacional (Brittany Hughes) y pediatría (Dr. Andrea Lin), incluyendo seguimiento del resultado de audiología pendiente.

Transición: se iniciará la planificación de transición al programa preescolar del condado de Guilford a partir de los 2;10 de edad, con reunión de transición programada para el 15 de enero de 2027; la familia será referida a Head Start de Guilford y a los Servicios Excepcionales de las Escuelas Públicas del condado de Guilford para determinar elegibilidad bajo la Parte B.

Capacitación familiar: se entregó a mamá y papá un folleto bilingüe sobre estrategias de modelado de lenguaje en el hogar; se recomienda que la abuela Rosa y la hermana Camila también usen expansión de frases cortas durante las comidas y el tiempo de juego, dado su rol diario en el cuidado de Teo.

Próxima revisión del IFSP programada para el 9 de abril de 2027. Revisión antes si hay cambio significativo en el estado del niño o en las circunstancias familiares, incluyendo el nacimiento de la hermana esperada. Contacto de la familia para coordinar citas futuras: mamá Lucía Fernández Morales al (336) 555-0147 (preferido, mensaje de texto) o papá Carlos Vásquez Ortiz al 336.555.0184; abuela Rosa Morales de Fernández disponible en horario diurno al (336) 555-0173.

Documentado por: Marisol Herrera Díaz, M.S., CCC-SLP, Terapias Bilingües del Piedmont, PLLC. Fecha de la nota: 9 de octubre de 2026.

CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Blue Ridge Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
482 Tate Boulevard, Hickory, NC 28601
Phone: (828) 555-0147 | Fax: (828) 555-0148
Email: intake@blueridgebilingualslp.com

Client Name: Mateo Andrés Fernández Reyes (called "Teo" by family)
Date of Birth: January 8, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Evaluation Dates: March 10, 2026 and March 12, 2026
Report Date: March 18, 2026
Record #: BR-20261-0462
Medicaid ID: 987654321A
Primary Language(s): English and Spanish
Examiner: Isabel Torres-Martínez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

Parent/Guardian Contact Information

Name	Relationship	Phone	Email
Marisol Reyes Flores	Mother	(828) 555-0298	marisolreyesf@gmail.com
Andrés Fernández Cruz	Father	(828) 555-0231	afernandezcruz22@yahoo.com

Home Address: 1197 Hollow Creek Road, Lenoir, NC 28645 (Caldwell County)

School/Program: Riverbend Elementary School, Caldwell County Schools
Classroom Teacher: Ms. Hannah Lopez, Pre-Kindergarten
Teaching Assistant: Mr. Carlos Medina
School-Based SLP (consulted by phone): Rachel Kim
Previous Daycare: Little Sprouts Early Learning Center

Referral Source: Dr. Daniel Osei, Catawba Valley Pediatrics
Service Coordinator: Brenda Hicks, Western Piedmont CDSA

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo is a 4;2-year-old boy referred by his pediatrician, Dr. Daniel Osei, for a comprehensive bilingual speech and language evaluation due to parent and teacher concern about limited intelligibility, reduced expressive vocabulary in both English and Spanish, and difficulty following multi-step directions in the classroom. Mateo's mother, Marisol Reyes Flores, reported that unfamiliar listeners frequently ask her to "translate" what Mateo is saying, even in Spanish. His teacher, Ms. Hannah Lopez, noted that Mateo often appears frustrated during circle time and relies on gesture to communicate wants and needs. This evaluation was requested to determine Mateo's speech sound production, receptive and expressive language skills, and eligibility for school-based or community-based speech-language services.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born on January 8, 2022, at Catawba Valley Medical Center following a pregnancy complicated by gestational hypertension. He was delivered at 38 weeks gestation via scheduled cesarean section, with a birth weight of 6 lbs, 10 oz and Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. Marisol Reyes Flores reported no complications during the newborn period and a brief hospital stay of two days. Mateo met early gross motor milestones within typical limits, per parent report, walking independently at 13 months.

Parents reported a history of frequent ear infections between 8 months and 22 months of age, with three documented episodes of otitis media treated with amoxicillin by Dr. Daniel Osei. Mateo had tympanostomy tubes placed at 23 months by an ear, nose, and throat physician, Dr. Priya Patel, at Catawba Valley Medical Center. A follow-up audiological evaluation on November 4, 2025 indicated hearing within normal limits bilaterally. No history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness was reported. Mateo's most recent well-child visit was on February 2, 2026, at which growth parameters were within normal limits.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo lives at home with his mother, Marisol Reyes Flores; his father, Andrés Fernández Cruz; and his older sister, Camila Fernández Reyes, age 7. Marisol Reyes Flores works at Foothills Poultry Processing, Inc., and Andrés Fernández Cruz works at Blue Ridge Furniture Works. Both parents report Spanish as their primary language, with Marisol Reyes Flores originally from the village of El Zapote, Honduras, and Andrés Fernández Cruz from San Marcos de Colón, Honduras. The family moved to Lenoir in 2019 to be near extended family already settled in the area.

Mateo's maternal grandmother, Hortensia Flores Pérez, lives with the family part-time and provides most after-school childcare while both parents work; she speaks exclusively Spanish to Mateo and reports that he understands her well but responds mostly in single words or gestures. Mateo also spends time regularly with two cousins who live nearby, Kevin Reyes Flores (age 6) and Dulce Reyes Flores (age 4), both of whom are reportedly more verbal and often "speak for" Mateo during play. The family's dog, Luna, is a frequent topic of Mateo's spontaneous language; during the evaluation he was heard saying, "Luna go" while pointing at the door.

Marisol Reyes Flores reported that Mateo's first words emerged around 18 months in Spanish ("mamá," "agua"), later than his sister, Camila Fernández Reyes, who reportedly spoke in short sentences by 24 months. English exposure increased substantially when Mateo began attending Little Sprouts Early Learning Center at 2;6 and later enrolled in Pre-Kindergarten at Riverbend Elementary School within Caldwell County Schools at 4;0. Parents estimate that Mateo hears approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English at home, while his school day is conducted almost entirely in English.

The family was previously connected to Western Piedmont CDSA for an early intervention screening at 30 months, coordinated by Brenda Hicks, which resulted in a recommendation for monitoring rather than direct services at that time. The family also receives nutrition support through the Caldwell County WIC Office.

EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Mateo has attended Riverbend Elementary School since August 25, 2025, placed in the Pre-Kindergarten classroom taught by Ms. Hannah Lopez with support from Mr. Carlos Medina. Classroom observation notes provided by Ms. Hannah Lopez describe Mateo as socially engaged but frequently unintelligible to peers and staff. He reportedly plays well with classmates Emma Thompson and Jayden Brooks during free choice time, and has a particular friendship with Sofia Martínez, who often repeats Mateo's requests aloud so the teaching staff can understand him. Ms. Hannah Lopez noted that Mateo follows one-step directions reliably but frequently needs repetition or demonstration for two-step directions.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted in both English and Spanish by Isabel Torres-Martínez, a bilingual speech-language pathologist employed by Blue Ridge Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC. No interpreter was required. Procedures included parent interview, review of records from Catawba Valley Pediatrics and Western Piedmont CDSA, standardized testing in both languages, speech sound sampling, language sampling, and classroom observation. Testing occurred across two sessions, on March 10, 2026 and March 12, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. and 10:00 a.m. respectively, in a quiet therapy room at the Blue Ridge Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC clinic.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo separated easily from his mother, Marisol Reyes Flores, and engaged readily with the examiner across both sessions. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of approximately 10 minutes before requiring a break. Mateo used gesture, pointing, and some vocal approximations to communicate throughout testing, and demonstrated frustration when unable to be understood, occasionally covering his mouth or looking away. Rapport was established quickly when the examiner incorporated reference to Mateo's dog, Luna, and his cousins, Kevin Reyes Flores and Dulce Reyes Flores, into play-based tasks. Results are considered a valid representation of Mateo's current speech and language skills in both languages.

STANDARDIZED TEST RESULTS

Test/Subtest	Date Administered	Standard Score	Percentile	95% Confidence Interval
Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), Auditory Comprehension	March 10, 2026	78	7th	71-85
Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), Expressive Communication	March 10, 2026	73	4th	66-80
Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), Total Language Score	March 10, 2026	74	4th	68-80
CELF Preschool-3, Sentence Structure	March 12, 2026	76	5th	69-83
CELF Preschool-3, Word Structure	March 12, 2026	81	10th	73-89
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), Sounds-in-Words	March 12, 2026	70	2nd	63-77

Spanish-language supplemental measures using informal criterion-referenced probes and the examiner's clinical judgment, since no normed Spanish articulation measure was available, indicated speech sound patterns in Spanish consistent with those observed in English, suggesting a true speech sound disorder rather than a second-language-learner pattern.

SPEECH SOUND PRODUCTION

Oral-motor structures and function were judged adequate for speech. Diadochokinetic rates were mildly reduced but within functional limits for age. Conversational speech intelligibility was estimated at approximately 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners such as Marisol Reyes Flores and Hortensia Flores Pérez.

Error patterns observed across English and Spanish samples included final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and gliding of liquids. For example, Mateo produced "ba" for "bath", "poon" for "spoon", and "wed" for "red". In Spanish, Mateo produced "pato" for "plato" and substituted [w] for /ɾ/ in words such as "perro", producing "pewo". He demonstrated stimulability for /r/ in isolation with moderate cues, and for final /t/ and /d/ in single words with minimal cues. He correctly produced /k/ and /g/ in initial position in 8 of 10 trials. No dysfluencies, resonance abnormalities, or voice quality concerns were noted in either language.

RECEPTIVE AND EXPRESSIVE LANGUAGE

In English, Mateo followed one-step directions in 9 of 10 trials but only 4 of 10 two-step directions without repetition. He identified basic vocabulary (body parts, common objects, and colors) with 85% accuracy but struggled with spatial concepts, correctly identifying "under" and "behind" but not "between" or "next to." Expressively, Mateo's utterances were primarily two- to three-word combinations such as "Luna go park" and "want juice now." Mean length of utterance was calculated at 2.4 morphemes, below the expected range of 3;0-4;0 for his age.

In Spanish, Mateo demonstrated comparable receptive skills to English, following simple commands from his grandmother, Hortensia Flores Pérez, with minimal difficulty, but his expressive Spanish was similarly limited to short phrases such as "quiero agua" and "Luna corre." Code-mixing was observed in approximately 20% of utterances, consistent with typical bilingual development rather than a language-specific deficit, though the overall reduced utterance length and limited grammatical morphology were present across both languages, supporting a primary language impairment rather than a language-difference profile.

PRAGMATIC AND SOCIAL COMMUNICATION

Mateo demonstrated age-appropriate eye contact, turn-taking during simple games, and joint attention. He initiated communication for requests but rarely for commenting or sharing information. During a play-based sample, Mateo turned to the examiner and said "look" while pointing at a toy dog, stating "like Luna," demonstrating appropriate use of gesture paired with verbalization despite limited expressive vocabulary.

CLASSROOM OBSERVATION

The examiner observed Mateo for 30 minutes on March 11, 2026, at 1:15 p.m., during free play and a structured circle-time activity in Ms. Hannah Lopez's classroom at Riverbend Elementary School. Mateo participated actively in a sorting activity alongside classmates Emma Thompson and Jayden Brooks, using gesture and single words to negotiate turns. During circle time, Mr. Carlos Medina provided visual supports that appeared to improve Mateo's ability to follow multi-step directions. Mateo's friend Sofia Martínez was observed translating his requests to the teaching staff on two occasions, consistent with the pattern described by Marisol Reyes Flores at home.

SUMMARY AND IMPRESSIONS

Mateo is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish-English) boy presenting with a moderate speech sound disorder and a moderate expressive and receptive language disorder affecting both languages. Standardized testing revealed scores in the below-average to well-below-average range across receptive language (78, 7th percentile), expressive language (73, 4th percentile), and articulation (70, 2nd percentile). Because deficits were observed consistently across both English and Spanish, these results are interpreted as reflecting a true communication disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition or bilingual code-mixing.

Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media and tympanostomy tube placement may have contributed to early speech and language delay, though his most recent audiological evaluation indicates hearing is now within normal limits. His strong social engagement, use of compensatory gesture, and stimulability for target sounds with cueing are favorable prognostic indicators for intervention.

DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSION

1. Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, both languages (F80.2)
2. Speech sound disorder (F80.0)

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for direct speech-language therapy services based on standardized scores falling more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in multiple domains.

NC INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM — IFSP REVIEW

Child: Mateo Isaías Hernández, DOB January 10, 2024, age 2;2 (26 months)
Case #: CDSA-2024-5567
Medicaid ID: 987654321B
CDSA Office: Piedmont CDSA, Burlington, Alamance County
Service Coordinator: Maria Gutierrez
Parents: Lucía Hernández (mother), Carlos Hernández (father)
Home address: 214 Magnolia Court, Mebane, 27302
Home phone: (919) 555-0148
Review date: March 3, 2026
Report by: Jennifer Alvarez, CCC-SLP, bilingual provider, Little Learners Program

S:
Visit conducted in home at 9:30 AM with Lucía Hernández present; interpreter Noelia Castillo assisted with Spanish/English exchange per family preference. Mother reports main concern remains Mateo's limited expressive vocabulary. In her words: "no me entiende y yo no le entiendo a él la mayoría del tiempo" (he doesn't understand me and I don't understand him most of the time). She states he uses mostly gestures, points, and a handful of approximations. Father, Carlos Hernández, joined by phone from work and added that Mateo gets frustrated quickly when not understood, sometimes hitting or throwing toys. Family priority ranked #1: more words for daily requests (food, drink, "more," "all done"). Priority #2: reduce frustration-related aggression toward Sol Hernández, his 6 years old sister. Priority #3: continued dual enrollment support between Little Learners Daycare and home so routines stay consistent.

Daily routine per mother: wakes 6:45 AM, breakfast with family, dropped at Little Learners Daycare by 7:30 AM on weekdays. Maternal grandmother, Rosa Fuentes, picks him up most afternoons around 3:00 PM and watches him until Lucía Hernández gets home from her shift around 5:30 PM. Bath and bedtime routine around 8:00 PM; mother notes he sleeps well, no feeding concerns currently. Family continues to receive support from Alamance County WIC for nutrition and formula/toddler supplement, and Alamance County DSS helped the family apply for food assistance last fall. Maria Gutierrez, service coordinator, has also connected the family with Smart Start of Alamance County for a childcare subsidy application and discussed a possible transition slot through Early Head Start for next fall if the subsidy is approved.

Mother reports Mateo attempted the word "sol" (sun) spontaneously twice this week while pointing out the window, consistent with the home practice target. Separately, during a tantrum Tuesday he was heard saying "Sol arriba," meaning he wanted his sister picked up — mother clarified this referenced his sister, not the vocabulary target, which created some confusion for grandmother Rosa Fuentes when reporting the utterance to mother. No new medical concerns; pediatrician Dr. Anand Patel saw him for a well visit last month, no referrals pending outside this team. Hearing screen at birth: pass bilaterally, no re-screen needed. No history of ear infections requiring tubes.

O:
Standardized and informal assessment conducted across two sessions combining CDSA office visit and home observation. Spanish-dominant exposure at home (~70%), English at daycare (~90%); exposure estimated via parent interview using a bilingual exposure questionnaire, consistent with prior evaluation.

| Measure | Date | Standard Score | 95% CI | Percentile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | March 3, 2026 | 73 | 68-78 | 4th |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | March 3, 2026 | 70 | 65-75 | 2nd |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | March 3, 2026 | 71 | 66-76 | 3rd |
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (prior) | September 10, 2025 | 65 | 59-71 | 1st |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication (prior) | September 10, 2025 | 62 | 56-68 | 1st |

Gains noted across both domains relative to prior administration; expressive growth of 8 standard score points over 26 months window, auditory comprehension growth of 8 points. Rate of growth still below expected trajectory for chronological age given 26-month timeframe.

Spontaneous word count during 20-minute home sample: 11 distinct words/approximations, up from 4 at prior review. Productions included "agua" (water), "tete" (approximation for "leche," milk), "mas" (more), "no," "ahí," "sol" (sun, x2 — target word, see S above), "papi," "ba" for "agua/vaso" unclear, "up," "dog" (approximated [dɑ]), and one two-word combination "mas agua." Articulation observed: word-initial /s/ produced correctly in 3 of 5 trials of target word "sol"; word-initial /d/ frequently substituted with [g] (e.g., "dog" → [gɑ]); liquids /l/ and /ɾ/ not yet in repertoire, consistent with developmental expectations at this age.

Observation at Little Learners Daycare on February 24, 2026: classroom teacher Angela Thompson reports Mateo plays near peers, especially classmate Diego Ramírez, but rarely initiates verbal exchange; mostly parallel play with brief gaze-sharing. During circle time Angela Thompson noted he imitated the song gesture for "sol, sol, sol" during a weather song, producing the target word with min cues (verbal model plus gesture). No peer conflicts observed during the 30-minute observation window.

Oromotor exam within normal limits; no structural concerns. Diadochokinetic rates age-appropriate for gross oral movement patterns. Play skills: engages in cause-effect toys independently, functional play with cars/dishes, beginning symbolic play (feeding doll). Joint attention present but inconsistent; responds to name 4 of 5 trials. Social communication checklist items largely within expected range except for expressive language-dependent items.

A:
Mateo continues to meet eligibility criteria for Part C services under the category of established developmental delay, expressive and receptive language, consistent with ICD-10 code F80.1 (expressive language disorder with receptive involvement). Current standard scores (70-73) place him in the moderately delayed range for both domains, improved from the severely delayed range at initial IFSP but still more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean. Bilingual exposure pattern accounted for in interpretation; delay is present and consistent across both languages per parent and teacher report, ruling out typical bilingual second-language acquisition pattern as sole explanation.

Behavioral concerns (hitting, throwing when frustrated) are judged secondary to communication frustration rather than a primary behavioral or sensory concern; no red flags for broader developmental concern noted on today's checklist. Continued dual-setting intervention (home/Little Learners Daycare and Little Learners Program clinic-based sessions) remains appropriate. Family's priorities align well with current outcome set; no change to eligibility category needed at this review. Recommend continuing current CPT-coded individual treatment sessions, code 92507, with added caregiver coaching time, code 92526 as applicable for feeding/communication coaching when swallowing-adjacent goals arise, though no feeding concerns at present.

P:
IFSP Outcome 1 (expressive vocabulary): Continue core vocabulary expansion targeting functional words across both languages — food/drink requests, "more/mas," "all done/ya," and family names. Strategies: modeling plus expansion (child says "agua," adult models "mas agua"), use of visual supports (laminated choice board) at home and Little Learners Daycare, consistent target word practice for word-initial /s/ using "sol" and similar words during daily sun/weather routine. Rosa Fuentes and Angela Thompson both trained on expansion strategy today; handout provided in Spanish and English.

IFSP Outcome 2 (reducing frustration behaviors): Introduce 3-5 core signs/gestures paired with words (more, help, all done) to give Mateo an alternative to hitting/throwing when not understood. Strategy: catch communication attempts early, model the word/sign, reinforce any approximation immediately. Discussed with Lucía Hernández and Carlos Hernández; Carlos Hernández to review handout and practice during evening routine. Sol Hernández included in brief coaching on waiting for brother to finish his turn to "talk" before responding, to reduce competition for attention that may trigger frustration.

IFSP Outcome 3 (consistency across settings and continued agency support): Maria Gutierrez to follow up on Smart Start of Alamance County subsidy application status by March 20, 2026 and confirm whether a transition evaluation for Early Head Start enrollment should begin this spring given approaching third birthday and IFSP-to-IEP transition timeline. Alamance County WIC visit already scheduled per mother for March 18, 2026 for routine recertification; no action needed from this team beyond documentation support if requested. Continue coordination with Little Learners Daycare via monthly consult visits so classroom strategies match home and clinic targets.

Service plan: Individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, continuing at Little Learners Program clinic site, beginning March 10, 2026 under current authorization. One home-based caregiver coaching visit monthly, next scheduled April 7, 2026 at 9:00 AM. One classroom consultation visit monthly at Little Learners Daycare, next scheduled March 24, 2026. Services remain billed under existing authorization through Piedmont CDSA; authorization renewal paperwork due before expiration on June 30, 2026.

Next scheduled IFSP review: September 8, 2026, six-month interval per Part C requirement. Family may contact this clinician at jalvarez@littlelearnersprogram.org or service coordinator Maria Gutierrez directly with questions between visits. General program information available at www.littlelearnersprogram.org and CDSA regional contact information at www.ncdhhs.gov/cdsa. Transportation assistance remains available through Alamance County DSS if needed for future clinic visits; family declined at this time, reporting reliable transportation.

Interpreter services continue to be offered and were utilized for today's full visit per family request; no additional language access barriers reported by family at this time. All materials provided bilingually (English/Spanish). Family demonstrated good understanding of strategies via teach-back at end of visit; mother repeated expansion strategy correctly and demonstrated sign for "more" independently.

Summary of progress since last IFSP: measurable gains in expressive vocabulary (+7 spontaneous words), improved standard scores in both domains, emerging word-initial /s/ production in target word "sol," and increased classroom engagement per teacher report. Continued moderate concern regarding expressive-receptive gap and behavioral frustration pending further vocabulary growth. Team, including family, agrees current outcomes and strategies remain appropriate; no changes to outcome wording needed at this time, only updated present levels and continued strategy refinement as documented above. Family thanked team for coordination across Piedmont CDSA, Alamance County WIC, Alamance County DSS, Smart Start of Alamance County, Little Learners Daycare, and Little Learners Program, noting it has reduced the burden of managing multiple appointments and paperwork across agencies. Visit concluded 10:45 AM. Signed electronically by Jennifer Alvarez, CCC-SLP.

HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO

Majo nació a las 37 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 2.6 kg y puntuación de Apgar de 8 y 9. Se quedó en la unidad de cuidados intermedios por 4 días por dificultad leve para alimentarse, pero no requirió sonda. La familia no reporta antecedentes de otitis media recurrente ni de pérdida auditiva. El diagnóstico actual en el expediente es trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo, código F80.2.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (en las palabras de la familia)

Durante la entrevista de revisión, la Sra. Mendoza Reyes compartió:

"Majo todavía no dice muchas palabras claras. Dice 'agua' pero suena como 'awa', y a veces solo señala lo que quiere y se frustra. Su hermano Juanito le entiende casi todo, pero en la guardería las maestras no le entienden y eso la hace llorar. Queremos que pueda decirle a Lupita y a Chuy lo que necesita, no solo a nosotros."

"También nos preocupa que no juega mucho con otros niños. En Little Learners Daycare, José Luis y Mateo juegan juntos pero Majo se queda sola con los bloques. La maestra, la Srta. Carmen Delgado Ruiz, dice que entiende instrucciones simples pero no inicia juego con otros niños."

El padre, Roberto Castillo Fuentes, añadió: "Trabajo en turnos rotativos y no siempre estoy en las sesiones, pero quiero aprender lo que practican para hacerlo también los fines de semana con ella."

Prioridades de la familia para los próximos seis meses:
1. Que Majo use más palabras y combine dos palabras para pedir cosas.
2. Que juegue al lado de otros niños sin llorar, primero en casa con Juanito y luego en la guardería.
3. Que la familia aprenda señas o gestos sencillos para usar en casa mientras se desarrolla el habla.
4. Que Majo participe más en el grupo de juego del fin de semana sin aferrarse a su mamá.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Majo se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con su abuela, Esperanza Reyes Luna, quien la cuida de lunes a viernes hasta que la mamá sale del trabajo a las 3:30 p.m.. Tres días por semana asiste a Little Learners Daycare de 9:00 a.m. a 1:00 p.m.. En producción espontánea, Majo usó un vocabulario de aproximadamente 20 palabras y combinó dos palabras en 1 de 10 oportunidades observadas, con edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo de 14-16 meses.
