RESULTADOS DEL IFSP CON ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Majo combinará dos palabras para pedir objetos y acciones en el hogar y en la guardería, en al menos 4 de 10 oportunidades observadas.
Estrategias: Usar el modelo de lenguaje expandido durante las comidas y el juego; la familia practicará frases como "más agua" y "quiero pelota" usando el enfoque de Hanen. La terapeuta modelará combinaciones de dos palabras durante las sesiones quincenales y enseñará a Esperanza Reyes Luna y a la Srta. Carmen Delgado Ruiz a ampliar los enunciados de Majo en vez de completarlos por ella.

Resultado 2: Majo jugará al lado de otro niño por al menos 5 minutos sin llorar, en 3 de 5 oportunidades observadas.
Estrategias: Practicar juego paralelo en casa con Juanito usando bloques y luego introducir turnos breves con José Luis y Mateo en la guardería, con apoyo visual y modelado de la terapeuta durante visitas de consulta. Se usarán estrategias del enfoque PROMPT para apoyar la producción motora oral mientras practica frases de juego compartido.

Resultado 3: La familia usará de manera consistente cinco señas o gestos sencillos (más, agua, ayuda, terminado, quiero) durante las rutinas diarias.
Estrategias: La terapeuta enseñará las señas a la mamá, al papá, a Guadalupe Castillo Fuentes y a Jesús Mendoza Reyes durante una sesión familiar. Se practicará el ciclo fonológico con el enfoque de Cycles para los sonidos finales omitidos, con una meta de producir /t/ final en palabras funcionales en 60-70% de oportunidades para la próxima revisión.

Resultado 4: Majo permanecerá en el grupo de juego del centro comunitario por 15 minutos sin buscar a su mamá, en 2 de 3 visitas consecutivas.
Estrategias: Practicar despedidas cortas con apoyo de un objeto de transición; la abuela y la tía acompañarán gradualmente menos tiempo dentro del salón mientras la terapeuta coordina con el personal del Centro Comunitario Horizontes.

FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES (en las palabras de la familia)

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Chuy was born at Triangle Regional Medical Center on January 15, 2024 at 34 weeks gestation. Birth weight was 4 lbs 2 oz, and Apgar scores were 6 and 8 at one and five minutes. He spent approximately 18 days in the NICU at Triangle Regional Medical Center for respiratory distress and feeding difficulty, requiring a nasogastric tube initially. Neonatologist Dr. Patricia Nguyen managed his NICU course; pediatrician Dr. Robert Kim has followed him since discharge and referred the family to the NC Infant-Toddler Program after Chuy's 12-month well-child visit raised concerns about limited babbling.

Lucía reports her pregnancy was complicated by preeclampsia, diagnosed around 30 weeks, which led to the early delivery. No other significant prenatal or postnatal complications are reported. Chuy passed his newborn hearing screening and has had no ear infections to date, per Lucía and confirmed in records from Dr. Robert Kim's office.

---

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT (Comunicación / Communication)

Receptive and expressive language were assessed using the Rosetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale and selected subtests of the PLS-5 (Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition), administered bilingually by Jennifer Castillo with input from both parents.

Auditory Comprehension standard score: 73 (age equivalent 18 months), confidence interval 65-81.
Expressive Communication standard score: 68 (age equivalent 15 months), confidence interval 60-76.

Chuy demonstrates an expressive vocabulary of approximately 12 words across both languages, including "mamá", "papá", "agua", "más", "pan", and "up". He does not yet combine two words consistently; 1 of 10 opportunities observed included a two-word approximation ("más agua"). He uses consistent gestures (pointing, reaching, pushing away) to communicate wants and needs, and responds to simple one-step directions in both Spanish and English with min cues.

Phonetic inventory includes /m/, /p/, /a/, /n/, and /w/ in word-initial position. Final consonants are frequently omitted; for example, Chuy produced [pa] for the target word "pan" with mod cues. Oral-motor structures and function appear within normal limits for feeding and emerging speech sound production; no concerns noted regarding drooling, chewing, or swallowing.

Social communication: Chuy demonstrates joint attention, shows toys to adults, and engages in brief reciprocal play, consistent with chronological age. He shows frustration when not understood, including a recent incident reported by Mrs. Patricia Gómez in which he pushed Juanito after being unable to communicate he wanted the same toy.

---

IFSP OUTCOMES / RESULTADOS (Updated at this Review)

Outcome 1: Chuy will combine two words to request and comment during daily routines (meals, play, bath), in Spanish and/or English, across home and daycare settings.
Status: Emerging. Chuy combined words 1 of 10 trials this review period, up from 0 of 10 at the last review.
Strategies: Parent coaching based on the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" approach, modeling expansions of Chuy's utterances (e.g., child says "agua," adult models "más agua") at mod cues, across both languages during daily routines. Mrs. Patricia Gómez will use the same expansion strategy during snack and play at daycare.

Outcome 2: Chuy will be understood by familiar communication partners outside the immediate family (e.g., Teo, Mrs. Patricia Gómez) for common words and short phrases.
Status: Not yet met. Intelligibility estimated at 30% to unfamiliar listeners and 60% to familiar listeners in context.
Strategies: Phonological awareness activities drawing on a modified Cycles approach targeting final consonants; visual supports modeled loosely after PECS to reduce frustration during transitions.

Outcome 3: The family will receive coaching and materials in Spanish to support language development at home, alongside English strategies used at daycare.
Status: In progress. Home visits conducted primarily in Spanish; bilingual picture books and a home communication log provided to Lucía and Miguel.

text:
Jesús Alberto Ramírez Torres, "Chuy" — speech-language evaluation report, with identifier markup, English/Spanish code-switching, letter style.

---

**Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC**
4521 Persimmon Creek Lane, Suite 2
Durham, NC 27705
Phone: (919) 555-2847 | Email: dfuentesward@piedmontbilingualspeech.com

October 2, 2026

**Re:** Speech-Language Evaluation / Evaluación de Habla y Lenguaje
**Child / Niño:** Jesús Alberto Ramírez Torres ("Chuy")
**Date of Birth / Fecha de Nacimiento:** March 14, 2022
**Case ID / CDSA:** CDSA-2026-00847
**Medicaid ID:** 482917364R
**Referring Agency:** Triangle Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA)
**Service Coordinator:** María Elena Castillo
**Evaluation Dates:** September 18, 2026 and September 25, 2026

Querida familia Alberto Ramírez Cruz y Lucía Torres Hernández,

Dear Mr. Alberto Ramírez Cruz and Ms. Lucía Torres Hernández,

Gracias por su paciencia y su calor durante las dos sesiones que pasamos con Chuy. It was a joy getting to know your familia, and I want to start by saying that Jesús is a sweet, curious, and funny little boy — "muy coqueto," as Lucía told me with a laugh during our first visit. This letter summarizes what we found during the evaluación, what it means, and what we recommend next.

**Antecedentes / Background**

Chuy was referred for a bilingual speech-language evaluation by his service coordinator at Triangle Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA), María Elena Castillo, after concerns were raised at his September 10, 2026 IFSP review about limited intelligibility and vocabulary in both English and Spanish. The family was also connected to our office through Durham County Department of Social Services (DSS), which has supported the family with housing assistance, and through Durham County WIC, which Lucía visits monthly for nutrition support for Chuy's baby brother. The family has also received parenting classes through Durham County Smart Start and, more recently, through a parent support group called Coalición de Familias Latinas por la Primera Infancia del Triángulo (COFLAPIT), which Alberto found through a flyer at church.

Chuy attends Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center three days a week, where his lead teacher, Ms. Keisha Jordan, and assistant teacher, Srta. Yolanda Pérez, both report that he is social and affectionate but hard to understand even in short phrases. "Él quiere jugar con todos," Srta. Pérez told me, "pero a veces los otros niños no le entienden." Two classmates he talks about often are Mateo "Teo" Sánchez and Juan "Juanito" Flores, who Chuy calls his "mejores amigos."

**Historial de Nacimiento y Médico / Birth and Medical History**

Jesús was born at 32 weeks gestation at Carolina Pines Regional Hospital on March 14, 2022, weighing 4 lbs 2 oz (1,870 grams), with Apgar scores of 6 and 8. He spent 19 days in the NICU at Carolina Pines Regional Hospital under the care of neonatologist Dr. Ananya Patel, with support from hospital interpreter Sofía Lugo, who helped Lucía and Alberto understand each step of his care during a very frightening time. "No hablábamos ni una palabra de inglés entonces," Lucía recalled, "y Sofía fue un ángel para nosotros."

Chuy's pediatrician, Dr. Marcus Whitfield, has followed him since discharge and referred him for an audiology screening at 18 months, which he passed bilaterally. There is no history of chronic ear infections, though Lucía noted he had "dos o tres" colds with some ear tugging as a baby. He has no diagnosed syndromes or genetic conditions. Family medical history is otherwise unremarkable; his maternal grandmother, Rosa Mendoza Torres ("Abuela Rosa"), reported that Lucía herself talked "un poquito tarde" as a toddler but caught up without therapy.

**Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje / Family and Language History**

Chuy lives with his parents, Alberto and Lucía, his older sister Guadalupe "Lupita" Ramírez Torres (age 8), and his baby brother José "Pepe" Ramírez Torres (age 1), in a home on Persimmon Creek Lane in Durham County. His grandmother, Rosa, babysits most afternoons while Alberto works at Blue Ridge Furniture Manufacturing and Lucía cares for Pepe at home.

Spanish is the primary language spoken at home. Alberto and Lucía speak almost entirely in Spanish with the children, while Lupita, who is in second grade and fluent in English from school, often code-switches with Chuy — "a veces le hablo en inglés, a veces en español, lo que salga primero," she told me with a shrug. Abuela Rosa speaks only Spanish. Chuy's exposure to English comes mainly from Lupita, from Little Sprouts, and from television.

Lucía described Chuy as "un niño muy cariñoso y bien travieso," who loves playing with his perrito Max and riding his bicycle up and down the driveway. Both parents report that Chuy's first words came late, around 22 months, and that his vocabulary has grown slowly since then. They estimate he currently uses somewhere between 75 and 100 words across both languages, mostly nouns, with very few verbs or two-word combinations. "Dice 'mamá, agua' pero no dice 'quiero agua,'" Lucía explained.

**Resultados de las Pruebas / Test Results**

Testing was conducted across two sessions, in a mix of English and Spanish, following Chuy's lead and using parent report to supplement direct observation. Below are the standardized measures administered.

```
Test / Subtest                                   Date              SS (95% CI)        %ile       AE
PLS-5 Spanish-English, Auditory Comprehension     September 18, 2026   73 (68-83)       4th      2;6-3;0
PLS-5 Spanish-English, Expressive Communication   September 18, 2026   70 (65-75)       2nd      2;3
GFTA-3, Sounds-in-Words                           September 25, 2026   76 (71-81)       5th      —
EOWPVT-SBE                                        September 25, 2026   82 (76-88)       12th     3;2
```

On the PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension subtest, Chuy showed relative strength in following simple directions with gestures but struggled with items requiring him to identify objects by function or understand negation ("muéstrame el que NO es rojo"). On Expressive Communication, he relied heavily on single words and gestures, rarely combining words into phrases even when modeled.

On the GFTA-3, Chuy demonstrated multiple phonological processes, consistent across English and Spanish. He produced final consonant deletion ("pelota" → "peota"), cluster reduction ("estrella" → "etteya"), and stopping of fricatives, substituting [t] for /s/ and [d] for /ɾ/. For "cup," he produced "tup," substituting [t] for /k/. Stimulability was fair for /s/ and /k/ in isolation with mod cues, but he could not yet produce either sound accurately in words.

On the EOWPVT-SBE, his bilingual total vocabulary score fell within the low average range, a relative strength compared to his expressive language and articulation scores.

**Observaciones Clínicas / Clinical Observations**

Throughout both sessions, Chuy was engaged, playful, and easy to redirect, though his frustration was evident when he could not make himself understood. During a play-based activity with toy animals, he pointed and said "guau guau tun," which Lucía confirmed meant "the dog is running" ("el perro está corriendo") — a phrase he could not yet produce verbally but clearly understood conceptually. When asked to imitate "estrella," he produced "etteya" consistently across three trials with min cues. When imitating "casa," he produced "tata," demonstrating both fronting and reduplication.

Chuy's oral mechanism exam was unremarkable; no structural concerns were noted with his lips, tongue, palate, or dentition. Diadochokinetic rates and oral-motor strength appeared age-appropriate, suggesting his speech sound errors are phonological rather than motor-based in origin.

Pragmatically, Chuy demonstrated good eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking in simple games, and he used gestures effectively to compensate for limited verbal output — pointing, pulling adults by the hand, and miming actions. He initiated communication frequently but relied on single words, approximations, and gesture far more than age expectations in either language.

**Impresiones / Impressions**

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and direct observation, Chuy presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language delay (ICD-10 F80.2) alongside a moderate speech sound disorder (ICD-10 F80.0) affecting both his English and Spanish phonological systems. His difficulties appear consistent across both languages, which supports a true bilingual language disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition patterns or a language difference related to limited English exposure. His relative strength in single-word vocabulary compared to grammar and sentence-level expressive language, along with his widespread phonological process use, suggests these delays will not resolve without targeted intervention.

Chuy's strong nonverbal communication skills, social engagement, and stimulability for several target sounds with cueing are positive prognostic indicators. His family's consistent, warm, language-rich home environment — in Spanish, English, or a mix of both — is also a significant strength to build on, not a barrier to address, and I want to be clear with you both: raising Chuy bilingüe is not causing his delay and should continue.

**Recomendaciones / Recommendations**

1. Chuy qualifies for ongoing Part C early intervention services through CDSA under his current IFSP. I recommend that speech-language therapy be added as a new service, with a new goal added under IFSP Outcome 3, targeting expressive vocabulary growth, early word combinations, and reduction of phonological process use.

2. Direct speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30 minutes per session (CPT 92523, CPT 92507), delivered bilingually in both English and Spanish, is recommended. Sessions should take place at 9:30 a.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays to align with Chuy's nap schedule at Little Sprouts.

3. Therapy approaches recommended include a combination of Hanen-based parent coaching strategies to build expressive language during daily routines, and the Cycles approach for phonological pattern remediation, targeting final consonant deletion and cluster reduction first.

4. I strongly encourage continued coaching for Alberto and Lucía in both languages, including simple strategies such as expanding Chuy's single words into short phrases ("agua" → "más agua, por favor") and narrating daily routines aloud.

5. I recommend coordination with Ms. Keisha Jordan and Srta. Pérez at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center to reinforce target vocabulary and sounds in the classroom, and continued communication with service coordinator María Elena Castillo at CDSA regarding the updated IFSP goal.

6. A follow-up re-evaluation is recommended in six months to monitor progress, tentatively scheduled for April 6, 2027, ahead of his next IFSP review on May 1, 2027.

7. Given the family's ongoing connection with COFLAPIT, I have included information about their bilingual parent support groups, which may be a helpful additional resource for Alberto and Lucía as they navigate this process.

Please do not hesitate to reach out with any questions. You can reach me directly at (919) 555-2847 or by email at dfuentesward@piedmontbilingualspeech.com. It was a true pleasure meeting Chuy, Lupita, and your whole familia, and I look forward to working together to help him find his voice — en los dos idiomas.

Con mucho cariño y respeto,

Daniela Fuentes-Ward, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist, Spanish-English
Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

> > RAZÓN DE LA REFERENCIA
> >
> > Majo fue referida por Ana Gutiérrez, coordinadora de servicios del CDSA de Cumberland, después de que su maestra en Little Learners Daycare, la Sra. Patricia Núñez, notó que la niña era difícil de entender comparada con sus compañeros de clase. Su madre, Lucía Castillo Pineda, también reportó preocupación porque Majo mezcla español e inglés de forma inconsistente y a veces se frustra cuando no la entienden.
> >
> > ANTECEDENTES
> >
> > María José vive con su madre, Lucía Castillo Pineda, su padre, Luis Hernández Soto, y su hermano mayor, Diego Hernández Castillo, de 7 años, en Fayetteville. La familia se mudó a Fayetteville desde La Esperanzita, Choluteca, Honduras, hace aproximadamente cinco años. Lucía trabaja dos empleos: de noche como CNA en Golden Oak Nursing Home y los fines de semana en Taquería El Sol. Luis trabaja en construcción. Debido al horario de ambos padres, Majo pasa la mayor parte del día en Little Learners Daycare y algunas tardes con su abuela materna, Rosa Pineda, quien también la cuida los fines de semana.
> >
> > HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA
> >
> > Según reporta la madre, el embarazo fue a término, con edad gestacional de 39 semanas. El parto fue vaginal sin complicaciones. Peso al nacer: 7 libras 2 onzas. Apgar: 8 al minuto uno y 9 al minuto cinco. No hubo hospitalización prolongada después del nacimiento.

María José alcanzó los hitos motores dentro de límites normales: se sentó sola a los 6 meses, caminó a los 13 meses. Las primeras palabras aparecieron tarde, alrededor de los 22 meses, y las combinaciones de dos palabras no surgieron hasta después de los 3 años. Lucía reporta que su pediatra, el Dr. Kevin Smith, recomendó observación en su cita de los 18 meses y de los 24 meses, pero fue hasta la visita de los 3 años que se hizo la referencia formal al CDSA de Cumberland.

No hay historial de pérdida auditiva reportada; se realizó un examen de audición el 15 de septiembre de 2026 con resultados dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos. No hay antecedentes de otitis media recurrente. No toma medicamentos actualmente. No hay diagnóstico médico adicional además del retraso de lenguaje (código F80.9).

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DEL LENGUAJE

El hogar es bilingüe: Lucía y Luis hablan principalmente español en casa, aunque Lucía usa algo de inglés en el trabajo y a veces con los niños. Diego es dominante en inglés debido a su escolaridad, pero entiende y responde en español con la familia. Según reporta la madre, no hay historial familiar de trastornos del habla o lenguaje, aunque menciona que un tío paterno, al que llaman cariñosamente tío Beto, "no hablaba bien hasta grande."

Majo escucha español con su familia inmediata y con su abuela Rosa, e inglés y español mezclados en Little Learners Daycare. Su maestra, la Sra. Patricia Núñez, reporta que Majo juega principalmente con dos compañeras, Emily y Valentina, y que suele usar gestos para comunicarse cuando las palabras no le salen. La familia tiene una perrita llamada Canela, a quien Majo menciona frecuentemente durante las sesiones de juego.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

La evaluación se realizó en dos sesiones en las oficinas de Little Learners Program, administradas en español con apoyo en inglés según fue necesario. Se utilizaron los siguientes instrumentos:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), subpruebas seleccionadas
- Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo durante juego dirigido
- Observación clínica en Little Learners Daycare el 7 de octubre de 2026

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

Tabla de puntuaciones:

| Prueba / Subprueba | Puntuación estándar | Percentil | Intervalo de confianza |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 78 | 7mo | 73-83 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 72 | 3er | 67-77 |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | 74 | 4to | 70-78 |
| GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | 68 | 2do | 63-73 |
| CELF Preschool-3 Sentence Structure | 75 | 5to | 70-80 |

Edad equivalente en comprensión auditiva: 2;6–3;0.

LENGUAJE RECEPTIVO

Majo obtuvo un puntaje estándar de 78 en Auditory Comprehension, que corresponde al percentil 7mo. Siguió instrucciones de dos pasos en 6 de 10 intentos, pero tuvo dificultad con conceptos espaciales como "detrás de" y "entre". Identificó correctamente 8/10 categorías básicas (animales, comida, ropa) pero solo 3 de 5 conceptos cuantitativos (más, menos, todos).

LENGUAJE EXPRESIVO

En Expressive Communication, obtuvo un puntaje estándar de 72 (percentil 3er). Su longitud media de enunciado fue de 3.1 morfemas, por debajo de lo esperado para su edad. Omitió morfemas gramaticales de forma consistente, incluyendo el plural y el pasado regular. Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, produjo enunciados como "Canela come mucho" y "yo quiero jugar", pero también mostró errores como "ayer yo come" en vez de "comí" y omisión del artículo en frases como "perro corre."

ARTICULACIÓN Y FONOLOGÍA

En el GFTA-3, obtuvo un puntaje estándar de 68 (percentil 2do). Se observaron los siguientes patrones de error:

- Sustitución de /ɾ/ por [l] en posición intervocálica (p. ej., "pelo" por "pero")
- Omisión de /s/ final en plurales
- Sustitución de /k/ por [t] en inicio de palabra
- Simplificación de grupos consonánticos, por ejemplo "fesa" por "fresa"

Inteligibilidad estimada: aproximadamente 60% con oyentes familiares y 40% con oyentes no familiares, usando contexto limitado.

PRAGMÁTICA Y JUEGO SOCIAL

Durante la observación en Little Learners Daycare, Majo inició interacción con Emily y Valentina usando principalmente gestos y palabras sueltas. Mostró frustración en dos ocasiones cuando sus compañeras no entendieron lo que quería decir sobre Canela, recurriendo a señalar y jalar la manga de la maestra, la Sra. Patricia Núñez.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Los resultados de esta evaluación son consistentes con un trastorno de lenguaje expresivo y receptivo de moderado a severo, con articulación significativamente afectada en ambos idiomas. El patrón de errores observado (sustitución de /ɾ/, simplificación de grupos consonánticos, omisión de morfemas gramaticales) es consistente con un retraso de lenguaje verdadero y no simplemente con el proceso típico de adquisición bilingüe, dado que los errores aparecen de forma similar en ambos idiomas y son más marcados que lo esperado para su edad y exposición lingüística.

Majo se beneficiaría de terapia continua centrada en el aumento de la longitud media de enunciado, el uso de morfemas gramaticales, y la producción de /ɾ/ y grupos consonánticos. Se recomienda un enfoque bilingüe que incorpore ambos idiomas del hogar, dado que la familia valora el mantenimiento del español como lengua primaria.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Continuar terapia del habla y el lenguaje a través del CDSA de Cumberland en el Little Learners Program, dos veces por semana, sesiones de 30 minutos, enfoque bilingüe español-inglés.
2. Incorporar el enfoque Hanen para fomentar el lenguaje en el contexto del juego, con participación de los padres cuando el horario laboral lo permita.
3. Trabajar producción de /ɾ/ y grupos consonánticos usando claves de mod cues (modelo más indicio táctil), avanzando hacia min cues conforme mejore la precisión.
4. Escribir dos nuevos objetivos del IFSP enfocados en morfología gramatical y ampliación del vocabulario cuantitativo y espacial.
5. Coordinar con la Sra. Patricia Núñez en Little Learners Daycare para reforzar vocabulario objetivo durante actividades de la clase.
6. Re-evaluación formal en aproximadamente 12 meses o antes de la transición al preescolar público, lo que ocurra primero.
7. Continuar monitoreo auditivo anual dado el historial de posible otitis previa reportada por la madre, aunque no confirmada en expediente.

Quedo disponible para cualquier pregunta antes de la reunión del IFSP programada para el 4 de noviembre de 2026.

Atentamente,

Mariana López Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP

Arrives Sunshine Beginnings Daycare by 8:00 a.m.; pickup ~5:30 p.m., usually by doña Lupe or older sister Sol Hernández Flores (age 5). Evenings: dinner together, bath, book routine with dad, bed ~8:00 p.m.. Weekends split between home and doña Lupe's house two blocks away; family reports baby brother Diego (age 8 months) also in home, which has increased household demands.

Employment affects scheduling. Mom works mornings at the Family Dollar store, serves evenings three days/week at El Rancho Alegre restaurant, and cleans offices weekends for Clean Sweep Commercial Services ("Trabajo en la tienda Family Dollar, en el restaurante El Rancho Alegre, y los fines de semana en el servicio de limpieza Clean Sweep Commercial Services"). Dad works overnight line at the Mercer Valley Poultry plant, picks up Saturday shifts at Catawba Valley Farms, and does side work for Blue Ridge Construction Group construction company ("Trabajo en la planta de Mercer Valley Poultry, los sábados en la granja Catawba Valley Farms, y a veces en la empresa de construcción Blue Ridge Construction Group"). Family requests evening or weekend sessions when possible; Jennifer Boyd to help identify respite coverage so doña Lupe is not the only caregiver available for appointments.

Other agencies: family receives benefits through Burke County WIC Clinic; enrolled with Smart Start of Burke County for childcare subsidy; open case with Burke County DSS for food assistance (no protective concerns). Pediatrician Dr. Patel manages well-child care; last visit noted no new medical concerns, hearing screen pass bilaterally. Mr. Tom, OT, sees Majo biweekly for fine motor/sensory regulation; no feeding concerns currently per OT or family report.

O:
Session at Sunshine Beginnings Daycare, Morganton, 9:15 a.m.–10:00 a.m., with classroom aide Miss Ana and lead teacher la maestra Carmen present for carryover coaching. Majo separated from doña Lupe without difficulty; briefly engaged peer Ethan over shared toy bin before returning to parallel play.

Admin PLS-5: Auditory Comprehension standard score 76 (5th percentile); Expressive Communication standard score 71 (3rd percentile); age equivalent 18-20 months; 90% CI 68-80. MacArthur-Bates CDI (Spanish/English combined) vocabulary ~45 words, predominantly nouns; minimal verbs, no spontaneous two-word combinations observed.

Articulation/phonology screen: stimulability fair for bilabials and alveolars; consonant inventory limited to /m, p, b, t, d, n/; final consonant deletion and cluster reduction present in both languages. Target word list for /s/ initial, picture naming: sol, sapo, silla, sopa — accuracy 2/9, errors produced as [h] or omitted. During a separate family-photo naming task, Majo pointed and said "Sol," approximated as [oh] with initial consonant omitted, spontaneously identifying her older sister — first noted spontaneous proper-name approximation this reporting period and a positive sign for emerging referential naming.

Receptive: followed one-step directions 8/10 trials without gesture cue; two-step directions 3/10 trials, improved to 6/10 with mod cues (gesture plus reduced rate). Identified body parts 6/8. Object ID from field of four 9/10.

Expressive: single-word utterances for wants/needs with min cues; imitated CV and CVC shapes with mod cues; MLU not calculable given limited spontaneous sample. No word combinations elicited despite PROMPT-informed tactile cueing; limited stimulability for combining today. Frequent jargon/vocal play; code-mixing (single English and Spanish words together) noted, consistent with bilingual input and not atypical for this exposure pattern.

Pragmatics: eye contact appropriate; joint attention established with mod cues; gaze shift to request observed 4/6 opportunities; reciprocal turn-taking in simple routines (peek-a-boo) 5/5.

Oral mechanism: structurally WNL; no feeding/swallowing concerns per Mr. Tom or family report. Services billed under CPT 92523 for today's reassessment; ongoing weekly treatment billed 92507.

A:
Majo presents with mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, ICD-10 F80.9, more pronounced expressively, consistent with prior evaluation. Scores remain below average (SS 71-76), below the -1.5 SD eligibility threshold maintained since initial IFSP. Bilingual exposure (Spanish primary at home, English/Spanish mixed at daycare) does not explain the delay; delay is present across both languages per parent/teacher report and direct observation, which rules out a typical bilingual-acquisition explanation alone.

Progress since last review (April 9, 2026) is mixed: gains noted in one-step following and joint attention; expressive vocabulary growth slower than projected (+8 words in 6 months). Spontaneous approximation of her sister's name ("Sol") marks an emerging milestone — first use of a person-referencing word beyond immediate caregiver labels ("mamá," "papá"). Persistent phonological patterns (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction) and continued inconsistency with two-step directions support continued direct, weekly intervention rather than consultative-only service.

Family engagement is strong; both parents and doña Lupe implement home strategies despite demanding schedules. Scheduling remains the primary barrier given parents' combined coverage of six part-time or shift jobs spanning store, restaurant, cleaning, plant, farm, and construction work; doña Lupe is primary daytime support and reports fatigue managing appointments without additional backup.

Eligibility for continued Infant-Toddler Program services is confirmed; delay remains documented in two developmental domains, communication and social-emotional functioning secondary to frustration behaviors. Transition planning toward preschool services must begin by 30 months per NC Infant-Toddler Program timeline; discussed possible Child Find referral closer to age 3.

P:
Continue direct bilingual SLP services 1x/week, 30 min, in-home/daycare, per current authorization. Family requests an evening slot on alternating weeks given mom's restaurant shift; Jennifer Boyd to confirm with Western Piedmont CDSA whether after-hours coverage is available under current funding.

Outcome 1 (communication, ongoing since initial IFSP June 3, 2025): Majo will use 2-word combinations to request/comment across settings. Strategies: expansion and modeling in both languages; Hanen-based "OWL" strategies (observe, wait, listen) coached with parents and doña Lupe; visual supports at Sunshine Beginnings Daycare coordinated with la maestra Carmen and Miss Ana. Criterion: 5 spontaneous 2-word combinations/session, 3 consecutive sessions.

Outcome 2 (communication): Majo will follow 2-step related directions without gesture cue 8/10 trials, 2 consecutive sessions. Strategies: carrier phrases, reduced rate, systematic fading from mod to min cues; home practice embedded in bath and mealtime routines, reviewed weekly with parents.

Outcome 3 (social-emotional, new this review): decrease frustration-related tantrums tied to communication breakdown from current daily to ≤3x/week per parent report. Strategies: core vocabulary board (English/Spanish), consistent sign/gesture pairing ("more," "help," "done"), and consistent contingent response to any communication attempt across caregivers, including doña Lupe and la maestra Carmen's classroom.

Continue OT biweekly with Mr. Tom; no new referrals indicated at this time. Service coordinator to follow up on respite support through Smart Start of Burke County so doña Lupe has backup for appointment coverage, and to confirm continued enrollment at Burke County WIC Clinic and food-assistance status with Burke County DSS.

Next IFSP review scheduled April 9, 2027. Transition conference regarding age 3 preschool services to be scheduled no later than January 2027 per NC Infant-Toddler Program timeline. Family contact: (828) 555-0193. CBTP scheduling line: scheduling@carolinabilingualtherapy.example.

Documentation reviewed with family bilingually; updated consent for continued services signed and on file. Daniela Ruiz, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish), Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Therapy Partners, PLLC.

Sibling: Camila Hernández (age 6, attends Fairview Elementary School)    Caregiver: abuela Rosa Cruz    Family Pet: Luna (dog)
Mother's Employer: Carolina Linen Services    Father's Employer: Blue Ridge Furniture Co.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES (in the family's own words)

During the review meeting held September 15, 2026 at Piedmont CDSA, Lucía Rodríguez shared, through interpreter Marisol Vega, that her biggest worry is that Teo "no habla casi nada en español ni en inglés," and that other children at Jellybean Junction sometimes "se burlan un poco" when he cannot tell them what he wants. Jorge Hernández added that at home Mateo points and grunts rather than using words, and that he worries Teo will fall behind his older sister Camila, who was "talking in full sentences by this age." Both parents want Teo to be able to ask for snacks, tell them when something hurts, and play pretend games with Camila and with his cousin Juanito during weekend visits. Lucía also noted that grandmother Rosa Cruz, who watches Teo on Tuesdays and Thursdays while Jorge works a second shift at Blue Ridge Furniture Co., has started using more gestures with him and would like coaching in Spanish on how to model two-word phrases.

Jorge also shared that his own mother raised him bilingual and worries that speaking "both languages at once" is confusing Teo. Daniela Fuentes reassured the family that dual-language exposure does not cause or worsen a language delay, and that strategies will support both English and Spanish growth. The family's top priority remains functional communication: Teo asking for "más," "agua," and "no" clearly enough that Rosa Cruz, Jorge, and Lucía all understand him without guessing.

DAILY ROUTINES

Wake Time: 7:00 AM    Breakfast Routine: eats with Camila Hernández and Lucía Rodríguez before the bus arrives

Snack Routine: Teo points at the pantry and whines; Lucía is working on waiting for him to vocalize before handing him crackers
Evening Routine: bath, books read in Spanish and English by Lucía Rodríguez, bed by 8:00 PM
Weekend Routine: visits to abuela Rosa Cruz's house; plays with cousin Juanito and the family dog Luna
Transportation Note: when Jorge's shift runs late, neighbor Teresa Blanchard picks Teo up from Jellybean Junction

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

On 9/2/2026, Teo was assessed using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale. His receptive language age equivalent was 14 months and his expressive language age equivalent was 11 months, compared to his chronological age of 2;6. Interaction-Attachment and Pragmatics items were both judged emerging, while Play and Gesture items fell within the average range.

The Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (Goldman-Fristoe-3) was administered on 09-02-2026. Teo produced only 6 of 34 target sounds correctly in single-word context, yielding a standard score of 58 (<1st percentile). He substituted /t/ for /k/ and omitted final consonants, saying "ba" for "ball" and "do" for "dog". Stimulability testing showed /m/ and /p/ were stimulable with mod cues.

The Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4), administered 2 de septiembre de 2026, yielded a cognitive scaled score of 9 (37th percentile), within the average range, with a confidence interval of 7-11. The Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition (PDMS-2), given the same day, produced a gross motor quotient of 96 (39th percentile) and a fine motor quotient of 88 (21st percentile), both within normal limits.

Birth History: Teo was born at 38 weeks gestational age, birth weight 6 lbs 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9. He has a diagnosis of Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.1) and was seen for a feeding evaluation under CPT 92526 with modifier -59 on June 18, 2026. A follow-up swallow study was ordered by Dr. Patricia Nguyen but the family has not yet scheduled it as of el martes 4 de junio.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

IFSP Outcome 1: Teo will combine two words to request desired objects and actions (e.g., "more juice", "go outside") during daily routines at home and at Jellybean Junction, as reported by Lucía Rodríguez, Jorge Hernández, and teacher Brianna Walsh. Strategies: caregiver coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" techniques; classroom staff including Brianna Walsh and assistant Darnell Ortiz will model expansion of Teo's single-word utterances using min to mod cues; Daniela Fuentes will coach the family in both English and Spanish during weekly home visits.

IFSP Outcome 2: Teo will imitate and spontaneously produce the sounds /m/, /b/, and /p/ in word-initial position with 80% accuracy (8/10 trials) across 3 consecutive sessions. Strategies: PROMPT-based tactile cueing; home practice with Rosa Cruz during Tuesday and Thursday caregiving using picture cards; data collected using SALT code [EW] to flag early word attempts; progress reviewed monthly by Daniela Fuentes.

IFSP Outcome 3: Teo will engage in 3 of 5 turn-taking exchanges during shared play with peers, including classmates Emma and Josiah at Jellybean Junction, and with his sister Camila Hernández at home. Strategies: Cycles approach adapted for pragmatic turn-taking; a visual turn-taking fan introduced by Brianna Walsh; PECS exchange supports introduced as a backup during high-frustration moments, with max cues faded to min cues over the review period.

IFSP Outcome 4: Lucía Rodríguez and Jorge Hernández will report increased confidence using bilingual strategies, measured by a caregiver confidence rubric completed at each review. Strategies: Daniela Fuentes will provide written home practice sheets in both Spanish and English; Marisol Vega will interpret during all team meetings and phone check-ins; Angela Whitfield will coordinate a referral to a bilingual parent support group through Smart Start of Guilford County.

CAROLINA PEDIATRIC SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES
4821 Monroe Road, Suite 210, Charlotte, NC 28205

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Vega (goes by "Mateo")
Date of Birth: April 14, 2021
Chronological Age: 5;5
Date of Evaluation: October 2, 2026
Report Date: October 9, 2026
Evaluating Clinician: Maria Santos, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Interpreter: Rosa Fernandez, Spanish Language Interpreter
Referring Physician: Dr. James Whitfield, MD
Medicaid ID: 928471603B
Case/Record ID: CPS-33021
Parents: Lucia Vega (mother), Carlos Cruz (father)
Home Phone: (704) 555-0148

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred by Dr. James Whitfield for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation due to concerns about delayed expressive language and reduced speech sound intelligibility, noted both en casa and at Little Learners Daycare. His mother, Lucia Vega, reports "no habla mucho para su edad" (he does not talk much for his age). His teacher, Ms. Lopez, in Lopez's room, notes that Mateo often points or gestures instead of using words, y se frustra cuando sus companeros no le entienden, including his classmate Emma, who frequently tries to play with him during center time.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY (Historia Familiar y de Lenguaje)

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucia Vega and Carlos Cruz, and his older sister, Sofia Cruz Vega, age 7. His grandmother, Carmen Vega, who the family calls Abuela Carmen, cares for him two afternoons a week after daycare. The family also has a dog named Rocky, whom Mateo loves to chase around the backyard.

At home, the language is "mezclado"—Lucia Vega reports that she and Carlos Cruz speak mostly Spanish with the children, while Sofia Cruz Vega often answers in English, which Lucia Vega says makes it hard to know "en que idioma le hablo a Mateo." Carlos Cruz works long shifts and reports that on weekends he tries to read bilingual books with Mateo, but Mateo "se distrae rapido y no se queda sentado." The family denies any other languages spoken in the home.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 39 weeks gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery at Novant Presbyterian Medical Center. Birth weight was 7 lbs 2 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. No NICU stay was required. Lucia Vega reports an unremarkable pregnancy with regular prenatal care.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with bilateral tympanostomy tubes placed at 18 months by Dr. Patricia Nguyen, ENT. Tubes were removed without complication, and the family reports no ear infections in the past year. Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. James Whitfield, of Carolina Kids Pediatrics, most recently screened vision and hearing on September 15, 2026; Mateo passed bilaterally with no concerns. No history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness is reported. Developmental milestones for gross motor skills were within normal limits; fine motor and self-feeding milestones were mildly delayed, per report, por lo cual recibe terapia ocupacional.

DEVELOPMENTAL AND EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Mateo attends Little Learners Daycare five days a week, currently placed in Ms. Lopez's room with 12 other children between ages 4 and 5. Ms. Lopez reports that Mateo primarily uses single words and occasional two-word combinations such as "mas agua" and "quiero eso," and that he understands simple one-step directions better when they are modeled first in Spanish. During a classroom observation conducted by this clinician with interpreter Rosa Fernandez present, Mateo was observed to use gesture and eye gaze to request a toy from Emma rather than verbalizing.

Mateo previously received early intervention services coordinated through Mecklenburg County CDSA, including speech-language therapy twice weekly, and a parent-coaching model based on Hanen's "It Takes Two to Talk" curriculum, delivered to Lucia Vega and Carlos Cruz with interpretation support. He transitioned at age three to outpatient services and now attends therapy twice weekly through the Little Learners Program, a clinic separate from, but often confused by family members with, Little Learners Daycare. There, treatment has included PROMPT for motor speech planning, alongside continued Hanen-based parent strategies. He also receives occupational therapy from Angela Byrne, OTR/L, and physical therapy from David Kim, PT, both at the Little Learners Program. His early intervention service coordinator, Angela Torres, continues to monitor his case through Mecklenburg County CDSA.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted in both English and Spanish, with standardized instruments administered in English and supplemented with informal Spanish-language probes conducted directly by this bilingual clinician and, for portions requiring parent interview, through interpreter Rosa Fernandez. Procedures included formal standardized testing, parent and teacher interview, classroom observation, and informal language sampling in both languages.

STANDARDIZED TEST RESULTS

Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5):

Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent
Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 5th | 3;2
Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd | 2;9
Total Language Score | 70 | 2nd | 95% CI: 64-76

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Fifth Edition (CELF-5), administered in English:

Index | Standard Score
Core Language Score | 72
Receptive Language Index | 78
Expressive Language Index | 65

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3):

Sounds-in-Words Standard Score: 62, 1st percentile. Estimated intelligibility in context was approximately 60% to unfamiliar listeners and 80% to familiar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

SPEECH SOUND PRODUCTION AND LANGUAGE SAMPLE

In connected speech, Mateo demonstrated final consonant deletion, fronting of velars (target /k/ produced as [t]), and consistent cluster reduction in both languages. When asked to name a cup of water, he said "agua" clearly during the Spanish probe but attempted "wa" for "water" during the English probe, omitting the final consonant entirely. He produced 8/10 target words correctly with moderate cues during a Spanish-language naming probe, compared to 3/10 correct on a parallel English-only probe administered with maximal cues.

Mean length of utterance in Spanish was estimated at 1.8 morphemes; in English, 1.2 morphemes, both below age expectations. Oral motor examination was within normal limits, with no concerns regarding structure, strength, or range of motion.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, interpreter-supported interview, and classroom observation, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with ICD-10 diagnosis F80.2. His speech sound disorder reduces intelligibility in both languages, though relative strengths are seen in Spanish, his primary home language. This presentation is not attributable to hearing loss, oral-motor dysfunction, or lack of language exposure, given consistent bilingual input at home from Lucia Vega and Carlos Cruz and consistent English-language exposure at Little Learners Daycare.

Mateo continues to qualify for speech-language services under both educational and medical criteria. His difficulties with intelligibility, combined with limited expressive vocabulary across both languages, place him at risk for frustration-related behaviors and reduced peer interaction, as already observed with Emma and other classmates in Ms. Lopez's room.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo should continue individual speech-language treatment twice weekly (CPT 92507), with goals targeting expressive vocabulary, early sentence structure, and speech sound accuracy in both Spanish and English.

2. A comprehensive follow-up speech sound evaluation (CPT 92523) is recommended in approximately six months to monitor progress toward intelligibility goals.

3. Continue bilingual service delivery through the Little Learners Program, with ongoing coordination between this clinician, OT Angela Byrne, and PT David Kim regarding sensory and motor factors that may affect attention and endurance during sessions.

4. Introduce a structured picture-based augmentative communication system such as PECS during periods of low intelligibility, to reduce frustration while verbal output continues to develop.

5. Consider a Cycles approach to phonological remediation, targeting final consonant production and velar fronting across both languages.

6. Continue parent coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies with Lucia Vega and Carlos Cruz, with interpreter Rosa Fernandez present to support full participation in coaching sessions conducted in Spanish.

7. If progress with PROMPT-based tactile-kinesthetic cueing plateaus, consider a trial of the Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol to support motor speech planning.

8. Maintain close coordination with Ms. Lopez at Little Learners Daycare regarding classroom communication supports, visual schedules, and structured peer interaction opportunities, including with Emma.

9. Share this report with Dr. James Whitfield and with service coordinator Angela Torres at Mecklenburg County CDSA to ensure continuity of services across providers.

10. Re-evaluate in approximately twelve months, or sooner if progress plateaus or new concerns arise, to update goals and confirm continued eligibility for services under ICD-10 code F80.2.

This evaluation and these recommendations were discussed with Lucia Vega and Carlos Cruz in Spanish with the assistance of interpreter Rosa Fernandez. The family expressed agreement with the recommendations and indicated they plan to continue services at the Little Learners Program and to share this report with Ms. Lopez at Little Learners Daycare.

Respectfully submitted,

Maria Santos, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services

HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y ANTECEDENTES MÉDICOS / BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo nació el 14 de marzo de 2024 en el Cone Health Women's Hospital en Greensboro, a las 6:42 a.m., con 34 semanas de edad gestacional tras labor de parto prematuro. Apgar scores were 6 and 8 at one and five minutes, birth weight 2,410 grams (5 lb 5 oz). He spent 11 days in the NICU, under the care of neonatologist Dr. Samuel Okafor and pediatrician Dr. Patricia Hale of Triad Pediatric Associates. Discharge diagnoses included prematurity (ICD-10 P07.39) and mild respiratory distress (ICD-10 P22.0). Su mamá, Lucía, recuerda que Mateo "no llanto fuerte" al nacer y necesitó CPAP por poco tiempo.

Developmental follow-up continued through Greensboro pediatrics. On 09/22/2025, Mateo was diagnosed with expressive-receptive language delay (ICD-10 F80.2) and features consistent with childhood apraxia of speech (ICD-10 F80.0) following an outpatient evaluation. Family history is otherwise unremarkable; Diego's side reports no known speech or language disorders, though Lucía notes a maternal uncle was "tardío para hablar" as a child.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

Lucía shared, en sus propias palabras: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Mateo no puede decir lo que quiere y se frustra, llora mucho cuando no lo entendemos." Ella añadió: "En casa hablamos los dos idiomas, pero en la guardería solo habla inglés con la maestra, y a veces se queda calladito." Diego stated, "I want him to be able to tell his grandmother in Spanish that he loves her, not just point at things." He also said he worries Mateo will "se quede atrás" compared to his cousins.

The family's priorities, in order, son: (1) que Mateo desarrolle comunicación funcional en inglés y español, tanto en casa como en la guardería; (2) que disminuyan las rabietas relacionadas con la frustración; (3) que la familia reciba estrategias para apoyarlo en casa, incluidas visitas con sus primos Valentina Torres y Andrés Torres, quienes lo visitan con frecuencia y notan que Mateo "se frustra rápido" cuando juegan juntos.

RUTINAS DIARIAS / DAILY ROUTINES

Mateo se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con sus hermanos Valeria y Joaquín antes de que su niñera, Rosa Jiménez, llegue a las 7:45 a.m. para llevarlo a él y a Valeria a Sunshine Bilingual Preschool. Su maestra ahí, Ms. Ashley Monroe, reports that Mateo plays well alongside classmates Ximena Alvarado and Liam Chen during centro de bloques, pero rara vez inicia juego verbal. En casa, la perrita de la familia, Canela, es una motivación fuerte; Mateo dirá "vamos" cuando Canela trae su correa. El baño es alrededor de las 7:30 p.m., seguido de un cuento bilingüe antes de dormir a las 8:15 p.m.. Los fines de semana, la familia visita a los abuelos, donde Mateo juega con su prima Valentina Torres y practica saludar en español.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS / OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

La familia recibe apoyo nutricional a través del WIC Program of Guilford County y tiene un caso abierto con el Guilford County Department of Social Services (Guilford DSS) para asistencia de vivienda. Lucía también asiste a clases de crianza a través de Smart Start of Guilford County. Valeria previously attended Greensboro Early Head Start before transitioning to pre-K this past fall.

Employment: Diego works at Piedmont Triad Manufacturing on second shift; Lucía works part-time at Fresh Market Grocers.

RESULTADOS DEL IFSP / IFSP OUTCOMES

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 3-4 word phrases in both English and Spanish to request and comment across settings.

Present level: On the Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual norms, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), age equivalent 2;6-3;0. On the CELF-5 Spanish, he scored in the below average range overall. He combines two words ("más agua," "quiero eso") with mod cues, and produces 3-word combinations 3 of 10 trials with max cues.

Strategy: Weekly direct therapy using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies and visual supports; home program coaching Lucía and Diego in both languages.

Outcome 2: Mateo will produce target sounds /k/, /g/, and /s/ in words with no more than min cues, in English and Spanish.

Present level: Speech sound inventory shows stimulable /k/ in isolation but omitted in words ("ato" for "gato"); /s/ substituted with [t] word-initially. Apraxia features noted: inconsistent productions of the same target, groping, and vowel distortions, consistent with ICD-10 F80.0. SALT transcript coded [EW] for an early word approximation of "pan."

Strategy: PROMPT-informed tactile-kinesthetic cueing, 2x weekly, 30-minute sessions, CPT code 92507, with home carryover using minimal pairs in both languages.

Outcome 3: Family will use consistent bilingual strategies to reduce frustration-related behaviors during transitions.

Strategy: Sarah Whitfield will coach Rosa Jiménez and classroom staff at Sunshine Bilingual Preschool in visual schedules and first-then boards; coordination with Ms. Ashley Monroe monthly. Marisol Peña will interpret during family coaching sessions as needed.

Intérprete: no requerida; evaluadora bilingüe certificada.

S: (SUBJETIVO)

Niño referido por CDSA de Piedmont a solicitud de Lucía Ramírez Torres (madre), quien reporta que su hijo Mateo ("Teo") no es entendido por personas fuera de la familia y que su hermana mayor, Camila Flores Ramírez ("Mila"), con frecuencia "traduce" lo que dice Teo a los adultos. Madre refiere preocupación desde los 18 meses cuando Mateo no decía palabras sueltas; pediatra, Dr. James Whitfield de Clínica Pediátrica Greensboro Kids' Health, recomendó evaluación a los 24 meses y la familia fue referida a CDSA de Piedmont para servicios de intervención temprana. Lucía Ramírez Torres también fue conectada con Smart Start para apoyo a la crianza y con WIC para nutrición infantil durante los primeros años.

Historia de nacimiento: embarazo a término, parto vaginal sin complicaciones en Hospital Moses Cone en Greensboro. Edad gestacional 39 semanas, peso al nacer 3,400 g, Apgar 9/9. Madre niega uso de alcohol o drogas durante el embarazo. No hospitalización neonatal.

Historia médica: dos episodios de otitis media (a los 8 meses y 14 meses) tratados con antibiótico; sin tubos de ventilación. Audiometría en Clínica Pediátrica Greensboro Kids' Health el 3 de febrero de 2025 arrojó audición dentro de límites normales bilateralmente. Sin diagnóstico de trastorno del espectro autista; madre reporta que CDSA de Piedmont descartó señales de alarma en esa área durante la evaluación inicial. Niño toma vitaminas pediátricas; sin alergias conocidas. Visión no evaluada formalmente, madre no reporta preocupación.

Historia familiar y de lenguaje: hogar bilingüe español-inglés. Lucía Ramírez Torres habla principalmente español con Mateo; Pedro Flores Díaz alterna español e inglés según el contexto, ya que trabaja en Flores Construction LLC donde el ambiente laboral es predominantemente en inglés. Camila Flores Ramírez ("Mila"), de 7 años, es bilingüe fluida y asiste a escuela primaria en inglés; con frecuencia ayuda a Mateo con tareas y actúa como intérprete informal entre su hermano menor y la maestra. La abuela materna, María Elena Torres Vega, cuida a Mateo tres días por semana mientras los padres trabajan y le habla exclusivamente en español. Madre reporta que no hay otros familiares con historia de retraso de habla o lenguaje, aunque un tío paterno tuvo "problema para hablar claro" de niño, resuelto sin terapia formal.

La familia asiste a Iglesia Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe en Greensboro, donde Mateo participa en clases de catecismo para niños pequeños los domingos; madre reporta que la maestra de catecismo también ha notado que Mateo "habla como más chiquito" comparado con otros niños del grupo. La familia también participa semanalmente en el programa Leamos Juntos de la biblioteca pública del Condado de Guilford, y madre ha buscado apoyo adicional en el Centro de Recursos para Familias Hispanas, donde le hablaron sobre grupos de padres con estrategias de lenguaje en casa.

Mateo asiste a Centro de Cuidado Infantil Little Sprouts cinco días por semana; su maestra, Jennifer López, reporta en formulario escrito que Mateo juega bien en paralelo pero tiene dificultad para unirse a juego cooperativo con compañeros, en particular con su compañera de clase Sofía Benítez, quien con frecuencia se frustra cuando no entiende lo que Mateo intenta comunicar. Jennifer López también reporta conductas de frustración (tirarse al piso, llorar) cuando no es comprendido.

En casa, Mateo tiene un perro llamado Max, con quien juega con frecuencia; madre reporta que dice "[EW] Max fuera" al querer sacarlo al patio, producción espontánea codificada por la evaluadora durante observación informal.

O: (OBJETIVO)

Evaluación administrada en español e inglés por Ana Patricia Gómez-Rivera, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, LLC, en el domicilio familiar en 412 Calle Primavera, Greensboro, con autorización de CDSA de Piedmont bajo código CPT 92523 (evaluación de producción de habla y comprensión/expresión de lenguaje) y CPT 92522, diagnóstico primario sospechado ICD-10 F80.2 (trastorno de lenguaje expresivo-receptivo mixto), descartar ICD-10 F80.0 (trastorno fonológico).

Conducta durante la sesión: Mateo cooperativo, buen contacto visual, atención sostenida con descansos breves cada 10-15 minutos. Transición de inicio de sesión difícil (llanto breve, 2 minutos), resuelta con apoyo visual tipo horario de actividades basado en principios de PECS.

Pruebas administradas:

1. Preschool Language Scales–5, Spanish Edition (PLS-5 Spanish):
   - Auditory Comprehension: puntaje estándar 76, percentil 5, intervalo de confianza 71-81
   - Expressive Communication: puntaje estándar 70, percentil 2, intervalo de confianza 65-75
   - Total Language Score: puntaje estándar 71, percentil 3
   - Edad equivalente expresiva: 2;6–3;0

2. Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals–5 (CELF-5), subpruebas administradas en inglés dado uso diario en guardería:
   - Sentence Structure: puntaje escalado 6
   - Word Structure: puntaje escalado 5
   - Core Language Score: puntaje estándar 74, percentil 4

3. Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation–3 (GFTA-3):
   - Puntaje estándar 68, percentil 2
   - Errores consistentes: sustitución de /k/ por [t] en posición inicial, omisión de /s/ final, sustitución de /ɾ/ por [l] (patrón esperado en adquisición del español, pero persistente más allá de lo típico para edad)
   - Inteligibilidad en oraciones conocidas por cuidador: 60%; para oyente no familiarizado: 30%

4. Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Test–3 (REEL-3), completado por madre en español:
   - Receptive Language Age Equivalent: 30 meses
   - Expressive Language Age Equivalent: 26 meses

Tabla de resultados resumida:

| Prueba | Dominio | Puntaje estándar/escalado | Percentil |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Spanish | Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 5 |
| PLS-5 Spanish | Expressive Communication | 70 | 2 |
| CELF-5 | Core Language | 74 | 4 |
| GFTA-3 | Articulación global | 68 | 2 |

Muestra de habla espontánea (SALT), 50 enunciados codificados:
- Longitud media de enunciado en palabras: 2.3
- Producciones destacadas: "quero(sic) agua" (meta: "quiero agua"), "[EW] Teo jugar", "no veo Max" (omisión de /s/ final en "veo" no aplica, nota: error en /s/ plural "Maxes" no se dio), "mamá [EW] vamos".
- Proporción de enunciados de dos palabras o más: 8/20 en muestra de juego libre; 3 of 5 en tarea estructurada de nombrado.

Comprensión de instrucciones de dos pasos en español: 6/10 correctas sin apoyo; con señalamiento (cueing mínimo): 9/10.

Praxis oral-motora: estructuras orales dentro de límites normales en reposo; leve dificultad para secuencias motoras orales rápidas (diadococinesia), sugiere posible componente de planificación motora del habla; no se cumplen criterios completos para apraxia infantil del habla pero se recomienda monitoreo.

Juego e interacción social: Mateo inicia contacto pero con repertorio comunicativo limitado; usa principalmente gestos y palabras sueltas para solicitar, con escasa expresión de comentarios o preguntas. Durante actividad de juego simbólico con figuras de animales, produjo "perro come" espontáneamente con apoyo de modelado (cueing moderado).

A: (ANÁLISIS)

Mateo Alejandro Flores Ramírez presenta trastorno de lenguaje mixto receptivo-expresivo de moderado a severo en ambos idiomas (español e inglés), con mayor afectación expresiva, consistente con ICD-10 F80.2; hallazgos de articulación cumplen criterios adicionales para trastorno fonológico, ICD-10 F80.0. Los puntajes en PLS-5 Spanish y CELF-5 son consistentes entre sí, lo que indica que las dificultades no se explican únicamente por exposición bilingüe sino que reflejan un trastorno primario de lenguaje presente en ambos idiomas del niño. El patrón fonológico (sustitución de /k/, omisión de /s/ final, sustitución de /ɾ/) es parcialmente típico de la adquisición temprana del español pero persiste más allá del rango esperado para 4;2, lo cual sustenta el diagnóstico fonológico concurrente.

La baja inteligibilidad para oyentes no familiarizados (30%) explica directamente las conductas de frustración reportadas por la madre, por la maestra Jennifer López y observadas en la sesión actual, y el rol de "traductora" asumido por la hermana Camila Flores Ramírez. El impacto funcional es significativo en el entorno de guardería, en particular en la interacción con compañeros como Sofía Benítez, y en actividades comunitarias como el catecismo en Iglesia Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe.

Pronóstico favorable con intervención bilingüe intensiva dado el ambiente de lenguaje enriquecido en casa, el apoyo de la abuela cuidadora María Elena Torres Vega, y la motivación familiar demostrada por la participación activa en Leamos Juntos y la búsqueda de recursos en Centro de Recursos para Familias Hispanas. Mateo cumple criterios para servicios de terapia de habla-lenguaje bajo el IFSP vigente, Resultado/Meta #3 (comunicación funcional) y Meta #4 (inteligibilidad articulatoria), según revisión programada por Sandra Patel en CDSA de Piedmont.

P: (PLAN)

1. Se recomienda terapia de habla-lenguaje individual, dos veces por semana, 30 minutos por sesión, en modalidad bilingüe (español primario con generalización a inglés), proporcionada por Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, LLC.

2. Enfoque de tratamiento combinado:
   - Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk") para entrenamiento a padres, dado el rol central de Lucía Ramírez Torres y Pedro Flores Díaz como modelos de lenguaje primarios; se incluirá a María Elena Torres Vega en sesiones de coaching dado su rol de cuidadora frecuente.
   - PROMPT para abordar el componente de planificación motora del habla observado en la praxis oral-motora.
   - Enfoque de Cycles para el patrón fonológico (ciclos de /k/, /s/ final, /ɾ/), con metas rotativas cada 4-6 semanas.
   - Apoyo visual con tablero de comunicación basado en principios de PECS como puente durante períodos de baja inteligibilidad, especialmente en Centro de Cuidado Infantil Little Sprouts.
   - Considerar programa Kaufman (Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol) si la respuesta a PROMPT es lenta, dado perfil de apraxia leve a monitorear.

3. Coordinación con Centro de Cuidado Infantil Little Sprouts: se enviará carta a Jennifer López con estrategias de aula (modelado de lenguaje, tiempo de espera, apoyo visual) y se solicitará observación conjunta en 6-8 semanas.

4. Coordinación con Dr. James Whitfield en Clínica Pediátrica Greensboro Kids' Health para re-chequeo auditivo en 1 de noviembre de 2026 si no hay progreso esperado, para descartar componente auditivo residual tras episodios de otitis.

5. Notificar a Sandra Patel, coordinadora de servicios en CDSA de Piedmont, para actualizar IFSP con resultados de esta evaluación; revisión de IFSP programada para 15 de julio de 2026.

6. Educación a la familia sobre estrategias de lenguaje dual en casa; se proporcionó folleto bilingüe y se refirió a sesiones grupales de padres en Centro de Recursos para Familias Hispanas.

7. Continuar participación en Leamos Juntos como apoyo de lenguaje emergente en ambos idiomas; se sugiere a la familia también explorar programas similares en Iglesia Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe para reforzar vocabulario social y rutinas de grupo.

8. Reevaluación formal en 6 meses con PLS-5 Spanish y GFTA-3 para medir progreso; revisión informal de inteligibilidad cada 4 semanas mediante muestra de habla breve.

9. Contacto de la clínica para seguimiento de citas: (336) 555-0148 o agomez.rivera@carolinabilingualslp.com; recursos adicionales disponibles en www.carolinabilingualslp.com.
