text:
SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Child's Name / Nombre del niño: Mateo Hernández Cruz ("Teo")
Date of Birth / Fecha de nacimiento: February 14, 2024
Chronological Age / Edad cronológica: 2;8
Date of Evaluation: October 6, 2026
Time of Session / Hora de la sesión: 9:00 AM to 11:30 AM
Evaluator / Evaluadora: Maria Fuentes, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Employer / Clínica: Triad Pediatric Therapy
Report Date: October 9, 2026
CDSA Case ID: CDSA-2847
Medicaid Number / Número de Medicaid: 748293615T
Referral Source: Guilford County DSS, coordinated through Service Coordinator Angela Brooks at Piedmont CDSA
Interpreter Used: [X] No [ ] Yes (evaluator is bilingual Spanish/English)

Setting observed / Entorno observado:
[X] Home [ ] Clinic [ ] Daycare only
[X] Classroom observation also conducted at Triad Early Head Start on October 2, 2026

Household members present during evaluation:
[X] Madre [X] Padre [ ] Abuela [X] Hermana [ ] Hermano

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA

Teo was referred by Angela Brooks of Piedmont CDSA following his annual IFSP review on July 15, 2026, due to concerns about limited expressive vocabulary and the absence of two-word combinations. Both parents and his classroom teacher at Triad Early Head Start, Ms. Patterson, share this concern.

His mother, Lucía, reported: "Teo solo dice 'mamá,' 'no,' y 'agua.' No combina palabras como su hermana Sol a esta edad." His father, Jorge, added in English: "He points to what he wants more than he talks. At daycare they say he's quiet too."

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Teo was born at 36 weeks gestation at Piedmont Regional Hospital in Greensboro on February 14, 2024. Birth weight was 5 lbs 10 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes respectively. He required a 9-day NICU stay for respiratory support. Newborn hearing screening was passed bilaterally, and no hearing loss has been identified since.

Pediatrician Dr. Nguyen has followed Teo since discharge. The most recent well-child visit, on September 3, 2026, noted no concerns outside of speech and language.

Ear infections: [X] Yes, 3 episodes, resolved [ ] Tubes placed
Vision/hearing screening: [X] Passed [ ] Referred

Gross motor milestones: sat independently at 7 months, walked at 15 months. Fine motor and feeding skills are age-appropriate per mother's report.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DEL LENGUAJE

Household composition / Composición del hogar:

Teo lives with his mother, Lucía Hernández Cruz; his father, Jorge Hernández Flores; his older sister, Sol Hernández (age 6); and his younger brother, Diego Hernández (age 18 months), at 482 Willow Creek Lane, Greensboro, NC 27406, in Guilford County.

Grandmother Rosa Flores lives nearby and helps with childcare two days a week. A family friend, Carmen Díaz, babysits on weekends.

Home language use:
[X] Spanish (primary language of the home) [X] English [ ] Other
Mother's language with child: [X] Spanish only
Father's language with child: [X] Spanish [X] English (more comfortable in English due to his job site)

Parent occupations / Ocupaciones de los padres:

Jorge works at Triad Construction Company (en español, la Compañía de Construcción Triad), frequently on job sites outside Greensboro, which limits his availability for daytime appointments.

Lucía currently cleans houses for Sparkle Clean Services (en español, Servicios de Limpieza Sparkle). Before Teo's birth, she worked the line at Carolina Poultry Plant (la Planta de Aves Carolina).

Extended family also contributes to childcare and transportation: an aunt, Yolanda Cruz, waits tables at El Ranchero Restaurant (el Restaurante El Ranchero); an uncle, Pedro Cruz, works seasonally at Green Valley Farm (la Granja Green Valley); and grandmother Rosa Flores previously worked at the Dollar General store (la tienda Dollar General) before retiring.

Agencies and services involved / Agencias y servicios involucrados: WIC, Guilford County Smart Start home-visiting program, Piedmont CDSA (Service Coordinator Angela Brooks, phone (336) 555-0148, email abrooks@piedmontcdsa.org), and a prior housing referral through Guilford County DSS.

Teo has received home-based developmental services since March 2025 through Piedmont CDSA, using a Hanen-based coaching model, It Takes Two to Talk, with his mother as the primary communication partner.

He currently attends Triad Early Head Start three mornings a week. [X] Daycare attendance confirmed. His teacher, Ms. Patterson, and classroom aide, Sra. Gutiérrez, report he mostly plays alone and relies on gestures to communicate.

LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION HISTORY

[ ] Monolingual Spanish exposure [X] Simultaneous bilingual exposure [ ] Sequential bilingual exposure

First words emerged around 14 months ("mamá," "agua"). No two-word combinations have been observed in either Spanish or English. Sol reportedly combined words by 18 months, which the family notes as a point of comparison.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS / OBSERVACIONES DEL COMPORTAMIENTO

[X] Cooperative [X] Easily separated from caregiver [ ] Required extended warm-up

Teo separated easily from his mother and explored toys independently throughout the session. He produced 12 single words, primarily nouns, and relied heavily on pointing and pulling adults toward desired objects. Joint attention was inconsistent and required moderate cues to establish.

During the second half of the session, his sister Sol joined and the two engaged in brief reciprocal bubble play. Teo called out, "ven, Sol!" while pulling her hand toward the bubble wand — his longest spontaneous utterance of the day, though it was functionally a vocative rather than a true combination.

STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENT RESULTS / RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale:
Interaction-Attachment — age equivalent 18-21 months
Pragmatics — age equivalent 15-18 months
Gesture — age equivalent 21-24 months
Play — age equivalent 18-21 months
Language Comprehension — age equivalent 15-18 months
Language Expression — age equivalent 12-15 months

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (Sounds-in-Words subtest): Standard score 78, 7th percentile

Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4:
Cognitive composite — 92 (30th percentile)
Language composite — 76 (5th percentile)
Motor composite — 95 (37th percentile)

Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5: Standard score 73 (4th percentile), confidence interval 68-78

Articulation and phonology sample: as part of the Sounds-in-Words probe, the target word "sol" (sun) was elicited in an initial-consonant-deletion context; Teo produced [ʔo], omitting the target phoneme /s/. Stimulability for /s/ was achieved only with maximal cues. The target word "pelota" was produced as [eota], deleting /p/ and /l/. "Agua" was produced correctly 2 of 3 trials.

Expressive vocabulary across both languages, combined and de-duplicated for cognate overlap, totaled 12 distinct words, consistent with a significant expressive language delay relative to 2;8.

IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES

Teo presents with a severe mixed receptive-expressive language delay (ICD-10 F80.2) across both of his languages, not attributable to hearing loss or oral-motor dysfunction. His limited phonetic inventory and reduced intelligibility at the single-word level also meet criteria for a co-occurring speech sound disorder (ICD-10 F80.0). CPT code 92523 was billed for this combined evaluation.

Performance fell more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in two developmental domains, meeting North Carolina eligibility criteria for continued Part C Early Intervention services. The discrepancy between Teo's expressive skills and his sister Sol's developmental trajectory at a comparable age, as described by the family, is consistent with — though not solely explanatory of — the magnitude of delay observed today.

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES

1. Continue CDSA-coordinated Early Intervention services; update IFSP Outcome 2 and Outcome 3 to reflect current expressive language and intelligibility targets.
2. Begin direct speech-language therapy twice weekly, combining PROMPT for motor-based support with a Cycles phonological approach to improve intelligibility.
3. Continue caregiver-implemented Hanen strategies (It Takes Two to Talk) with Lucía as primary communication partner. If expressive gains remain slow over the next 3 months, consider introducing PECS as a functional communication bridge, with transition to the Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol once single-word imitation stabilizes.
4. Continue WIC nutrition support and Guilford County Smart Start home visits; coordinate scheduling with Angela Brooks given Jorge's variable construction schedule.
5. Refer to Dr. Nguyen for ENT evaluation given 3 prior ear infections, to rule out any contributing conductive component.
6. Share written strategies in Spanish with grandmother Rosa Flores and babysitter Carmen Díaz, both frequent caregivers, to support consistency across settings.
7. Re-evaluate in 6 months or prior to the next IFSP annual review, anticipated July 2027.

[X] Copy of this report provided to family in Spanish and English
[X] Copy sent to Piedmont CDSA c/o Angela Brooks
[ ] Copy sent to Guilford County DSS

Respectfully submitted,

Maria Fuentes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Triad Pediatric Therapy
Phone: (336) 555-0199 | Email: mfuentes@triadpediatrictherapy.com
Report Date: October 9, 2026

text:
+ Nombre: Mateo Alejandro Fernández Ríos
+ Apodo: Teo
+ EC: 4;2
+ Fecha de nacimiento: 3 de enero de 2022 (01/03/2022)
+ Fecha de evaluación: 3 de marzo de 2026 (03/03/2026)
+ Hora de inicio / Hora de finalización: 9:15 a.m. – 11:40 a.m.
+ Contexto: Evaluación clínica ambulatoria de lenguaje y habla, realizada en las oficinas de Carolina Bilingüe de Habla y Lenguaje, PLLC, en Garner, Carolina del Norte, con una sesión complementaria de observación en el hogar de la familia en calle Hollow Oak #214, Garner, NC 27529.
+ Evaluadora: Dra. Ana María Castillo, CCC-SLP
+ Médico que refiere: Dr. Steven Marks, pediatra, Clínica Pediátrica de Garner
+ Coordinadora de servicios: Karen Smith, CDSA del Condado de Wake
+ ID Medicaid: 920384756A
+ ID de miembro de seguro (secundario): BCBSNC-884271039
+ ID de niño del NC ITP: ITP-2026-00482
+ Número de autorización: AUTH-2026-003381
+ Número de expediente: REC-48213

Resumen: Mateo es un niño de 4;2 años, bilingüe en desarrollo (español e inglés), que fue referido para esta evaluación por el Dr. Marks y por la maestra principal de Little Learners Daycare, la Srta. Pamela López, debido a preocupaciones persistentes sobre su habla poco inteligible y su lenguaje expresivo limitado, tanto en español como en inglés. Mateo recibe actualmente servicios de intervención temprana a través del Programa Little Learners, coordinado por el CDSA del Condado de Wake, bajo un Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) cuya revisión más reciente ocurrió el el martes 4 de junio de 2025. Esta evaluación se realizó para actualizar el perfil de lenguaje de Mateo antes de la próxima revisión del IFSP y para determinar la necesidad continua de servicios directos de patología del habla y lenguaje.

Antecedentes: La familia fue referida inicialmente al CDSA del Condado de Wake el 12 de enero de 2024 después de que la pediatra anterior, la Dra. Carmen Ibáñez, notara un retraso notable en el lenguaje expresivo de Mateo durante su visita de los 18 meses. La madre, Lucía Rodríguez Paredes, reportó que Mateo dijo sus primeras palabras alrededor de los 22 meses, mucho más tarde que su hermana mayor, Valentina Fernández Rodríguez. Desde el 1 de septiembre de 2024, Mateo asiste de lunes a viernes a Little Learners Daycare, en el Condado de Johnston, donde pasa aproximadamente ocho horas diarias en un ambiente mayormente en inglés. Su maestra asistente, la Srta. Jennifer Gómez, también ha expresado preocupación por la frustración de Mateo cuando sus compañeros, como Ethan y Sofía, no logran entender lo que él intenta comunicar durante el juego libre.

En el hogar, Mateo vive con su madre, Lucía Rodríguez Paredes; su padre, Carlos Fernández Soto; su hermana, Valentina Fernández Rodríguez, de 7 años; y, varios días a la semana, con su abuela materna, Rosa Paredes, quien cuida a los niños por las tardes mientras los padres trabajan. La familia también tiene un perro llamado Rocky, al que Mateo menciona con frecuencia durante las sesiones de juego.

Historia de nacimiento y desarrollo: Mateo nació a las 38 semanas de gestación mediante parto vaginal sin complicaciones mayores en el Hospital Regional de Clayton, con un peso al nacer de 3,100 gramos y puntuaciones de Apgar de 8 y 9 al minuto uno y cinco respectivamente. No requirió estancia en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales. La madre reporta un embarazo sin complicaciones, aunque menciona haber tenido una infección urinaria tratada durante el segundo trimestre.

El desarrollo motor grueso y fino de Mateo se reporta dentro de los límites esperados: caminó solo a los 13 meses y usa actualmente utensilios y crayones de manera apropiada para su edad. Sin embargo, el desarrollo del lenguaje se ha mantenido retrasado desde la infancia temprana. Mateo ha tenido múltiples episodios de otitis media, incluyendo uno de los oídos tratado médicamente en noviembre de 2023 y otro en julio de 2024; se le colocaron tubos de ventilación (miringotomía) el 9 de septiembre de 2024 en una cirugía ambulatoria realizada por el Dr. Wesley Tran, otorrinolaringólogo, en el Hospital Pinares. Desde la cirugía, la madre reporta una ligera mejoría en la atención auditiva de Mateo, aunque las preocupaciones de lenguaje y habla persisten. Un examen de audición más reciente, realizado el 15 de enero de 2026, resultó dentro de los límites normales en ambos oídos.

El expediente médico de Mateo incluye los diagnósticos F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo) y F80.1 (trastorno del lenguaje expresivo), documentados por el Dr. Marks el 20 de febrero de 2025. La evaluación actual se facturó bajo el código CPT 92523 (evaluación de habla y lenguaje), con el modificador GN correspondiente a servicios de patología del habla y lenguaje.

Historia familiar y de lenguaje: El idioma principal del hogar es el español. Lucía Rodríguez Paredes habla con Mateo casi exclusivamente en español, mientras que Carlos Fernández Soto alterna entre español e inglés dependiendo del contexto. La madre trabaja de noche en el turno nocturno del Hospital Pinares, como auxiliar de enfermería, de 11:00 p.m. a 7:00 a.m., de domingo a jueves. El padre mantiene dos empleos: durante el día trabaja en el almacén de Cedar Ridge Furniture, y por las noches, tres veces por semana, trabaja en una tienda de conveniencia que la familia conoce solamente como "QT". Debido a estos horarios, la abuela materna, Rosa Paredes, y ocasionalmente una tía, Marisol Paredes, ayudan con el cuidado de los niños durante las tardes y noches.

Lucía reporta que Mateo entiende más de lo que puede expresar, tanto en español como en inglés. En casa, usa oraciones cortas de dos a tres palabras, como "quiero agua" o "no más", y con frecuencia recurre a gestos o a tomar la mano de un adulto para señalar lo que necesita. Valentina a menudo "traduce" para su hermano menor cuando él se frustra al no poder comunicarse con otros adultos. La familia asistió a dos sesiones de capacitación para padres a través del Smart Start del Condado de Wake, en octubre de 2025, enfocadas en estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en el hogar.

Mateo también fue evaluado previamente en español con apoyo de una intérprete certificada, Yesenia Ortiz, durante la evaluación inicial de elegibilidad del 5 de febrero de 2024. En esa ocasión se determinó elegibilidad para servicios de intervención temprana bajo la Parte C, con un retraso significativo documentado en el dominio de comunicación.

Resultados de las pruebas: Durante la sesión actual, Mateo se mostró cooperador, aunque mostró períodos breves de frustración cuando no podía nombrar o describir objetos con rapidez. Se administraron pruebas estandarizadas en español e inglés, además de observación estructurada del juego y muestra de lenguaje espontáneo.

| Prueba / Subprueba | Idioma | Puntuación estándar | Percentil | Edad equivalente |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 – Comprensión Auditiva | Español | 76 | 5 | 2;6–3;0 |
| PLS-5 – Comunicación Expresiva | Español | 71 | 3 | 2;3–2;9 |
| PLS-5 – Lenguaje Total | Español | 70 | 2 | 2;6 |
| CELF Preescolar-3 – Conceptos y Siguiendo Instrucciones | Inglés | 78 | 7 | — |
| CELF Preescolar-3 – Estructura de Oraciones | Inglés | 73 | 4 | — |
| GFTA-3 – Articulación | Español/Inglés | 65 | 1 | — |
| BESA – Morfosintaxis | Español | 68 | 2 | — |

En la subprueba de Comprensión Auditiva del PLS-5, Mateo siguió instrucciones de dos pasos correctamente en 6 de 10 ensayos (60%) y señaló imágenes de vocabulario básico con precisión de 7/10. En producción de habla, se observaron errores de sustitución consistentes: sustituyó /s/ por [t] en posición inicial, como en "tol" para "sol", y omitió consonantes finales en el español, por ejemplo "flo" para "flor". En inglés, se observó el mismo patrón de simplificación de grupos consonánticos, produciendo "poon" en lugar de "spoon" con min cues del modelo de la evaluadora.

Durante una actividad de juego simbólico con figuras de animales, Mateo señaló un muñeco y dijo espontáneamente "eso é Rocky", refiriéndose a su perro Rocky, demostrando el uso de vocabulario personal relevante aunque con errores fonológicos y gramaticales consistentes con su perfil general.

Un intervalo de confianza del 95% para la puntuación compuesta de Lenguaje Total del PLS-5 fue de 65-77, ubicando a Mateo en el rango muy por debajo del promedio comparado con sus pares de la misma edad cronológica (4;2) en ambos idiomas evaluados.

Impresiones clínicas: Con base en los resultados estandarizados, la observación clínica y el reporte de los padres y maestros, Mateo presenta un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo de moderado a severo, con un componente fonológico significativo, consistente con el diagnóstico F80.2 documentado anteriormente. Sus dificultades están presentes en ambos idiomas, lo cual indica un trastorno de lenguaje primario y no simplemente una diferencia típica asociada al desarrollo bilingüe. La inteligibilidad del habla de Mateo se estima en aproximadamente 40% con oyentes familiares y menos del 20% con oyentes no familiares, lo cual limita significativamente su participación social con compañeros como Ethan y Sofía en Little Learners Daycare.

Las habilidades de comprensión auditiva, aunque también por debajo del promedio, se mantienen relativamente más fuertes que las habilidades expresivas, lo cual es un factor pronóstico positivo. La frustración conductual reportada por la Srta. López y la Srta. Gómez parece estar directamente relacionada con la brecha comunicativa de Mateo, más que con un problema conductual primario.

Recomendaciones: Se recomienda que Mateo continúe recibiendo servicios de patología del habla y lenguaje a través del Programa Little Learners y del CDSA del Condado de Wake, con una frecuencia mínima de dos sesiones individuales de 30 minutos por semana, idealmente en un modelo bilingüe o con apoyo de interpretación consistente. Se sugiere actualizar los Resultados 1 y 2 del IFSP para reflejar objetivos específicos en fonología (reducción de procesos de simplificación final y sustitución de fricativas) y en morfosintaxis expresiva en ambos idiomas.

Se recomienda específicamente lo siguiente:

1. Continuar la terapia directa de habla y lenguaje usando un enfoque de Cycles para los patrones fonológicos identificados, con apoyo visual y modelado en ambos idiomas.
2. Incorporar estrategias del enfoque Hanen para que los padres y la abuela puedan apoyar el lenguaje expresivo de Mateo durante las rutinas diarias en el hogar.
3. Coordinar con Little Learners Daycare para que la Srta. López y la Srta. Gómez refuercen el vocabulario trabajado en terapia durante las actividades de clase.
4. Realizar una nueva evaluación auditiva de seguimiento en enero de 2027 para monitorear la función auditiva tras los tubos de ventilación.
5. Programar la próxima revisión del IFSP antes del 4 de junio de 2026, fecha límite anual establecida por el CDSA del Condado de Wake.
6. Proveer a la familia materiales educativos en español sobre estimulación del lenguaje, a través del programa WIC y Programa Little Learners.

Se discutieron estos resultados con Lucía Rodríguez Paredes el mismo día de la evaluación. La familia puede comunicarse con esta evaluadora al (919) 555-0148 o con la coordinadora de servicios, Karen Smith, al (919) 555-0271, para cualquier pregunta sobre este informe o sobre la coordinación de servicios continuos.

Informe preparado y firmado electrónicamente por Dra. Ana María Castillo, CCC-SLP, Carolina Bilingüe de Habla y Lenguaje, PLLC, el 6 de marzo de 2026 (2026-03-06).

Estimada familia Carlos de la Cruz y Lucía Rodríguez-Paredes:

Les escribo para resumir la reunión de revisión del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) de su hijo Mateo de la Cruz, realizada el 14 de septiembre de 2026 en las oficinas del CDSA del Piedmont, ubicadas en 2200 Avenida Lakeview, Oficina 110, Greensboro, Carolina del Norte 27403. Su coordinadora de servicios, Ana Martínez, no pudo asistir en persona pero participó por teléfono desde la oficina satélite en Burlington. Yo soy Isabel Fuentes, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe de Piedmont Pediatric Therapy, PLLC, y preparé este resumen junto con la terapeuta ocupacional, Rebecca Hahn.

Primero, gracias por recibirnos en su hogar en 145 Calle Primrose, Burlington, Condado de Alamance, Carolina del Norte 27215 para la sesión de observación del 10 de septiembre de 2026. Fue un placer conocer también a la hermana mayor de Mateo, Sofía de la Cruz, y a su abuela, Rosa Paredes, quien los cuida los días que ambos padres trabajan.

**Información de contacto**

El número de caso del CDSA es IT-48291 y el número de Medicaid de Mateo es 784321905B. Pueden comunicarse con nuestra oficina al (336) 555-0142 o escribirnos a ifuentes@piedmontpediatrictherapy.com. También pueden encontrar información general sobre el programa Infant-Toddler en www.ncei.org.

**Lo que la familia nos dijo**

Durante la reunión, la señora Rodríguez-Paredes compartió lo siguiente: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Mateo todavía no combina palabras como su hermana lo hacía a esta edad. En la casa solo dice 'mamá', 'agua' y 'más', y se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos." El señor de la Cruz añadió: "Queremos que pueda jugar con los otros niños en la iglesia sin que se sienta aislado, y que la maestra sepa cómo ayudarlo cuando se frustra."

Las prioridades que la familia estableció para este año son: que Mateo use frases de dos palabras para pedir lo que necesita, que participe en las actividades grupales de la guardería y la iglesia, y que la familia aprenda estrategias para usarlas en casa durante las comidas, el baño y la hora de dormir.

**Rutinas diarias**

Mateo se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con su familia. A las 8:30 a.m. lo llevan al centro Little Steps Early Head Start, donde está en el salón de la maestra Pamela Ocampo. Allí, durante el tiempo de bloques, juega ocasionalmente con su compañero de salón, Daniel Chen. Toma una siesta de las 12:30 p.m. a la 2:00 p.m. y come su merienda a las 3:00 p.m.. Regresa a casa cerca de las 4:30 p.m., cena con la familia a las 6:00 p.m. y se acuesta a las 8:00 p.m.. Los domingos, la familia asiste a misa en la Iglesia Bautista Monte Carmelo, y algunos sábados por la mañana participan en el programa de lectura bilingüe de la Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Alamance, donde Mateo disfruta las canciones con movimiento.

**Otras agencias que apoyan a la familia**

Además de los servicios del Infant-Toddler Program, la familia recibe apoyo nutricional de WIC del Condado de Alamance y está inscrita en el programa Smart Start de Alamance para actividades de desarrollo infantil. La señora Rodríguez-Paredes trabaja como cajera en Food Lion en Burlington, y el señor de la Cruz trabaja en construcción con Builders Supply of Alamance.

La familia también mencionó que cuando Mateo cumpla tres años, pasará al sistema escolar local. Actualmente están explorando opciones con el Sistema de Escuelas Públicas del Condado de Alamance-Burlington, posiblemente en el Preescolar Hillcrest, si califica para servicios de educación especial preescolar.

**Resultados de la evaluación**

Administré el PLS-5 en español e inglés. En Comprensión Auditiva, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 76 (intervalo de confianza 70-82, percentil 5). En Comunicación Expresiva obtuvo 70 (percentil 2), con una edad equivalente de 18 meses. Su edad cronológica actual es 2;6. Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, produjo vocabulario de una sola palabra en un 8 de 10 intentos, pero combinó dos palabras solo en un 2 de 10 intentos. Cuando se le pidió nombrar un perro, dijo "guau guau" en lugar de la palabra completa, y al señalar una pelota dijo "pe" por "pelota".

Para la codificación de servicios se usó el código 92523, y el diagnóstico correspondiente es F80.9.

**Resultado 1: Comunicación funcional**

Mateo combinará dos palabras para pedir objetos o acciones deseadas en al menos tres entornos (casa, guardería y visitas familiares), con apoyo mínimo de un adulto, medido mediante muestra de lenguaje y reporte de los padres.

Estrategias: usaremos el enfoque Hanen para enseñar a la familia a seguir la iniciativa de Mateo y expandir sus emisiones ("agua" se convierte en "más agua"). También incorporaremos apoyos visuales inspirados en PECS durante las comidas y el juego. Pamela Ocampo usará las mismas estrategias en el salón.

**Resultado 2: Producción de sonidos**

Mateo producirá los sonidos /p/, /m/ y /b/ en posición inicial de palabra con un 80% de precisión, con señales mínimas de modelo verbal.

Estrategias: usaremos el enfoque PROMPT para apoyar la colocación articulatoria, junto con juego sensorial y canciones bilingües que refuercen los sonidos objetivo.

**Servicios y fechas**

Las sesiones de terapia del habla y lenguaje continuarán los martes de 9:00 a.m. a 9:45 a.m. en el centro Little Steps Early Head Start, y las sesiones de terapia ocupacional con Rebecca Hahn serán los jueves de 10:00 a.m. a 10:30 a.m. en el mismo lugar. El IFSP original se firmó el 3 de marzo de 2026, y esta revisión de seis meses se completó el 14 de septiembre de 2026. La próxima revisión está programada para el 14 de marzo de 2027, y la evaluación anual completa se llevará a cabo antes del 3 de marzo de 2027.

El médico de cabecera de Mateo, el Dr. Esteban Villalobos, fue informado de los resultados y apoya la continuación de los servicios.

**Consentimiento**

La familia dio su consentimiento verbal durante la reunión; la firma formal se completará en la próxima visita domiciliaria, programada para el 25 de septiembre de 2026 a las 2:00 p.m..

Gracias por su participación activa y por compartir con nosotros lo que es importante para Mateo y su familia. Si tienen preguntas antes de nuestra próxima visita, no duden en llamarme al (336) 555-0142 o escribirme a ifuentes@piedmontpediatrictherapy.com.

Con cariño y respeto,

Isabel Fuentes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje Bilingüe
Piedmont Pediatric Therapy, PLLC
Coordinadora de servicios: Ana Martínez, CDSA del Piedmont

PIEDMONT CDSA — NC INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) — ANNUAL REVIEW
Revisión Anual del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Child's Full Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Aguilar (preferred/apodo: "Teo")
Date of Birth: April 14, 2023
Date of Previous IFSP: March 18, 2026
Date of This Review: September 22, 2026
Medicaid ID: 987654321B
CDSA Record/Case ID: PC-2026-04471

Home Address: 482 Larkspur Lane, Hillsborough, Orange County, NC 27278
Home Phone: (919) 555-2847

Madre/Mother: Lucía Rodríguez Flores, who grew up in La Esperanza, a small village outside Catacamas, Honduras, before moving to North Carolina in 2019.
Padre/Father: Carlos Flores Aguilar
Hermana/Sibling: Camila Flores Rodríguez, age 6, enrolled in first grade.
Family pet: a dog named Rocky, referenced frequently during the home visit.

Primary home language: Spanish and English (hogar bilingüe — both parents and Camila code-switch regularly; Teo is exposed to both languages from birth).

Service Coordinator: Brenda Whitfield, Piedmont CDSA
CDSA Office: Piedmont CDSA, 215 Eastgate Drive, Burlington, NC 27215
Office Phone: (336) 555-9012

Report prepared by: Ana María Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist
Employer: Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC
Email: ana.castillo@carolinabilingualtherapy.com
Phone: (919) 555-3321

Pediatrician: Dr. Howard Jennings, UNC Children's Primary Care
Child's Daycare: Little Sprouts Daycare and Learning Center, Mebane, NC
Classroom Teacher: Ms. Keisha Lopez

Birth History: Born at 38 weeks gestation, birth weight 3.4 kg, Apgar scores of 8 and 9. No NICU stay reported. Eligibility established under NC's established-condition category (ICD-10 F80.2, Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder).

2. SERVICE COORDINATION / COORDINACIÓN DE SERVICIOS

Brenda Whitfield has served as service coordinator for the family since intake. During the visit on September 10, 2026, Brenda Whitfield reviewed procedural safeguards with Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Carlos Flores Aguilar in both English and Spanish, with this evaluator (this SLP) providing interpretation support as needed. The family confirmed continued consent for services and signed updated authorization forms. Brenda Whitfield also coordinated transportation through Piedmont CDSA's family support fund for the review meeting, since the family's car was in the shop that week.

3. FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES / PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA

During the home visit, Lucía Rodríguez Flores shared the following in her own words:

"Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no me puede decir lo que quiere. Se frustra mucho — grita, llora, y a veces me jala la ropa. Quiero que pueda pedirme las cosas, aunque sea con pocas palabras."

("What worries me most is that Teo can't tell me what he wants. He gets very frustrated — he screams, cries, and sometimes pulls on my clothes. I want him to be able to ask me for things, even with just a few words.")

Carlos Flores Aguilar added, in English: "At daycare, Ms. Lopez says he plays next to the other kids but doesn't really talk to them. We just want him to have friends like Ethan and Sofia do with each other."

Family priorities identified:
1. Increase Teo's expressive vocabulary for daily wants and needs, in both Spanish and English.
2. Reduce frustration-related behaviors (screaming, grabbing) by giving him functional communication alternatives.
3. Support turn-taking and play skills with peers at daycare.
4. Continue bilingual input at home; the family does not want to reduce Spanish exposure, even as English increases at daycare.

Family resources: a supportive extended family nearby, including maternal cousins Diego Pineda and Valentina Pineda, who visit weekly and play with Teo and Camila Flores Rodríguez. A trusted babysitter, Marisol Pineda (the cousins' mother), watches Teo two afternoons a week while Lucía Rodríguez Flores works a shift at a local restaurant.

4. CHILD'S PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT — SPEECH-LANGUAGE / NIVELES ACTUALES DE DESARROLLO

Standardized Assessment: Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual administration, conducted by this evaluator on September 15, 2026.

Auditory Comprehension standard score: 73-83 (95% confidence interval), corresponding to the 4th-13th percentile.
Expressive Communication standard score: 68-78, 2nd-7th percentile.
Total Language Score: 65-80.
Age equivalent range across subtests: 2;6–3;0, compared to his chronological age of 2;5 at testing.

These scores reflect significant delay in both receptive and expressive language relative to same-age peers, consistent across both English and Spanish administration conditions. Teo's Spanish and English scores were comparable, indicating a true language delay rather than a difference attributable to bilingualism alone.

Speech Sample Analysis: A 50-utterance spontaneous speech sample was collected during play with Lucía Rodríguez Flores and this clinician. Teo produced primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations. Representative productions included:

- "Rocky corre" (target: "Rocky corre" — Rocky is the family dog; production judged intelligible, no sound errors noted on this utterance).
- "Camila cayó" when describing his sister falling off a swing at the park, approximated as "Camila ca" with final consonant deletion.
- Target word "pan" (bread) produced as [pã], glottal substitution for final /n/ omitted; initial /p/ and medial /a/ intact.
- Target word "agua" produced as "aba," showing /ɾ/-for-/g/... correction: glide substitution of [w] for /g/, i.e., [aba] for /agua/.
- Target "más" produced correctly as [mas].

Phonological patterns noted: final consonant deletion, occasional cluster reduction, and substitution of [w] for /g/ in intervocalic position. Intelligibility in context was judged at approximately 60% to unfamiliar listeners and 8/10 utterances intelligible to familiar listeners (parents).

Teo used gestures (pointing, pulling adult's hand) in place of verbal requests in 9 of 10 observed requesting opportunities. He demonstrated joint attention and turn-taking in simple cause-effect play with moderate cues (mod cues) from this clinician, but required maximal cues (max cues) to imitate two-word combinations.

SALT-coded transcript excerpt available in working file, utterance 14 flagged [EW] (unintelligible word) during the dog-play segment referenced above.

5. DAILY ROUTINES AND NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS / RUTINAS DIARIAS

Home routine: Teo wakes around 7:00 a.m. and eats breakfast with Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Camila Flores Rodríguez before Camila Flores Rodríguez leaves for school at 7:45 a.m.. Rocky is a constant presence during morning play, and Teo often initiates play by patting Rocky's head and vocalizing.

Daycare routine: Teo attends Little Sprouts Daycare and Learning Center Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.. Ms. Keisha Lopez reports that during circle time, Teo sits near classmates Ethan Brooks and Sofia Nguyen but rarely initiates verbal exchanges, preferring to hand toys silently.

Babysitting routine: On Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, Marisol Pineda cares for Teo alongside her own children, Diego Pineda and Valentina Pineda, at her home. Marisol Pineda reports that Teo follows one-step directions in Spanish ("dame el vaso") with minimal cues but needs repetition for two-step directions.

Community routine: The family visits a neighborhood park on weekends where Teo observes other children playing but does not yet approach unfamiliar peers independently.

6. OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED / OTRAS AGENCIAS

The family receives nutritional support through WIC at the Orange County office and has been connected to Smart Start of Orange County for a childcare subsidy application. Brenda Whitfield noted that the family is not currently enrolled with DSS but may qualify for additional food assistance; a referral packet was given to Carlos Flores Aguilar during this visit.

A physical therapy evaluation was also completed by Jenna Whitmore, PT, DPT, due to mild gross motor delays noted at the prior review; results indicated age-appropriate gross motor skills at this time, and PT services were discontinued per team consensus on September 22, 2026.

7. IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES / RESULTADOS Y ESTRATEGIAS

Outcome 1: Teo will use a minimum of 20 functional words or signs across home, daycare, and community settings to request desired items and actions, in Spanish and/or English, as measured by parent and teacher report and direct observation, within the next 6 months.

Strategies: Family and daycare staff will use Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, including following Teo's lead, expanding his utterances, and offering choices during play and mealtimes. Rocky's presence will be used as a motivating context for requesting ("quieres jugar con Rocky?").

Outcome 2: Teo will reduce frustration behaviors (screaming, grabbing) to 2 or fewer episodes per observed session by using a functional communication alternative (word, approximation, or gesture-plus-vocalization) in 7 of 10 opportunities, within 4 months.

Strategies: This clinician will introduce PROMPT-informed tactile cueing to shape sound approximations, paired with a simple core-vocabulary board in Spanish and English. Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Marisol Pineda will be coached on honoring communication attempts before behaviors escalate.

Outcome 3: Teo will initiate a greeting or simple request with one familiar peer (such as Ethan Brooks or Sofia Nguyen) in 3 of 5 observed opportunities at daycare, within 6 months.

Strategies: Ms. Keisha Lopez will structure small-group play with visual supports; this clinician will model parallel talk and peer-directed requesting during consultative visits.

Services recommended: Individual speech-language therapy, 2x per week, 45 minutes per session, delivered in home and daycare settings, billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation) and CPT 92507 (individual treatment) as applicable.

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) — ANNUAL REVIEW

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández ("Teo")    Date of Birth: April 3, 2023    Age at Review: 2;6
CDSA Case/Child ID: CDSA-87245    Medicaid ID: 998471235B
Initial IFSP Date: December 14, 2025    This Review Date: October 2, 2026    Next Review Due: April 2, 2027
Service Coordinator: Brenda Collins    Office Phone: (336) 555-0148    Cell: 336.555.0149
CDSA Office: Piedmont CDSA    Office Address: 2100 Yanceyville Street, Greensboro, NC 27405
Mother/Guardian: Guadalupe Hernández Pérez ("Lupita")    Home Phone: 336-555-0192
Father/Guardian: Jesús Cruz Ramírez ("Chuy")    Cell Phone: (336) 555 0177
Home Address: 418 Willow Bend Road, Asheboro, NC 27203    County: Randolph County
Primary Home Language: Spanish    Secondary Language: English (emerging)    Interpreter Requested: Yes — Spanish
Evaluating/Reporting Clinician: Jennifer A. Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Employer: Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC    Clinician Phone: 919-555-0211    Email: jalvarez@carolinabilingualtherapy.com

FAMILY INFORMATION AND BACKGROUND

Teo lives at home with his parents, Lupita and Chuy, and his two older brothers, José Cruz Hernández ("Pepe"), age 7, and Juan Cruz Hernández ("Juanito"), age 5. Teo's grandmother, María Elena Pérez Gómez ("abuela Mari"), watches the boys most weekday mornings while both parents work. abuela Mari can be reached at 336-555-0133 and also keeps in touch with family in Michoacán by calling her sister at +52 443 555 0123 most Sundays.

Lupita works the early shift as a cleaning employee (empleada de limpieza) for Starlight Cleaning Services, a cleaning company (empresa de limpieza) based in High Point. Chuy works at Carolina Poultry Processors, a chicken processing plant (planta procesadora de pollo) in Siler City, where he has worked for four years. Teo's uncle, Marco Antonio Hernández Pérez ("tío Marco"), works for Triad Construction Company, a construction company (compañía de construcción) that builds in Randolph County. His aunt, Rosa Isela Pérez Gómez, works at Dollar Mart, a store (tienda) near downtown Asheboro. A paternal uncle, Pedro Cruz Ramírez, works at Green Valley Farms, a farm (granja) outside Siler City, and his wife, Carmen Lidia Ramírez Soto, helps on weekends at El Rancho Grande Restaurant, a family restaurant (restaurante) in Siler City.

Teo was born at 37 weeks gestation, weighing 6 lbs 4 oz, with Apgar scores of 8/9. Lupita reports no complications during pregnancy or delivery. The family's pediatrician, Dr. Michael Osei, referred Teo to the CDSA after a well-child visit on June 9, 2026.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

Lupita shared, "Queremos que Teo aprenda a hablar más palabras para que no se frustre." In English she added, "We want him to use more words so he doesn't get frustrated." Chuy said, "A veces grita porque no lo entendemos, y eso nos pone tristes." ("Sometimes he screams because we don't understand him, and that makes us sad.") Both parents want Teo to communicate in Spanish at home and to be ready for Head Start in English next year. Lupita added, "También queremos que juegue bien con sus hermanos Pepe y Juanito, porque ahora se enoja rápido cuando no lo entienden."

DAILY ROUTINES

abuela Mari arrives at 6:45 a.m. so Lupita can leave for Starlight Cleaning Services by 7:00 a.m.. Teo eats breakfast around 7:30 a.m., usually eggs or oatmeal, and watches a children's program in Spanish until 9:00 a.m.. He naps from about 12:30 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. and plays outside with Juanito in the late afternoon once Pepe gets home from school around 3:15 p.m.. Dinner is at 6:00 p.m. when Chuy returns from Carolina Poultry Processors. Bath time is 7:30 p.m., and bedtime is 8:30 p.m., with Lupita usually reading a short board book in Spanish beforehand.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

The family receives nutrition support through Randolph County WIC and has an open case with Randolph County DSS for food assistance. abuela Mari recently enrolled Teo in a parent-child playgroup through Smart Start of Randolph County. The family's church, through Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza, also provides occasional transportation to appointments.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT — COMMUNICATION

Evaluation completed September 18, 2026 by Jennifer A. Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, with Spanish-language support from interpreter Rosalinda Vega. Teo was administered the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition, Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish). Auditory Comprehension standard score fell in the 73-83 range (9th percentile), with an age equivalent of 1;8–2;0. Expressive Communication standard score was 62 (1st percentile), age equivalent 1;4–1;7. Total Language standard score was 70, confidence interval 65-75.

Teo's expressive vocabulary includes approximately 25 words in Spanish and 3 words in English. He combines two words inconsistently, in about 3 of 5 opportunities during structured play. Articulation screening showed accurate production of /p/, /m/, and /n/, with omission of final consonants and substitution of [w] for /ɾ/ in words such as the target "carro," which Teo produced as "cawo." He correctly imitated the target word "agua" with moderate cues in 8/10 trials.

Teo qualifies for Early Intervention under the diagnosed condition expressive language disorder, ICD-10 F80.1. Individual speech-language treatment sessions were billed under CPT 92523 with modifier -59 when co-treated with occupational therapy.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Teo will use two-word combinations in Spanish to request and comment during play, increasing from 30% to 75% accuracy across three consecutive sessions. Strategy: coach Lupita and Chuy using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies during daily routines, including mealtime and bath time; model expansion of single words heard from Teo.

Outcome 2: Teo will produce final consonants in familiar words with minimal cues in 8/10 opportunities. Strategy: integrate PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing during individual sessions; share a home practice list of target words with the family in Spanish.

Outcome 3: Teo will follow two-step directions in Spanish within the home routine in 4 of 5 trials, to support readiness for a bilingual preschool setting. Strategy: abuela Mari and Lupita will practice simple sequenced directions during daily chores; service coordinator Brenda Collins will connect the family with bilingual preschool openings through Smart Start of Randolph County.

SERVICES AND SCHEDULE

Provider: Jennifer A. Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP    Employer: Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC
Start Date: December 14, 2025    Projected End Date: April 2, 2027

Service: Developmental Therapy    Frequency: 1x/week, 60 minutes    Location: Home
Provider: Carlos Reyes, M.Ed.    Employer: Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC
Start Date: January 5, 2026    Projected End Date: April 2, 2027

Service: Service Coordination    Frequency: Monthly contact, quarterly home visit
Provider: Brenda Collins    Agency: Piedmont CDSA
Next Scheduled Visit: November 6, 2026 at 10:00 a.m.

Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Therapies, PLLC (Carolina Pediatric Therapies / CPST)
NOTA DE REVISIÓN DEL IFSP — NC Infant-Toddler Program

Fecha de revisión: 11 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del IFSP inicial: 14 de abril de 2026
Fecha de la próxima revisión: 11 de abril de 2027

Niña: María José Hernández Fernández ("MJ")
Fecha de nacimiento: 3 de julio de 2024 (edad cronológica approx 2;3)
ID de expediente: 2048673915
ID de Medicaid: 920384756A
Dirección: 742 Hollyhock Lane, Greensboro, NC 27410 (Condado de Guilford)
Tel. CG principal: (336) 555-0148
Email de la familia: hernandezfam24@gmail.com

Madre/CG: Lucía Fernández-Castillo, Tel.: (336) 555-0162
Padre/CG: Miguel Hernández Soto
Coordinadora de servicios: Ana Gómez, CDSA Regional del Piedmont, oficina de Condado de Guilford, Tel.: (336) 555-0199
Terapeuta de habla-lenguaje bilingüe: Catalina Owens, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Therapies, PLLC
Pediatra: Dr. Robert Kim

---

I. INFORMACIÓN DE LA FAMILIA

Pt es niña de 2;3 (nacida a las 38 semanas de gestación, peso al nacer 3,100 g, Apgar 8/9) que vive c/ ambos padres y su hermano mayor Diego Hernández Fernández (edad 5 años) en Greensboro. La abuela materna, Rosa del Río Martínez, cuida a pt 2-3 días/sem mientras CGs trabajan; tmb ayuda ocasionalmente la tía Carmen Fernández-Castillo. Sra. Fernández-Castillo trabaja en Piedmont Triad Manufacturing y Sr. Hernández Soto trabaja en construcción, horario variable.

La familia es monolingüe español en casa; ambos CGs entienden algo de inglés pero prefieren comunicarse en español c/ el equipo. Hermano Diego es bilingüe emergente y a veces interpreta entre MJ y sus compañeros ingleses. Pt asiste a Early Head Start del Condado de Guilford 4 días/sem, salón de la Srta. Brenda López, donde juega c/ compañeros de clase incluyendo a Noah Williams y Zoe Patterson. CG reporta que pt recibe apoyo de WIC del Condado de Guilford p/ nutrición y que la familia fue referida recientemente a DSS del Condado de Guilford p/ asistencia c/ vivienda; tmb reciben recursos de Smart Start de Guilford County Partnership for Children p/ cuidado infantil subvencionado. Familia niega otros problemas de vivienda/seguridad/alimentación fuera de lo ya mencionado.

---

II. PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (en palabras de la familia)

Durante la reunión, Lucía Fernández-Castillo expresó: "Lo que más me preocupa es que María José no dice casi nada comparado c/ Diego a esa edad. Ella señala y hace ruidos pero no usa palabras. A veces pienso que es porque le hablamos en dos idiomas, pero mi suegra dice que no es por eso." Miguel Hernández Soto agregó: "En la guardería dicen que ella se frustra mucho y a veces muerde o grita cuando no la entienden. Queremos que pueda jugar c/ los otros niños sin tanta frustración, y que nos diga lo que necesita."

CG tmb reportó inquietud sobre la alimentación: "A veces se atraganta c/ comidas más duras y prefiere cosas blandas como puré y yogur." La abuela Rosa del Río Martínez comentó durante parte de la visita: "Yo también fui tardía p/ hablar de niña, pero igual me preocupa que no mejore sola."

Prioridades identificadas por la familia, en orden: (1) aumentar vocabulario funcional en español e inglés; (2) reducir conductas de frustración relacionadas a comunicación, especialmente morder y gritar; (3) apoyo c/ alimentación segura y ampliación de texturas; (4) información sobre servicios de transición antes de que MJ cumpla 3 años.

---

III. RUTINAS DIARIAS

Pt se despierta approx 6:30 a.m., desayuna c/ la familia (cereal, fruta en puré, leche), y sale p/ Early Head Start del Condado de Guilford approx 7:45 a.m.. Permanece en el programa hasta 4:00 p.m., luego regresa a casa c/ mamá o c/ abuela Rosa del Río Martínez cuando mamá trabaja tarde. Rutina de la tarde incluye merienda, tiempo de juego c/ Diego en la sala, baño approx 7:00 p.m., y rutina de sueño c/ libro y canción approx 8:00 p.m.; pt duerme toda la noche la mayoría de los días. Comidas familiares ocurren alrededor de la mesa c/ ambos padres cuando el horario lo permite.

Los fines de semana la familia a menudo visita a Rosa del Río Martínez y a la tía Carmen Fernández-Castillo, y asiste a misa los domingos approx 10:00 a.m.. CG reporta que pt disfruta mucho del parque y del columpio, momento que el equipo identificó como oportunidad natural p/ practicar peticiones.

---

IV. HISTORIA Y RESULTADOS DE EVALUACIONES

Hx de desarrollo: hx prenatal y perinatal sin complicaciones mayores reportadas; hx médica incluye otitis media recurrente (dx H66.90) c/ tubos de miringotomía colocados 2 de febrero de 2026 por Dr. Robert Kim. No hx familiar significativa de trastornos del habla/lenguaje reportada, aunque CG menciona que Rosa del Río Martínez (abuela) fue "tardía p/ hablar" de niña según relato familiar.

Eval inicial realizada 20 de marzo de 2026 por Catalina Owens, M.S., CCC-SLP, c/ intérprete no requerida (terapeuta bilingüe). Instrumentos administrados:

- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale: Interacción-Apego en el rango dentro de lo esperado; Pragmática en el rango emergente; Gesto en el rango dentro de lo esperado; Juego en el rango emergente; Comprensión del Lenguaje edad equivalente 14-16 meses; Expresión del Lenguaje edad equivalente 12-14 meses.
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4): Comunicación Receptiva puntaje escalado 6 (percentil 9); Comunicación Expresiva puntaje escalado 5 (percentil 5); Cognitivo puntaje escalado 8; Motor Grueso puntaje escalado 9 (dentro de lo esperado); Motor Fino puntaje escalado 8.
- Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition (PDMS-2): Cociente Motor Total 88 (percentil 21), IC 95% 81-95.
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) administrado parcialmente (pt verbal limitada); se observaron sustituciones de /p/ por [b] y omisión de consonantes finales. Pt dijo "bola" p/ blanco "pelota" y "aba" p/ blanco "agua", y "ete" p/ blanco "leche".

Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo (SALT): 15 enunciados en 10 min de juego libre; predominan enunciados de 1 palabra; se codificaron 3 instancias de [EW] jerga ininteligible. MLU no calculable de forma confiable a este nivel.

Impresión clínica: Trastorno del lenguaje mixto receptivo-expresivo, dx F80.2, de moderado a severo, c/ retraso fonológico emergente. CPT facturado: 92523 (evaluación de habla y lenguaje).

---

V. OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

- CDSA Regional del Piedmont (condado de Guilford): coordinación de servicios, Ana Gómez, SC.
- Early Head Start del Condado de Guilford: Srta. Brenda López, maestra principal.
- WIC del Condado de Guilford: apoyo nutricional p/ la familia.
- DSS del Condado de Guilford: referido p/ asistencia de vivienda, trabajadora de caso Teresa Núñez.
- Smart Start de Guilford County Partnership for Children: subvención de cuidado infantil.
- Consultorio pediátrico de Dr. Robert Kim, Cone Health Pediatrics - Westover.
- Audiología: Dra. Patricia Álvarez, Au.D., re: hx de otitis media y tubos.

---

VI. RESULTADOS (OUTCOMES) DEL IFSP C/ ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: María José usará approx 20 palabras funcionales (en español y/o inglés) p/ pedir objetos/acciones preferidas durante rutinas diarias, observado en 4 de 5 oportunidades c/ mod cues, p/ la próxima revisión.
Estrategias: modelo de lenguaje aumentado (técnica Hanen, "sígueme la corriente"); espera estructurada ("time delay") durante meriendas y juego; uso de gestos naturales emparejados c/ palabra. CG y maestra Srta. Brenda López implementarán en casa y en Early Head Start del Condado de Guilford.

Resultado 2: María José combinará 2 palabras ("más galleta", "quiero agua") en 3 de 5 oportunidades c/ mínimas cues.
Estrategias: expansión de enunciados ("expansion/recast"); lectura interactiva de libros c/ pausas; enfoque PROMPT p/ apoyar producción motora del habla durante palabras funcionales objetivo.

Resultado 3: María José reducirá conductas de frustración (morder, gritar) relacionadas a comunicación de 5-7 episodios/día a 2 o menos, medido por reporte de CG y maestra.
Estrategias: enseñanza de gesto de reemplazo (señalar, llevar de la mano) c/ apoyo visual tipo PECS fase 1; reforzamiento inmediato de intentos comunicativos; consistencia entre casa y Early Head Start del Condado de Guilford.

Resultado 4: Familia recibirá educación sobre seguridad alimentaria y texturas apropiadas, c/ CG reportando 0 episodios de atragantamiento en rutinas de comida en el hogar.
Estrategias: consulta c/ terapia ocupacional p/ evaluación de alimentación (referido pendiente); modificación de texturas en casa; técnicas de corte y presentación de alimentos revisadas c/ CG en sesión 25 de septiembre de 2026.

Resultado 5 (prioridad de la familia — transición): CG recibirá información escrita y verbal sobre el proceso de transición del Part C al preescolar/Part B antes de que pt cumpla 2;6, incluyendo opciones de evaluación de elegibilidad p/ servicios preescolares del condado.
Estrategias: SC Ana Gómez proveerá folleto bilingüe de transición y calendario de reunión de transición approx 3 de enero de 2027.

---

VII. SESIONES DE TERAPIA Y FECHAS DE SERVICIO

Terapia de habla-lenguaje: 2x/sem, 30 min/sesión, en el hogar, c/ Catalina Owens, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Carolina Pediatric Therapies. CPT: 92507 (tx individual de habla-lenguaje).

Fechas de sesiones recientes revisadas p/ este informe: 2 de septiembre de 2026, 9 de septiembre de 2026, 16 de septiembre de 2026, 23 de septiembre de 2026, 30 de septiembre de 2026, 7 de octubre de 2026. Asistencia buena, c/ 1 cancelación b/c enfermedad.

Referido pendiente a terapia ocupacional (alimentación) a través de CDSA Regional del Piedmont; eval de TO programada p/ 28 de octubre de 2026.

Consulta de audiología de seguimiento programada 15 de diciembre de 2026 c/ Dra. Patricia Álvarez re: estado post-tubos.

---

VIII. RESUMEN Y PRÓXIMOS PASOS

El equipo, incluyendo a Lucía Fernández-Castillo, Miguel Hernández Soto, SC Ana Gómez, y terapeuta Catalina Owens, acordó continuar servicios de habla-lenguaje 2x/sem, agregar referido de TO, y programar reunión de transición antes de 3 de julio de 2027 (fecha límite de elegibilidad de Part C). CG firmó consentimiento informado p/ continuación de servicios y referido de TO en la reunión de 11 de octubre de 2026. CG verbalizó acuerdo c/ todos los resultados revisados y no solicitó cambios adicionales en este momento.

Próxima revisión del IFSP: 11 de abril de 2027 o antes si cambian las necesidades de la familia.

Report Written By: Ana Maria Castillo, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners
Interpreter: none required; evaluation and review conducted bilingually by Ms. Castillo

Present Levels / Preocupaciones de la Familia

This review was completed in the home at 4:00 PM on October 3, 2026, with both parents present. Lucia shared her concerns primarily in Spanish, with Ms. Castillo translating as needed for Carlos.

Lucia stated, "Mateo entiende casi todo lo que le decimos, pero todavia no habla mucho. El dice 'mama' y 'agua' pero no junta palabras." She reported that Mateo has started to imitate the family dog's name, Canela, saying something close to "Nela" when the dog comes near.

Carlos added, in English, "He gets frustrated when we don't understand him. He'll point and grunt, and sometimes he hits himself on the leg." Both parents agreed that Mateo's main need right now is funcional language — "necesitamos que el pueda decir lo que quiere," said Lucia. She also mentioned, "en la noche se pone bien mal, llora y se pega en la cabeza cuando no lo entendemos."

The family's priority for this review is increasing Mateo's expressive vocabulary and reducing frustration-related behaviors at daycare and at home. Carlos also asked whether Mateo might need a hearing recheck, since "a veces parece que no escucha bien cuando esta jugando."

Daily Routines

Mateo wakes around 6:30 AM and is dropped off at Little Learners Daycare by 7:15 AM, where he is in Ms. Lopez's room with seven other toddlers, including his friend Diego. His grandmother, Rosa Flores, picks him up most days at 5:30 PM because both parents work late.

Lucia works the evening shift at Servicios de Limpieza Estrella (Star Cleaning Services), typically from 3:00 PM to 11:00 PM. Carlos trabaja en la compania de construccion Pinnacle Construction Company, leaving the house before 6:00 AM most mornings. Grandmother Rosa Flores works mornings at Restaurante El Fogon and is available for pickup in the afternoons. Mateo's uncle, Ernesto Rodriguez, works night shift at Planta Procesadora Avicola Carolina and sometimes helps on weekends. Mateo's aunt, Marisol Rodriguez, works at Mercado La Economica and brings groceries by on Sundays, when the whole family gathers. A family friend, Beto Hernandez, works at Sunrise Farms and sometimes brings fresh vegetables for the family on weekends.

Bath time is around 7:00 PM and bedtime is 8:00 PM. Lucia reports that mealtimes are the hardest part of the day: "Mateo se frustra mucho cuando quiere mas comida y no sabe pedirla." Weekends are usually spent at the grandmother's house, where Mateo plays with his cousin, Isabela, and the family dog, Canela.

Other Agencies Involved

The family also receives support from WIC through the Chatham County office and has applied for services through Smart Start of Chatham County. Chatham County DSS assisted the family with the Medicaid renewal completed on September 12, 2026. The family's pediatrician, Dr. Hannah Kim, at Chatham Pediatrics, referred Mateo for the initial evaluation after noting limited expressive language at his 18-month well-child visit, and a follow-up hearing screen is pending at UNC Children's Hospital.

Evaluation Summary

Mateo (2;6) was administered the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) in both English and Spanish, with scores reported using the higher of the two administrations per item, consistent with bilingual assessment guidelines. Auditory Comprehension standard score: 79 (8th percentile); Expressive Communication standard score: 65 (1st percentile); Total Language Score: 70 (2nd percentile), confidence interval 62-78. Age equivalent for expressive language: 14 months. A brief cognitive screen using the Bayley-4 Cognitive Scale yielded a scaled score of 9, within the average range, suggesting the expressive delay is specific to language rather than global.

Birth history is unremarkable: Apgar scores of 8 and 9, gestational age 39 weeks, birth weight 7 lbs 2 oz. No significant medical history. Hearing screening at birth was within normal limits bilaterally, though parents have requested a repeat screen given current concerns.

During play-based observation, Mateo used approximately 12 single words consistently, including "mas," "agua," and "up," and produced the phonemes /m/ and /a/ clearly, with limited production of /p/ and /t/ in word-initial position. He imitated "arriba" with moderate cues during a gross motor routine, and attempted "bola" with maximal cues.

Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1 (IFSP Outcome #1): Mateo will use 2-word combinations to request desired items and activities in both English and Spanish, as reported by family and observed by provider, in 8 of 10 opportunities across two consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Ms. Castillo will coach Lucia and Carlos using Hanen-based strategies (It Takes Two to Talk) during mealtime and play routines, modeling expansion of single words into two-word phrases ("mas agua," "mama up"). Coaching sessions will occur in the home and will include Rosa Flores when available, since she provides significant daytime care.

Outcome 2 (IFSP Outcome #2): Mateo will reduce frustration-related behaviors (hitting, self-directed aggression) by using a functional communication alternative (pointing paired with a word or approximation) in 3 of 5 observed frustration events.
Strategies: Visual supports and a core word board will be introduced at Little Learners Daycare in coordination with Ms. Lopez, and at home. Ms. Castillo will train Ms. Lopez and classroom aide Mr. Davis on cueing hierarchy, prompting Mateo to point before escalating, with minimal to moderate cues as needed.

Outcome 3 (IFSP Outcome #3): Mateo will increase his inventory of word-initial consonants in spontaneous speech, targeting /p/, /t/, and /b/, producing each in at least 3 of 5 trials during structured play.
Strategies: Speech sound stimulation using a modified PROMPT approach, paired with high-frequency bilingual vocabulary (papa, bola, taza). Home practice sheet will be provided in Spanish and English.

Transition Planning

Because Mateo turns three in April 2027, the team briefly discussed transition options. Denise Watkins explained the timeline for the transition conference and the family's rights regarding Child Find and preschool special education eligibility. Lucia stated she would like Mateo to stay at Little Learners Daycare with Ms. Lopez as long as possible, "porque el ya la conoce y se siente comodo." A formal transition conference will be scheduled closer to Mateo's third birthday.

Services

Mateo will continue to receive weekly developmental therapy through Little Learners Program, the community-based early intervention therapy provider contracted through Central Regional CDSA. Sessions are held on Tuesdays from 10:00 AM to 10:45 AM at the family home, and on Thursdays from 2:30 PM to 3:15 PM at Little Learners Daycare, coordinated with Ms. Lopez's schedule.

Speech-language therapy with Ms. Castillo will continue once weekly for 45 minutes, on Mondays from 9:00 AM to 9:45 AM, alternating between the home and Little Learners Daycare.

Service Coordination visits with Denise Watkins will continue monthly, with the next visit scheduled for November 7, 2026.

Next IFSP Review Date: April 3, 2027

EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE / SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
4420 Tidewater Drive, Suite 210, Durham, NC 27707
Tel: (919) 555-0148 | Fax: (919) 555-0149 | intake@carolinapedslp.com

IDENTIFYING INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

- Child's Name / Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fernández (called "Teo" at home)
- Date of Birth / Fecha de nacimiento: June 9, 2022
- Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;5
- CDSA Record #: CDSA-2022-04471
- Medicaid ID: 987654321B
- Mother / Madre: Lucía Rodríguez Méndez
- Father / Padre: Carlos Cruz Ortiz
- Home Address: 118 Cottonwood Lane, Durham, Durham County, NC 27703
- Home Phone: (919) 555-0271
- Primary Language in the Home: Spanish and English / español e inglés
- CDSA Office: Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Triángulo, referred to by families as the "CDSA del Triángulo"
- Service Coordination Agency: Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Familiares de Durham, known in daily use as "ACSF Durham"
- Service Coordinator: Brenda Nichols
- Evaluating Clinician: Jennifer Hayes-Watkins, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Spanish/English
- Interpreter Present: Sandra Paredes (certified medical interpreter)
- Dates of Evaluation: September 15, 2026 and September 22, 2026
- Report Date: September 29, 2026

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE LA REFERENCIA

- Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language re-evaluation by Brenda Nichols at ACSF Durham as part of his transition from Part C early intervention through CDSA del Triángulo into Part B preschool services.
- His mother, Lucía Rodríguez Méndez, reported during the intake call that "Teo no habla bien todavía — se le entiende solo la mitad de lo que dice" ("Teo still doesn't talk well — only about half of what he says is understood").
- Ms. Angela Lopez, his Pre-K teacher at Forest Pines Elementary School, part of Durham Public Schools, submitted a classroom observation form noting unintelligible speech and difficulty following two-step directions in the large-group setting.
- The family's pediatrician, Dr. Ahmed Hassan, recommended the referral at Mateo's 4-year well-child visit, citing concerns consistent with F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder).

BACKGROUND INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE ANTECEDENTES

- Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Méndez; his father, Carlos Cruz Ortiz; his older sister, Valentina Cruz Rodríguez (age 7); and his younger brother, Diego Cruz Rodríguez (age 1).
- His maternal grandmother, Rosa Fernández Méndez, lives nearby and cares for Mateo on weekday mornings before preschool. The family calls her "Abuela Rosa."
- A part-time babysitter, Marisol Pineda, picks Mateo and Valentina up from school on Fridays.
- The family's dog, Rocky, is frequently mentioned in Mateo's spontaneous speech; during the session he pointed at the window and said, "Rocky afuera" ("Rocky outside").
- Lucía works as a logistics coordinator at Blue Ridge Produce Distributors; Carlos is employed at Triangle HVAC Services.
- Mateo attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Center from August 2023 to June 2026 before enrolling at Forest Pines Elementary School.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

- Lucía reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with routine prenatal care.
- Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestational age at WakeMed Faison Women's and Children's Hospital on June 9, 2022.
- Birth weight: 6 lbs 11 oz. Apgar scores: 8 at one minute, 9 at five minutes.
- No NICU stay was reported. Lucía stated, "no tuvo ningún problema al nacer" ("he had no problems at birth").
- Developmental milestones: sat independently at 7 months; walked at 14 months; first words emerged around 18 months in Spanish only.
- History of recurrent otitis media between 12 and 24 months, treated with multiple courses of antibiotics; bilateral myringotomy tubes were placed at 22 months by Dr. Marcus Whitfield, ENT, at UNC Health Children's.
- A follow-up audiological evaluation at UNC Health Children's, administered by audiologist Grace Olumide, documented hearing within normal limits bilaterally as of March 10, 2024.
- No seizure history, no significant illness or hospitalization since tube placement.
- Current ICD-10 working diagnosis: F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), to be confirmed pending this evaluation.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DEL LENGUAJE

- Lucía and Carlos both report that Spanish is the dominant language spoken in the home; English is used primarily by Valentina and during school-related activities.
- Lucía estimated that Mateo hears approximately 80% Spanish and 20% English input across a typical week.
- Per family report, Abuela Rosa speaks exclusively Spanish with Mateo, while Ms. Lopez's classroom is conducted primarily in English with some Spanish support from a bilingual classroom assistant, Mr. Trevor Banks.
- Lucía shared, "en casa le hablamos puro español, pero cuando llega de la escuela mezcla las dos — a veces dice 'I want agua' o 'dame el book'" ("at home we speak only Spanish with him, but when he gets home from school he mixes both — sometimes he says 'I want water' or 'give me the book'").
- No family history of speech, language, or learning disorders was reported on either side of the family.
- Valentina is reportedly a strong student at Forest Pines Elementary School with no history of speech-language concerns.
- Carlos noted that he himself was a "late talker" as a child but did not receive formal intervention and ultimately "spoke fine by school age."

EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

- Mateo is currently enrolled in the Pre-Kindergarten classroom of Ms. Angela Lopez at Forest Pines Elementary School, within Durham Public Schools.
- His school day runs from 7:45 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.
- Ms. Lopez reports that Mateo participates willingly in circle time but is frequently unintelligible to peers, particularly during show-and-tell.
- A classmate, Ethan Brooks, reportedly told Ms. Lopez that he "can't understand what Mateo is saying" during a recent pretend-play activity.
- Another classmate, Sofia Alvarado, is described by Ms. Lopez as patient with Mateo and often "translates" his requests to other children.
- Mateo's family receives support from WIC and previously participated in a Smart Start parenting workshop series through Durham County DSS.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES / INSTRUMENTOS ADMINISTRADOS

- Review of records, including the March 2024 audiological report and prior CDSA early intervention progress notes.
- Parent/caregiver interview with Lucía Rodríguez Méndez, conducted bilingually with interpreter support from Sandra Paredes.
- Classroom observation at Forest Pines Elementary School on September 17, 2026 from 9:15 a.m. to 10:00 a.m..
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), English administration.
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5), English administration.
- CELF Preschool-3, Core Language subtests, English administration.
- Spanish language sample analysis using narrative retell and informal conversation with Jennifer Hayes-Watkins and interpreter support.
- Oral mechanism examination.
- Review of the June 2024 Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale results from the initial CDSA evaluation at 2;3, retained for developmental comparison.
- Review of the June 2024 Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 (Bayley-4) cognitive and motor subtests, administered at that time by Rachel Kim, CDSA developmental specialist.

CLINICAL OBSERVATIONS / OBSERVACIONES CLÍNICAS

- Mateo presented as a friendly, cooperative child who engaged readily with both the examiner and the interpreter.
- Attention and engagement were adequate for standardized testing within 15-20 minute blocks before brief breaks were needed.
- Spontaneous speech was approximately 50% intelligible to unfamiliar listeners in connected speech, improving to 70% intelligible in single words.
- Phonological processes observed included final consonant deletion (e.g., "ka" for "cat"), cluster reduction (e.g., "top" for "stop"), and gliding of liquids (e.g., /w/ for /ɾ/ in Spanish, as in "guapo" produced as "wapo").
- During the Spanish language sample, Mateo used primarily two- and three-word utterances, such as "quiero agua" and "Rocky corre" (note: "Rocky" marked separately as the pet's name within the sample).
- Code-switching was noted within single utterances, e.g., "I want jugo" and "dame el book," consistent with typical bilingual development but complicated by the underlying language impairment.
- Oral mechanism examination was within normal limits for structure and function; no evidence of dysarthria or apraxia-specific sequencing errors.
- Hearing was judged functionally adequate based on behavioral observation and the March 10, 2024 audiological report.

TEST RESULTS / RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3): Standard Score 73 (65-81 confidence interval), Percentile Rank 4th. Sounds in error included /s/, /r/, /θ/, and consonant clusters in the medial and final word positions.
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5): Standard Score 81, Percentile Rank 10th, Age Equivalent 3;2.
- CELF Preschool-3, Core Language Score: Standard Score 76, Percentile Rank 5th.
  - Sentence Structure subtest: Scaled Score 6.
  - Word Structure subtest: Scaled Score 5.
  - Expressive Vocabulary subtest: Scaled Score 7.
- Historical Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (administered June 14, 2024 at 2;3): Receptive Language Age Equivalent 16-18 months; Expressive Language Age Equivalent 14-16 months.
- Historical Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 (Bayley-4) (administered June 14, 2024): Cognitive Composite 92; Fine Motor Scaled Score 9; Gross Motor Scaled Score 10.
- Speech sound accuracy during single-word probe: 8/10 correct productions of word-initial stops; 3/10 correct productions of word-final fricatives.
- Following two-step directions in English: 6/10 trials correct (60%) with no cues; improved to 8/10 (80%) with mod cues (gestural plus verbal repetition).
- Following one-step directions in Spanish: 9/10 trials correct (90%) with no cues.

IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES

- Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, consistent with F80.2, affecting both his home language (Spanish) and his school language (English), though the impairment is proportionally more pronounced in expressive language and in speech sound production across both languages.
- His language difficulties are not attributable solely to bilingual language exposure; deficits are present relative to same-age peers in both Spanish and English, which supports a true language disorder rather than a language difference.
- Speech sound production deficits, including reduced intelligibility (approximately 50% in connected speech), are consistent with a moderate speech sound disorder with phonological process patterns atypical for his age in both languages.
- Lucía expressed concern that Mateo's unintelligibility is affecting his confidence at school: "le da pena cuando los niños no le entienden, y se queda callado" ("he feels embarrassed when the other children don't understand him, and he goes quiet").
- Ms. Lopez's classroom observations of difficulty following multi-step directions and limited peer-directed communication are consistent with the standardized findings.
- Given the family's strong Spanish-language home environment, continued bilingual intervention — rather than English-only therapy — is clinically indicated to support both languages and to avoid further widening the gap between home and school communication.

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES

- Qualification for Part B preschool speech-language services through Durham Public Schools under the eligibility category of Speech-Language Impairment.
- Individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, focused on articulation and expressive language goals in both English and Spanish.
- Continued bilingual service delivery is strongly recommended; sessions should not be conducted in English only.
- Therapy approaches to consider: Cycles approach for phonological remediation; PROMPT for motor-based articulation support; parent coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies for the home environment.
- Continued collaboration between the IFSP/IEP team, Ms. Angela Lopez, Mr. Trevor Banks, and the treating SLP to reinforce carryover of targets into the classroom.
- Referral for a repeat audiological screening is not indicated at this time given the March 10, 2024 results, but should be revisited if middle ear effusion recurs.
- Home practice suggestions provided to Lucía Rodríguez Méndez and Carlos Cruz Ortiz in Spanish, including modeling full sentences, expanding on Mateo's utterances, and reducing code-switching pressure during structured practice time.
- IFSP transition meeting recommended within 30 days, coordinated by Brenda Nichols at ACSF Durham, to finalize the transition from CDSA del Triángulo to school-based services.
- Re-evaluation recommended in approximately 12 months, or sooner if progress plateaus.

SESSION LOG / REGISTRO DE SESIONES

- September 15, 2026, 1:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m.: Initial evaluation session, standardized testing (GFTA-3, PPVT-5). CPT 92523 billed (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).
- September 22, 2026, 10:30 a.m. to 11:15 a.m.: Continued evaluation, CELF Preschool-3 administration and Spanish language sample. CPT 92523 billed.
- September 17, 2026, 9:15 a.m. to 10:00 a.m.: Classroom observation at Forest Pines Elementary School, no CPT code billed (observation only).
- Anticipated ongoing treatment sessions, pending authorization: CPT 92507 (treatment of speech, language, voice, communication, and/or auditory processing disorder), twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, proposed schedule Tuesdays and Thursdays, 3:30 p.m. to 4:00 p.m., pending scheduling confirmation with the family and Forest Pines Elementary School.

AUTHORIZATION AND CONTACT INFORMATION

- Authorization requested from CDSA del Triángulo for continued services pending the IFSP transition meeting.
- Questions regarding this report may be directed to Jennifer Hayes-Watkins, M.S., CCC-SLP, at Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Partners, PLLC, (919) 555-0148, or by email at jhayeswatkins@carolinapedslp.com.
- Family may also contact Brenda Nichols at ACSF Durham, (919) 555-0392, regarding service coordination and transition planning.
- A copy of this report has been shared, with family consent, with Dr. Ahmed Hassan's office and with Ms. Angela Lopez at Forest Pines Elementary School.

This report reflects Mateo's speech and language functioning as observed on the dates listed above and should be considered alongside ongoing classroom and family observations. Como se le explicó a la familia, los resultados de esta evaluación apoyan la necesidad de servicios continuos de terapia de habla y lenguaje en ambos idiomas, español e inglés, para asegurar que Mateo pueda comunicarse con confianza tanto en casa como en la escuela.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Hayes-Watkins, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
