Subject: IFSP Annual Review — Mateo Fernández Cruz ("Teo") — October 6, 2026 — Notes & Next Steps

From: Ana Torres, M.S., CCC-SLP <ana.torres@littlelearnersprogram.org>
To: Melissa Ruiz <mruiz@cumberlandcdsa.org>
Cc: Carlos Fernández <carlosf.nc@gmail.com>, Lucía Rodríguez <lucia.rodriguez84@gmail.com>, Daniela López <dlopez@littlelearnersdaycare.com>, J. Ortiz, OTR/L <jortiz@littlelearnersprogram.org>

Hola a todos,

Gracias a todos por venir a la reunión anual del IFSP de Teo el October 6, 2026 en la oficina de Cumberland CDSA en 412 Hay Street, Fayetteville. Resumen abajo para el expediente, con copia para el equipo.

Background: Mateo nació el February 14, 2024 en Cape Fear Valley Medical Center, a las 32 weeks de gestación, peso al nacer 1,620 grams, Apgar 6/9. Pasó 19 days en la NICU de Cape Fear Valley Medical Center bajo el cuidado de la Dra. Aisha Patel (neonatóloga). Su pediatra actual es el Dr. Samuel Hassan, quien hizo la referencia inicial a Cumberland CDSA después de la visita de los 18 months por falta de palabras y por reflujo persistente. Diagnóstico actual: F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder).

Family concerns and priorities (en las palabras de la familia): Durante la reunión, Lucía Rodríguez dijo: "Queremos que Teo pueda decirnos qué necesita, que no se frustre tanto y que no muerda a su hermana." Carlos Fernández añadió: "También nos preocupa el habla — en casa habla los dos idiomas pero en la guardería dicen que no habla casi nada." La hermana mayor, Valentina ("Vale"), de 4 years, a veces traduce para Teo en casa, lo cual el equipo discutió como un patrón a monitorear. Rosa Cruz, la abuela materna, cuida a Teo dos tardes por semana mientras Lucía trabaja, y reportó: "Él me entiende todo en español, pero casi no me contesta con palabras."

Daily routines: Teo asiste a Little Learners Daycare de lunes a viernes de 7:30 a.m. a 5:00 p.m.. Su maestra, Daniela López, reporta que participa en el círculo de canciones pero se aísla durante el juego libre. Las comidas, el baño y la rutina de dormir ocurren principalmente en español en casa; en la guardería, todo es en inglés. Los fines de semana la familia visita a Rosa Cruz en Spring Lake, donde Teo juega con sus primos.

Other agencies involved: La familia recibe WIC y está en lista de espera para Smart Start de Cumberland County para transporte a terapia. DSS cerró un caso de monitoreo nutricional en March 2025 sin hallazgos. El Medicaid ID del niño es RC48213907B; expediente de caso en Cumberland CDSA: CDSA-2024-01187.

Evaluation results (evaluación del September 22, 2026): En PLS-5, Auditory Comprehension produjo una puntuación estándar de 73, intervalo de confianza 68-78, percentil 4th, edad equivalente 2;6–3;0. Expressive Communication: puntuación estándar 79, rango 73-83, edad equivalente 2;3–2;9. En CELF-5 (administrado en inglés dado su exposición en la guardería), Core Language Score cayó en 70-80. El inventario de sonidos mostró omisión de /s/ final y sustitución de /r/ por [w] en ambos idiomas; por ejemplo produjo "[w]opa" por "ropa" con min cues, y "ba[w]co" por "barco" con mod cues.

Outcomes and strategies:

Outcome 1 (IFSP Outcome #1): Teo usará de 2 a 3 palabras combinadas para pedir, comentar y protestar en inglés y en español, en casa y en la guardería. Estrategia: Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" para los padres; modelado de combinaciones de palabras durante rutinas diarias; Ms. López usará el mismo vocabulario objetivo durante el círculo. text:
TRIANGLE BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
Comprehensive Speech-Language Evaluation / Evaluación Integral del Habla y el Lenguaje

Child's Name	Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez
Date of Birth	March 3, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation	4;2
Gestational Age at Birth	36 weeks
Date(s) of Evaluation	August 11, 2026 and August 13, 2026
Date of Report	September 2, 2026
Evaluator	Jennifer Kim, M.S., CCC-SLP (bilingual English/Spanish)
Referral Source	Dr. Patricia Nguyen, Carolina Kids Pediatrics
Date of Referral	June 10, 2026
CDSA Record #	DUR-2026-0587
NC Medicaid ID	928471650B
Home Address	742 Willow Creek Lane, Durham, NC 27703
County	Durham County

Padres / Parents or Guardians

Name	Relationship	Phone	Email
Lucía Rodríguez Martínez	Mother	(919) 555-0148	lucia.rodriguez82@gmail.com
Carlos Flores	Father	(919) 555-0193	—

Reason for Referral / Motivo de la Remisión

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Nguyen at Carolina Kids Pediatrics following his 4;0 well-child visit, at which his mother, Lucía, reported concern that Mateo "no habla casi nada" compared to his sister at the same age. Lucía stated that Mateo uses mostly single words and gestures, and that unfamiliar listeners, including his daycare teachers, often cannot understand him. Mateo was also referred to the Agencia de Servicios para el Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Durham (CDSA de Durham) for Part C early intervention eligibility determination. Service coordination is being provided through the Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Infantiles del Triángulo (Coordinación Infantil del Triángulo), with Rosa Jiménez serving as Mateo's assigned service coordinator.

This evaluation was requested to describe Mateo's receptive and expressive language skills, speech sound production, and oral-motor functioning in both English and Spanish, and to make recommendations regarding eligibility for early intervention services and appropriate therapeutic programming.

Background Information / Historia del Desarrollo

Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 36 weeks gestation at Pinehurst Medical Center on March 3, 2022, via planned cesarean section due to breech presentation. Birth weight was 5 lbs 8 oz. Apgar scores were reported as 7 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Mateo spent 4 days in the NICU for monitoring related to mild respiratory distress and was discharged home with no ongoing medical concerns. Lucía reported no significant illnesses, no history of chronic ear infections, and no hospitalizations since birth. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening and has had no documented hearing concerns since. He is not currently on any medications. His most recent well-child visit with Dr. Nguyen on June 3, 2026 noted age-appropriate growth, with speech-language development flagged for referral.

Developmental Milestones

Lucía reported that Mateo sat independently around 7 months, walked independently around 15 months, and began using single words around 18 months, though vocabulary growth has been notably slower than that of his older sister. Carlos added, "Cuando Sol tenía su edad, ya hablaba muchísimo más," comparing Mateo's language development unfavorably to that of his sister at a similar age. Fine and gross motor milestones were reported as within normal limits, and no concerns were raised regarding feeding, though Lucía noted Mateo was a "picky eater" as a toddler who preferred soft, pureed textures longer than typical.

Family and Language History

Mateo lives at home with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Martínez; his father, Carlos Flores; and his older sister, Sol Flores Rodríguez, age 7. The family's primary language spoken in the home is Spanish, though Lucía reported that English is used increasingly with Sol since she started school, and that both children hear a mix of both languages throughout the day. Lucía estimated that Mateo hears approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English at home, primarily from her and from his maternal grandmother, Lupe, who the family affectionately calls doña Lupe. Doña Lupe cares for Mateo and Sol three afternoons a week after daycare and school, and speaks almost exclusively Spanish with both children. Carlos works long shifts at Pinecrest Furniture Manufacturing and is often away from the home for extended periods, which Lucía noted limits his availability to participate in daily language routines.

Lucía denied any family history of speech, language, or learning disabilities, though she mentioned that a maternal uncle "tardó en hablar de niño pero después habló bien," suggesting a possible, though unconfirmed, family history of late language emergence. The family also has a dog, Rocky, a small terrier mix, who Mateo is reportedly very attached to and frequently references in play and conversation.

Educational History

Mateo attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Childcare Center five days a week from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.. His current classroom teacher, Miss Ana, reported that Mateo is social with peers but often resorts to pointing, pulling adults by the hand, or using single words to communicate his needs. Miss Ana noted that Mateo gets along well with a classmate, Diego, and the two are frequently observed playing together during free choice time, though Mateo's limited verbal output sometimes leads to frustration when Diego does not understand what he wants. Mateo's teacher from the previous school year, la maestra Carmen, had also expressed concern about his limited expressive vocabulary relative to his peers, and had encouraged the family to pursue a formal evaluation at that time.

Mateo is not currently enrolled in any therapeutic services. He has not previously received speech-language intervention. He receives occasional occupational therapy consultation informally through daycare staff but has no formal OT services in place at this time; this is addressed further in the Recommendations section below.

Assessment Procedures

The following formal and informal assessment procedures were used to evaluate Mateo's speech and language skills in both English and Spanish:

- Parent interview and case history review, conducted bilingually with Lucía and Carlos
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), Sounds-in-Words subtest
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5)
- Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition (PDMS-2), Fine Motor Quotient
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4), Cognitive subtest, administered in collaboration with the CDSA developmental specialist
- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, administered through structured play-based observation
- Oral mechanism examination
- Speech and language sample collected during structured and unstructured play, in both English and Spanish
- Clinical observation across both evaluation sessions

Behavioral Observations

Mateo presented as a friendly, curious child who separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and play materials across both sessions. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of approximately 10-15 minutes before requiring a break or a change of activity. Mateo was cooperative throughout testing, though he occasionally vocalized frustration, saying "no" or pushing materials away, when tasks became difficult or when he did not have the words to express what he wanted. Rapport was established quickly, in part through code-switching between English and Spanish depending on which language Mateo responded to more readily. Results of this evaluation are considered a valid representation of Mateo's current speech-language skills.

Test Results / Resultados de las Pruebas

Standardized Test Results

Test/Subtest	Standard Score	Percentile Rank	Age Equivalent
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (English)	78	7th	2;9-3;0
PLS-5 Expressive Communication (English)	72	3rd	2;6-2;9
PLS-5 Total Language Score (English)	73	4th	2;7-2;10
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (Spanish)	81	10th	3;0-3;3
PLS-5 Expressive Communication (Spanish)	75	5th	2;8-2;11
Goldman-Fristoe-3 Sounds-in-Words	65	1st	<2;0
Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5	85	16th	3;4
Peabody Developmental Motor Scales-2 Fine Motor	90	25th	3;9
Bayley-4 Cognitive	82	12th	3;2

On the PLS-5, Mateo's scores fell within the moderately delayed range in both English and Spanish, with slightly stronger performance in Spanish, consistent with his home language environment. His Goldman-Fristoe-3 score fell well below average, with a Percent Consonants Correct (PCC) of 52%, indicating significant speech sound delay. His PPVT-5 score suggested receptive vocabulary within the low average range when assessed in English alone, though this is likely an underestimate of his total conceptual vocabulary across both languages, given that several items he could not identify in English were correctly identified when presented in Spanish during informal probing. Mateo's Bayley-4 Cognitive score and PDMS-2 Fine Motor score both fell within the low average range, suggesting that nonverbal cognitive and fine motor skills are relatively stronger areas, and that his primary area of concern is specific to speech and language.

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale

Administered through play-based observation, the Rossetti indicated delays across the Interaction-Attachment, Pragmatics, Gesture, and Play domains consistent with the standardized findings above. Mateo demonstrated appropriate joint attention and turn-taking during play, used a variety of gestures (pointing, reaching, pulling) to communicate, and engaged in simple pretend play sequences with toy animals and vehicles, suggesting relative strength in social-communicative foundations despite limited verbal output.

Articulation and Phonology

Oral mechanism examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech production, with adequate labial, lingual, and velopharyngeal movement observed. No concerns regarding oral-motor strength or coordination were noted during the feeding history interview or structural exam.

During the Goldman-Fristoe-3 and supplemental Spanish articulation probing, Mateo demonstrated a restricted phonetic inventory and multiple phonological process patterns affecting intelligibility in both languages. The following error patterns were noted:

Target Word	Target Sound	Child's Production	Cueing Level
sol (sun)	/s/ initial	"tol"	mod cues
casa	/s/ medial	"cata"	min cues
carro	/ɾ/	"cado"	max cues
flor	/f/ + consonant cluster	"por"	mod cues
water	/w/	"[w]ader"	spontaneous
key	/k/	"[k]i"	spontaneous

Mateo demonstrated fronting of velars inconsistently, final consonant deletion, and gliding of liquids, including the Spanish tap /ɾ/, which was consistently produced as [d]. Of note, the target word "sol" (meaning sun) was selected as a stimulus item for initial /s/ in Spanish, and it is coincidental that this word matches the name of Mateo's sister; it was not used in reference to her during testing. Connected speech intelligibility was estimated at 40% for familiar listeners and well below that for unfamiliar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

Language Sample and Pragmatics

During a structured play sample, Mateo produced a combination of single words, occasional two-word combinations, and frequent gestures. Representative utterances included "Rocky no" when his dog was moved away from a toy during a video call with his grandmother, and "Sol no" when his sister attempted to take a toy truck from him during the second session, which his mother had brought along. Mateo also produced "mas agua" when requesting a drink and "upa papi" when he wanted his father, Carlos, to pick him up, demonstrating emerging two-word combinations primarily in Spanish. Mean length of utterance was calculated at 1.4 morphemes, consistent with the Expressive Communication scores above.

Pragmatically, Mateo demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking in play-based interactions, and he readily initiated communication through gesture even when verbal attempts were unsuccessful. He showed some frustration behaviors, including brief tantrums, when he was not understood, which both his mother and Miss Ana reported occur several times daily at home and at daycare respectively.

Hearing and Vision

Mateo passed a pure-tone hearing screening administered during this evaluation at 20 dB HL bilaterally across 500-4000 Hz. No concerns regarding vision were reported by the family, and Mateo has not required glasses or vision correction.

Impressions / Impresiones Clínicas

Based on parent report, teacher report, standardized and criterion-referenced assessment results, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a moderate expressive and receptive language delay affecting both English and Spanish, along with a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder characterized by multiple phonological process errors and a restricted consonant inventory. His difficulties appear consistent across both languages he is exposed to, which supports a primary diagnosis of a speech-language disorder rather than a language difference attributable solely to bilingual exposure. His social-communicative skills, joint attention, and nonverbal cognitive abilities appear to be relative strengths, suggesting a good prognosis for progress with consistent, intensive intervention.

Mateo meets eligibility criteria for Part C early intervention services in North Carolina on the basis of a 25% or greater delay in the communication domain, as documented by standardized testing above. This diagnosis and the resulting eligibility determination will be formally reviewed and documented by the CDSA de Durham team, with service coordination continuing through Rosa Jiménez at Coordinación Infantil del Triángulo.

Recommendations / Recomendaciones

1. Mateo is recommended for speech-language therapy services through the IFSP process, to address both receptive and expressive language delays and speech sound production errors. Intervention should be provided bilingually, in both English and Spanish, to support continued development in both of Mateo's home languages.

2. A bilingual, play-based therapeutic approach is recommended, incorporating elements of Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies to support parent-implemented language facilitation in the home, alongside direct articulation intervention using a Cycles approach to target Mateo's phonological process errors.

3. An occupational therapy evaluation is recommended to screen for any fine motor or sensory regulation concerns that may be contributing to frustration behaviors, given his borderline fine motor performance on the PDMS-2.

4. Continued close collaboration with daycare staff, including Miss Ana, is recommended to support generalization of therapy targets across settings.

5. Family education regarding bilingual language development is recommended to address concerns raised by extended family members, including doña Lupe, regarding whether speaking two languages is contributing to Mateo's delays; current research does not support this concern, and continued exposure to both English and Spanish is recommended.

6. Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan as needed.

Proposed Service Schedule

Service	Frequency	Duration	Provider
Speech-Language Therapy	2x/week	30 minutes	Jennifer Kim, M.S., CCC-SLP
Occupational Therapy Evaluation	1x (initial)	60 minutes	Mr. Tom, OTR/L
Service Coordination	1x/month	—	Rosa Jiménez

Next Steps

The IFSP meeting will be scheduled by CDSA de Durham with the family, this evaluator, and the service coordinator, Rosa Jiménez, within the next 30 days, per state timelines. The family has requested that the meeting be scheduled for a weekday evening or weekend when Carlos can attend, given his work schedule at Pinecrest Furniture Manufacturing. A tentative IFSP review date has been set for October 20, 2026 at 4:30 p.m., pending confirmation with the family.

This evaluator is available to answer any questions regarding this report or the recommendations above. Thank you to the Mateo's family for their openness and participation throughout this evaluation process. Gracias a la familia Flores Rodríguez por su colaboración y confianza durante este proceso.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Kim, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

Email: jkim@trianglebilingualslp.com

INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y EL LENGUAJE

Fecha del informe: 10 de octubre de 2026
Nombre del niño/a: Mateo Alejandro Ramírez Flores (le decimos "Teo" o "Mateíto" en casa)
Fecha de nacimiento: 15 de marzo de 2022
Edad en el momento de la evaluación: 4;7
Número de Medicaid: 784512093B

Evaluadora: Sandra Patiño, M.S., CCC-SLP, Patóloga del Habla y el Lenguaje bilingüe, TPCNC
Médico de cabecera: Dr. Felipe Montes, Pediatría Triangle Kids Pediatrics
Agencia de intervención temprana: Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Durham ("CDSA de Durham")
Guardería/Centro: Estrellitas Early Learning Center

Estimados Lucía Ramírez y Javier Flores:

Les escribo para compartir con ustedes, con mucho cariño, los resultados de la evaluación del habla y el lenguaje de su hijo Mateo. Fue un placer conocer a Teo y ver lo curioso, cariñoso y platicador que es. Este informe explica lo que encontramos durante las dos sesiones de evaluación, lo que estos resultados significan, y qué recomendamos para ayudarlo a seguir creciendo en sus dos idiomas, el español y el inglés.

MOTIVO DE LA REMISIÓN

La maestra de Teo en Estrellitas Early Learning Center, la Maestra Brenda Collins, notó que Mateo usa oraciones más cortas que sus compañeros de clase y que a veces sus amiguitos no le entienden cuando habla rápido. Ella habló con ustedes y, junto con la coordinadora de servicios de la CDSA de Durham, la Sra. Katherine Nguyen, se hizo la remisión a nuestra clínica el 18 de agosto de 2026. Ustedes también compartieron que en casa, su abuela Lupita (la Sra. Guadalupe Flores Reyes) a veces tiene que repetir lo que Mateo dice para que otras personas en la familia lo entiendan.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Vi a Teo en dos sesiones en nuestra oficina de TPCNC en Durham. La primera sesión fue el 2 de octubre de 2026 de 9:30 a.m. a 11:00 a.m., y la segunda fue el 6 de octubre de 2026 de 2:00 p.m. a 3:15 p.m.. Durante ambas sesiones, Mateo estuvo acompañado por su mamá, Lucía, quien ayudó a traducir algunas preguntas y a calmarlo cuando se sentía frustrado con una tarea difícil.

Usé pruebas estandarizadas en español y en inglés, observación de juego libre, una muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, un examen de los mecanismos orales, y un cuestionario que ustedes llenaron en casa sobre el desarrollo de Teo y el uso de los dos idiomas. También revisé los registros médicos y escolares que ustedes compartieron conmigo.

Pruebas administradas:
- Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition, Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish)
- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA), subpruebas de Morfosintaxis y Fonología
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), subprueba de Conceptos y Direcciones (en inglés, como medida informal)
- Examen informal del mecanismo oral motor
- Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo (100 enunciados) durante juego con bloques y figuras de animales
- Cuestionario de historia del desarrollo y del lenguaje llenado por los padres

HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Mateo nació el 15 de marzo de 2022 en el Duke Regional Hospital en Durham, después de un embarazo de 39 semanas. El parto fue por cesárea debido a presentación podálica. Su puntuación de Apgar fue 8/9 y su peso al nacer fue de 3.2 kg (7 libras, 1 onza). No hubo complicaciones en la sala de recién nacidos y fue dado de alta a los dos días con su mamá.

Según el cuestionario y la conversación con ustedes, Mateo tuvo tres infecciones de oído entre los 8 meses y los 18 meses de edad, tratadas con antibióticos por el Dr. Felipe Montes. No se colocaron tubos de ventilación. Una evaluación de audición realizada el 12 de febrero de 2025 mostró audición dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos. No hay diagnóstico de autismo, retraso motor, ni ninguna condición genética conocida. Mateo toma un multivitamínico diario y no tiene alergias conocidas.

Sus hitos motores gruesos y finos se desarrollaron dentro de rangos esperados: se sentó solo a los 6 meses, caminó a los 13 meses, y actualmente puede saltar en un pie y abotonar su abrigo con ayuda mínima.

HISTORIA DEL LENGUAJE Y DE LA FAMILIA

Mateo es el segundo de tres hijos. Su hermano mayor, Jesús Ramírez Flores, a quien todos llaman "Chuy", tiene 7 años y está en segundo grado sin ninguna preocupación de lenguaje. Su hermanita menor, Luz, tiene 11 meses y todavía no dice palabras, lo cual es apropiado para su edad.

En casa se habla principalmente español. Lucía y Javier hablan español entre ellos y con los niños, aunque Javier a veces mezcla algunas palabras en inglés que aprende en su trabajo en Triangle Poultry Processing, Inc.. Lucía trabaja medio tiempo en Sunrise Cleaning Services y pasa las tardes en casa con los niños. Según el cuestionario, la exposición de Mateo al español es de aproximadamente 75% y al inglés de aproximadamente 25%, principalmente a través de la guardería, la televisión, y el contacto con su hermano Chuy, quien ya está más expuesto al inglés en la escuela.

La familia de Lucía es originaria de un pueblo pequeño llamado El Rosario, Jalisco, México, donde todavía vive su madre, la abuela Lupita, cuando no está de visita en Durham. La familia vive actualmente en 4521 Walnut Creek Lane, Durham, Carolina del Norte 27703. Lupita vive con la familia varios meses al año y cuida a los niños mientras Lucía trabaja. También mencionaron a un tío, José Ramírez, a quien todos llaman "Pepe", que vive cerca y visita los fines de semana, y un primo, Juanito, que juega con Mateo cuando la familia se reúne.

La familia tiene un perrito llamado Rocky, al que Teo adora. Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, Mateo dijo con mucho entusiasmo "Rocky come" y después "yo y Chuy vamos a correr", mostrando enunciados de tres y cinco palabras con estructura gramatical generalmente apropiada para su edad, aunque con algunos errores de concordancia que se describen más abajo.

Según el reporte de los padres, Mateo dijo sus primeras palabras alrededor de los 14 meses y empezó a combinar dos palabras cerca de los 26 meses, un poco más tarde de lo esperado. No asistió a terapia de lenguaje antes de esta evaluación.

RESULTADOS: LENGUAJE RECEPTIVO Y EXPRESIVO

En el PLS-5 Spanish, Mateo obtuvo los siguientes resultados:

| Subprueba | Puntaje estándar | Percentil | Intervalo de confianza |
|---|---|---|---|
| Comprensión Auditiva | 88 | 21 | 81-95 |
| Comunicación Expresiva | 79 | 8 | 72-86 |
| Puntaje Total del Lenguaje | 82 | 12 | 76-88 |

En el BESA, subprueba de Morfosintaxis, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 81 (percentil 10), lo cual confirma, usando una medida diseñada específicamente para niños bilingües, que presenta dificultades con el lenguaje expresivo mayores de lo esperado para su edad y su nivel de exposición a los dos idiomas.

En la medida informal del CELF Preschool-3, subprueba de Conceptos y Direcciones (administrada en inglés dada su exposición parcial a ese idioma), obtuvo una edad equivalente de 3;4–3;8, por debajo de su edad cronológica, aunque esta medida debe interpretarse con cautela ya que fue diseñada para hablantes monolingües de inglés.

En la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, la longitud media de enunciado de Mateo en morfemas fue de 3.6, lo cual está por debajo del rango esperado de 4.2-5.0 para su edad. Observé errores consistentes de omisión del artículo ("quiero pelota" en vez de "quiero la pelota") y errores de concordancia de género en aproximadamente 6 de 10 oportunidades observadas ("la perro" en vez de "el perro"). También usa principalmente oraciones simples y rara vez combina dos cláusulas.

En cuanto a vocabulario, Mateo nombró correctamente 18 de 25 (72%) objetos y acciones presentados en láminas, usando una mezcla de español e inglés apropiada para un niño bilingüe de su edad y nivel de exposición.

RESULTADOS: HABLA Y ARTICULACIÓN

En el GFTA-3, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 85 (percentil 16), con errores notables en los sonidos /ɾ/ y /s/ en posición final de sílaba, y sustitución ocasional de /k/ por [t] en palabras como "zapato" producida como "tapato". Durante el juego, cuando intentó decir "sapo", lo produjo como "apo", omitiendo el sonido inicial.

En español, se observaron también errores con el sonido /r/ múltiple, por ejemplo produciendo "perro" como "pelo", y simplificación de grupos consonánticos, por ejemplo "flor" producida como "for". Estos patrones son consistentes entre ambos idiomas, lo cual sugiere un patrón fonológico subyacente y no simplemente una diferencia esperada entre dialectos o entre idiomas.

Con claves de apoyo, Mateo pudo corregir varios de estos sonidos. Con claves mínimas logró producir "flor" correctamente en 2 de 5 intentos, y con claves moderadas (imitación directa con modelo visual) logró 4 de 5 intentos correctos. Esto es una señal positiva: Mateo responde bien al apoyo y tiene buena capacidad de imitación, lo cual es un buen indicador para el progreso en terapia.

Su inteligibilidad general fue estimada en aproximadamente 70% en contexto conocido (con la familia) y aproximadamente 50% con oyentes desconocidos, según el reporte de los padres y mi propia observación durante la sesión.

EXAMEN ORAL MOTOR Y OTRAS OBSERVACIONES

El examen informal del mecanismo oral no mostró anomalías estructurales significativas. El frenillo lingual es de longitud normal, el paladar es intacto, y la simetría facial es adecuada. Mateo mostró buen control motor oral durante la alimentación y durante las tareas de imitación de movimientos (por ejemplo, sacar la lengua, soplar, sonreír), sin señales de apraxia del habla en la infancia ni de disartria.

En cuanto a pragmática y habilidades sociales de comunicación, Mateo mantuvo buen contacto visual, inició juego con la evaluadora, y usó gestos apropiadamente para complementar su lenguaje verbal. Se observó que a veces se frustra cuando no logra comunicar lo que quiere decir, por ejemplo cuando trató de contarme sobre un día en el parque con su amigo de la guardería, Diego, y no pudo encontrar las palabras, se tapó la cara con las manos y dijo "no puedo". Con apoyo y paciencia, pudo seguir intentando.

RESUMEN Y DIAGNÓSTICO

Basándome en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, el examen oral motor, y la información compartida por la familia y por la Maestra Brenda Collins, considero que Mateo presenta:

1. Un trastorno de lenguaje expresivo, con dificultades desproporcionadas en comparación con su comprensión, consistente en ambos idiomas (español e inglés), que no se explica simplemente por su exposición bilingüe. Código diagnóstico: F80.1 (Trastorno del lenguaje expresivo).

2. Un trastorno fonológico leve a moderado, con patrones de error consistentes en ambos idiomas, que afecta su inteligibilidad, especialmente con oyentes que no lo conocen bien. Código diagnóstico: F80.0 (Trastorno fonológico).

Es importante que ustedes sepan que el hecho de que Mateo esté aprendiendo dos idiomas NO es la causa de estas dificultades. Los niños bilingües se desarrollan de forma saludable en sus dos idiomas, y las dificultades que vemos aquí aparecen en ambos idiomas de forma similar, lo cual nos ayuda a confirmar que se trata de un verdadero trastorno y no de una diferencia típica del bilingüismo.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Recomiendo que Mateo reciba terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, idealmente dos veces por semana por 30 minutos cada sesión, en un modelo bilingüe que incluya tanto español como inglés, dado el perfil de exposición que describieron.

2. Para el trastorno fonológico, recomiendo el uso del Enfoque de Ciclos (Cycles Approach) para abordar los patrones de simplificación de grupos consonánticos y los errores con /ɾ/ y /s/, con técnicas de PROMPT para apoyar la colocación articulatoria cuando sea necesario.

3. Para el lenguaje expresivo, recomiendo actividades centradas en la expansión de enunciados y en la concordancia de género y artículos, incorporando estrategias del modelo Hanen para que ustedes, como familia, puedan apoyar el desarrollo del lenguaje de Mateo durante las actividades diarias en casa.

4. Códigos de facturación sugeridos para los servicios de terapia: CPT 92523 (evaluación de producción del habla y del lenguaje) ya utilizado en esta evaluación, y CPT 92507 para las sesiones individuales de tratamiento continuo.

5. Recomiendo que la familia continúe exponiendo a Mateo a ambos idiomas de manera consistente, sin eliminar ninguno de los dos, ya que el bilingüismo seguirá beneficiando su desarrollo cognitivo y social a largo plazo.

6. Sugiero una revisión del Plan de Servicio Individualizado para la Familia (IFSP) con la coordinadora de servicios de la CDSA de Durham, la Sra. Katherine Nguyen, para incorporar los objetivos de lenguaje y habla como parte de los servicios de intervención temprana de Mateo. El Objetivo de IFSP sugerido es el Objetivo 3, enfocado en comunicación funcional.

7. Recomiendo una próxima revisión del progreso en aproximadamente 12 semanas, programada tentativamente para la semana del 12 de enero de 2027, para ajustar el plan de tratamiento según sea necesario.

8. Finalmente, sugiero que la familia comparta este informe con la Maestra Brenda Collins en Estrellitas Early Learning Center para que el personal del salón pueda apoyar a Mateo usando frases cortas, dándole tiempo para responder, y celebrando sus intentos de comunicación, sin corregirlo de forma que lo haga sentir mal.

PALABRAS FINALES

Teo es un niño alegre, cariñoso, y muy motivado para comunicarse con las personas que ama, especialmente con su hermano Chuy, su hermanita Luz, su perrito Rocky, y por supuesto con ustedes. Con el apoyo adecuado, tiene todo el potencial para seguir creciendo en sus dos idiomas y para comunicarse con más claridad y confianza. Fue un gusto conocerlo a él y a toda su familia, incluyendo a la abuela Lupita, quien claramente lo cuida con mucho amor.

Si tienen alguna pregunta sobre este informe, o si desean programar la primera sesión de terapia, no duden en comunicarse conmigo directamente al (919) 555-0148, extensión 204, o por correo electrónico a spatino@tpcnc-slp.com. También pueden comunicarse con nuestra recepción general en info@tpcnc-slp.com.

Con mucho cariño y respeto,

Sandra Patiño, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y el Lenguaje, licencia de Carolina del Norte

— Grace Whitfield, CCC-SLP

text:
Patient Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Ramírez
Preferred Name: Teo
Date of Birth: June 14, 2021
Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Gender: Male
Primary Language(s): Spanish, English (simultaneous bilingual)
Medicaid ID: 745219863B
Case/Record ID: LDE-20395
Referral Source: Dr. Anita Patel, Pediatrics, Guilford Family Health Center
Evaluation Date(s): August 18, 2025 and August 25, 2025
Report Date: September 2, 2025
Clinician: Jennifer Suárez-Hall, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Employer/Practice: Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC
Interpreter Present: Rosa Elena Campos (Spanish, certified medical interpreter)
Service Coordinator: Denise Walker, Piedmont CDSA
Home Address: 1420 Winding Creek Lane, Apt 3B, Greensboro, NC 27406
County: Guilford County
Phone (Home): (336) 555-0142
Phone (Mom Cell): (336) 555-0198
Email: lflores1988@gmail.com
Daycare/School: Little Sprouts Head Start

RAZÓN DE REFERIDO / REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo, called Teo at home and at school, was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by his pediatrician, Dr. Anita Patel, after his teacher at Little Sprouts Head Start, Ms. Amanda Lopez, expressed concern that Teo was "muy callado" in the classroom and rarely initiated speech with peers. His mother, Lucía Flores Ramírez, reports that at home Teo habla bastante, pero se le entiende poco — he talks a lot, but he is hard to understand. Lucía also noted that her son mixes Spanish and English "como ensalada," switching mid-sentence without apparent difficulty, which she was told by a neighbor might be normal for a bilingual child, but she wanted a professional opinion because Teo's older sister, Valentina, did not have similar difficulty at this age.

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO / BIRTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY

Teo was born on June 14, 2021 at Moses H. Cone Memorial Hospital at 38 weeks gestational age via scheduled cesarean section. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. Lucía reported an uncomplicated pregnancy, though she noted mild gestational hypertension managed with monitoring in the third trimester. There were no NICU admissions.

Developmental milestones were reported as follows: sat independently at 6 months, walked at 13 months, first words emerged around 14-16 months in Spanish ("mamá," "agua," "perro"). Lucía stated that Teo's first two-word combinations did not appear until closer to 26 months, which she now recognizes was later than her daughter's. There is no reported history of recurrent ear infections, though Teo had one episode of otitis media at approximately 18 months, treated with antibiotics, with no tympanostomy tubes placed. A hearing screening at Little Sprouts Head Start in May 2025 showed normal results bilaterally.

Family medical history is notable for a maternal cousin with a diagnosed language delay and a paternal uncle who reportedly "no hablaba bien" as a child, though no formal diagnosis was obtained. Lucía denied any genetic syndromes, seizure history, or significant head trauma.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Teo lives with his mother, Lucía Flores Ramírez, his sister, Valentina, age 7, and his maternal grandmother, Rosa Pérez, who moved to the United States two years ago to help with childcare. Teo's father, referred to in records only by his initials, H.F., lives separately and has limited, inconsistent contact; Lucía reported he speaks primarily Spanish when he does see the children.

Lucía works nights as a housekeeping supervisor at Carolina Suites Hotel near the airport, and picks up weekend shifts through a staffing agency everyone in the family just calls ABC, sorting packages at a regional distribution center. Because of her schedule, Rosa and, occasionally, a neighbor known to the family only as M.R., provide after-school supervision for both children while Lucía sleeps during the day before her shift.

Rosa is originally from a small village called El Jocotillo, near Copán, Honduras, and she reports that in the home she speaks almost exclusively Spanish with Teo, often using regional vocabulary and expressions from her hometown — for example, she calls a drinking straw a "pajilla" rather than "pajita," and she says Teo has picked up some of these words himself. Lucía grew up partly in Comitán, Chiapas, México, before immigrating as a teenager, and she reports feeling "entre dos idiomas" herself, sometimes unsure which language to use with her children.

Language exposure at home is estimated at roughly 70% Spanish and 30% English, with English increasing since Teo started at Little Sprouts Head Start in January 2024. Valentina frequently code-switches with Teo during play, and Lucía reports that Valentina sometimes "traduce" for her brother when he gets frustrated trying to be understood by English-speaking adults. The family's dog, Luna, is mentioned frequently by Teo in both languages ("Luna run," "Luna está durmiendo"), and clinician observed this as a reliable topic for eliciting spontaneous speech.

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES / BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

During both evaluation sessions, Teo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and books. He was observed to be social but reserved with this examiner initially, warming over the course of the session, consistent with his mother's report of being "tímido con gente nueva." Attention to task was adequate for structured activities of 10-15 minutes with min-to-mod cues to maintain engagement.

Interpreter Rosa Elena Campos assisted with portions of the Spanish-language administration and with clarifying parent report during history-taking, particularly around idiomatic phrases Lucía used to describe Teo's speech ("se le enreda la lengua," "habla como atropellado").

Teo demonstrated frequent code-switching within utterances, e.g., "I want el carro rojo," and "no me gusta that one," consistent with typical bilingual language use rather than word-finding difficulty, as he readily supplied the target word in the other language when prompted.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS / TEST RESULTS

Standardized and informal measures were administered in both English and Spanish where appropriate, with Spanish administration prioritized given Teo's home language dominance. Conceptual scoring was used where available to account for his bilingual lexicon.

| Measure | Date Administered | Domain | Standard Score | 95% CI | Percentile |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Spanish Auditory Comprehension | August 18, 2025 | Receptive | 82 | 76-88 | 12th |
| PLS-5 Spanish Expressive Communication | August 18, 2025 | Expressive | 71 | 64-78 | 3rd |
| Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) Morphosyntax Spanish | August 25, 2025 | Expressive | 78 | 70-86 | 7th |
| BESA Morphosyntax English | August 25, 2025 | Expressive | 85 | 77-93 | 16th |
| BESA Semantics (Combined) | August 25, 2025 | Receptive/Expressive | 88 | 80-96 | 21st |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) Spanish-adapted | August 25, 2025 | Speech Sound Production | 74 | 68-80 | 4th |
| Oral Mechanism Exam | August 18, 2025 | Structural/Functional | Within normal limits | — | — |

Speech Sound Production: On the GFTA-3 Spanish-adapted protocol, Teo produced several phonological patterns consistent with his dialectal and bilingual background, including final consonant deletion in both languages (e.g., "sol" → [so], "cat" → [kæ]) and fronting of /ɾ/ in medial position (e.g., "carro" produced as [kado]). He correctly produced /k/ in isolation and in 8/10 trials of word-initial position but omitted it in 3 of 5 trials of word-final position. Stimulability testing showed Teo could approximate target sounds with mod cues, improving to 7/10 accuracy for /ɾ/ with modeling and tactile cueing.

During connected speech sampling using the SALT protocol, Teo's mean length of utterance was 3.2 morphemes in Spanish and 2.9 morphemes in English, both below age expectations. Several utterances were coded [EW] for word-level errors not attributable to dialectal variation. When asked to name a picture of a dog, he said "Luna bark," substituting his own pet's name for the target word, which was noted but not scored as an error given the clear semantic association.

Receptive and Expressive Vocabulary: On informal probes, Teo demonstrated a vocabulary that, when combined across both languages (conceptual scoring), fell closer to age expectations than when either language was scored in isolation, a pattern consistent with typical bilingual development rather than a primary language disorder.

Oral-Motor and Feeding: Oral mechanism examination was within normal limits for structure and function. No feeding or swallowing concerns were reported or observed.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS / CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Teo presents with a speech sound disorder and expressive language delay that are evident across both of his languages, which supports a true, underlying disorder rather than a difference attributable solely to bilingualism or dialectal variation. His receptive language skills are a relative strength, falling within the low-average to below-average range, while expressive language and speech sound production fall below age expectations in both English and Spanish.

Diagnosis: Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0) and Language Disorder, Expressive-Receptive (ICD-10 F80.2).

Teo's pattern of code-switching, observed throughout testing and reported at home, is consistent with typical bilingual language use and should not be targeted for reduction; rather, it reflects appropriate cross-linguistic flexibility given his dual-language environment. His difficulties are best explained by a disorder affecting both of his languages concurrently.

RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo qualifies for speech-language intervention services under North Carolina's Infant-Toddler Program criteria and should be referred to Piedmont CDSA for IFSP development; this report should be shared with service coordinator Denise Walker to support IFSP Outcome 2 (expressive communication) and IFSP Outcome 3 (speech sound production).

2. Individual speech-language therapy is recommended 2x/week for 30-minute sessions, ideally delivered by a bilingual provider or with consistent interpreter support, using therapeutic approaches such as Cycles phonological approach for speech sound targets and a Hanen-informed coaching model to support Lucía and Rosa in facilitating language at home.

3. Given Lucía's demanding work schedule between Carolina Suites Hotel and her weekend shifts through ABC, therapy scheduling flexibility should be prioritized; evening or Saturday morning slots were requested by the family. A phone consultation is recommended for 6:30 PM on weekdays, when Lucía is awake before her night shift begins at 11:00 PM.

4. Continued bilingual language exposure at home is strongly encouraged. The family should not reduce Spanish input in an attempt to "help" English development; research supports continued dual-language exposure.

5. Classroom-based support at Little Sprouts Head Start is recommended; consultation with Ms. Amanda Lopez regarding visual supports and extended processing time would be beneficial.

6. Re-evaluation of speech sound production and expressive language is recommended in approximately 6 months, or sooner if significant progress is noted, to determine continued eligibility and adjust goals.

7. A referral to audiology for a follow-up hearing evaluation is recommended given the history of one episode of otitis media, to rule out any subtle hearing-related contribution, though no current concerns were raised.

8. Family was provided with bilingual home-practice materials and encouraged to continue narrating daily routines in Spanish, incorporating Teo's interest in Luna as a motivating topic for language practice.

This evaluation and report were completed by Jennifer Suárez-Hall, M.S., CCC-SLP, of Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC, with interpretation support from Rosa Elena Campos. Please direct questions to the clinician at (336) 555-0177 or via the practice's secure portal. A copy of this report has been forwarded to Dr. Anita Patel at Guilford Family Health Center and to service coordinator Denise Walker at Piedmont CDSA with family consent, documented on August 18, 2025.

Her service coordinator, Marisol Peña, confirmed by email (mpena@asitnd-nc.org) that the six-month review will take place on November 3, 2026. ASITND will send updated eligibility paperwork, referencing case number AS-2026-04471, before that date. An interpreter from ASITND, Héctor Villalobos, joined by phone to support the family during the brief check-in.

Today's goals targeted expressive vocabulary and early phonology, drawn from IFSP Outcome 2. Using cards from her annual evaluation battery, which included the Goldman-Fristoe 2 (standard score 81, 11th percentile), the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (age equivalent 2;6–3;0), the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test (standard score 78), and the Bayley-4 cognitive composite (73-83, 90% CI), we practiced initial /k/ and final /t/ in single words. María José produced "car" clearly with min cues and attempted "cat", gliding the final consonant as [w] with mod cues, achieving 8/10 on structured trials. We used strategies from Hanen to expand her spontaneous utterances; when shown a picture of a dog, she said "María" want Rocky run," referencing her own dog at home.

During the session, her classmate Benjamin Alvarez briefly joined the table for a turn-taking activity, and María José shared a toy with him without prompting, a notable social gain. Ms. Carter noted that María José's older brother, Diego Fernández, sometimes picks her up early on Thursdays, which can shorten group time.

Plan: continue weekly sessions targeting final consonants and two-word combinations, incorporate PROMPT cueing for /t/ and /k/, and share home strategies with Lucía Fernández at pickup. Next session scheduled for September 25, 2026. Medicaid authorization for continued services is on file under member ID 987654321B.

text:
CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Hernández Flores
Date of Birth: April 8, 2022  Age at evaluation: 4;2
Dates of Evaluation: June 10, 2026 and June 12, 2026
Report Date: June 18, 2026
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Rodríguez (mamá), Jorge Hernández (papá)
Referral Source: Dr. Patricia Nwosu, pediatrician, Cumberland Pediatric Associates
School District: Cumberland County Schools
School/Classroom: Sherwood Park Elementary, Pre-K room of la maestra Carmen, assistant Miss Ana
Evaluating SLP: Rebecca Sutton, M.S., CCC-SLP
Agency: Carolina Bilingual Speech Services
Interpreter: Marisol Peña (consecutive interpretation, family interview)
Service Coordinator: Mr. Tom, Cumberland-Harnett CDSA
Medicaid ID: MC4471829K
Case ID: CBS-2026-0317
Address: 412 Willow Bend Rd, Fayetteville, Cumberland County, NC 28303
Phone: (910) 555-0148
Email: lucia.rodriguez84@gmail.com

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Pt referred by Dr. Nwosu and the Cumberland-Harnett CDSA service coordinator, Mr. Tom, due to parent and teacher concern re: limited expressive language and reduced intelligibility in both Spanish and English. Eval requested to determine eligibility for continued EI/preschool services and to clarify whether presentation reflects typical bilingual dvlpt vs. true delay.

BACKGROUND / HISTORY OF PRESENTING CONCERN
Mateo is a 4;2 y.o. bilingual (Spanish-dominant home, English exposure at school) male seen for comprehensive speech-language eval. Primary concerns per mamá Lucía and la maestra Carmen include: limited MLU, unintelligible speech to unfamiliar listeners (approx 30% intelligible in connected speech per parent est.), frustration behaviors at Sherwood Park Elementary, and reliance on gesture/pointing w/ peers. Family first noticed delay approx 18 months when Mateo had <5 words compared to sibling at same age.

Mamá Lucía stated, "A veces me frustro porque no entiendo lo que quiere decir, y él se enoja conmigo." Papá Jorge added, "En casa hablamos español, pero en la escuela todo es inglés, y no sé si eso lo confunde o no." Per report, family goal is for Mateo to communicate wants/needs w/o tantrums and to be understood by extended family, incl. abuela Rosa, who speaks only Spanish.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY
Pregnancy c/b gestational diabetes, diet-controlled. Born at 37 weeks gestational age via C-section at Cape Fear Valley Medical Center April 8, 2022. Birth weight 5 lbs 11 oz (2.58 kg). Apgar scores 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 min. Brief NICU stay x 3 days for respiratory monitoring, resolved w/o intervention. Hearing screen passed bilaterally 03/02/2026 (tympanometry + OAE). No hx of chronic OM reported by mom, though CG (doña Lupe) reports occasional ear pulling, "se agarra las orejas," unclear significance. Pt followed by PT 1x/wk through Cumberland-Harnett CDSA for mild hypotonia, first noted by Dr. Nwosu at 18-month well check. No hx of seizure, head injury, or hospitalization since birth. Current meds: none. Vision screening WNL per Dr. Nwosu 05/14/2026.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY
Mateo lives w/ mamá Lucía Rodríguez, papá Jorge Hernández, and older sister Camila (7 y.o.) at above address. Home language is Spanish (approx 80% Spanish/20% English per parent report, using bilingual input freq survey). Paternal abuela Rosa lives nearby and provides childcare 2x/wk; weekday mornings pt is cared for by babysitter doña Lupe b/c both parents work outside home. Mamá works at Fayetteville Poultry Processing; papá works at Carolina Tile & Flooring. Sister Camila attends 2nd grade at a different school in the district and per mom "hablaba mucho antes" at Mateo's current age, suggesting a discrepancy from typical sibling pattern. Family denies known hx of speech/lang/learning disorder, though report a paternal uncle who "no hablaba bien de niño" per family report, unconfirmed.

Mateo began combining words around 26 months, notably later than typical bilingual milestones. First words emerged approx 16 months ("mamá," "agua," "no"). Current expressive repertoire per parent report approx 60 words combined across both languages, primarily nouns, few verbs or function words. Pt attends Sherwood Park Elementary Pre-K 5x/wk, 8:15 AM–2:30 PM, in the classroom of la maestra Carmen, w/ assistant Miss Ana. La maestra Carmen reports pt relies heavily on gesture and single words w/ peers; classmate Diego frequently translates/mediates for Mateo during circle time. Miss Ana noted 2 episodes in the past month of pt hitting peer Jacob during centers when unable to express a want, resolved w/ redirection.

OBSERVATION / PLAY-BASED ASSESSMENT
Two sessions completed: Session 1 (home visit) June 10, 2026, 9:00 AM–10:15 AM; Session 2 (clinic visit) June 12, 2026, 1:30 PM–2:45 PM. Interpreter Marisol Peña present for Session 1 to support parent interview; eval itself conducted directly by bilingual SLP.

During free play w/ toy animals, pt picked up a stuffed dog (family reports home pet, a dog named Nico) and imitated examiner model, saying "Nico corre," approximated as [ˈtole] for target "corre", demonstrating cluster reduction and substitution of /k/ with [t] word-initially. Pt engaged in reciprocal play approx 8 of 10 turns w/ min cues; required mod cues to sustain joint attention beyond 3 exchanges. Pt used primarily single-word utterances w/ occasional 2-word combinations ("más agua," "no quiero"), MLU calculated at 1.8 morphemes across Spanish and English samples combined.

STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENT RESULTS

Test — Standard Score — Percentile — Age Equivalent
Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5) Auditory Comprehension — 73 — 4th percentile — 2;6
PLS-5 Expressive Communication — 68 — 2nd percentile — 2;3
PLS-5 Total Language Score — 70 — 2nd percentile (CI 65-75) — —
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) Sounds-in-Words — 65 — 1st percentile — —
Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5) — 79 — 8th percentile — 3;2
CELF Preschool-3 Sentence Structure — 71 — 3rd percentile — —

Supplemental data from EI record review: Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 (Bayley-4) Gross Motor scaled score 7, Fine Motor scaled score 8, administered November 2024 by EI team. Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale items administered informally during Session 1 to supplement interactive checklist; pt met approx 3 of 5 items at the 24-30 month band.

ARTICULATION/PHONOLOGY
GFTA-3 administered in English; informal Spanish phonology probe administered using single-word picture naming. Error patterns observed across both languages: cluster reduction (e.g., target "azul" → [aˈul]), final consonant deletion (target "pan" → [pa]), and substitution of /ɾ/ with [l] (target "perro" → [ˈpelo]). In English, substitution of /k/ with [t] and /g/ with [d] noted consistently (fronting pattern). Intelligibility in connected speech estimated at approx 35% to unfamiliar listener, approx 65% to familiar listener/family, consistent w/ parent report.

IMPRESSIONS
Mateo presents w/ a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and concomitant phonological disorder affecting both Spanish and English, not attributable solely to typical bilingual acquisition patterns or reduced input. Scores fall consistently >1.5 SD below mean across both receptive and expressive domains, in both languages, which per current bilingual-eval best practice supports a true disorder rather than a language difference. Hypotonia and motor delay (per PT/Bayley-4 data) may contribute to oral-motor coordination difficulties affecting articulation but do not fully account for the expressive language profile. Frustration-related behavior at school (hitting peer Jacob) appears secondary to communication breakdown rather than a primary behavioral concern.

Diagnostic impressions:
- Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder, ICD-10 F80.2
- Phonological Disorder, ICD-10 F80.0
- CPT code for eval: 92523 (eval of speech sound production w/ eval of lang comprehension and expression)

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Continued speech-language therapy 2x/wk, 30 min individual sessions, bilingual service delivery strongly recommended given home language dominance.
2. Incorporate PROMPT for oral-motor/articulatory placement work targeting fronting pattern and /ɾ/ substitution.
3. Cycles phonological approach recommended given multiple concurrent error patterns across two languages.
4. Parent coaching using Hanen It Takes Two to Talk program recommended to build caregiver responsivity strategies; CG doña Lupe and abuela Rosa should be included in coaching sessions given significant caregiving time.
5. Consider PECS as backup/supplemental AAC strategy for high-frustration moments at school, to be trialed by la maestra Carmen's classroom team at Sherwood Park Elementary in collaboration w/ school-based SLP.
6. Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol may be considered as an alternative/adjunct approach if progress w/ Cycles plateaus, particularly for word-level motor planning difficulties.
7. Update IFSP to reflect current scores; recommend new outcome addressing bilingual expressive language, documented as IFSP Outcome #2.
8. Referral to audiology for repeat hearing screen given parent-reported ear-pulling behavior, though no significant hx currently.
9. Continue PT services through Cumberland-Harnett CDSA to address hypotonia; coordinate goals across disciplines.
10. Classroom accommodations: visual schedule, simplified directions, peer support strategies (not relying solely on peer Diego for translation), and praise for communication attempts rather than correction of errors.
11. Follow-up re-eval recommended in approx 6 months to monitor progress and reassess eligibility status.

This report and all recommendations were reviewed w/ family via interpreter Marisol Peña on June 12, 2026. Family verbalized understanding and agreement w/ plan. Copy of report to be sent to Cumberland-Harnett CDSA service coordinator Mr. Tom and to Dr. Nwosu's office at Cumberland Pediatric Associates pending signed release.

Submitted by,
Rebecca Sutton, M.S., CCC-SLP

March 3, 2026

Estimada familia Carlos Vega Martínez y Daniela Flores Soto:

Les escribo para compartir con ustedes los resultados de la revisión del Plan de Servicio Familiar Individualizado (IFSP) de su hijo Mateo Vega Flores. La reunión se llevó a cabo el February 26, 2026 en su hogar, ubicado en 214 Hollyfield Lane, Greensboro, condado de Guilford, 27405. Fue un gusto verlos de nuevo a ustedes, a Mateo y a su hermana mayor, Sofía, quien tiene 5 años y estuvo presente parte de la visita. Mateo ahora tiene 26 meses de edad. Nació el January 14, 2024 en el Hospital Moses Cone Memorial, con un peso al nacer de 2,850 gramos, edad gestacional de 36 semanas y puntaje de Apgar de 8 y 9.

Como coordinadora de servicios de la familia, Ana Gutiérrez, de la oficina del Centro de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA), estuvo presente en la reunión, junto con su servidora, Marisol Jiménez, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe de Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners, PLLC. Para esta visita no se necesitó intérprete, ya que yo hablo español con la familia directamente, pero el CDSA puede proveer uno en cualquier momento si la familia lo prefiere. Pueden comunicarse con la oficina del CDSA al (336) 555-0177, o con Ana directamente a su celular, 336-555-0199.

Preocupaciones y prioridades de la familia

Durante la reunión, Daniela compartió: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Mateo todavía no dice muchas palabras que entendamos. En casa solo le entendemos a veces, y a veces se frustra y llora porque no sabemos qué quiere." Carlos agregó: "Queremos que pueda decirle a su maestra en la guardería lo que necesita, y que juegue con los otros niños sin frustrarse. También nos gustaría saber qué podemos hacer nosotros en casa, en español, porque no todas las actividades que nos dan están en nuestro idioma." La familia también mencionó que les gustaría más apoyo con las rutinas de la noche, ya que Daniela trabaja de noche en el turno nocturno en Novant Health Forsyth Medical Center como auxiliar de enfermería, y Carlos se queda solo con los niños varias noches a la semana. Ambos padres acordaron que su prioridad principal para esta revisión es que Mateo empiece a combinar palabras y a usar gestos y sonidos de manera más consistente para pedir lo que necesita.

Rutinas diarias

Mateo se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna junto con su hermana, Sofía, antes de que ella salga para su programa preescolar. Luego asiste a la guardería Little Sprouts Learning Center de 8:30 a.m. a 4:00 p.m., donde su maestra, la señorita Brenda López, reporta que Mateo juega bien al lado de otros niños pero rara vez inicia el juego de manera verbal. Un compañerito de clase, Liam, suele ofrecerle juguetes, y Mateo responde casi siempre con gestos en lugar de palabras. Por las tardes, después de recogerlo de la guardería, Mateo juega en el patio con su perro, Rocky, y le encanta perseguirlo por el jardín gritando "¡Rocky, vamos!" En varias ocasiones también se le ha escuchado decir "Sofía no" cuando su hermana le quita algún juguete durante el juego. Los fines de semana, cuando la abuela paterna cuida a los niños mientras los padres hacen mandados, ella reporta observaciones similares sobre su comunicación. La hora de la cena familiar es alrededor de las 6:30 p.m., y la rutina de baño y de dormir comienza cerca de las 8:00 p.m., con un cuento corto que Carlos le lee en español.

Otras agencias involucradas

La familia también recibe apoyo de WIC para nutrición infantil y está inscrita en el programa Smart Start de Guilford County para actividades de desarrollo temprano los sábados. Además, la abuela materna, Rosa Martínez, quien vive en México y habla con la familia casi todos los días por videollamada, puede contactarse al +52 55 1234 5678 si en algún momento necesitan ayuda para traducir algún documento o si Daniela no está disponible durante el día por su horario nocturno.

Resultados de la evaluación

Administramos el Preschool Language Scale, Quinta Edición (PLS-5), en su forma en español, con las siguientes puntuaciones: Comprensión Auditiva, puntaje estándar de 76 (percentil 5, rango 70-82); Expresión Verbal, puntaje estándar de 71 (percentil 3, rango 65-77). La edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo fue de 16 meses, comparado con su edad cronológica de 26 meses. Estos resultados, junto con la observación clínica durante el juego y la rutina familiar, respaldan el diagnóstico de F80.2 (trastorno del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo mixto). En cuanto al habla, Mateo produjo correctamente el sonido /k/ en posición inicial en 8/10 intentos (80% de precisión) con apoyo de claves táctiles mínimas, pero sustituyó el sonido /s/ por [t] en palabras como "sopa" y "sol". El examen oral motor no mostró hallazgos estructurales que expliquen estas dificultades.

Resultados del IFSP y estrategias

Resultado 1: Mateo usará al menos 20 palabras nuevas de manera espontánea para pedir objetos o acciones durante las rutinas familiares en los próximos 6 meses.
Estrategia: La familia usará el enfoque Hanen durante la hora de la comida y el juego, nombrando objetos en voz alta y esperando con expectativa para que Mateo intente comunicarse antes de dárselos. Carlos practicará esto especialmente durante las tardes, y Daniela lo hará en los días que no trabaja.

Resultado 2: Mateo combinará dos palabras (por ejemplo, "más agua" o "Mateo arriba") en al menos 3 de 5 oportunidades observadas durante las sesiones de terapia y en el hogar.
Estrategia: Se usará modelado de lenguaje expandido; cuando Mateo diga una palabra sola, el adulto responderá expandiendo a una frase corta de dos palabras, usando claves de nivel moderado (mod cues) según se necesite, y reduciendo las claves conforme mejore su consistencia.

Resultado 3: Mateo producirá el sonido /s/ correctamente en posición inicial de palabra en al menos 4 de 5 intentos con claves mínimas, usando el programa Cycles para el desarrollo fonológico durante ciclos de dos a tres semanas cada uno.

Servicios y frecuencia

Mateo continuará recibiendo terapia de lenguaje individual una vez por semana, 30 minutos por sesión (código 92507), proporcionada por Marisol Jiménez de CPTP, en el hogar de la familia como su ambiente natural. También se realizará una reevaluación formal del habla y el lenguaje (código 92523) antes de la próxima revisión del IFSP, programada para el August 28, 2026. Como Mateo se acerca a su tercer cumpleaños, también comenzaremos a hablar sobre la planificación de transición hacia los servicios del sistema escolar local.

Información de contacto y facturación

El número de identificación de Medicaid de Mateo es 987654321B, y su número de expediente en el CDSA es CDSA-2026-04471. Si tienen preguntas sobre la facturación o necesitan reprogramar una cita, pueden llamar a nuestra oficina principal al 1-800-555-0123 o escribir a mjimenez@carolinapediatrictherapy.com. También pueden encontrar información general sobre nuestros servicios en www.carolinapediatrictherapy.com.

Próximos pasos

La próxima visita de terapia está programada para el March 10, 2026 a las 3:00 p.m. en su hogar. Si necesitan cambiar esta cita, por favor llamen al consultorio con al menos 24 horas de anticipación. También recibirán una llamada de seguimiento de Ana Gutiérrez del CDSA para coordinar la revisión semestral y confirmar que todos los servicios siguen funcionando bien para la familia.

Gracias por su confianza y por el trabajo tan dedicado que hacen todos los días con Mateo. Es un privilegio acompañarlos en este proceso, y tanto Ana como yo estamos aquí para apoyarlos en español o en inglés, lo que sea más cómodo para la familia.

Con cariño y respeto,

Marisol Jiménez, MS, CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje Bilingüe
Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners, PLLC (CPTP)

Correo electrónico: mjimenez@carolinapediatrictherapy.com

Home Phone:  (704) 555-7732          Parent Email:  lucia.rivas82@gmail.com
Medicaid ID:  8827461305A          Insurance Member ID:  BCBS-NC-5591732
NC ITP Child ID:  ITP-2021-048852          Record/Authorization #:  AUTH-2026-003317
Evaluation Date:  September 15, 2026          Report Date:  September 22, 2026
Evaluator:  Dr. Jennifer Alvarez, CCC-SLP, bilingual (Spanish/English)
Interpreter:  Ms. Carla Jiménez (used for portions of parent interview only)
Service Coordinator:  Keisha Brown, Mecklenburg County Partnership for Children

REASON FOR REFERRAL

María José (called "Majo" at home) was referred by her pediatrician, Dr. Michael Chen, for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation due to parental and teacher concern about limited intelligibility in both English and Spanish. Her mother, Lucía, reports, "No le entiendo casi nada cuando habla rápido" (I barely understand her when she talks fast). Majo currently attends Beatties Ford Road Early Head Start Center, where her teacher, Ms. Hannah Lopez, noted similar concerns and completed a referral checklist. Her assistant teacher, Mr. Derek Simmons, echoed these concerns in a brief phone conversation with the clinician on September 10, 2026.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA MÉDICA

María José was born at 34 weeks gestational age at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center in Charlotte on April 2, 2021, following a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia and gestational hypertension. Delivery was by emergency cesarean section. Birth weight was 4 lbs, 2 oz, and Apgar scores were 6 and 8 at one and five minutes. She spent 11 days in the NICU at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center for respiratory support and feeding difficulties, including a brief period on a nasal cannula. Per mother's report, "estuvo en incubadora casi dos semanas, y yo no podía cargarla" (she was in the incubator for almost two weeks, and I couldn't hold her).

Majo was followed by Dr. Patricia Owens, audiologist, at Atrium Health Hemby Children's Hospital Ear, Nose & Throat – SouthPark Campus, after failing her newborn hearing screen bilaterally. A follow-up ABR at 4 months of age was within normal limits bilaterally. She has had three documented episodes of otitis media between the ages of 18 and 30 months, treated first with antibiotics and later with tympanostomy tubes (CPT 69436) placed at August 10, 2023 at the same ENT practice. Current hearing is reported as normal per audiologic re-check on March 3, 2026.

Medical diagnoses include history of prematurity and recurrent otitis media (ICD-10 H66.90). No seizure history, no known genetic syndrome, and no significant hospitalizations since the NICU stay aside from a brief ER visit for a febrile illness at 2 years of age. Vision screening is within normal limits. Feeding history is unremarkable; mother denies any current feeding or swallowing concerns.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y LINGÜÍSTICA

María José lives with her mother, Lucía Rivas Campos; her father, Carlos Alberto Mendoza Soto; and her older brother, Diego Mendoza Rivas (age 9). Her maternal grandmother, Rosa Campos, moved in with the family in January 2025 and provides after-school child care along with the children's aunt, Marta Rivas, who helps on weekends. The family's small dog, Canela, was present and calm during the home-visit portion of the intake.

Lucía was born and raised in Aldea Las Flores, a small village near Copán Ruinas, Honduras, and moved to the United States in 2015. She reports Spanish as her first and dominant language and describes her own schooling in Honduras as limited to primary grades. Carlos was born in Charlotte to parents who had emigrated from Honduras years earlier and is a balanced bilingual speaker, comfortable switching between languages mid-sentence. At home, the family estimates speaking approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English, with Lucía speaking almost exclusively in Spanish to the children and Carlos code-switching freely depending on topic. Diego primarily responds in English but understands Spanish well and often translates informally for his mother at appointments.

Lucía works at Queen City Poultry Processing on the packaging line, and Carlos works night shifts as a warehouse supervisor. Family routines are described as "muy ocupados entre semana, pero los domingos siempre cocinamos juntos" (very busy during the week, but on Sundays we always cook together). Rosa speaks only Spanish and is the primary caregiver during the hours between daycare pickup and the parents' return from work.

Developmental milestones were reportedly delayed: María José walked independently at 17 months and said her first recognizable words around 20 months. Mother reports first words were in Spanish ("agua," "mamá"). The family was referred to Mecklenburg County Partnership for Children (Smart Start) for early intervention services at 18 months and began receiving home-based speech therapy through the Infant-Toddler Program at 22 months, delivered initially by early interventionist Ms. Angela Kim. An IFSP outcome (Outcome 2: increase intelligibility of 2-3 word phrases in daily routines) was in place prior to this evaluation, with a review scheduled for November 4, 2026.

The family also received nutritional support through the Mecklenburg County WIC Office until María José turned 5, and the family's case was briefly open with Mecklenburg County Department of Social Services during a period of housing instability in 2022, which has since resolved. Lucía attended a parent group hosted by Mecklenburg County Partnership for Children focused on bilingual language stimulation strategies and reports finding it helpful: "aprendí que no pasa nada si le hablo en los dos idiomas" (I learned it's okay to talk to her in both languages).

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

The evaluation was conducted in a combination of English and Spanish from 10:00 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. in a quiet therapy room, with a short break at 10:45 a.m.. María José separated easily from her mother and engaged readily with toys and testing materials. She demonstrated a preference for Spanish during unstructured play but switched to English for most structured tasks presented in English. Attention was adequate throughout, with occasional redirection needed during longer tasks. Rapport was established quickly; she referred to the clinician as "Miss Jenny" throughout the session and asked at one point, "¿jugamos otra vez?" (can we play again?).

ASSESSMENT RESULTS

The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both English and Spanish as appropriate:

Test                                                      Domain                      Standard Score   Percentile
Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), English Edition         Auditory Comprehension     78              7th
PLS-5, English Edition                                       Expressive Communication   74              4th
Preschool Language Scales-5, Spanish Edition                 Auditory Comprehension     85              16th
PLS-5, Spanish Edition                                       Expressive Communication   81              10th
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)              Sound Production           70              2nd
Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA)                  Morphosyntax               82              12th

On the GFTA-3, María José demonstrated multiple phonological error patterns consistent with a moderate speech sound disorder affecting both languages. She produced consistent cluster reduction (e.g., target "star" produced as [tɑ]), final consonant deletion, and gliding of liquids (e.g., /r/ realized as [w]). In Spanish, she showed difficulty with the trilled /r/ and the tap /ɾ/, frequently substituting [l], as in her production of "perro" as [pelo]. When asked to name a picture of a star, she said "tá" for target "star," and when asked to repeat "quiero agua," she produced "kelo awa." With mod cues, she was able to self-correct roughly 3 of 5 trials of the Spanish tap /ɾ/.

Speech intelligibility was estimated at 60% in known context and 40% in unknown context, consistent with parent and teacher report of difficulty being understood by unfamiliar listeners. Oral mechanism exam was within normal limits for structure and function. Diadochokinetic rates were judged appropriate for age.

Language sampling in both languages revealed mean length of utterance of 3.1 morphemes in English and 3.4 morphemes in Spanish, both below the expected range of 4.0–4.5 for her age. She used present progressive and plural -s inconsistently in English, correct on 8/10 opportunities for progressive -ing but only 4/10 for plural -s, and showed omission of gender agreement markers in Spanish articles (e.g., "el pelota" instead of "la pelota"). Pragmatic skills, including joint attention, turn-taking, and requesting, were judged age-appropriate in both languages, and her play skills were commensurate with chronological age.

IMPRESSIONS

María José Mendoza Rivas presents with a moderate speech sound disorder and mild-to-moderate expressive and receptive language delay in both English and Spanish, consistent with a diagnosis of Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0) and Developmental Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.1). Her difficulties are present in both languages, which rules out the pattern typically seen in typically developing bilingual children whose difficulties are isolated to the non-dominant language.

Her history of prematurity, NICU stay, and recurrent otitis media are plausible contributing risk factors for both the speech sound disorder and the broader language delay. Performance across both English and Spanish measures, combined with parent and teacher report, supports a true bilingual communication disorder rather than a language difference secondary to limited English exposure. María José's stronger relative performance in Spanish is consistent with her home language environment and should guide treatment language allocation moving forward.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. María José qualifies for and should receive speech-language therapy services at a frequency of 2x/week, 30 minutes individual sessions, delivered bilingually with primary emphasis on Spanish given relative strengths and home language dominance, supported by Hanen-informed parent coaching strategies.
2. Continue IFSP services through Mecklenburg County Partnership for Children; update Outcome 2 to reflect current intelligibility targets and add a new outcome targeting Spanish morphosyntax, specifically article gender agreement.
3. Direct intervention should target cluster reduction, final consonant deletion, liquid gliding, and the Spanish /r/–/ɾ/ contrast using a Cycles approach across both languages, with periodic probes in English to monitor generalization.
4. Recommend continued audiologic monitoring given history of recurrent otitis media; follow up with Dr. Patricia Owens at Atrium Health Hemby Children's Hospital Ear, Nose & Throat – SouthPark Campus as needed, and at minimum annually.
5. Share results with Ms. Hannah Lopez and Mr. Derek Simmons at Beatties Ford Road Early Head Start Center to support classroom-based language strategies in both languages.
6. Provide Lucía Rivas Campos and Carlos Alberto Mendoza Soto with a bilingual home strategies handout and encourage continued rich Spanish language input, as "el español en casa es un punto fuerte, no un obstáculo" (Spanish at home is a strength, not an obstacle).
7. Coordinate with service coordinator Keisha Brown prior to the scheduled IFSP review on November 4, 2026 to ensure continuity of services.
8. Re-evaluate in 6 months to monitor progress and adjust treatment language allocation as needed.

Report prepared by Dr. Jennifer Alvarez, CCC-SLP, Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Associates, PLLC, on September 22, 2026. Questions may be directed to (704) 555-0148 or intake@carolinabilingualslp.com.
