text:
Este informe resume la reunión de revisión del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) de Mateo Alejandro Fernández Ruiz, a quien su familia llama cariñosamente "Teo", niño de 26 meses de edad corregida, nacido el 14 de agosto de 2024 con 32 semanas de edad gestacional y un peso al nacer de 1,580 gramos. La reunión se llevó a cabo el 7 de octubre de 2026 en las oficinas de la CDSA del Piedmont Triad, ubicada en 2210 Yanceyville Street, Greensboro, NC 27405. El número de expediente del niño es CDSA-77294 y su número de Medicaid es 852617439A. La familia reside en 142 Willow Bend Lane, Greensboro, NC 27410, en el condado de Guilford. Participaron en la reunión la madre, Lucía Ruiz Hernández (336-555-0147, lucia.ruizh82@example.com), y el padre, Carlos Fernández Soto, quien se conectó por teléfono desde su trabajo en Triad Metal Fabricators. También estuvo presente la abuela materna, Rosa Hernández Díaz, quien cuida a Teo dos días por semana mientras sus padres trabajan. La coordinadora de servicios, Juana Ortiz (a quien la familia llama "J. Ortiz"), facilitó la reunión, y yo, Mariana Castillo, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe certificada (CCC-SLP) de Carolina Pines Early Intervention Services, redacté este informe.

Teo nació en el Carolina Pines Health – Hospital Infantil Guilford, Campus de Elm Street tras un embarazo complicado por preeclampsia materna. Pasó 18 días en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales (UCIN) del mismo hospital, donde recibió apoyo respiratorio y alimentación por sonda. Su puntaje de Apgar fue de 6 al minuto y 8 a los cinco minutos. Su pediatra, la Dra. Hannah Kim, de Carolina Pines Health – Clínica Pediátrica, Campus de Friendly Center, refirió a Teo al programa de intervención temprana a los 4 meses de edad corregida por preocupaciones sobre su tono muscular bajo y retraso en los hitos motores. A los 14 meses, la familia notó que Teo no imitaba sonidos ni usaba gestos como señalar, y fue remitido a audiología. La Dra. Priya Patel, audióloga de Carolina Pines Health – Otorrinolaringología y Audiología, Campus de Westover, realizó una prueba de emisiones otoacústicas y un timpanograma el 3 de marzo de 2025; los resultados fueron normales en ambos oídos, aunque la familia reporta que Teo ha tenido tres episodios de otitis media tratados con antibióticos, el más reciente en enero de 2026. No se ha colocado tubos de ventilación hasta la fecha.

Durante la reunión, Lucía expresó su principal preocupación en sus propias palabras: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no me dice lo que quiere y se frustra mucho, grita y se tira al piso." Añadió que en casa usan tanto español como inglés, porque Carlos habla principalmente inglés en el trabajo pero español en casa, y que les gustaría que Teo aprendiera ambos idiomas sin que esto retrasara más su comunicación. Carlos compartió: "Yo quiero que él pueda jugar con su hermana y con los otros niños del vecindario sin tanta frustración." La hermana mayor de Teo, Valentina Fernández Ruiz, de 6 años, a menudo intenta traducir lo que su hermano quiere decir, y los padres notan que esto a veces hace que Teo dependa de ella en lugar de intentar comunicarse directamente. La abuela, Rosa, agregó que durante los días que ella lo cuida, Teo señala la alacena cuando tiene hambre pero rara vez vocaliza, y que a veces confunde el llanto de hambre con el de sueño. Las prioridades de la familia para este período del IFSP son: que Teo use palabras o señas para pedir comida y ayuda, que disminuyan las rabietas relacionadas con la frustración comunicativa, y que la familia reciba más estrategias bilingües para usar en casa.

La familia describió la rutina diaria de Teo. Se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con la familia; los días que va a la guardería, Carlos lo lleva a las 7:45 a.m. a Burbujas y Sonrisas Centro de Aprendizaje Temprano, ubicado en 905 Spring Garden Street, Greensboro. Su maestra en el salón de gateadores, la Srta. Ashley Pruitt, reporta que Teo disfruta de la hora de música a las 9:30 a.m. pero se frustra durante la transición al patio a las 10:15 a.m., cuando debe esperar su turno para los juguetes. Teo tiene una siesta de las 12:30 p.m. a las 2:00 p.m. y su mamá lo recoge a las 5:00 p.m.. En casa, la cena familiar es alrededor de las 6:30 p.m., seguida de tiempo de juego con Valentina y, a veces, con el vecino, Jayden Morales, quien tiene la misma edad. Teo tiene un perrito llamado Max, al que le gusta perseguir por el patio, y esto se ha identificado como un momento natural para practicar vocabulario de acción como "corre" y "ven". Se baña a las 7:15 p.m. y se acuesta a las 8:00 p.m. después de leer cuentos, actividad durante la cual la familia reporta que Teo señala las imágenes pero aún no nombra objetos familiares de manera consistente.

La evaluación de habla y lenguaje se realizó en dos sesiones, el 15 de septiembre de 2026 y el 22 de septiembre de 2026, en el hogar de la familia y en Burbujas y Sonrisas Centro de Aprendizaje Temprano. Se administró la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale en ambos idiomas, con apoyo de la madre como informante para los ítems en español. Teo obtuvo una puntuación equivalente de edad de 11-13 meses en el área de lenguaje receptivo y de 9-11 meses en lenguaje expresivo, con un desempeño más fuerte en interacción-apego que en los dominios lingüísticos, reflejando una discrepancia significativa de aproximadamente 13 meses entre su edad cronológica corregida y sus habilidades expresivas. Se administró también la Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4) por una evaluadora del equipo interdisciplinario; Teo obtuvo una puntuación compuesta de 76 en el dominio de lenguaje receptivo (percentil 5) y de 71 en lenguaje expresivo (percentil 3), ambos dentro del rango de retraso significativo, con un intervalo de confianza de 65-83. En el área motora, obtuvo una puntuación compuesta de 88 (percentil 21), reflejando mejoría desde la evaluación anterior. Dado que Teo aún no combina palabras, no fue posible administrar completamente el Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3; sin embargo, durante el muestreo de habla espontánea se observó que produce principalmente vocales y algunas consonantes labiales, con producciones como "mamá" y "pa" para "papá", además de aproximaciones como "tete" para "Max" (su perrito). Se observaron los fonemas /m/, /p/ y /b/ de manera consistente, mientras que /t/, /d/ y /k/ aparecen solo con apoyo máximo. No se administró el Peabody en esta ocasión debido a la edad y al nivel actual de Teo, pero el equipo recomienda considerarlo como medida de seguimiento del vocabulario receptivo en la próxima revisión, una vez que combine palabras de manera más consistente.

Además de los servicios de intervención temprana, la familia recibe apoyo del Departamento de Servicios Sociales del condado de Guilford (DSS) para asistencia con cuidado infantil subsidiado, y participa en el Programa WIC del condado de Guilford para apoyo nutricional. La familia fue referida recientemente a Smart Start of Guilford County para considerar un programa de alfabetización familiar en el hogar, y la coordinadora de servicios Juana Ortiz está explorando con la familia la posibilidad de inscribir a Teo en Early Head Start de Guilford County una vez que cumpla 30 meses, como complemento a los servicios actuales de intervención temprana. Lucía mencionó que también ha estado en contacto con una trabajadora social, S. Nguyen, de la misma agencia de DSS, para renovar la documentación de elegibilidad de Medicaid este trimestre. El equipo de IFSP coordinará con estas agencias para evitar duplicación de servicios y asegurar que todos los proveedores compartan información consistente sobre el progreso de Teo, con el consentimiento firmado de la familia.

El equipo, junto con la familia, desarrolló tres resultados para este período del IFSP. El Resultado 1 establece que Teo usará al menos 10 palabras o aproximaciones de palabras de manera espontánea para pedir objetos y actividades preferidas, en español o en inglés, durante las rutinas diarias en el hogar y en la guardería. Las estrategias incluyen el uso del encuadre de enseñanza Hanen para seguir el interés de Teo, ofrecer opciones con apoyo visual durante las comidas y el juego, y modelar lenguaje con espera estructurada (sabotaje comunicativo) durante actividades motivadoras como perseguir a Max. El Resultado 2 establece que Teo disminuirá los episodios de rabietas relacionadas con la comunicación de un promedio de 6 veces al día a 2 veces al día o menos, medido por un registro diario que mantendrán los padres y la maestra, Srta. Ashley Pruitt. Las estrategias incluyen enseñar un sistema básico de intercambio de imágenes inspirado en PECS con tres símbolos iniciales (agua, más, ayuda), y capacitar a la familia y al personal de la guardería para reconocer y responder a los intentos comunicativos tempranos antes de que escalen a la frustración. El Resultado 3 se centra en el apoyo bilingüe familiar: los padres aumentarán el uso de estrategias de lenguaje enriquecido (expansión, narración paralela) en ambos idiomas durante al menos 15 minutos diarios de juego dirigido por el niño. Yo, como patóloga del habla y lenguaje, modelaré estas estrategias en español durante las sesiones, y coordinaré con el programa de inglés en la guardería para asegurar consistencia en ambos entornos lingüísticos, usando el enfoque PROMPT para apoyar la producción motora del habla cuando sea apropiado.

Los servicios de terapia de habla y lenguaje continuarán con una frecuencia de dos sesiones de 45 minutos por semana, una en el hogar y una en Burbujas y Sonrisas Centro de Aprendizaje Temprano, a partir del 14 de octubre de 2026 y hasta la próxima revisión del IFSP, programada para el 7 de abril de 2027. El código de facturación correspondiente es CPT 92507, con el código ICD-10 F80.1 documentado como diagnóstico primario de trastorno del lenguaje expresivo y F80.9 como diagnóstico secundario de trastorno del lenguaje no especificado. El equipo también acordó una consulta de seguimiento con audiología en Carolina Pines Health – Otorrinolaringología y Audiología, Campus de Westover antes de la próxima revisión, dado el historial de otitis media recurrente, programada tentativamente para enero de 2027. La coordinadora de servicios, Juana Ortiz, realizará una llamada de seguimiento el 9 de noviembre de 2026 para verificar el progreso hacia el Resultado 2 y ajustar las estrategias según sea necesario. Todos los documentos de consentimiento fueron firmados por Lucía Ruiz Hernández en la reunión, y una copia del IFSP actualizado se entregará a la familia y a Burbujas y Sonrisas Centro de Aprendizaje Temprano antes del 21 de octubre de 2026.

Antes de concluir la reunión, la familia planteó una pregunta adicional sobre la posibilidad de que Teo reciba terapia ocupacional, dado que también muestra sensibilidad táctil con ciertas texturas de comida. El equipo acordó que la coordinadora Juana Ortiz solicitará una evaluación de terapia ocupacional con T. Alvarado, terapeuta ocupacional del equipo de la CDSA del Piedmont Triad, y que los resultados se compartirán en la próxima revisión. Rosa Hernández Díaz se comprometió a implementar las estrategias de espera estructurada durante los días que cuida a Teo, y la familia recibirá un folleto bilingüe con ejemplos visuales de las estrategias discutidas. Se recordó a la familia que pueden comunicarse con la coordinadora de servicios al 336-555-0199 o por correo electrónico a jortiz@cdsapiedmont.example.org con cualquier pregunta entre visitas. La reunión concluyó a las 4:45 p.m., con todos los participantes expresando acuerdo con el plan descrito. Este informe fue redactado por mí, Mariana Castillo, CCC-SLP, y revisado por la coordinadora de servicios Juana Ortiz antes de su distribución final a la familia el 9 de octubre de 2026.

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Fernández Rodríguez
Date of Birth: July 19, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Parents/Guardians: Carlos Fernández Cruz and Lucía Rodríguez Molina
Home Address: 1420 Holloway Street, Durham, NC 27701
County of Residence: Durham County
CDSA Case Number: CDSA-2026-04471
Medicaid ID: 920114887B
Home Phone: (919) 555-0162
Primary Home Language: Spanish Secondary Language: English
Evaluation Dates: September 2, 2026 and September 9, 2026
Report Date: September 14, 2026
Evaluator: Rachel Whitfield, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist, Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Service Coordinator: Patricia Gómez, Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Tempranos del Triángulo (ACSTT)
Referring Agency: Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios Especiales del Condado de Durham, known locally as the CDSA de Durham
Referring Physician: Dr. James Whitaker, Triangle Pediatric Associates
Daycare/Preschool: Little Sprouts Early Learning Center

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred to the CDSA de Durham by Dr. Whitaker at Mateo's June 24, 2026 well-child visit, after Mateo's parents and his teacher at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, Ms. Amanda Lopez, raised concerns about limited intelligibility, short sentence length, and frustration during communication attempts. Carlos and Lucía report that strangers and even extended family outside the household struggle to understand Mateo, while they themselves understand roughly 70-80% of his speech in context. Ms. Lopez reports that Mateo is understood by classmates only about half the time during free play, and that two classmates, Jayden Thompson and Emma Castillo, often ask an adult to interpret for him.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his parents, Carlos Fernández Cruz and Lucía Rodríguez Molina, and his older sister, Sol Fernández Rodríguez, age 7, a second grader at a different school. The family's maternal grandmother, Carmen Molina, lives nearby and provides childcare two afternoons a week. A babysitter, Daniela Reyes, watches Mateo and his sister on Tuesday evenings while their parents work. The family also has a dog, Rocky, of whom Mateo is very fond; several of his earliest words, per parent report, referenced Rocky. Mateo frequently plays with his cousins, Valentina Ortiz Rodríguez and Diego Ortiz Rodríguez, on weekends.

During the September 9, 2026 session, when a balloon rolled out of reach, Mateo called out "¡Sol, ven!" to get his sister's attention, demonstrating spontaneous two-word combinations with appropriate pragmatic use.

Mateo attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center four days a week, where his lead teacher is Ms. Amanda Lopez and his assistant teacher is Mr. David Nguyen. He has not previously received speech-language services. An occupational therapist, Kevin Park, OTR/L, completed a brief fine-motor screening at the family's request and found no concerns requiring referral.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at Duke Regional Hospital on July 19, 2022 at 38 weeks gestational age via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 6 lb 14 oz. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. Lucía reports an unremarkable pregnancy with regular prenatal care. Mateo met early gross motor milestones within expected ranges (walked at 13 months) but was reportedly late to combine words, per parent report, not doing so until 28 months.

Mateo's hearing was screened on September 2, 2026 and he passed bilaterally at 20 dB across 500-4000 Hz. He has had three episodes of otitis media, the most recent in February 2026, treated with antibiotics without need for tubes. Oral-peripheral examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech; no concerns with dentition, tongue mobility, or velopharyngeal function were noted. Mateo's pediatric record lists a diagnosis under ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), pending confirmation by this evaluation, along with a secondary notation of ICD-10 F80.0 (phonological disorder).

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo is being raised bilingually. Lucía and Carmen Molina speak primarily Spanish with him at home, while Carlos speaks a mix of Spanish and English. Sol speaks both languages with Mateo interchangeably, often code-switching mid-sentence, which is typical for the household. Parents estimate Mateo's current language exposure at roughly 60-40 Spanish-to-English at home, with English exposure increasing substantially at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center. There is no family history of hearing loss. Carlos reports that he himself was a "late talker" who received speech therapy briefly as a preschooler in Puerto Rico, though records are unavailable. No other family members are reported to have diagnosed speech, language, or learning disorders.

Carlos works at Bluefield Manufacturing Solutions in Morrisville, and Lucía works part-time at a dental office. The family's primary caregivers during the day are Carmen Molina and staff at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

Assessment was conducted across two sessions, September 2, 2026 and September 9, 2026, in the family's home, with instructions and prompts provided in both English and Spanish depending on the child's response and parent preference. Rachel Whitfield, M.S., CCC-SLP is fully bilingual and administered all measures directly without need for interpretation. Procedures included parent interview, informal play-based observation, standardized testing in both languages, a 100-utterance language sample, a Spanish phonology sample, oral-mechanism examination, and hearing screening.

TEST RESULTS

| Test / Subtest | Standard Score | 90% CI | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Spanish-English Bilingual Edition, Auditory Comprehension | 73 | 68-78 | 4th | 2;6–3;0 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 78 | 73-83 | 7th | 2;9–3;3 |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | 75 | 70-80 | 5th | 2;9–3;0 |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | 82 | 75-89 | 12th | 3;3–3;9 |
| Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), Core Language Score | 76 | 71-81 | 5th | — |

All standard scores reflect a mean of 100 with a standard deviation of 15. Scores between 78-89 are classified as "Below Average," and scores below 78 are classified as "Severely Below Average" per test manual criteria.

Language Sample (English and Spanish combined, 100 utterances): Mean length of utterance was 2.3 morphemes, below expectations for chronological age. Mateo used primarily two- and three-word combinations ("mas agua," "Rocky come," "no quiero") and omitted grammatical morphemes in both languages, including Spanish gender/number agreement and English plural -s and third-person -s.

Speech Sound Production (Spanish phonology sample): Mateo attempted the target word "sol" ("sun") and produced [tol] for /sol/, substituting [t] for /s/ in 3 of 5 trials, improving to an accurate [sol] with minimal cues. He demonstrated stimulable production of /s/ in isolation and in the word "sopa" with moderate cues. Additional sound errors included final consonant deletion (e.g., "pa" for "pan"), fronting of /k/ to [t], and gliding of /ɾ/ to [w] in words such as "carro," produced as [tawo]. In English, Mateo produced 8/10 word-initial consonants correctly but only 40% of word-final consonants correctly. His intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at 30-40% to unfamiliar listeners and 70-80% to familiar listeners.

Oral-Peripheral Examination: Within normal limits; no structural concerns.

Hearing Screening: Passed bilaterally, see above.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Mateo presents with a mixed expressive-receptive language disorder (CPT 92523, modifier -59 applied for combined evaluation billing) and a moderate phonological disorder affecting intelligibility across both Spanish and English. His scores fall consistently in the below-average to severely-below-average range across both receptive and expressive measures, and his sound system shows patterned, rule-based errors (fronting, final consonant deletion, liquid gliding) that are consistent with a phonological disorder rather than isolated articulation errors, and that affect both of his languages similarly, supporting a true bilingual language/phonological disorder rather than a difference attributable to typical second-language acquisition. His difficulties are not explained by hearing status, oral structure, or insufficient language exposure, and his pattern of errors is consistent across both languages rather than reflecting cross-linguistic transfer alone.

Given his age (4;2) and the degree of delay observed, Mateo meets eligibility criteria for Part C early intervention services through the CDSA de Durham under the established-condition and developmental-delay pathways.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo should receive speech-language therapy services at a frequency of twice weekly, 30-minute sessions, through his IFSP, with services delivered primarily in Spanish and generalized to English as appropriate, consistent with best practice for bilingual language development.
2. Therapy should incorporate Hanen-based parent-coaching strategies to build Carlos and Lucía's capacity to support language growth across both languages in daily routines.
3. A Cycles phonological approach is recommended to target Mateo's patterned sound errors (final consonant deletion, fronting, liquid gliding) across both languages.
4. PROMPT techniques may be introduced to support motor-placement awareness for /s/ and /ɾ/, given his stimulability with cueing.
5. Continued coordination with Little Sprouts Early Learning Center staff, including Ms. Amanda Lopez and Mr. David Nguyen, is recommended to support generalization in the classroom.
6. Re-screening of hearing is recommended at the next well-child visit given his history of recurrent otitis media.
7. This report, along with present levels, will support development of IFSP Outcome 1 (functional communication) and Outcome 2 (intelligibility/speech sound production) at the upcoming review.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Mateo. Please contact me with any questions.

Rachel Whitfield, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

text:
INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
482 Willowbrook Lane, Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601
Teléfono: (828) 555-0147 | Correo electrónico: vjimenez@piedmontpeds-slp.com | Sitio web: www.piedmontpeds-slp.com

Fecha del informe: 2 de octubre de 2026
Fechas de evaluación: 25 de septiembre de 2026 y 30 de septiembre de 2026

INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Nombre del niño: Emiliano Castillo Reyes ("Emi")
Fecha de nacimiento: 3 de marzo de 2023
Edad cronológica al momento de la evaluación: 3;7
Sexo: Masculino
Número de caso / Medicaid: NC4471839K
Número de expediente: PPSLP-20261002-0391

Madre: Gabriela Castillo Luna
Padre: Hugo Reyes Delgado
Dirección familiar: 482 Willowbrook Lane, Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601
Teléfono de contacto: (828) 555-9284

Fuente de referencia: Piedmont CDSA, coordinadora de servicio Claudia Henao
Evaluación previa: 15 de marzo de 2025, realizada por Mónica Alvarado, CCC-SLP, en Piedmont CDSA, cuando Emi tenía 2;0 años

Evaluadora: Valeria Jiménez Soto, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe (inglés/español), licencia de Carolina del Norte #SLP-19284

RAZÓN DE LA REMISIÓN Y ANTECEDENTES

Emiliano, a quien su familia llama cariñosamente "Emi", es un niño de 3;7 años que fue remitido para una evaluación integral de habla y lenguaje por recomendación de su pediatra, el Dr. Antonio Vidal, debido a preocupaciones persistentes sobre la inteligibilidad de su habla y retrasos leves en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo, tanto en inglés como en español. Emi recibe actualmente servicios de intervención temprana a través de Piedmont CDSA bajo un Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP), cuya revisión más reciente ocurrió el 14 de agosto de 2026.

La presente evaluación fue solicitada para determinar la elegibilidad continua de Emi para los servicios de intervención temprana, actualizar los objetivos del IFSP y proporcionar recomendaciones específicas para el hogar, el centro preescolar y las sesiones de terapia. Esta evaluación se suma a la evaluación inicial de 15 de marzo de 2025, que había documentado retrasos leves en lenguaje expresivo y receptivo a la edad de 2;0.

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Emi nació a las 38 semanas de gestación en el Catawba Valley Women's Hospital en Hickory, mediante parto vaginal sin complicaciones. Su peso al nacer fue de 6 libras, 11 onzas, y su puntuación de Apgar fue de 8 al minuto uno y 9 a los cinco minutos. La madre, Gabriela, reportó un embarazo sin complicaciones significativas, sin exposición a tabaco, alcohol o sustancias controladas, y con atención prenatal regular.

El historial médico de Emi incluye tres episodios documentados de otitis media, el más reciente registrado el 12 de enero de 2026. Debido a la recurrencia de estas infecciones, se colocaron tubos de ventilación (timpanostomía bilateral) en un procedimiento realizado por el Dr. Ricardo Flores, otorrinolaringólogo, aproximadamente dos semanas después. No se reportan hospitalizaciones adicionales, cirugías mayores, convulsiones, lesiones cerebrales ni diagnósticos genéticos conocidos. Una audiometría de seguimiento realizada el 20 de enero de 2026 arrojó resultados normales bilaterales, sin evidencia de pérdida auditiva conductiva ni neurosensorial.

Los hitos del desarrollo motor grueso se alcanzaron dentro de límites generalmente esperados: se sentó sin apoyo a los 7 meses y caminó de manera independiente a los 14 meses. Sin embargo, los hitos de comunicación fueron notablemente más lentos: según el reporte de los padres, Emi dijo sus primeras palabras alrededor de los 18 meses y comenzó a combinar dos palabras cerca de los 30 meses, ambos considerados hitos tardíos para su edad. La evaluación visual más reciente, realizada en su control pediátrico de rutina, no reveló anomalías.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Emi vive con su madre, Gabriela Castillo Luna; su padre, Hugo Reyes Delgado; su hermana mayor, Sol Castillo Reyes, de 6 años; y su hermano, Mateo Castillo Reyes, de 9 años. La familia reside en una casa unifamiliar en Hickory. La abuela materna, Rosario Luna, ayuda con el cuidado de Emi tres tardes por semana después de que termina el día en su centro preescolar. La familia también tiene un perro llamado Max, al cual Emi disfruta cuidar y con el cual practica rutinas de juego simbólico.

El hogar es bilingüe y el español es el idioma predominante en la comunicación diaria. La madre, Gabriela, habla principalmente español con los niños, mientras que el padre, Hugo, alterna entre inglés y español según el contexto. La hermana, Sol, y el hermano, Mateo, hablan ambos idiomas con fluidez y a menudo traducen o interpretan para Emi en situaciones sociales fuera del hogar, incluyendo citas médicas. Gabriela trabaja como supervisora de turno en Greenfield Textile Manufacturing, y Hugo trabaja de manera independiente como técnico de climatización. La familia también recibe apoyo nutricional a través de WIC.

No se reporta historia familiar de trastornos del habla o lenguaje en otros miembros cercanos, aunque Gabriela mencionó que un tío materno tuvo dificultades de aprendizaje durante la escuela primaria, sin diagnóstico formal documentado.

HISTORIA EDUCATIVA Y SERVICIOS ACTUALES

Emi asiste al centro Semillitas de Luz Early Learning Studio en Hickory de lunes a viernes, de 8:00 a.m. a 3:30 p.m.. Su maestra principal, la Maestra Diana Pérez, reporta que Emi interactúa bien con sus compañeros, incluyendo a su amigo cercano Santiago, pero que otros compañeros, como Valentina y Bryson, a veces tienen dificultad para entender lo que dice y le piden que repita sus enunciados varias veces antes de comprenderlo.

Actualmente, Emi recibe terapia de habla y lenguaje dos veces por semana y terapia ocupacional una vez por semana a través de Piedmont CDSA. El horario actual de servicios es el siguiente:

| Día | Hora de inicio | Hora de fin | Ubicación |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lunes | 9:00 a.m. | 9:45 a.m. | Semillitas de Luz Early Learning Studio, Hickory |
| Miércoles | 4:15 p.m. | 5:00 p.m. | Domicilio familiar, 482 Willowbrook Lane, Hickory |
| Jueves | 1:30 p.m. | 2:15 p.m. | Oficina de Piedmont CDSA, Conover |

La familia expresa satisfacción general con los servicios actuales, pero solicita más estrategias prácticas para el hogar, particularmente durante las comidas y el tiempo de juego con sus hermanos.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Se administraron los siguientes instrumentos estandarizados y procedimientos informales durante dos sesiones de evaluación, alternando entre español e inglés según la respuesta del niño:

- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5), administrado en español
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4, Subescala de Lenguaje (Bayley-4)
- Observación clínica estructurada y muestra de lenguaje espontáneo
- Entrevista con los padres, Gabriela Castillo Luna y Hugo Reyes Delgado
- Examen orofacial y de estructuras motoras del habla

Toda la evaluación fue realizada por la evaluadora, Valeria Jiménez Soto, quien es bilingüe certificada y no requirió el uso de un intérprete.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS ESTANDARIZADAS

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale: Emi obtuvo puntuaciones consistentes con un nivel funcional de 24–27 meses en comprensión interactiva-atención y de 22–25 meses en lenguaje expresivo gestual, considerablemente por debajo de su edad cronológica de 3;7.

GFTA-3: puntuación estándar de 71 (intervalo de confianza del 95%: 65–77), percentil 3, equivalente de edad de 2;6–3;0.

PPVT-5 (español): puntuación estándar de 78 (intervalo de confianza del 95%: 72–84), percentil 7, equivalente de edad de 2;8–3;1.

Bayley-4, Subescala de Lenguaje: puntuación escalada de 6 (intervalo de confianza del 95%: 4–8), percentil 9, equivalente de edad de 26–29 meses.

| Prueba | Puntuación estándar/escalada | Percentil | Intervalo de confianza (95%) | Equivalente de edad |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GFTA-3 | 71 | 3 | 65–77 | 2;6–3;0 |
| PPVT-5 (español) | 78 | 7 | 72–84 | 2;8–3;1 |
| Bayley-4 Lenguaje | 6 | 9 | 4–8 | 26–29 meses |
| Rossetti Expresivo | N/A | N/A | N/A | 22–25 meses |

ANÁLISIS FONOLÓGICO Y DE ARTICULACIÓN

En la prueba de articulación, Emi demostró un patrón de simplificación de grupos consonánticos y procesos de frontalización, sustituyendo consistentemente el fonema /s/ por [t] en posición inicial de palabra. Para la palabra objetivo "sol", utilizada específicamente para evaluar el fonema /s/, produjo [tol]. Este mismo patrón fue observado en palabras como "sapo" → [tapo] y "silla" → [tiya], lo cual sugiere un proceso fonológico generalizado más que una dificultad aislada con una sola palabra.

También se observó simplificación de grupos consonánticos, por ejemplo "flor" → [for], y procesos de reducción de sílabas finales en palabras polisilábicas. El inventario fonético funcional de Emi incluye los fonemas /m/, /p/, /t/, /n/, /k/ y /w/ de manera consistente, mientras que /s/, /ɾ/ y los grupos consonánticos con /l/ y /ɾ/ se producen con mod cues o se omiten por completo.

MUESTRA DE LENGUAJE ESPONTÁNEO Y OBSERVACIÓN CLÍNICA

Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, Emi produjo enunciados de tres a cuatro palabras como "quiero jugo" y "mi hermana Sol no está", demostrando uso apropiado de pronombres posesivos pero omisión ocasional de artículos definidos. Cuando se le presentó una lámina con la imagen de un sol durante la tarea de nombrado espontáneo, Emi señaló la imagen y dijo "sol" claramente, articulando el sonido inicial como [t] en lugar de /s/, lo cual es consistente con el patrón fonológico descrito anteriormente.

Emi también demostró comprensión adecuada de instrucciones de dos pasos (por ejemplo, "pon el carro en la caja y dame el libro"), lograda en 8/10 ensayos, pero tuvo mayor dificultad con conceptos espaciales como "detrás" y "entre", logrando solo 3 de 5 respuestas correctas con min cues.

EXAMEN OROFACIAL Y MOTOR DEL HABLA

Durante el examen orofacial, se observó simetría facial normal, rango de movimiento adecuado de labios y mandíbula, y un frenillo lingual dentro de límites normales. No se identificaron signos de apraxia del habla infantil ni de disartria. El tono muscular oral fue adecuado para la edad, y no se observaron dificultades de alimentación ni babeo excesivo durante la evaluación.

COMUNICACIÓN SOCIAL Y PRAGMÁTICA

En el área pragmática, Emi demostró buen contacto visual, toma de turnos conversacionales apropiada para su edad, y uso de gestos para complementar su comunicación verbal limitada. Durante el juego con su compañero Santiago en el centro preescolar, según observación reportada por la Maestra Diana Pérez, Emi inicia interacciones sociales con frecuencia, pero se frustra cuando sus compañeros no logran entender sus intentos verbales, recurriendo entonces a señalar objetos o llevar a un adulto de la mano hacia lo que desea comunicar.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, la observación clínica estructurada y los reportes de los padres y la maestra, Emi presenta un trastorno mixto de lenguaje receptivo-expresivo (código ICD-10 F80.2) con un componente fonológico significativo (código ICD-10 F80.0), que afecta tanto el español como el inglés de manera comparable. Sus habilidades de lenguaje receptivo se encuentran aproximadamente 12–14 meses por debajo de lo esperado para su edad cronológica, mientras que el lenguaje expresivo se encuentra aproximadamente 14–16 meses por debajo.

La inteligibilidad del habla de Emi se estima en aproximadamente 40% para oyentes familiares y 20% para oyentes no familiares, lo cual es consistente con las preocupaciones reportadas tanto por su maestra, la Maestra Diana Pérez, como por sus padres, Gabriela Castillo Luna y Hugo Reyes Delgado.

Estos hallazgos indican que Emi continúa siendo elegible para servicios de intervención temprana bajo los criterios de Carolina del Norte, y se recomienda la continuación de terapia de habla y lenguaje con un enfoque dirigido a fonología, vocabulario expresivo y estructura gramatical en ambos idiomas.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Continuar la terapia de habla y lenguaje dos veces por semana, con sesiones de 45 minutos cada una, utilizando los códigos CPT 92523 y CPT 92610 según corresponda para facturación.
2. Actualizar los objetivos del IFSP para incluir el Objetivo 3.2 (aumentar el inventario fonético funcional) y el Objetivo 4.1 (expandir el vocabulario expresivo bilingüe a 300 palabras).
3. Incorporar el enfoque Hanen en las sesiones centradas en el hogar, para fomentar la participación activa de ambos padres, Gabriela Castillo Luna y Hugo Reyes Delgado, durante las rutinas diarias.
4. Utilizar el método PROMPT para apoyar la producción motora del habla, con atención particular a los grupos consonánticos iniciales y al fonema /s/.
5. Implementar el Enfoque de Ciclos (Cycles Approach) para abordar sistemáticamente los procesos fonológicos identificados, incluyendo la sustitución de /s/ por [t] y la simplificación de grupos consonánticos.
6. Practicar en casa con una lista de palabras objetivo que incluya "sapo", "silla", "sopa" y "sol", reforzando la producción correcta del fonema /s/ en posición inicial durante tres sesiones breves de 5 minutos por semana.
7. Coordinar con la Maestra Diana Pérez en Semillitas de Luz Early Learning Studio para reforzar estrategias de comunicación durante el día escolar, incluyendo el uso de apoyos visuales y espera estructurada.
8. Involucrar a la hermana, Sol Castillo Reyes, y al hermano, Mateo Castillo Reyes, en actividades de juego dirigido que modelen enunciados más largos, dado su rol activo como intérpretes informales para Emi.
9. Programar una reevaluación auditiva de seguimiento con el Dr. Ricardo Flores en 6 meses si persisten episodios de otitis media.
10. Reevaluar el progreso de Emi en aproximadamente abril de 2027, o antes de la próxima revisión del IFSP, programada para el 14 de febrero de 2027.

Para preguntas sobre este informe, favor de contactar a Valeria Jiménez Soto, M.S., CCC-SLP, al teléfono (828) 555-0147 o al correo electrónico vjimenez@piedmontpeds-slp.com. the home is primarily spanish speaking mamá Lucía and papá Carlos both grew up in oaxaca and speak spanish to all the kids aunque a veces se les sale el inglés porque llevan 9 años aquí en durham teo is the youngest of three big sister Valentina Hernández Cruz is 7 and in second grade she's described as "súper habladora, para nada como su hermanito" and she translates for teo constantly which the family was told to cut back on so he has to communicate for himself middle sibling is baby brother Diego who is 14 months and just starting to pull to stand abuela Rosa Cruz Martínez lives two streets over and watches the kids tuesdays and thursdays while mamá works a half shift at Sunrise Linen Services abuela speaks only spanish to the kids and reports teo "se enoja y me jala la mano cuando quiere algo, no me dice nada" there's also a part time babysitter named Yesenia Portillo who helps on fridays she notes similar frustration behaviors

the family attends Iglesia Bautista Monte Horeb on calle angier most sundays and teo goes to the nursery room there run by volunteers mamá says he mostly sits by himself during group time and doesn't join in cuando cantan las canciones the family also used to go to the toddler story time at the library but stopped when abuela rosa had knee surgery and couldn't drive them there's no pets currently aside from the family dog Canela who teo adores during the session he ran to the window and said "canela afuera" pointing, which was noted as a two word spanish combination spontaneous and appropriate

teo attends a small home-based program called Casa de los Angelitos three days a week tuesday wednesday and friday from 8:00 am to 1:00 pm his main teacher there is Miss Flor Jiménez who reports he follows the group routine okay with visual cues like the picture schedule but rarely initiates talking to peers during free play two classmates mentioned by name were Sofía and Liam who miss flor says often try to include him but he just hands them a toy instead of using words miss flor also said on el martes 4 de junio during a parent pickup conversation "yo creo que entiende más de lo que habla, pero se frustra rápido" which aligns with what mamá reports at home an occupational therapist Jenny Kim, OTR/L also from Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC sees teo weekly for fine motor goals and was consulted briefly during this visit regarding sensory considerations for seating during testing

during the language sample teo produced mostly one word utterances in spanish with a few two word combinations like "más agua" and "canela afuera" mean length of utterance was calculated at 1.4 morphemes which is low for age he used pointing and pulling an adult's hand as his primary request strategy for about 80% of observed requests imitation was stronger than spontaneous production he imitated 8 of 10 target words when modeled directly getting 8/10 correct on direct imitation trials but dropped to 3 of 10 spontaneously without a model articulation was judged mildly delayed with final consonant deletion noted for example target "pan" produced as "pa" and target "sol" produced as "so" these patterns were consistent across both languages suggesting a true phonological pattern rather than a dialectal feature

during one activity he was shown a picture of a boy running and asked to label it he said "[k]orre" for "corre" substituting an unaspirated stop which was coded [EW] in the transcript for word level substitution he required mod cues meaning a verbal model plus a visual gesture to approximate several two syllable words and needed max cues for three syllable words receptively he followed one step directions in spanish 9/10 trials or 90% but two step directions dropped to 4/10 or 40% accuracy

impressions / impresiones clínicas

teo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both spanish and english though spanish being the dominant input language shows the clearer picture of his underlying language level his scores fall in the low range across both receptive and expressive domains on a standardized bilingual measure with expressive skills notably weaker than receptive this is not accounted for by bilingual exposure alone since the pattern is consistent across both languages which supports a true language disorder rather than typical second language acquisition or normal bilingual development his articulation shows mild delay with consonant final deletion patterns that would be expected to resolve with intervention but are presently impacting intelligibility especially to unfamiliar listeners mamá reports strangers often can't understand him, only familia entiende lo que dice

CONFIDENTIAL — SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
4820 Ridgewood Lane, Durham, NC 27705
Tel: (919) 555-0148 | Fax: (919) 555-0149

Client/Paciente: Mateo Alejandro Ríos Vargas ("Teo")
DOB/Fecha de nacimiento: February 18, 2023
Age at eval/Edad al momento de la evaluación: 3;7
Medicaid ID: 920481736B
Record/Case #: CDSA-2026-01842
Eval date/Fecha de evaluación: September 22, 2026
Parents/Padres: Lucía Vargas Ríos (mamá), Carlos Ríos Peña (papá)
Address/Dirección: 118 Calle del Sol, Durham, Durham County, NC 27703
Phone/Teléfono: (984) 555-0271
Language(s)/Idiomas en el hogar: Spanish (dominant), English (emerging)
Referred by/Referido por: Dr. Patricia Nguyen, Triangle Pediatrics of Durham
CDSA: el Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Discapacidades del Área de Durham (CDSA de Durham)
Service Coordinator/Coordinadora de servicios: Nora Jiménez, la Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios para la Niñez Temprana del Triángulo (la Agencia Triángulo)
Evaluator/Evaluadora: Ana Delgado Soto, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual SLP

**Reason for Referral / Motivo de la Remisión**

Teo es un niño de 3;7 remitido por Dr. Patricia Nguyen b/c of concerns re: expressive lang delay and unintelligible speech noted at his 3-yr well check. Mamá Lucía reports pt "no habla casi nada en inglés y en español se le entiende poco" — he barely speaks English, and in Spanish he is hard to understand. CG Carlos adds pt gets frustrated, "se enoja y empuja cuando no lo entendemos" — gets angry and pushes when we don't understand him. Referral initiated thru CDSA de Durham; eval requested by Nora Jiménez to inform IFSP eligibility ahead of the October 6, 2026 IFSP review.

**Background Information / Antecedentes**

Hx obtained via parent interview (mixed EN/ES) w/ Lucía and Carlos, review of CDSA referral packet, and consult c/ Nora Jiménez. Family resides w/ pt's older sister, Valentina (age 6, currently in 1st grade), and maternal grandmother doña Lupe, who provides daytime childcare approx 3x/wk while parents work. Carlos works 2nd shift at Blue Ridge Furniture Manufacturing; Lucía works part-time at Durham Regional Medical Billing. Family receives support thru WIC and was previously connected w/ a Smart Start bilingual playgroup, discontinued June 2026 b/c of transportation.

Extended family remains closely involved despite geographic distance; paternal grandparents reside in Mexico and visit approx 1x/yr, and pt's tía, tía Rosa, stays w/ the family each summer and reportedly serves as an additional caregiver and Spanish-language model during those visits. Pt's cousin, Diego, also stays during summer visits and per parent report the two boys "se entienden perfecto sin hablar casi" — understand each other perfectly without talking much — which parents cite as evidence pt's social-communication desire is intact despite limited verbal output.

**Birth and Medical History / Historia Médica y del Nacimiento**

Per mamá report, prenatal care was provided by Dr. Rachel Kim; pregnancy reached 37 weeks 2 days, uncomplicated except mild gestational diabetes managed by diet. Pt delivered via NSVD at Duke Regional Hospital, birth weight 6 lbs 2 oz, Apgar 8/9. No NICU stay. Hx of recurrent OM (otitis media) w/ 4 documented episodes btwn 8 months and 18 months; bilateral PE tubes placed March 11, 2025 by Dr. Owen Baptiste, ENT. Parents report hearing improved post-tubes per follow-up audiogram April 29, 2025, results WNL bilaterally. No hx of seizures, no hospitalizations beyond the outpt tube placement. Current meds: none. Vision screening WNL at last well visit.

**Family and Language History / Antecedentes Familiares y Lingüísticos**

Home language environment is predominantly Spanish; both parents and doña Lupe speak Spanish w/ pt >90% of time per parent report. Lucía states "en casa solo hablamos español, pero él ve dibujos animados en inglés" — at home we only speak Spanish, but he watches cartoons in English. English exposure occurs primarily at daycare (approx 25 hrs/wk) and incidentally via screen media.

Fam hx: Carlos reports personal hx of late talking, "yo también hablé tarde, pero se me arregló" — I also talked late, but it worked itself out. No other reported fam hx of speech/lang/hearing disorders, autism, or genetic conditions. Valentina reportedly met early lang milestones WNL and is bilingual Spanish-English.

Developmental milestones per parent report: sat unsupported approx 7 months, walked independently approx 14 months. First words (Spanish) emerged approx 16-18 months per report, though parents note vocab growth has been slow since. No current words in English reported at home.

**Cultural and Linguistic Considerations / Consideraciones Culturales y Lingüísticas**

Current performance was interpreted relative to bilingual acquisition norms, not monolingual English norms, given Spanish-dominant home exposure. A period of a few months of apparent "silence" or reduced output during early English exposure is typical in young bilingual learners and was not, by itself, considered diagnostic. However, pt's delays are present in Spanish, his dominant and most-exposed language, across both standardized measures and spontaneous sample, which per current bilingual-assessment best practice indicates a true language disorder rather than a typical bilingual developmental pattern or "silent period."

**Educational / Daycare History**

Pt currently attends Little Scholars Daycare 5 days/wk, in Ms. Lopez's room (toddler classroom). Per Ms. Lopez, pt "plays alongside peers but rarely initiates verbal interaction" and uses gestures/pointing to request. Prior to enrollment there (January 2026), pt was cared for in a home daycare setting run by la maestra Carmen, who reportedly expressed early concern re: pt's limited verbal output compared to other children in her care. Pt's primary peer at current daycare is a classmate, Sofía, whom parents say pt "busca siempre" — always looks for — during drop-off; a second classmate, Liam, reportedly participates alongside pt in small-group circle time w/o reported peer conflict.

Pt also shows strong positive affect toward the daycare van driver, known to the family as Mr. Tom; per Lucía, pt waves and vocalizes enthusiastically each morning when Tom's van arrives, which parents cite as an example of pt's intact social motivation. Parents also note pt refers to the evaluator as "Miss Ana" at home following a prior screening visit, and has reportedly asked to "ir a jugar con Miss Ana" since.

**Assessment Procedures / Procedimientos de Evaluación**

Eval conducted in clinic setting over one 90-minute session, September 22, 2026, 9:30 a.m.–11:00 a.m., w/ both parents present for portions of session. Mixed EN/ES administration per standard bilingual protocol; evaluator (Ana Delgado Soto) is a native Spanish speaker fluent in both langs, so no interpreter was required for direct testing. A brief follow-up phone call w/ Carlos on September 24, 2026 re: hx clarification was conducted w/ the help of Mrs. Pérez, agency interpreter, due to a work schedule conflict.

Tools administered:
- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (parent report + direct observation, English and Spanish items)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), w/ Spanish sound inventory supplemented informally
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 (Bayley-4), Cognitive and Language subtests
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5), Spanish form administered given language dominance
- Oral mechanism exam, hearing screening (pass bilaterally at 20 dB, 500-4000 Hz)
- Language sample analysis, 50-utterance sample coded per SALT conventions

**Test Results / Resultados**

| Test/Subtest | Date Administered | Standard Score | 95% CI | Percentile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rossetti Interaction-Attachment | September 22, 2026 | 70 | 64-76 | 2nd |
| Rossetti Pragmatics | September 22, 2026 | 68 | 61-75 | 2nd |
| Bayley-4 Receptive Language | September 22, 2026 | 76 | 70-82 | 5th |
| Bayley-4 Expressive Language | September 22, 2026 | 62 | 55-69 | 1st |
| PPVT-5 (Spanish form) | September 23, 2026 | 79 | 72-86 | 8th |
| GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | September 23, 2026 | 65 | 58-72 | 1st |

Note: two session dates reflect that the PPVT-5 and GFTA-3 were completed at a brief follow-up play-based session on September 23, 2026 due to pt fatigue during the initial visit.

**Oral Mechanism / Hearing**

Oral structures WNL for speech; adequate labial, lingual, and velopharyngeal function observed during feeding and play. Hearing screening pass bilaterally (see above); no current audiological concerns, though hx of OM warrants ongoing monitoring.

**Speech Sound Production**

Phonemic inventory in Spanish includes /m/, /n/, /p/, /b/, /t/, /d/, /k/ produced consistently; /ɾ/ (tap r) and /r/ (trill) not yet observed, substituted w/ [l] or omitted. Target word "pelota" (ball) produced as [peota], consistent w/ liquid simplification. Final consonant deletion noted in multisyllabic words, e.g., "sol" (sun) produced as [so]. In English, pt attempted "dog," produced as [dɔ], demonstrating cross-linguistic consistency of final consonant deletion, suggesting a phonological rather than purely bilingual-acquisition-related pattern.

Pt has a strong bond w/ the family dog, Rocky; per parent report, pt's first clearly intelligible word was the dog's name. During play in session, pt attempted to call the dog, producing [woki] as an approximation of "Rocky." Intelligibility estimated at 30% to unfamiliar listeners and 60% to familiar listeners (parents), consistent w/ parent report.

**Language Sample / Pragmática**

50-utterance spontaneous sample (mixed EN/ES) analyzed; MLU 1.8 morphemes, below expected range for age (expected approx 3.0-3.5). Pt used primarily single-word utterances and some two-word combos ("más agua" — more water; "no quiero" — don't want). Pt demonstrated functional gestures (pointing, reaching, pulling adult toward desired object) to compensate for limited verbal output. Turn-taking and joint attention WNL for age; pt initiated bids for attention w/ eval'r approx 8 times across session, and responded to name consistently.

During session, when mamá Lucía held up a toy and asked "¿qué es esto?" pt pointed and said "guau guau" (approximating "perro"/dog), demonstrating semantic knowledge exceeding expressive output.

**Behavioral Observations**

Pt presented as social, engaged, and generally cooperative, w/ mod cues needed to maintain task attention across session. Frustration noted 1x when pt was unable to retrieve a desired word, resulting in brief vocal protest; resolved w/ CG reassurance ("Carlos se lo dijo tranquilo y el niño se calmó" — Carlos spoke to him calmly and the child settled). No significant behavioral concerns reported by Ms. Lopez or parents outside of communication-related frustration.

**Impressions / Impresiones Clínicas**

Based on standardized testing, parent/CG report, and direct observation, Teo presents w/ a Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder, more pronounced expressively, in the context of bilingual (Spanish-English) language development. Scores fall in the below-average to significantly-below-average range across both receptive and expressive domains in Spanish (dominant language), indicating a true language disorder rather than a typical bilingual second-language acquisition pattern (ICD-10 F80.2, Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder). A concurrent Speech Sound Disorder is also indicated (ICD-10 F80.0) given phonological process patterns observed consistently across both langs.

Hx of recurrent OM may have contributed to early lang delay via reduced auditory access during a critical period, though current hearing is WNL. Family provides a linguistically rich, supportive home environment; no concerns re: stimulation or exposure. Pt meets criteria for CDSA eligibility under the NC Infant-Toddler Program criteria (>25% delay in 2 domains).

**Recommendations / Recomendaciones**

1. Pt is a candidate for ongoing speech-language tx services; recommend 2x/wk, 45-min sessions, in-home or in clinic, Spanish-primary w/ English exposure incorporated per family preference.
2. Target areas: expressive vocabulary growth, two-to-three-word combinations, improved speech sound inventory (targeting /r/, /ɾ/, final consonants), and functional communication strategies to reduce frustration.
3. Consider parent-coaching strategies (e.g., modeling, expansion techniques per Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" approach); family expressed strong interest in home-based strategies they can use w/ doña Lupe during daytime care.
4. Continue hearing monitoring given hx of OM; refer back to Dr. Patricia Nguyen or audiology if new concerns arise.
5. Collaborate w/ Little Scholars Daycare staff, incl. Ms. Lopez, to reinforce communication strategies in the classroom; consult note to be shared w/ written consent.
6. Share results w/ CDSA de Durham and service coordinator Nora Jiménez to inform IFSP development at the upcoming review, scheduled October 6, 2026.
7. Re-eval recommended in 6 months to monitor progress and adjust goals (IFSP outcome #2 and #3).
8. Family may benefit from connection w/ a bilingual parent support group thru Smart Start if transportation barriers resolve.
9. Medicaid prior authorization will need renewal to cover recommended frequency; see billing note below.

**Billing/Authorization**

CPT codes used for this eval: 92523 (speech/lang eval) and 92522 (eval of speech sound production). Prior authorization obtained thru Medicaid, Auth #AUTH-2026-77341, valid thru March 31, 2027.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Teo. Please contact this office at (919) 555-0148 w/ questions.

Respectfully submitted,

Ana Delgado Soto, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

CAROLINA BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
4815 Jones Franklin Road, Suite 220, Raleigh, NC 27606

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT
(Bilingual Spanish/English Administration)

Client: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: March 3, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Dates of Evaluation: September 15, 2026 and September 18, 2026
Evaluator: Hannah Whitfield, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Spanish-English Clinician
Interpreter/Language Support: Carolina Vásquez, Certified Medical Interpreter
Referral Source: Wake County CDSA (Children's Developmental Services Agency), via Service Coordinator Brianna Hayes
Record/Case Number: 24-WCCDSA-00871
NC Medicaid ID: 9004471852B
Home Address: 482 Birchwood Lane, Garner, NC 27529 (Wake County)
Parents/Guardians: Lucía Rodríguez (mother), Diego Flores (father)
Current Program/School: Oak Grove Elementary School, Pre-K/Exceptional Children classroom, Ms. Patricia Lopez, Wake County Public School System

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo is a 4;2-year-old bilingual Spanish-English-speaking boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language re-evaluation by Wake County CDSA in preparation for his transition from Part C early intervention to Part B preschool services through Wake County Public School System. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez, and his classroom teacher, Ms. Patricia Lopez, raised concerns about his intelligibility, expressive vocabulary, and sentence structure in both languages, and about his difficulty following multi-step directions during circle time at Oak Grove Elementary School. Mateo's previous IFSP, developed through Wake County CDSA, is due for its annual review, and this evaluation will inform updated outcomes and eligibility determination.

BACKGROUND AND DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez and Diego Flores, and his older sister, Camila, in Garner, NC. The family's cat, Nala, is frequently mentioned by Mateo during play-based sessions, and he often narrates her movements around the house. Lucía Rodríguez works second shift at Food Lion Distribution Center #412, and Diego Flores works at Case Farms in Dudley, NC. Because of their work schedules, Mateo and Camila are cared for several afternoons each week by their babysitter, Yesenia Torres, who speaks primarily Spanish with the children. Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Rodríguez, also helps with childcare on weekends and reports that Mateo enjoys playing with his cousins, Ángel Rodríguez and Sofía Rodríguez, during family gatherings.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestational age at WakeMed Cary Hospital on March 3, 2022, following a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia. Birth weight was 4 pounds, 6 ounces, and Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. He was admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at WakeMed Cary Hospital for 19 days, where he required supplemental oxygen and nasogastric tube feeding. His attending neonatologist in the NICU was Dr. Linda Chao. Lucía Rodríguez reported that feeding sessions in the NICU were scheduled around 2:30 PM and 8:00 PM to accommodate her work breaks, and that nursing staff worked closely with her on bottle-feeding techniques before discharge.

Following discharge, Mateo was followed by pediatrician Dr. Samuel Okafor at WakeMed Physician Practices – Pediatrics at Brier Creek for routine well-child care and prematurity-related monitoring. At approximately 18 months, Lucía Rodríguez reported recurrent ear infections, and Mateo was referred to UNC Health Rex Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology, Rex Hospital Campus, where he was seen by otolaryngologist Dr. Priya Nair. Bilateral myringotomy tubes were placed at 19 months of age, with documented resolution of otitis media episodes thereafter. Audiologist Dr. Megan Caldwell, also at UNC Health Rex Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology, Rex Hospital Campus, completed a follow-up audiological evaluation on June 10, 2026, which showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally, with normal middle ear function on tympanometry. No further ENT or audiology concerns have been reported. Mateo's medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no reported seizures, significant illnesses, or hospitalizations beyond the NICU stay and tube placement surgery.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo is being raised bilingually. Lucía Rodríguez reports that Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home, used by both parents, Rosa Rodríguez, Yesenia Torres, and extended family including Ángel Rodríguez and Sofía Rodríguez. English exposure has increased since Mateo began attending the Pre-K/Exceptional Children classroom at Oak Grove Elementary School under Ms. Patricia Lopez, where instruction occurs primarily in English with some bilingual support staff. His sister, Camila, who is in third grade and attends Oak Grove Elementary School as well, frequently code-switches between Spanish and English at home and often serves as a language model and interpreter for Mateo during family conversations.

Lucía Rodríguez reported that Mateo's early language milestones were delayed relative to Camila's development at the same age: his first words emerged around 22 months, and he was not combining words into short phrases until close to 3 years. He began receiving early intervention services through Wake County CDSA at approximately 2;6, including speech-language therapy, with services coordinated by Brianna Hayes. Diego Flores noted that he, too, was described as a "late talker" by his own mother and did not become easily understood by unfamiliar listeners until around age 5, which the family considers relevant given Mateo's current intelligibility concerns.

EDUCATIONAL AND SOCIAL HISTORY

Mateo has attended Oak Grove Elementary School since August 25, 2025, in Ms. Patricia Lopez's Pre-K/Exceptional Children classroom, which includes both typically developing peers and children receiving special education services. Ms. Patricia Lopez reports that Mateo is social and eager to interact with classmates, particularly Logan and Aiden, with whom he frequently plays during free choice time. However, she notes that Mateo's peers often ask him to repeat himself, and that he sometimes becomes frustrated and gives up on communication attempts when not understood on the first try. Ms. Patricia Lopez also reported that Mateo has difficulty following two-step directions given only in English, such as "put your folder away and sit on the carpet," though he follows similar directions more reliably when given in Spanish or paired with gestures.

Mateo previously attended a home daycare for approximately eight months before transitioning to Oak Grove Elementary School; no concerns from that setting were available for review at this time.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo presented as a friendly, curious child who separated easily from Lucía Rodríguez in the waiting area and engaged readily with Hannah Whitfield and interpreter Carolina Vásquez across both evaluation sessions, which began at approximately 9:15 AM and 10:00 AM respectively. He demonstrated good eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during structured play and testing tasks. His speech was frequently difficult to understand, particularly in connected speech and when producing multisyllabic words, with intelligibility estimated at approximately 40% in English and 60% in Spanish to an unfamiliar listener. He used gestures and pointing to supplement verbal communication when he was not understood, but did not display significant frustration during the evaluation sessions themselves. Mateo required occasional redirection to remain seated during tabletop tasks but was generally cooperative and attentive, with best performance noted when tasks were presented in brief segments with visual supports.

ASSESSMENT TOOLS ADMINISTERED

The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both English and Spanish as appropriate, with interpretation support from Carolina Vásquez:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English Bilingual Edition
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Phonology subtests
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Fifth Edition (CELF-5), selected subtests
- Speech sample analysis (conversational and single-word)
- Oral-motor and oral-peripheral examination
- Parent and teacher interview and rating scales

TEST RESULTS

Standard Score	Percentile Rank	Age Equivalent	Qualitative Range
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension	78	7th	2;9	Below Average
PLS-5 Expressive Communication	72	3rd	2;6	Below Average
PLS-5 Total Language Score	73	4th	2;7	Below Average
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words	65	1st	--	Severe
BESA Morphosyntax	70	2nd	--	Below Average
BESA Phonology	68	2nd	--	Below Average
CELF-5 Following Directions	71	3rd	--	Below Average

On the PLS-5, Mateo achieved a Total Language standard score of 73 (73-83 confidence interval), falling within the Below Average range and indicating delays in both receptive and expressive language relative to same-age peers in both languages. His Auditory Comprehension standard score of 78 suggests mild-to-moderate receptive delays, while his Expressive Communication standard score of 72 reflects more pronounced expressive delays, consistent with teacher and parent report.

Articulation testing via the GFTA-3 yielded a standard score of 65, in the Severe range, with error patterns including final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and gliding of liquids. Mateo produced /w/ for /ɾ/ and /l/ in both languages (e.g., he produced "[wojo]" for the target word "rojo"), and consistently reduced consonant clusters, producing "[peyo]" for the target "perro." In English, he produced "[bu]" for the target word "blue" and "[wa]" for the target word "run." Stimulability testing showed that Mateo could approximate several target sounds in isolation with max cues, including moderate success producing /k/ and /g/ in the initial position with mod cues, suggesting good candidacy for direct articulation intervention.

On the BESA Morphosyntax subtest, Mateo scored 70 (2nd percentile), with omissions of grammatical morphemes in both languages, including article omission, verb tense marking errors, and plural marker omission. He was observed to say "the dog run" for "the dog is running" and "yo come" instead of "yo como," reflecting difficulty with verb conjugation in Spanish as well. BESA Phonology results (68, 2nd percentile) were consistent with GFTA-3 findings, supporting a diagnosis of speech sound disorder affecting both languages equally, which is consistent with a primary disorder rather than a language-difference pattern.

On the CELF-5 Following Directions subtest, Mateo scored 71 (3rd percentile), correctly following 3 of 5 two-step directions and 1 of 5 three-step directions presented in English, improving to 4 of 5 and 2 of 5 respectively when directions were presented in Spanish, consistent with teacher-reported classroom performance.

Oral-peripheral examination revealed adequate structure and function of the oral mechanism for speech production, with no evidence of structural abnormality, and diadochokinetic rates within normal limits for age.

IMPRESSIONS

Mateo presents with a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder and moderate expressive and mild-to-moderate receptive language delay, evident across both English and Spanish and therefore consistent with a true communication disorder rather than a typical pattern of bilingual language development or second-language acquisition. His history of chronic otitis media, resolved with bilateral myringotomy tube placement under the care of Dr. Priya Nair at UNC Health Rex Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology, Rex Hospital Campus, likely contributed to early speech and language delays, though current audiological status is within normal limits per Dr. Megan Caldwell's most recent evaluation. His history of prematurity, with a NICU stay at WakeMed Cary Hospital under the care of Dr. Linda Chao, is also a known risk factor for speech-language delay. Mateo's strengths include strong social communication skills, good attention and engagement during structured tasks, intact oral-motor structures, and a supportive bilingual home and school environment.

Mateo meets eligibility criteria for continued speech-language services under the category of Speech or Language Impairment as he transitions from Wake County CDSA Part C services to Part B preschool special education services coordinated through Wake County Public School System.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo should receive direct speech-language therapy services, recommended at a minimum of twice weekly for 30-minute sessions, targeting articulation and expressive language goals in both English and Spanish.
2. Therapy should utilize a cycles approach (Cycles) for phonological pattern remediation, targeting final consonant deletion and cluster reduction as priority patterns, supplemented by minimal pairs activities.
3. A combination of PROMPT and traditional articulation therapy techniques is recommended to address placement and manner errors for /ɾ/, /l/, and consonant clusters in both languages.
4. Hanen-based strategies (It Takes Two to Talk) are recommended for home carryover, with coaching provided to Lucía Rodríguez, Diego Flores, and babysitter Yesenia Torres to support language modeling in the home.
5. Continued collaboration with Ms. Patricia Lopez and classroom staff at Oak Grove Elementary School is recommended, including visual supports and bilingual direction-giving strategies to support Mateo's comprehension in the classroom.
6. Continued monitoring of hearing status is recommended given history of chronic otitis media; routine audiological re-evaluation with Dr. Megan Caldwell or another audiologist at UNC Health Rex Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology, Rex Hospital Campus is recommended if any recurrence of ear infection symptoms occurs.
7. Referral for an updated IFSP/IEP transition meeting is recommended, to be coordinated by Brianna Hayes at Wake County CDSA, in collaboration with Wake County Public School System Exceptional Children's staff.
8. Family should continue to use both Spanish and English consistently in the home, as there is no evidence that bilingual exposure is contributing to Mateo's delays; rather, a true underlying speech-language disorder is present across both languages.

IFSP OUTCOME REVIEW

Nota de sesión diaria – 11 de octubre de 2026, 3:15 p.m.

Mateo Hernández (4;2) recibió su sesión de terapia de habla y lenguaje en el hogar familiar en Durham, Carolina del Norte, como seguimiento a la meta 2 de su IFSP. Estuvo presente su mamá, Lucía Hernández, y por un momento su hermana mayor, Sol Hernández, de 7 años, quien llegó temprano de la escuela.

Mateo mostró buena disposición durante toda la sesión. Trabajamos el sonido inicial /s/ en palabras monosílabas, usando tarjetas con dibujos de "sol", "sopa" y "silla". Produjo el fonema objetivo con 8/10 intentos correctos usando claves mínimas, una mejora respecto a la sesión anterior. Cuando mostró la tarjeta del "sol", lo nombró espontáneamente dos veces sin apoyo. Su hermana, Sol Hernández, observó la actividad y sonrió al escuchar que compartía nombre con la palabra practicada.

Según la evaluación reciente con el PLS-5, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 73 (percentil 4) en Comunicación Expresiva. Continuamos usando el enfoque Cycles para generalizar los patrones fonológicos trabajados.

La coordinadora de servicios, Marta Gómez, de la Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Infantiles del Condado de Durham (ACSI de Durham), llamó durante la sesión para confirmar la próxima revisión del IFSP. El caso de Mateo permanece abierto en el Centro de Desarrollo y Discapacidades del Área de Piedmont (CDSA de Piedmont), bajo el expediente CDSA-48213.

La familia reportó que Mateo fue aceptado en el Distrito Escolar del Condado de Durham y comenzará en enero en la Escuela Primaria Oak Hill, en el salón de la maestra Sra. López. Lucía Hernández mencionó además que recibe apoyo del Departamento de Servicios Sociales (DSS) para la renovación de Medicaid, que sigue inscrita en WIC, y que está en lista de espera para Smart Start y para el programa Early Head Start del condado.

El número de Medicaid de Mateo es 987654321A. Se recomienda continuar sesiones semanales y reevaluar el progreso fonológico en cuatro semanas.
